legend: Red is a Pokemon trainer who has beaten the Kanto Pokemon League, and wants to get to Johto for new challenges. To get there, he needs to travel by train.

The region has N$$$N$$$ train stations labelled from 1$$$1$$$ to N$$$N$$$. Ash starts at station 1$$$1$$$ and needs to get to station N$$$N$$$ to enter Johto. There are M$$$M$$$ bidirectional train lines, where the ith$$$i^{\text{th}}$$$ train line connects stations Xi$$$X_i$$$ and Yi$$$Y_i$$$, and multiple train lines may connect the same pair of cities. It is possible to get from city 1$$$1$$$ to city N$$$N$$$ with the train lines, but it may not be possible to get from city 1$$$1$$$ to some other cities with the train lines.

To use the ith$$$i^{\text{th}}$$$ train line, Red needs to pay Ci$$$C_i$$$ dollars for a lifetime pass, after which he may use the train line as many times as he wants. He can only purchase the pass for the ith$$$i^{\text{th}}$$$ train line when he is at station Xi$$$X_i$$$ or Yi$$$Y_i$$$, and he can only purchase it once.

The payment system is online, where Red only needs to make a delayed bulk payment for the passes he bought when he enters Johto (due to immigration policies). Note that when he reaches station N$$$N$$$, he does not need to pay yet, and can continue taking trains. He only pays when he exits station N$$$N$$$ and reaches the immigration counter.
Due to a bug in the system, he will only need to pay for the passes with the K$$$K$$$ smallest costs (or all of them if he bought fewer than K$$$K$$$ passes) when he reaches Johto.
Help Red determine the minimum amount of money (in dollars) he needs to spend to get from Kanto to Johto.
input: The first line of the input contains 3 integers N,M,K$$$N, M, K$$$ (2≤N≤105$$$2 \leq N \leq 10^5$$$, 1≤K≤M≤2⋅105$$$1 \leq K \leq M \leq 2 \cdot 10^5$$$).
The next M$$$M$$$ lines of the input each contain 3 integers Xi,Yi,Ci$$$X_i, Y_i, C_i$$$ (1≤Xi,Yi≤N$$$1 \leq X_i, Y_i \leq N$$$, Xi≠Yi$$$X_i \neq Y_i$$$, 1≤Ci≤109$$$1 \leq C_i \leq 10^9$$$).
It is guaranteed that Red can get from station 1$$$1$$$ to station N$$$N$$$ using the train lines.
output: Output a single integer, the minimum amount of money (in dollars) Red needs to spend to get from station 1 to station N$$$N$$$.
note: In the first sample, note that Red cannot buy the pass for the train line connecting stations 3$$$3$$$ and 6$$$6$$$, as there is no way to reach those cities by train.

To get to city N$$$N$$$, Red may buy the pass to travel between stations 1$$$1$$$ and 2$$$2$$$, travel to station 2$$$2$$$, buy the pass to travel between stations 2$$$2$$$ and 7$$$7$$$, travel to station 7$$$7$$$, buy the pass to travel between stations 7$$$7$$$ and 5$$$5$$$, travel to station 5$$$5$$$, buy the pass to travel between stations 5$$$5$$$ and 4$$$4$$$, travel back to station 7$$$7$$$ (note that he does not have to travel to station 4$$$4$$$ after buying the pass), then go to immigration.
The passes he buys cost 3,3,2,2$$$3, 3, 2, 2$$$ in that order, and he pays for the K=2$$$K = 2$$$ cheapest, for a cost of 2+2=4$$$2 + 2 = 4$$$. It can be shown this is the minimum possible.

In the second sample, Red may travel 1→2→6→4→7$$$1 \rightarrow 2 \rightarrow 6 \rightarrow 4 \rightarrow 7$$$, buying the passes between consecutive cities in the route, and pay 4+3+2+3=12$$$4 + 3 + 2 + 3 = 12$$$ as he only buys 4$$$4$$$ passes but K=5$$$K = 5$$$. It can be shown this is the minimum possible.

In the third sample, Red may buy all the passes, and he only pays for the K=2$$$K = 2$$$ passes between stations 1$$$1$$$ and 2$$$2$$$ which cost 1$$$1$$$ each, for a total cost of 1+1=2$$$1 + 1 = 2$$$.

legend: In Piplup Nation, they are under attack by a horde of Chimchars. The battlefield can be represented by a line with N$$$N$$$ areas labeled 1$$$1$$$ to N$$$N$$$ from left to right.

Each Piplup can unleash a powerful Hydro Pump leftward, damaging Chimchars that are on its left (including its own area). Notably, the ith$$$i^{\text{th}}$$$ Piplup can fire a Hydro Pump that deals Di$$$D_i$$$ damage to all Chimchars in area j≤i$$$j \leq i$$$. (Total damage to Chimchars)−(Total Cost)$$$(\text{Total damage to Chimchars}) - (\text{Total Cost})$$$.
note: If we choose to make Piplup 3$$$3$$$ and 5$$$5$$$ fire, the damage dealt to the chimchars would be [6,3,2,3,1]$$$[6, 3, 2, 3, 1]$$$.

legend.ai: 在 Piplup Nation 中，他们正遭受一群 Chimchar 的攻击。战场可以表示为一条包含 N$$$N$$$ 个区域的线段，这些区域从左到右编号为 1$$$1$$$ 到 N$$$N$$$。

legend: You are stuck in a desert. The desert can be thought of as a Cartesian grid. There are many oases in the desert of which you know the xy$$$xy$$$-coordinates. You are going to be making a series of trips between pairs of oases, i.e., each trip has a starting oasis and an ending oasis. For any trip, you can stop in other oases along the way (as many as you'd like).

You obviously need water to travel in the desert. It turns out that every 1$$$1$$$ unit traveled in the desert requires 1$$$1$$$ unit of water. You need to determine what canteen size to use for each trip. You'd like to use the smallest canteen size for each trip (no one wants to carry more than what is needed).

You can fill up the canteen used in a trip at each oasis along the way to hold you until the next oasis. Thus, the maximum Euclidean distance between pairs of consecutive oases along your path for the trip determines the canteen size you need. For example, if you traveled from (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$ to (2,4)$$$(2, 4)$$$ to (4,5)$$$(4, 5)$$$, then your maximum distance would be approximately 4.472$$$4.472$$$, the distance between (0,0)$$$(0,0)$$$ and (2,4)$$$(2,4)$$$, because this is longer than the distance between (2,4)$$$(2,4)$$$ and (4,5)$$$(4,5)$$$. This distance determines the canteen size needed for the trip.

Given the number of oases in the desert and several trips (each trip with a starting oasis and an ending oasis), determine the maximum Euclidean distance between pairs of consecutive oases along the path for each trip.

legend: As an entertainment after the programming contest, you hold a game event for the participants.

Two sets of cards, red ones and blue ones, are used in the game. Both of the two sets have the same number of cards as the number of the participants, and each card has one integer written on it. It is known that the contents of these two sets are the same; the integers on the red cards are the same as those on the blue cards as multisets. Even though, you don't know what integers are actually written on the cards. The same integer may be written on two or more cards of the same color, and the integers may be negative.

You distributed one red card and one blue card to each of the participants. As the game result depends on the sum of the integers on the two cards distributed to each participant, you asked all the participants to declare their sums.

Your task is to find a possible card distribution consistent with the participants' declarations, that is, a combination of integers on the cards distributed to each participant. Note that such a combination might not exist, as the participants may commit miscalculations. In such a case, report that there is no consistent combination.

The end of the input is indicated by a line consisting of a zero.
output: For each dataset, if there exists no combination of integers on the cards distributed to each participant that is consistent with the participants' declarations, output "No" in one line. legend.ai: 作为编程竞赛后的娱乐活动，你为参赛者举办了一场游戏活动。
游戏中使用两组卡片，分别为红色卡片和蓝色卡片。两组卡片的数量都与参赛者人数相同，并且每张卡片上都写有一个整数。已知这两组卡片的内容相同，即红色卡片上的整数与蓝色卡片上的整数构成相同的多重集合。不过，你不知道卡片上实际写着哪些整数。同一种颜色的两张或更多卡片上可能写有相同的整数，并且这些整数可能为负数。
你给每位参赛者分发一张红色卡片和一张蓝色卡片。由于游戏结果取决于分发给每位参赛者的两张卡片上的整数之和，你要求所有参赛者报出他们的和。

legend: The king of Belle Aire People's Country has come up with a new plan: he has heard about the popular phenomenon called "King of the Hill", and he would like to become one as well. To do so, he has ordered you to raise a flag on the highest hill in his square kingdom, which has dimensions n×n$$$n \times n$$$. You are given a very expensive (it is gold- and jewel-embedded) satellite-based height-measuring system. This equipment is highly accurate: the heights on every location in the kingdom are represented with distinct integers. However, to cut costs, you are only allowed to take 10n+100$$$10n+100$$$ measurements before reporting back to the king.

Furthermore, you know for certain that there is only a single point that is the absolute highest: this is the only point for which its height is larger than the (up to) four orthogonally adjacent points that lie inside the kingdom. In other words, there are no local maxima besides the global maximum.
Interaction

This is an interactive problem. Your submission will be run against an interactor, which reads from the standard output of your submission and writes to the standard input of your submission. This interaction needs to follow a specific protocol:
The interactor first sends one line with an integer n$$$n$$$ (1≤n≤10000$$$1\leq n\leq 10\,000$$$), the width and height of the kingdom.

Then, your program should make at most 10n+100$$$10n+100$$$ queries to find the highest point in the kingdom. Each query is made by printing one line of the form "? x$$$x$$$ y$$$y$$$" (1≤x,y≤n$$$1\leq x,y\leq n$$$). The interactor will respond with an integer v$$$v$$$ (1≤v≤109$$$1 \leq v \leq 10^9$$$), indicating the height at coordinate (x,y)$$$(x, y)$$$.

When you have determined the height of the highest point in the kingdom v$$$v$$$, print one line of the form "! v$$$v$$$", after which the interaction will stop. Printing the answer does not count as a query.
The interactor is not adaptive: the heights in the kingdom are fixed up front, and do not depend on your queries.
Make sure you flush the buffer after each write.
A testing tool is provided to help you develop your solution.
Using more than 10n+100$$$10n+100$$$ queries will result in a wrong answer.

legend: ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b754851489993be0f4dd88988605584ec40ee4d6.png)

As huge card game nerds, Alice and her friends are very hyped about meeting up and trying out the card game everybody seems to talk about these days. Due to a traffic jam, Alice is a bit late to the party and her friends are impatiently waiting for her. They have already distributed all cards and everybody is ready to go, except for Alice. She has just picked up her cards and insists on sorting them by suit first. For that, she repeatedly picks one card from her hand and inserts it somewhere else until her cards are grouped by suit. Her friends are getting increasingly annoyed with Alice and she wants to sort her cards as quickly as possible. How many cards does Alice need to move before they can start playing?
input: The input consists of:

One line with a string $$$s$$$ ($$$1\leq|s|\leq 10^5$$$), representing the suits of Alice's cards as they are initially ordered. The string consists of the characters h, d, c, and s (hearts, diamonds, clubs and spades).
output: Output a single integer, the minimum number of cards Alice has to move in order to sort the cards by suit.

legend: Dmitry has recently learned a simple rule to check if an integer is divisible by 3. An integer is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3.
Later he also learned that the same rule can be used to check if an integer is divisible by 9. An integer is divisible by 9 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 9.

Dmitry's elder sister Daria wants to trick him by showing that the same rule can be applied to any divisor $$$d$$$. To do this, she wants to show Dmitry an example of a positive integer $$$n$$$ such that $$$n$$$ is divisible by $$$d$$$, and the sum of the digits of $$$n$$$ is also divisible by $$$d$$$. Help her to find such a number.
input: The only line contains a single integer $$$d$$$ ($$$1\le d\le 1000$$$).
output: Print a positive integer $$$n$$$ divisible by $$$d$$$ such that the sum of its digits is also divisible by $$$d$$$.
The value of $$$n$$$ must consist of at most $$$10^6$$$ digits and must not have leading zeroes. It can be shown that such an integer always exists. If there are multiple answers, print any of them.

statement.title: C. Tomorrow Will Be Better Than Yesterday

legend: Pavel knows for sure — tomorrow is always better than yesterday.
He decided to prove this using geometry.
To do this, Pavel considered n consecutive days and assigned a point on the plane (xi, yi) to each day.
He considers day i + 1 to be better than day i if one of the two conditions is met:
either xi < xi + 1;
or xi = xi + 1, but yi < yi + 1.

Pavel is only unsure about one thing — whether he has chosen the correct coordinate system for his calculations. He is confident that only rotations and/or reflections can be used to find the correct coordinate system.
Help Pavel — find any rectangular (orthogonal) coordinate system in which each subsequent day will be better than the previous one.
input: The first line contains an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 105) — the number of days analyzed by Pavel.
Each of the following n lines contains two integers xi and yi ( - 105 ≤ xi,  yi ≤ 105) — the point assigned by Pavel to the i-th day.
output: In the first line, print YES if such a rectangular coordinate system exists, and NO otherwise.
If the desired coordinate system exists, print two more lines.
In the second line, print two integers Xx and Yx (|Xx|, |Yx| ≤ 109;|Xx| + |Yx| > 0) — the coordinates of the vector aligned with the axis Ox of the new coordinate system.
In the third line, print two integers Xy and Yy (|Xy|, |Yy| ≤ 109;|Xy| + |Yy| > 0) — the coordinates of the vector aligned with the axis Oy of the new coordinate system.
The vectors (Xx, Yx) and (Xy, Yy) must be perpendicular to each other.
If there are multiple valid answers, print any.
note: First test example
First, consider the points assigned to the days and the found vectors in the original coordinate system:
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/0d2356397e44d246d0dd08562e9d634c7eb4ce09.png)
Now let's show these same points in the coordinate system based on the found vectors:
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/1d48a2e49ed7e7b98f2433ec9fa15fb7beb82ba2.png)
The coordinates of the points after transitioning to the new coordinate system:
It is clear that each subsequent point is "better" than the previous one in the new coordinate system.

显然，在新的坐标系中，每个后续点都比前一个点“更好”。

legend.ai: 帕维尔确信——明天总是比昨天更好。
他决定使用几何学来证明这一点。
为此，帕维尔考虑了连续的 n 天，并为每一天在平面上指定了一个点 (xi, yi)。
如果满足以下两个条件之一，他就认为第 i + 1 天比第 i 天更好：
或者 x_i < x_{i+1}；
或者 x_i = x_{i+1}，但 y_i < y_{i+1}。
Pavel 只对一件事感到不确定——他是否为计算选择了正确的坐标系。他确信只有通过旋转和/或反射才能找到正确的坐标系。
请帮助 Pavel——找出任意一个矩形（正交）坐标系，使得每一天都比前一天更好。

向量 (Xx, Yx) 和 (Xy, Yy) 必须相互垂直。
如果有多个合法答案，输出任意一个即可。

legend: ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c7e54b68d8f4e6602d6e061f7e27c3c65cb7c106.png)

A mouse party is a bunch of mice standing on the vertices of a convex polygon in the two-dimensional plane. When Medea crashes a mouse party, she jumps, out of nowhere, to some point inside the party's polygon. All the mice and Medea can be considered as points in the two-dimensional plane, meaning that they have no shape or dimensions.

Medea is still careful, however. She considers how the mice might encircle her, so that she runs away before they get a chance to do so. Medea defines an encirclement as a subset of exactly three mice such that she lies strictly inside the triangle constructed with the mice as vertices. An example can be seen in Figure M.1.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/9dd22f9dd582ae4bf8b1ee3f00ec8b1ae4282754.png)

One day, Medea decided to crash on a party of mice. She does not jump accurately, so she does not know exactly which point inside the mouse party she is going to jump to – all she knows is that she will jump to a uniformly random point with real coordinates inside the mouse party.

Medea wants to know the expected number of distinct encirclements after she lands inside the party. This turned out to be too difficult to calculate, even for Medea's 200 IQ points, so she asked for your help!
input: The input consists of:
One line with an integer n$$$n$$$ (3≤n≤2⋅105$$$3 \leq n \leq 2\cdot 10^5$$$), the number of mice.
n$$$n$$$ lines, each with two integers x$$$x$$$ and y$$$y$$$ (|x|,|y|≤107$$$|x|, |y| \leq 10^7$$$), the coordinates of a mouse.
output: Output the expected number of encirclements after Medea lands inside the polygon.

legend: One day, Alice challenged Bob with the interactive programming problem described below.

You have a tree (an acyclic connected graph). Each node of the tree has exactly one parent, except the root node, which has no parent. Nodes that are not parents of any nodes are called leaves. You know the structure of the tree, because you know the parent of each node that is not the root.

Each node contains an integer value. A node that is not a leaf contains the sum of the values of all its direct children. Thus, all the values in the tree are determined by the values contained in the leaves.
The picture below depicts an example. The leaves are marked as gray, while the other nodes are white. Each node shows the value it contains.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/43e48d72564666edc0f0e8ee826f63da079a9e0e.png)
Initially, you don't know any of the node values, but you can query them one by one. Your task is to figure out the value of each node in the tree, making as few queries as possible.

Bob solved this problem very easily. Then, to spice things up, Alice asked him: "given the tree structure, how many different solutions to this problem exist?" That is, how many different minimal sets of queries exist that allow one to figure out all the values stored in the tree? (Two sets of queries are considered different if and only if there is a node that is queried in one set but not in the other.)
input: The tree has N$$$N$$$ nodes in total. Each node is identified by an integer between 1$$$1$$$ and N$$$N$$$, where node 1$$$1$$$ is the root.
The input consists of two lines. The first line contains only the integer N$$$N$$$.

The second line contains N−1$$$N-1$$$ integers P1,P2,…,PN−1$$$P_1, P_2, \ldots, P_{N-1}$$$, separated by a single space, where Pi$$$P_i$$$ is the parent of node i+1$$$i + 1$$$, for i=1,2,…,N−1$$$i = 1, 2, \ldots, N - 1$$$.
output: The output consists of a single line, which must contain the number of different minimal solutions to the problem faced by Bob. As this number may be large, your answer must be calculated mod 1000000007$$$1000000007$$$ (109+7)$$$(10^9 + 7)$$$.

legend.ai: 一天，Alice 向 Bob 提出了下面所描述的交互式编程问题。
你有一棵树（一个无环连通图）。树中的每个节点恰好有一个父节点，根节点除外，根节点没有父节点。不作为任何节点父节点的节点称为叶子。由于你知道每个非根节点的父节点，因此你知道这棵树的结构。
每个节点中都包含一个整数值。非叶节点中的值等于其所有直接子节点的值之和。因此，树中的所有值都由叶节点中的值决定。
下图展示了一个例子。叶子节点标记为灰色，而其他节点为白色。每个节点都显示其包含的值。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/43e48d72564666edc0f0e8ee826f63da079a9e0e.png)
起初，你不知道任何节点的值，但可以逐个查询它们。你的任务是用尽可能少的查询，确定树中每个节点的值。
Bob 很容易地解决了这个问题。然后，为了增添趣味，Alice 问他：“给定树的结构，解决这个问题的不同方案有多少种？”也就是说，有多少个不同的最小查询集合，可以据此确定树中存储的所有值？（当且仅当存在某个节点在一个集合中被查询而在另一个集合中未被查询时，才认为两个查询集合不同。）

input.ai: 这棵树总共有 N$$$N$$$ 个节点。每个节点都由一个介于 1$$$1$$$ 和 N$$$N$$$ 之间的整数标识，其中节点 1$$$1$$$ 是根节点。
输入由两行组成。第一行只包含整数 N$$$N$$$。
第二行包含 N−1$$$N-1$$$ 个整数 P1,P2,…,PN−1$$$P_1, P_2, \ldots, P_{N-1}$$$，它们由单个空格分隔，其中，Pi$$$P_i$$$ 是节点 i+1$$$i + 1$$$ 的父节点(i=1,2,…,N−1$$$i = 1, 2, \ldots, N - 1$$$)。

output.ai: 输出由一行组成，其中必须包含 Bob 所面对问题的不同最小解的数量。由于该数可能很大，你的答案必须对 1000000007$$$1000000007$$$ (109+7)$$$(10^9 + 7)$$$ 取模。

legend: Ties are usually an issue on elections and games. Recently, a new game, called Between Us, was created. The game is played by a number of players over a social network. On each turn, there are multiple votings, where a player may receive only votes from friends. The player getting the largest number of votes wins the game.

The game is still in its design phase, but the game developers faced a very common issue: since the number of friends of a given player is usually small, ties are very common, which makes the game less fun. To avoid this situation, they decided to add a new module to the match-making system, where it will try to form groups of players such that each player has an odd number of friends in the same group.

This problems turned out to be more challenging than they expected and they are now focusing on a simpler variation: given a set of players, the module must find a partition of the players in at most two groups, satisfying the restriction that each player must have an odd number of friends in his group. The problem is that this partition is not always possible. Your task is to determine whether the partition is possible.
input: The first line of input contains two integers, P$$$P$$$ and F$$$F$$$, the number of players and the number of friendship relations, respectively, satisfying 2≤P≤100$$$2 \le P \le 100$$$ and 1≤F≤P×(P−1)/2$$$1 \le F \le P \times (P - 1)/2$$$. Each of the next F$$$F$$$ lines will contain two integers A$$$A$$$ and B$$$B$$$, with 1≤A,B≤P$$$1 \le A, B \le P$$$ and A≠B$$$A \neq B$$$, meaning that players A$$$A$$$ and B$$$B$$$ are friends. Each friendship relation is given at most once, that is, if a line contains A$$$A$$$ and B$$$B$$$, no other line contains both numbers.
output: Output a single line containing one character. If the partition is possible, then write the upper case letter 'Y'; otherwise write the uppercase letter 'N'.

legend.ai: 平局通常是选举和游戏中的一个问题。最近，一款名为 Between Us 的新游戏诞生了。该游戏由若干名玩家通过社交网络进行。在每个回合中，会进行多次投票，玩家只能从朋友那里获得选票。获得最多票数的玩家赢得游戏。
游戏仍处于设计阶段，但游戏开发者遇到了一个非常常见的问题：由于某个玩家的朋友数量通常很少，平局非常常见，这使得游戏变得不那么有趣。为了避免这种情况，他们决定在匹配系统中加入一个新模块，尝试组建玩家小组，使得每名玩家在同一小组中都有奇数名朋友。
事实证明，这个问题比他们预想的更具挑战性，因此他们现在专注于一个更简单的变体：给定一组玩家，该模块必须将玩家划分为至多两个组，并满足每名玩家在其所在组中必须有奇数名朋友这一限制。问题在于，这种划分并不总是可能。你的任务是判断这种划分是否可行。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含两个整数 P$$$P$$$ 和 F$$$F$$$，分别表示玩家数和朋友关系数，满足 2≤P≤100$$$2 \le P \le 100$$$ 且 1≤F≤P×(P−1)/2$$$1 \le F \le P \times (P - 1)/2$$$。接下来的 F$$$F$$$ 行中，每行包含两个整数 A$$$A$$$ 和 B$$$B$$$，满足 1≤A,B≤P$$$1 \le A, B \le P$$$ 且 A≠B$$$A \neq B$$$，表示玩家 A$$$A$$$ 和 B$$$B$$$ 是朋友。每条朋友关系最多给出一次，也就是说，如果某一行包含 A$$$A$$$ 和 B$$$B$$$，则不会有其他行同时包含这两个数字。

output.ai: 输出一行，包含一个字符。如果划分可行，则输出大写字母“Y”；否则输出大写字母“N”。

legend: One of the most useful tools nowadays are text editors, their use is so important that the Unique Natural Advanced Language (UNAL) organization has studied many of the benefits working with them.

They are interested specifically in the feature "find", that option looks when a pattern occurs in a text, furthermore, it counts the number of times the pattern occurs in a text. The tool is so well designed that while writing each character of the pattern it updates the number of times that the corresponding prefix of the total pattern appears on the text.

Now the UNAL is working with the editor, finding patterns in some texts, however, they realize that many of the patterns appear just very few times in the corresponding texts, as they really want to see more number of appearances of the patterns in the texts, they put a lower bound on the minimum number of times the pattern should be found in the text and use only prefixes of the original pattern. On the other hand, the UNAL is very picky about language, so they will just use the largest non-empty prefix of the original pattern that fit into the bound.
input: The first line contains the text A (1 ≤ |A| ≤  105) The second line contains the original pattern B (1 ≤ |B| ≤  |A|) The third line contains an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤  |A|) - the minimum number of times a pattern should be found on the text.
output: A single line, with the prefix of the original pattern used by the UNAL, if there is no such prefix then print "IMPOSSIBLE" (without the quotes)

legend.ai: 如今，文本编辑器是最有用的工具之一，它们的重要性如此之高，以至于独特自然高级语言（Unique Natural Advanced Language，UNAL）组织研究了使用文本编辑器工作的诸多益处。
他们尤其感兴趣的是“查找”功能：该选项会查找模式串在文本中的出现情况，并且还会统计模式串在文本中出现的次数。这个工具设计得非常完善：在输入模式串的每个字符时，它都会更新整个模式串的相应前缀在文本中出现的次数。
现在，UNAL 正在使用该编辑器，在一些文本中查找模式串。然而，他们发现许多模式串在相应文本中只出现了很少几次。由于他们确实希望看到模式串在文本中出现得更多，他们规定了模式串在文本中出现次数的下界，并且只使用原模式串的前缀。另一方面，UNAL 对语言非常挑剔，因此他们只会使用原模式串中出现次数达到该下界的最长非空前缀。

input.ai: 第一行包含文本 A（1 ≤ |A| ≤ 10^5）。第二行包含原模式串 B（1 ≤ |B| ≤ |A|）。第三行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ |A|），表示模式串在文本中至少应出现的次数。

output.ai: 输出一行，即 UNAL 使用的原模式串的前缀；如果不存在这样的前缀，则输出“IMPOSSIBLE”（不含引号）。

statement.title: A. Nicoleta and the circle of kids

legend: Nicoleta is a happy kid, he goes every day to school and is always complaining about waking up early and having to complete his homework assignments. His favorite professor, Afonsox, is very funny and created a new challenge for him.

Even though Nicoleta is just a kid, Afonsox introduced him to the world of graph theory. Nicoleta is amazed, he is very obsessed with this graph that Afonsox decided to call K-round graph. A K-round graph with N vertices is a graph where every vertex u, numbered from 0 to N - 1, has an edge to vertices (u + 1)%N, ..., (u + K)%N. Here a%b is the operator that gives the remainder of the integer division of a by b. Also, an edge between vertices u and (u + i)%N has value i.

Nicoleta likes this graph because if you draw it, it looks like a circle of kids, where each kid has K arms with different lengths with which they can reach the K next kids, like the picture below, which he drew in his notebook. Imagining this makes Nicoleta smile.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c50f877bb8bceec1f8c85e90fe420ec1ffc1f602.png)

The challenge Afonsox has proposed to Nicoleta is for him to find the sum of all the values of the edges in the maximum spanning tree of a given K-round graph. A maximum spanning tree of a graph is composed of all of its vertices and a subset of edges such that there is one and only one path from one vertex to another and the sum of the values of the edges is maximal. Can you help Nicoleta finding the answer to Afonsox challenge?
input: The input consists of a single line containing two integers N and K (1 ≤ K < N ≤ 109), indicating the number of vertices in the graph and the number of outgoing edges from every vertex.
output: Output a single integer - the sum of the values of the edges in the maximum spanning tree of the K-round graph.

legend.ai: Nicoleta 是一个快乐的孩子，他每天都去上学，总是抱怨必须早起并完成家庭作业。他最喜欢的老师 Afonsox 非常风趣，为他设计了一个新的挑战。

尽管 Nicoleta 还只是个孩子，Afonsox 还是把他带入了图论的世界。Nicoleta 十分惊讶，并且非常着迷于这个图，Afonsox 决定称其为 K-round 图。一个具有 N 个顶点的 K-round 图是一种图，其中每个编号从 0 到 N - 1 的顶点 u 都与顶点 (u + 1)%N、...、(u + K)%N 之间存在一条边。这里，a%b 是整数 a 除以 b 所得余数的运算符。此外，顶点 u 与 (u + i)%N 之间的边的权值为 i。
Nicoleta 喜欢这个图，因为如果把它画出来，它看起来就像一圈孩子，每个孩子都有 K 条长度各不相同的手臂，可以够到接下来的 K 个孩子，就像下面这幅他在笔记本上画的图一样。想到这一点，Nicoleta 就会微笑。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c50f877bb8bceec1f8c85e90fe420ec1ffc1f602.png)
Afonsox 给 Nicoleta 提出的挑战是：求出给定 K-轮图的最大生成树中所有边的权值之和。图的最大生成树由图中的所有顶点和部分边组成，并且满足任意两个顶点之间有且仅有一条路径，同时边的权值之和最大。你能帮助 Nicoleta 找到 Afonsox 挑战的答案吗？

input.ai: 输入包含一行，其中有两个整数 N 和 K（1 ≤ K < N ≤ 10^9），分别表示图中的顶点数以及每个顶点的出边数。

output.ai: 输出一个整数——K-轮图的最大生成树中所有边的权值之和。

legend: Sancho was making a road trip with his family and got really bored, so he recorded the position and initial speed of every car on the highway. For Sancho, the highway is an infinite straight line, the starting time is 0, the cars are moving points, and no car will pass another car (Sancho is very idealistic).

The cars maintain their initial speed unless they are slowed down by other cars. Car A is slowed down by car B if B started in front of A, but after a while, A reached B. When this happens, both cars move together and A's speed becomes the same as B's.

Sancho knows that there will be only a finite amount of times that a car will be slowed down by another car, and wants to know when the last slowing down will take place. If no car will be slowed down, the answer is 0.
input: The first line of the input contains a single integer N (1 ≤ N ≤ 105), indicating the number of cars.
N lines follow. The i-th line contains two integers Si and Vi (0 ≤ S, V ≤ 109), indicating the starting position of the i-th car and its speed. No two cars start in the same position.
output: Output a single decimal number - the time of the last slow down. Your answer will be considered correct if the absolute or relative error is no greater than 10 - 4.

Namely: let's assume that your answer is a, and the official answer is b. The checker program will consider your answer correct, if ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/4403ac426d6dfe4c9db1500d50ce3649b4e1a729.png).

legend.ai: Sancho 和家人一起驾车旅行时感到非常无聊，于是他记录下了高速公路上每辆车的位置和初始速度。对 Sancho 来说，高速公路是一条无限延伸的直线，起始时间为 0，车辆是移动的点，并且没有车辆会超过另一辆车（Sancho 非常理想主义）。
车辆会保持初始速度，除非被其他车辆减速。如果车辆 B 一开始在车辆 A 前方，但一段时间后 A 追上了 B，则 A 会被 B 减速。此时两车一起行驶，A 的速度变得与 B 相同。
Sancho 知道每辆车被另一辆车减速的总次数是有限的，他想知道最后一次减速发生在什么时候。如果没有车辆被减速，则答案为 0。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含一个整数 N（1 ≤ N ≤ 10^5），表示车辆的数量。
接下来有 N 行。第 i 行包含两个整数 Si 和 Vi（0 ≤ S, V ≤ 10^9），分别表示第 i 辆车的起始位置和速度。没有任何两辆车从同一位置出发。

output.ai: 输出一个十进制小数——最后一次减速发生的时间。如果你的答案的绝对误差或相对误差不超过 10^{-4}，则该答案被视为正确。
也就是说：假设你的答案为 a，官方答案为 b。若满足 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/4403ac426d6dfe4c9db1500d50ce3649b4e1a729.png)，评测程序将认为你的答案正确。

legend: Slava has a set of N$$$N$$$ numbers: x1,x2,x3,…,xn$$$x_1, x_2, x_3, \dots, x_n$$$. At one turn, he can get a non-empty set y1,y2,y3,…,ym$$$y_1, y_2, y_3, \dots, y_m$$$, in which for any i$$$i$$$ from 1$$$1$$$ to m$$$m$$$ yi$$$y_i$$$ is included in the set x1,x2,…,xn$$$x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n$$$, and then he can add in the set X$$$X$$$ sum of all products of numbers of all the possible subsets y1,y2,…,ym$$$y_1, y_2, \dots, y_m$$$. note: Consider set of numbers X=[14,15],L=100$$$X = [14, 15], L = 100$$$.
We can get set Y$$$Y$$$ like that:

legend: Recently Polycarp started to develop a text editor that works only with correct bracket sequences (abbreviated as CBS).

Note that a bracket sequence is correct if it is possible to get a correct mathematical expression by adding "+"-s and "1"-s to it. For example, sequences "(())()", "()" and "(()(()))" are correct, while ")(", "(()" and "(()))(" are not. Each bracket in CBS has a pair. For example, in "(()(()))":
1st bracket is paired with 8th,
2d bracket is paired with 3d,
3d bracket is paired with 2d,
4th bracket is paired with 7th,
5th bracket is paired with 6th,
6th bracket is paired with 5th,
7th bracket is paired with 4th,
8th bracket is paired with 1st.

Polycarp's editor currently supports only three operations during the use of CBS. The cursor in the editor takes the whole position of one of the brackets (not the position between the brackets!). There are three operations being supported:
«L» — move the cursor one position to the left,
«R» — move the cursor one position to the right,

«D» — delete the bracket in which the cursor is located, delete the bracket it's paired to and all brackets between them (that is, delete a substring between the bracket in which the cursor is located and the one it's paired to).

After the operation "D" the cursor moves to the nearest bracket to the right (of course, among the non-deleted). If there is no such bracket (that is, the suffix of the CBS was deleted), then the cursor moves to the nearest bracket to the left (of course, among the non-deleted).
There are pictures illustrated several usages of operation "D" below.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d7a7bf600a5eb5bed1277fc362346e5196fdca65.png)
All incorrect operations (shift cursor over the end of CBS, delete the whole CBS, etc.) are not supported by Polycarp's editor.
Polycarp is very proud of his development, can you implement the functionality of his editor?
input: The first line contains three positive integers n, m and p (2 ≤ n ≤ 500 000, 1 ≤ m ≤ 500 000, 1 ≤ p ≤ n) — the number of brackets in the correct bracket sequence, the number of operations and the initial position of cursor. Positions in the sequence are numbered from left to right, starting from one. It is guaranteed that n is even.
It is followed by the string of n characters "(" and ")" forming the correct bracket sequence.

Then follow a string of m characters "L", "R" and "D" — a sequence of the operations. Operations are carried out one by one from the first to the last. It is guaranteed that the given operations never move the cursor outside the bracket sequence, as well as the fact that after all operations a bracket sequence will be non-empty.
output: Print the correct bracket sequence, obtained as a result of applying all operations to the initial sequence.
note: In the first sample the cursor is initially at position 5. Consider actions of the editor:
command "R" — the cursor moves to the position 6 on the right;
command "D" — the deletion of brackets from the position 5 to the position 6. After that CBS takes the form (())(), the cursor is at the position 5;
command "L" — the cursor moves to the position 4 on the left;
command "D" — the deletion of brackets from the position 1 to the position 4. After that CBS takes the form (), the cursor is at the position 1.
Thus, the answer is equal to ().

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，光标初始位于位置 5。考虑编辑器执行的操作：
操作“R”——光标向右移动到位置 6；
命令 “D”——删除位置 5 到位置 6 的括号。此后，CBS 的形式为 (())()，光标位于位置 5；
命令 “L”——光标向左移动到位置 4；
命令 “D”——删除位置 1 到位置 4 的括号。此后，CBS 的形式为 ()，光标位于位置 1。
因此，答案等于 ()。

input.ai: 第一行包含三个正整数 n、m 和 p（2 ≤ n ≤ 500 000，1 ≤ m ≤ 500 000，1 ≤ p ≤ n）——合法括号序列中的括号数、操作数以及光标的初始位置。序列中的位置从左到右编号，从 1 开始。保证 n 为偶数。
接下来给出一个由 n 个字符“(”和“)”组成的合法括号序列。
随后给出一个由 m 个字符“L”、“R”和“D”组成的字符串，表示操作序列。操作将按照从第一个到最后一个的顺序依次执行。保证给出的操作不会将光标移到括号序列之外，并且所有操作执行完毕后，括号序列非空。

output.ai: 输出对初始序列执行全部操作后得到的合法括号序列。

legend.ai: 最近，Polycarp 开始开发一款只适用于正确括号序列（缩写为 CBS）的文本编辑器。
注意，如果可以通过向一个括号序列中添加若干个“+”和“1”来得到一个正确的数学表达式，那么该括号序列就是正确的。例如，括号序列 "(())()"、"()" 和 "(()(()))" 是正确的，而 ")("、"(()" 和 "(()))(" 则不是。CBS 中的每个括号都有一个与之配对的括号。例如，在 "(()(()))" 中：
第 1 个括号与第 8 个括号配对，
第 2 个括号与第 3 个括号配对，
第 3 个括号与第 2 个括号配对，
第 4 个括号与第 7 个括号配对，
第 5 个括号与第 6 个括号配对，
第 6 个括号与第 5 个括号配对，
第 7 个括号与第 4 个括号配对，
第 8 个括号与第 1 个括号配对。
在使用 CBS 时，Polycarp 的编辑器目前只支持三种操作。编辑器中的光标占据某个括号的整个位置（而不是两个括号之间的位置！）。支持以下三种操作：
«L» — 将光标向左移动一个位置，
«R» — 将光标向右移动一个位置，
«D»——删除光标所在的括号、与其匹配的括号以及两者之间的所有括号（也就是说，删除从光标所在括号到与其匹配括号之间的子串）。
执行操作“D”后，光标会移动到右侧最近的括号（当然，是在未被删除的括号中）。如果不存在这样的括号（也就是说，CBS 的后缀被删除了），那么光标会移动到左侧最近的括号（当然，也是未被删除的括号）。
下面给出了操作“D”的几种用法示意图。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d7a7bf600a5eb5bed1277fc362346e5196fdca65.png)
Polycarp 的编辑器不支持所有不正确的操作（将光标移到 CBS 的末尾之外、删除整个 CBS 等）。
Polycarp 对自己的开发成果非常自豪，你能实现他的编辑器的功能吗？

legend: The Smart Beaver from ABBYY has once again surprised us! He has developed a new calculating device, which he called the "Beaver's Calculator 1.0". It is very peculiar and it is planned to be used in a variety of scientific problems.

To test it, the Smart Beaver invited n scientists, numbered from 1 to n. The i-th scientist brought ki calculating problems for the device developed by the Smart Beaver from ABBYY. The problems of the i-th scientist are numbered from 1 to ki, and they must be calculated sequentially in the described order, since calculating each problem heavily depends on the results of calculating of the previous ones.

Each problem of each of the n scientists is described by one integer ai, j, where i (1 ≤ i ≤ n) is the number of the scientist, j (1 ≤ j ≤ ki) is the number of the problem, and ai, j is the number of resource units the calculating device needs to solve this problem.

The calculating device that is developed by the Smart Beaver is pretty unusual. It solves problems sequentially, one after another. After some problem is solved and before the next one is considered, the calculating device allocates or frees resources.

The most expensive operation for the calculating device is freeing resources, which works much slower than allocating them. It is therefore desirable that each next problem for the calculating device requires no less resources than the previous one.

You are given the information about the problems the scientists offered for the testing. You need to arrange these problems in such an order that the number of adjacent "bad" pairs of problems in this list is minimum possible. We will call two consecutive problems in this list a "bad pair" if the problem that is performed first requires more resources than the one that goes after it. Do not forget that the problems of the same scientist must be solved in a fixed order.

To lessen the size of the input, each of the next n lines contains five integers ki, ai, 1, xi, yi, mi (0 ≤ ai, 1 < mi ≤ 109, 1 ≤ xi, yi ≤ 109) — the number of problems of the i-th scientist, the resources the first problem requires and three parameters that generate the subsequent values of ai, j. For all j from 2 to ki, inclusive, you should calculate value ai, j by formula ai, j = (ai, j - 1 * xi + yi) mod mi, where a mod b is the operation of taking the remainder of division of number a by number b.
To get the full points for the first group of tests it is sufficient to solve the problem with n = 2, 1 ≤ ki ≤ 2000.
To get the full points for the second group of tests it is sufficient to solve the problem with n = 2, 1 ≤ ki ≤ 200000.
To get the full points for the third group of tests it is sufficient to solve the problem with 1 ≤ n ≤ 5000, 1 ≤ ki ≤ 5000.

The problems of the first scientist require 1 and 2 resource units, the problems of the second one require 3 and 4 resource units. legend.ai: ABBYY 的聪明海狸再次让我们大吃一惊！他研发了一种新的计算设备，并将其命名为“海狸的计算器 1.0”。它非常独特，计划用于各种科学问题。
为了测试它，Smart Beaver 邀请了 n 位科学家，他们的编号从 1 到 n。第 i 位科学家为 ABBYY 的 Smart Beaver 开发的设备带来了 ki 道题目。第 i 位科学家的题目编号从 1 到 ki，并且必须按照给定顺序依次计算，因为每道题的计算都高度依赖于前一道题的计算结果。
每位科学家的每道题都由一个整数 ai,j 描述，其中 i（1 ≤ i ≤ n）表示科学家的编号，j（1 ≤ j ≤ ki）表示题目的编号，而 ai,j 表示计算设备解决该题所需的资源单位数。
Smart Beaver 开发的计算设备相当特殊。它会按顺序逐个解决题目。解决某道题后、处理下一道题之前，计算设备会分配或释放资源。
对于计算设备而言，代价最高的操作是释放资源，其速度远慢于分配资源。因此，最好让计算设备接下来处理的每道题所需的资源不少于前一道题。
现在给出科学家们提供的题目信息。你需要将这些题目排列成某种顺序，使列表中相邻“坏”题对的数量尽可能少。如果列表中前一道题所需的资源多于后一道题，我们就称这两个连续的题目构成一个“坏题对”。请不要忘记，同一位科学家的题目必须按照固定顺序解决。

要获得第一组测试的全部分数，只需解决 n = 2、1 ≤ kᵢ ≤ 2000 的问题。
要获得第二组测试的全部分数，只需解决 n = 2、1 ≤ kᵢ ≤ 200000 的问题。
要获得第三组测试的全部分数，只需解决 1 ≤ n ≤ 5000、1 ≤ kᵢ ≤ 5000 的问题。

output.ai: 在第一行输出一个整数——最优顺序中“坏”数对的数量。
如果问题总数不超过 200000，还需输出 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a16730dcbb2402871e20647c8aba55beada5c1b6.png) 行——问题的最优顺序。在每一行中输出两个用一个空格分隔的整数，分别表示该问题所需的资源数量和提出该问题的科学家的编号。科学家的编号按照输入顺序从 1 到 n 编号。

legend: You are responsible for installing a gas pipeline along a road. Let's consider the road (for simplicity) as a segment [0,n]$$$[0, n]$$$ on OX$$$OX$$$ axis. The road can have several crossroads, but for simplicity, we'll denote each crossroad as an interval (x,x+1)$$$(x, x + 1)$$$ with integer x$$$x$$$. So we can represent the road as a binary string consisting of n$$$n$$$ characters, where character 0 means that current interval doesn't contain a crossroad, and 1 means that there is a crossroad.

Usually, we can install the pipeline along the road on height of 1$$$1$$$ unit with supporting pillars in each integer point (so, if we are responsible for [0,n]$$$[0, n]$$$ road, we must install n+1$$$n + 1$$$ pillars). But on crossroads we should lift the pipeline up to the height 2$$$2$$$, so the pipeline won't obstruct the way for cars.

We can do so inserting several zig-zag-like lines. Each zig-zag can be represented as a segment [x,x+1]$$$[x, x + 1]$$$ with integer x$$$x$$$ consisting of three parts: 0.5$$$0.5$$$ units of horizontal pipe + 1$$$1$$$ unit of vertical pipe + 0.5$$$0.5$$$ of horizontal. Note that if pipeline is currently on height 2$$$2$$$, the pillars that support it should also have length equal to 2$$$2$$$ units.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d9d49d8d0560a060a2f1fc785ef616c3b1af3c0b.png)

Each unit of gas pipeline costs us a$$$a$$$ bourles, and each unit of pillar — b$$$b$$$ bourles. So, it's not always optimal to make the whole pipeline on the height 2$$$2$$$. Find the shape of the pipeline with minimum possible cost and calculate that cost.
Note that you must start and finish the pipeline on height 1$$$1$$$ and, also, it's guaranteed that the first and last characters of the input string are equal to 0.
input: The fist line contains one integer T$$$T$$$ (1≤T≤100$$$1 \le T \le 100$$$) — the number of queries. Next 2⋅T$$$2 \cdot T$$$ lines contain independent queries — one query per two lines.

The first line contains three integers n$$$n$$$, a$$$a$$$, b$$$b$$$ (2≤n≤2⋅105$$$2 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$, 1≤a≤108$$$1 \le a \le 10^8$$$, 1≤b≤108$$$1 \le b \le 10^8$$$) — the length of the road, the cost of one unit of the pipeline and the cost of one unit of the pillar, respectively.
The second line contains binary string s$$$s$$$ (|s|=n$$$|s| = n$$$, si∈{0,1}$$$s_i \in \{0, 1\}$$$, s1=sn=0$$$s_1 = s_n = 0$$$) — the description of the road.
It's guaranteed that the total length of all strings s$$$s$$$ doesn't exceed 2⋅105$$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output: Print T$$$T$$$ integers — one per query. For each query print the minimum possible cost of the constructed pipeline.

legend.ai: 你负责沿着一条道路铺设燃气管道。我们将道路(为简单起见)看作 OX$$$OX$$$ 轴上的线段 [0,n]$$$[0, n]$$$。道路上可能有多个十字路口，但为简单起见，我们将每个十字路口表示为区间 (x,x+1)$$$(x, x + 1)$$$，其中 x$$$x$$$ 为整数。因此，我们可以将道路表示为一个由 n$$$n$$$ 个字符组成的二进制字符串，其中字符 0 表示当前区间不包含十字路口，字符 1 表示包含十字路口。
通常，我们可以将管道沿道路铺设在高度为 1$$$1$$$ 个单位的位置，并在每个整数点设置支柱(因此，如果我们负责铺设 [0,n]$$$[0, n]$$$ 道路的管道，就必须安装 n+1$$$n + 1$$$ 根支柱)。但在十字路口处，我们应将管道抬高至高度 2$$$2$$$，这样管道就不会妨碍汽车通行。

我们可以通过插入若干条类似之字形的线段来实现这一点。每条之字形线段都可以表示为区间 [x,x+1]$$$[x, x + 1]$$$，其中 x$$$x$$$ 为整数，并由三部分组成：长度为 0.5$$$0.5$$$ 个单位的水平管道 + 长度为 1$$$1$$$ 个单位的竖直管道 + 长度为 0.5$$$0.5$$$ 个单位的水平管道。注意，如果管道当前处于高度 2$$$2$$$，支撑它的支柱长度也应等于 2$$$2$$$ 个单位。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d9d49d8d0560a060a2f1fc785ef616c3b1af3c0b.png)
燃气管道的每个单位需要花费 a$$$a$$$ 布尔，每个单位支柱需要花费 b$$$b$$$ 布尔。因此，将整条管道建在高度 2$$$2$$$ 并不总是最优。请找出成本可能最小的管道形状，并计算该成本。
注意，你必须在高度 1$$$1$$$ 开始和结束管道，并且保证输入字符串的第一个和最后一个字符都等于 0。

保证所有字符串 s$$$s$$$ 的总长度不超过 2⋅105$$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$。

legend: Vasya participates in a ski race along the X axis. The start is at point 0, and the finish is at L, that is, at a distance L meters from the start in the positive direction of the axis. Vasya has been training so hard that he can run one meter in exactly one second.
Besides, there are n take-off ramps on the track, each ramp is characterized by four numbers:
xi represents the ramp's coordinate
di represents from how many meters Vasya will land if he goes down this ramp
ti represents the flight time in seconds

pi is the number, indicating for how many meters Vasya should gather speed to get ready and fly off the ramp. As Vasya gathers speed, he should ski on the snow (that is, he should not be flying), but his speed still equals one meter per second.

Vasya is allowed to move in any direction on the X axis, but he is prohibited to cross the start line, that is go to the negative semiaxis. Vasya himself chooses which take-off ramps he will use and in what order, that is, he is not obliged to take off from all the ramps he encounters. Specifically, Vasya can skip the ramp. It is guaranteed that xi + di ≤ L, that is, Vasya cannot cross the finish line in flight.

Vasya can jump from the ramp only in the positive direction of X axis. More formally, when using the i-th ramp, Vasya starts gathering speed at point xi - pi, jumps at point xi, and lands at point xi + di. He cannot use the ramp in opposite direction.
Your task is to find the minimum time that Vasya will spend to cover the distance.
input: The first line contains two integers n and L (0 ≤ n ≤ 105, 1 ≤ L ≤ 109). Then n lines contain the descriptions of the ramps, each description is on a single line. Each description is a group of four non-negative integers xi, di, ti, pi (0 ≤ xi ≤ L, 1 ≤ di, ti, pi ≤ 109, xi + di ≤ L).
output: Print in the first line the minimum time in seconds Vasya needs to complete the track. Print in the second line k — the number of take-off ramps that Vasya needs to use, and print on the third line of output k numbers the number the take-off ramps Vasya used in the order in which he used them. Print each number exactly once, separate the numbers with a space. The ramps are numbered starting from 1 in the order in which they are given in the input.
note: In the first sample, Vasya cannot use ramp 2, because then he will need to gather speed starting from point -3, which is not permitted by the statement. The optimal option is using ramp 1, the resulting time is: moving to the point of gathering speed + gathering speed until reaching the takeoff ramp + flight time + moving to the finish line = 0 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 15.

In the second sample using ramp 1 is not optimal for Vasya as t1 > d1. The optimal option is using ramp 2, the resulting time is: moving to the point of gathering speed + gathering speed until reaching the takeoff ramp + flight time + moving to the finish line = 14 + 1 + 1 + 0 = 16.

legend.ai: Vasya 参加了一场沿 X 轴进行的滑雪比赛。起点位于 0 点，终点位于 L 点，也就是说，终点在坐标轴正方向上距离起点 L 米处。Vasya 训练得非常刻苦，因此他恰好可以在一秒内跑一米。
此外，赛道上还有 n 个起跳坡道，每个坡道由四个数表示：
xi 表示该坡道的坐标
d_i 表示如果 Vasya 沿着这条跳台下滑，他将在距离起点多少米处落地
t_i 表示飞行时间，单位为秒
p_i 表示 Vasya 应助跑多少米来加速，以做好准备并飞离跳台。Vasya 加速时应在雪地上滑行（也就是说，他不应处于飞行状态），但他的速度仍然等于每秒 1 米。
Vasya 可以沿 X 轴向任意方向移动，但禁止越过起始线，即不能进入负半轴。Vasya 可以自行选择使用哪些起跳台以及使用顺序，也就是说，他不必从遇到的所有跳台起跳。具体来说，Vasya 可以跳过某个跳台。保证 x_i + d_i ≤ L，即 Vasya 在飞行过程中无法越过终点线。
Vasya 只能沿 X 轴的正方向从跳台起跳。更形式化地说，使用第 i 个跳台时，Vasya 从点 x_i - p_i 开始加速，在点 x_i 起跳，并在点 x_i + d_i 落地。他不能反方向使用跳台。
你的任务是求出 Vasya 走完这段距离所需的最短时间。

input.ai: 第一行包含两个整数 n 和 L（0 ≤ n ≤ 10^5，1 ≤ L ≤ 10^9）。接下来 n 行包含坡道的描述，每个描述占一行。每个描述由四个非负整数 xi、di、ti、pi 组成（0 ≤ xi ≤ L，1 ≤ di、ti、pi ≤ 10^9，xi + di ≤ L）。

output.ai: 第一行输出 Vasya 完成赛道所需的最短时间（单位：秒）。第二行输出 k——Vasya 需要使用的起飞坡道数量；第三行输出 k 个数字，表示 Vasya 按使用顺序使用的起飞坡道编号。每个编号必须恰好输出一次，数字之间用空格分隔。坡道按照输入中的顺序从 1 开始编号。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，Vasya 不能使用 2 号坡道，因为这样他就需要从 -3 点开始加速，而题面不允许这样做。最优方案是使用 1 号坡道，所得时间为：移动到加速点 + 加速直到到达起飞坡道 + 飞行时间 + 移动到终点 = 0 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 15。
在第二个样例中，使用 1 号坡道对 Vasya 来说不是最优的，因为 t1 > d1。最优方案是使用 2 号坡道，所得时间为：移动到加速点 + 加速直到到达起飞坡道 + 飞行时间 + 移动到终点 = 14 + 1 + 1 + 0 = 16。

legend: Sasha is taking part in a programming competition. In one of the problems she should check if some rooted trees are isomorphic or not. She has never seen this problem before, but, being an experienced participant, she guessed that she should match trees to some sequences and then compare these sequences instead of trees. Sasha wants to match each tree with a sequence a0, a1, ..., ah, where h is the height of the tree, and ai equals to the number of vertices that are at distance of i edges from root.

Unfortunately, this time Sasha's intuition was wrong, and there could be several trees matching the same sequence. To show it, you need to write a program that, given the sequence ai, builds two non-isomorphic rooted trees that match that sequence, or determines that there is only one such tree.

Two rooted trees are isomorphic, if you can reenumerate the vertices of the first one in such a way, that the index of the root becomes equal the index of the root of the second tree, and these two trees become equal.
The height of a rooted tree is the maximum number of edges on a path from the root to any other vertex.
input: The first line contains a single integer h (2 ≤ h ≤ 105) — the height of the tree.

The second line contains h + 1 integers — the sequence a0, a1, ..., ah (1 ≤ ai ≤ 2·105). The sum of all ai does not exceed 2·105. It is guaranteed that there is at least one tree matching this sequence.
output: If there is only one tree matching this sequence, print "perfect".

Otherwise print "ambiguous" in the first line. In the second and in the third line print descriptions of two trees in the following format: in one line print ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/84c4dd28c25918521bfe375641bc52bcedd18589.png) integers, the k-th of them should be the parent of vertex k or be equal to zero, if the k-th vertex is the root.
These treese should be non-isomorphic and should match the given sequence.
note: The only tree in the first example and the two printed trees from the second example are shown on the picture:
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/391ac13640fa692361683e9c23619eb4e8bce1c5.png)

legend.ai: Sasha 正在参加一场编程竞赛。在其中一道题中，她需要判断一些有根树是否同构。她以前从未见过这道题，但作为一名经验丰富的参赛者，她猜测应该将树与某些序列进行匹配，然后比较这些序列，而不是直接比较树。Sasha 希望将每棵树与一个序列 a0、a1、...、ah 匹配，其中 h 是树的高度，ai 等于距离根恰好 i 条边的顶点数量。
遗憾的是，这一次 Sasha 的直觉错了，可能存在多棵与同一序列相匹配的树。为了说明这一点，你需要编写一个程序，给定序列 ai，构造两棵不同构的有根树，使它们都与该序列相匹配；或者判断这样的树是否只有一棵。
如果可以对第一棵树的顶点重新编号，使得其根的编号与第二棵树的根的编号相同，并且重新编号后的两棵树完全相同，那么称这两棵有根树同构。
有根树的高度是从根到任意其他顶点的路径上边数的最大值。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 h（2 ≤ h ≤ 10^5）——树的高度。
第二行包含 h + 1 个整数——序列 a0, a1, ..., ah（1 ≤ ai ≤ 2·10^5）。所有 ai 的总和不超过 2·10^5。保证至少存在一棵与该序列相匹配的树。

output.ai: 如果与该序列相匹配的树只有一棵，则输出 "perfect"。
否则，第一行输出 "ambiguous"。第二行和第三行按照以下格式输出两棵树的描述：在一行中输出 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/84c4dd28c25918521bfe375641bc52bcedd18589.png) 个整数，其中第 k 个数应为顶点 k 的父节点；如果第 k 个顶点是根，则该数应为 0。
这两棵树应当不同构，并且应与给定的序列相匹配。

note.ai: 第一组样例中的唯一一棵树和第二组样例中输出的两棵树如图所示：
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/391ac13640fa692361683e9c23619eb4e8bce1c5.png)

problems.hint: Some of the $S$ edges are necessary.

legend: After Santa Claus and his assistant Elf delivered all the presents and made all the wishes come true, they returned to the North Pole and found out that it is all covered with snow. Both of them were quite tired and they decided only to remove the snow from the roads connecting huts. The North Pole has n huts connected with m roads. One can go along the roads in both directions.

The Elf offered to split: Santa Claus will clear up the wide roads and the Elf will tread out the narrow roads. For each road they decided who will clear it: Santa Claus or the Elf. To minimize the efforts they decided to clear the road so as to fulfill both those conditions:
between any two huts should exist exactly one simple path along the cleared roads;
Santa Claus and the Elf should clear the same number of roads.
At this point Santa Claus and his assistant Elf wondered which roads should they clear up?
input: The first input line contains two positive integers n and m (1 ≤ n ≤ 103, 1 ≤ m ≤ 105) — the number of huts and the number of roads. Then follow m lines, each of them contains a road description: the numbers of huts it connects — x and y (1 ≤ x, y ≤ n) and the person responsible for clearing out this road ("S" — for the Elf or "M" for Santa Claus). It is possible to go on each road in both directions. Note that there can be more than one road between two huts and a road can begin and end in the same hut.
output: Print "-1" without the quotes if it is impossible to choose the roads that will be cleared by the given rule. Otherwise print in the first line how many roads should be cleared and in the second line print the numbers of those roads (the roads are numbered from 1 in the order of occurrence in the input). It is allowed to print the numbers of the roads in any order. Each number should be printed exactly once. As you print the numbers, separate them with spaces.
note: A path is called simple if all huts on it are pairwise different.

legend.ai: 圣诞老人和他的助手精灵送完所有礼物并实现了所有愿望后，他们回到了北极，却发现那里已经被积雪覆盖。他们两人都相当疲惫，于是决定只清除连接各个小屋的道路上的积雪。北极有 n 个由 m 条道路连接的小屋。人们可以沿道路双向通行。
精灵提出分工：圣诞老人清理宽阔的道路，而精灵清理狭窄的道路。对于每条道路，他们决定由谁来清理：圣诞老人还是精灵。为了尽量减少工作量，他们决定以满足以下两个条件的方式清理道路：
任意两个小屋之间恰好存在一条仅由已清理道路组成的简单路径；
圣诞老人和精灵应清理数量相同的道路。
此时，圣诞老人和他的助手精灵想知道应该清理哪些道路？

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含两个正整数 n 和 m（1 ≤ n ≤ 10³，1 ≤ m ≤ 10⁵），分别表示小屋的数量和道路的数量。接下来有 m 行，每行包含一条道路的描述：它连接的小屋编号 x 和 y（1 ≤ x，y ≤ n），以及负责清理这条道路的人（“S”表示精灵，“M”表示圣诞老人）。每条道路都可以双向通行。注意，两个小屋之间可能有多条道路，并且一条道路的起点和终点可能是同一个小屋。

output.ai: 如果无法按照给定规则选择要清理的道路，则输出不带引号的“-1”。否则，第一行输出需要清理的道路数量，第二行输出这些道路的编号（道路按照它们在输入中出现的顺序从 1 开始编号）。道路编号可以按任意顺序输出。每个编号必须恰好输出一次。输出编号时，请用空格分隔。

note.ai: 如果一条路径上的所有小屋两两不同，则称该路径为简单路径。

problems.hint: Consider the weight for each element.

legend: After the educational reform Polycarp studies only two subjects at school, Safety Studies and PE (Physical Education). During the long months of the fourth term, he received n marks in them. When teachers wrote a mark in the journal, they didn't write in what subject the mark was for, they just wrote the mark.

Now it's time to show the journal to his strict parents. Polycarp knows that recently at the Parent Meeting the parents were told that he received a Safety Studies marks and b PE marks (a + b = n). Now Polycarp wants to write a subject's name in front of each mark so that:
there are exactly a Safety Studies marks,
there are exactly b PE marks,
the total average score in both subjects is maximum.

An average subject grade is the sum of all marks in it, divided by the number of them. Of course, the division is performed in real numbers without rounding up or down. Polycarp aims to maximize the x1 + x2, where x1 is the average score in the first subject (Safety Studies), and x2 is the average score in the second one (Physical Education).
input: The first line contains an integer n (2 ≤ n ≤ 105), n is the number of marks in Polycarp's Journal. The second line contains two positive integers a, b (1 ≤ a, b ≤ n - 1, a + b = n). The third line contains a sequence of integers t1, t2, ..., tn (1 ≤ ti ≤ 5), they are Polycarp's marks.
output: Print the sequence of integers f1, f2, ..., fn, where fi (1 ≤ fi ≤ 2) is the number of a subject to which the i-th mark should be attributed. If there are several possible solutions, then print such that the sequence f1, f2, ..., fn is the smallest lexicographically.
The sequence p1, p2, ..., pn is lexicographically less than q1, q2, ..., qn if there exists such j (1 ≤ j ≤ n) that pi = qi for all 1 ≤ i < j, аnd pj < qj.
note: In the first sample the average score in the first subject is equal to 4, and in the second one — to 4.5. The total average score is 8.5.

legend.ai: 教育改革后，Polycarp 在学校只学习两门课程：安全教育和体育（Physical Education）。在第四学期漫长的几个月里，他在这两门课中获得了 n 个成绩。当老师把成绩写入成绩册时，他们没有写明成绩对应的科目，只写下了成绩本身。
现在到了把成绩册给他严格的父母看的时候。Polycarp 知道，最近在家长会上，父母被告知他获得了 a 个安全教育成绩和 b 个体育成绩（a + b = n）。现在，Polycarp 想在每个成绩前写上对应的科目名称，使得：
恰好有 a 个安全教育成绩，
恰好有 b 个体育成绩，
两门科目的平均分之和最大。
某科目的平均分等于该科目所有成绩之和除以成绩数量。当然，除法在实数范围内进行，不进行向上或向下取整。Polycarp 的目标是最大化 x1 + x2，其中 x1 是第一门科目（安全教育）的平均分，x2 是第二门科目（体育）的平均分。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n（2 ≤ n ≤ 105），表示 Polycarp 的成绩单中成绩的数量。第二行包含两个正整数 a、b（1 ≤ a，b ≤ n - 1，a + b = n）。第三行包含一个整数序列 t1，t2，...，tn（1 ≤ ti ≤ 5），表示 Polycarp 的成绩。

output.ai: 输出整数序列 f1，f2，...，fn，其中 fi（1 ≤ fi ≤ 2）表示第 i 个成绩应被归入的科目编号。如果有多种可行解，则输出其中字典序最小的序列 f1，f2，...，fn。
如果存在一个 j（1 ≤ j ≤ n），使得对于所有 1 ≤ i < j，都有 pi = qi，且 pj < qj，则称序列 p1，p2，...，pn 的字典序小于序列 q1，q2，...，qn。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，第一门科目的平均分为 4，第二门科目的平均分为 4.5。平均分之和为 8.5。

problems.hint: How do we decide the lexicographical order.

legend: Archeologists have found a secret pass in the dungeon of one of the pyramids of Cycleland. To enter the treasury they have to open an unusual lock on the door. The lock consists of n words, each consisting of some hieroglyphs. The wall near the lock has a round switch. Each rotation of this switch changes the hieroglyphs according to some rules. The instruction nearby says that the door will open only if words written on the lock would be sorted in lexicographical order (the definition of lexicographical comparison in given in notes section).

The rule that changes hieroglyphs is the following. One clockwise rotation of the round switch replaces each hieroglyph with the next hieroglyph in alphabet, i.e. hieroglyph x (1 ≤ x ≤ c - 1) is replaced with hieroglyph (x + 1), and hieroglyph c is replaced with hieroglyph 1.

Help archeologist determine, how many clockwise rotations they should perform in order to open the door, or determine that this is impossible, i.e. no cyclic shift of the alphabet will make the sequence of words sorted lexicographically.
input: The first line of the input contains two integers n and c (2 ≤ n ≤ 500 000, 1 ≤ c ≤ 106) — the number of words, written on the lock, and the number of different hieroglyphs.

Each of the following n lines contains the description of one word. The i-th of these lines starts with integer li (1 ≤ li ≤ 500 000), that denotes the length of the i-th word, followed by li integers wi, 1, wi, 2, ..., wi, li (1 ≤ wi, j ≤ c) — the indices of hieroglyphs that make up the i-th word. Hieroglyph with index 1 is the smallest in the alphabet and with index c — the biggest.
It's guaranteed, that the total length of all words doesn't exceed 106.
output: If it is possible to open the door by rotating the round switch, print integer x (0 ≤ x ≤ c - 1) that defines the required number of clockwise rotations. If there are several valid x, print any of them.
If it is impossible to open the door by this method, print  - 1.
note: Word a1, a2, ..., am of length m is lexicographically not greater than word b1, b2, ..., bk of length k, if one of two conditions hold:
at first position i, such that ai ≠ bi, the character ai goes earlier in the alphabet than character bi, i.e. a has smaller character in the first position where they differ;
if there is no such position i and m ≤ k, i.e. the first word is a prefix of the second or two words are equal.
The sequence of words is said to be sorted in lexicographical order if each word (except the last one) is lexicographically not greater than the next word.
In the first sample, after the round switch is rotated 1 position clockwise the words look as follows:
In the second sample, words are already sorted in lexicographical order.
In the last sample, one can check that no shift of the alphabet will work.

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含两个整数 n 和 c（2 ≤ n ≤ 500 000，1 ≤ c ≤ 10^6）——锁上写出的单词数量以及不同象形文字的数量。
接下来的 n 行中，每行描述一个单词。第 i 行以整数 l_i（1 ≤ l_i ≤ 500 000）开头，随后是 l_i 个整数 w_i, 1，w_i, 2，...，w_i, l_i（1 ≤ w_i, j ≤ c），表示组成第 i 个单词的象形文字的编号。编号为 1 的象形文字是字母表中最小的，编号为 c 的象形文字是最大的。
保证所有单词的总长度不超过 10^6。

output.ai: 如果可以通过旋转圆形开关来打开门，则输出整数 x（0 ≤ x ≤ c - 1），它表示所需的顺时针旋转次数。如果有多个合法的 x，输出其中任意一个。
如果无法通过这种方法打开门，则输出 -1。

note.ai: 长度为 m 的单词 a1, a2, ..., am 在字典序上不大于长度为 k 的单词 b1, b2, ..., bk，当以下两个条件之一成立时：
在第一个满足 ai ≠ bi 的位置 i 上，字符 ai 在字母表中比字符 bi 更靠前，即 a 在它们第一个不同的位置上的字符更小；
如果不存在这样的位置 i 且 m ≤ k，即第一个单词是第二个单词的前缀，或者两个单词相等。
如果每个单词（最后一个除外）按字典序都不大于下一个单词，则称该单词序列按字典序排列。
在第一个样例中，将圆形开关顺时针旋转 1 个位置后，单词如下所示：
在第二个样例中，单词已经按字典序排列。

legend.ai: 考古学家在 Cycleland 的一座金字塔地牢中发现了一条秘密通道。为了进入宝库，他们必须打开门上的一把特殊的锁。这把锁由 n 个单词组成，每个单词由若干个象形文字构成。锁附近的墙上有一个圆形开关。每旋转一次开关，象形文字都会按照某些规则发生变化。旁边的说明写道：只有当锁上写出的单词按字典序排列时，门才会打开（字典序比较的定义见注释部分）。
改变象形文字的规则如下。顺时针旋转一次圆形开关，会将每个象形文字替换为字母表中的下一个象形文字，即象形文字 x（1 ≤ x ≤ c - 1）会被替换为象形文字（x + 1），而象形文字 c 会被替换为象形文字 1。
请帮助考古学家确定需要顺时针旋转多少次才能打开门，或者判断这是不可能的，即不存在任何字母表的循环移位能使这些单词按字典序排列。

statement.title: A. Variable, or There and Back Again

legend: Life is not easy for the perfectly common variable named Vasya. Wherever it goes, it is either assigned a value, or simply ignored, or is being used!

Vasya's life goes in states of a program. In each state, Vasya can either be used (for example, to calculate the value of another variable), or be assigned a value, or ignored. Between some states are directed (oriented) transitions.
A path is a sequence of states v1, v2, ..., vx, where for any 1 ≤ i < x exists a transition from vi to vi + 1.

Vasya's value in state v is interesting to the world, if exists path p1, p2, ..., pk such, that pi = v for some i (1 ≤ i ≤ k), in state p1 Vasya gets assigned a value, in state pk Vasya is used and there is no state pi (except for p1) where Vasya gets assigned a value.
Help Vasya, find the states in which Vasya's value is interesting to the world.
input: The first line contains two space-separated integers n and m (1 ≤ n, m ≤ 105) — the numbers of states and transitions, correspondingly.
The second line contains space-separated n integers f1, f2, ..., fn (0 ≤ fi ≤ 2), fi described actions performed upon Vasya in state i: 0 represents ignoring, 1 — assigning a value, 2 — using.

Next m lines contain space-separated pairs of integers ai, bi (1 ≤ ai, bi ≤ n, ai ≠ bi), each pair represents the transition from the state number ai to the state number bi. Between two states can be any number of transitions.
output: Print n integers r1, r2, ..., rn, separated by spaces or new lines. Number ri should equal 1, if Vasya's value in state i is interesting to the world and otherwise, it should equal 0. The states are numbered from 1 to n in the order, in which they are described in the input.
note: In the first sample the program states can be used to make the only path in which the value of Vasya interests the world, 1 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/70a0795f45d32287dba0eb83fc4a3f470c6e5537.png) 2 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/70a0795f45d32287dba0eb83fc4a3f470c6e5537.png) 3 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/70a0795f45d32287dba0eb83fc4a3f470c6e5537.png) 4; it includes all the states, so in all of them Vasya's value is interesting to the world.

The second sample the only path in which Vasya's value is interesting to the world is , — 1 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/70a0795f45d32287dba0eb83fc4a3f470c6e5537.png) 3; state 2 is not included there.
In the third sample we cannot make from the states any path in which the value of Vasya would be interesting to the world, so the value of Vasya is never interesting to the world.

legend.ai: 对于名为 Vasya 的这个再普通不过的变量来说，生活并不容易。无论它出现在哪里，要么会被赋值，要么会被直接忽略，要么会被使用！
瓦西亚的生命以程序的状态形式存在。在每个状态中，瓦西亚要么被使用（例如，用于计算另一个变量的值），要么被赋予一个值，要么被忽略。某些状态之间存在有向（带方向的）转移。
路径是状态序列 v1, v2, ..., vx，其中对于任意 1 ≤ i < x，都存在从 vi 到 vi+1 的转移。
如果存在路径 p1, p2, ..., pk，使得对于某个 i (1 ≤ i ≤ k) 有 pi = v，且在状态 p1 中瓦西亚被赋予一个值，在状态 pk 中瓦西亚被使用，并且除了 p1 之外不存在状态 pi 让瓦西亚被赋予一个值，那么瓦西亚在状态 v 中的值对世界是有意义的。
请帮助瓦西亚，找出所有瓦西亚的值对世界有意义的状态。

input.ai: 第一行包含两个空格分隔的整数 n 和 m (1 ≤ n, m ≤ 105)，分别表示状态数和转移数。
第二行包含空格分隔的 n 个整数 f1, f2, ..., fn (0 ≤ fi ≤ 2)，fi 描述在状态 i 中对瓦西亚执行的操作：0 表示忽略，1 表示赋予一个值，2 表示使用。
接下来的 m 行包含由空格分隔的整数对 a_i、b_i（1 ≤ a_i、b_i ≤ n，a_i ≠ b_i），每对整数表示从编号为 a_i 的状态到编号为 b_i 的状态的转移。两个状态之间可以有任意条转移。

output.ai: 输出 n 个整数 r_1、r_2、...、r_n，以空格或换行分隔。如果 Vasya 在状态 i 中的值对世界来说是有趣的，则 r_i 应为 1，否则应为 0。状态按照它们在输入中的描述顺序编号为 1 到 n。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，可以利用程序的状态构造出唯一一条使 Vasya 的值对世界有趣的路径：1 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/70a0795f45d32287dba0eb83fc4a3f470c6e5537.png) 2 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/70a0795f45d32287dba0eb83fc4a3f470c6e5537.png) 3 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/70a0795f45d32287dba0eb83fc4a3f470c6e5537.png) 4；它包含所有状态，因此在所有状态中 Vasya 的值都对世界有趣。
在第二个样例中，唯一一条使 Vasya 的值对世界有趣的路径是 1 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/70a0795f45d32287dba0eb83fc4a3f470c6e5537.png) 3；状态 2 不在其中。
在第三个样例中，我们无法从这些状态构造出任何一条能使 Vasya 的值对世界有趣的路径，因此 Vasya 的值永远不会对世界有趣。

legend: Polycarp loves not only to take pictures, but also to show his photos to friends. On his personal website he has recently installed a widget that can display n photos with the scroll option. At each moment of time the widget displays exactly one photograph with the option showing the previous/next one. From the first photo, you can switch to the second one or to the n-th one, from the second photo you can switch to the third one or to the first one, etc. Thus, navigation is performed in a cycle.

Polycarp's collection consists of m photo albums, the i-th album contains ai photos. Polycarp wants to choose n photos and put them on a new widget. To make watching the photos interesting to the visitors, he is going to post pictures so that no two photos from one album were neighboring (each photo will have exactly two neighbors, the first photo's neighbors are the second and the n-th one).
Help Polycarp compile a photo gallery. Select n photos from his collection and put them in such order that no two photos from one album went one after the other.
input: The first line contains two integers n and m (3 ≤ n ≤ 1000, 1 ≤ m ≤ 40), where n is the number of photos on the widget, and m is the number of albums. The second line contains m integers a1, a2, ..., am (1 ≤ ai ≤ 1000), where ai is the number of photos in the i-th album.
output: Print the single number -1 if there is no solution. Otherwise, print n numbers t1, t2, ..., tn, where ti represents the number of the album of the i-th picture in the widget. The albums are numbered from 1 in the order of their appearance in the input. If there are several solutions, print any of them.

legend.ai: Polycarp 不仅喜欢拍照，还喜欢把自己的照片展示给朋友。最近，他在个人网站上安装了一个可以通过滚动浏览 n 张照片的组件。在任意时刻，该组件恰好显示一张照片，并提供查看上一张/下一张照片的选项。对于第一张照片，可以切换到第二张或第 n 张；对于第二张照片，可以切换到第三张或第一张，依此类推。因此，导航是在一个环中进行的。
Polycarp 的照片集合由 m 个相册组成，第 i 个相册包含 ai 张照片。Polycarp 想要选择 n 张照片并将它们放入一个新的组件中。为了让访客观看照片时更有趣，他打算按照如下方式发布照片：同一个相册中的任意两张照片都不能相邻（每张照片恰好有两个相邻的照片，第一张照片相邻的是第二张和第 n 张）。
请帮助 Polycarp 编排照片画廊。从他的照片集合中选择 n 张照片，并按照这样的顺序排列，使得同一个相册中的任意两张照片都不会相邻。

input.ai: 第一行包含两个整数 n 和 m（3 ≤ n ≤ 1000，1 ≤ m ≤ 40），其中 n 表示组件中的照片数量，m 表示相册数量。第二行包含 m 个整数 a1，a2，...，am（1 ≤ ai ≤ 1000），其中 ai 表示第 i 个相册中的照片数量。

output.ai: 如果无解，输出一个数 -1。否则，输出 n 个数 t1，t2，...，tn，其中 ti 表示组件中第 i 张照片所属的相册编号。相册按照它们在输入中的出现顺序从 1 开始编号。如果有多个解，输出任意一个即可。

legend: Petya loves lucky numbers very much. Everybody knows that lucky numbers are positive integers whose decimal record contains only the lucky digits 4 and 7. For example, numbers 47, 744, 4 are lucky and 5, 17, 467 are not.

Petya loves long lucky numbers very much. He is interested in the minimum lucky number d that meets some condition. Let cnt(x) be the number of occurrences of number x in number d as a substring. For example, if d = 747747, then cnt(4) = 2, cnt(7) = 4, cnt(47) = 2, cnt(74) = 2. Petya wants the following condition to fulfil simultaneously: cnt(4) = a1, cnt(7) = a2, cnt(47) = a3, cnt(74) = a4. Petya is not interested in the occurrences of other numbers. Help him cope with this task.
input: The single line contains four integers a1, a2, a3 and a4 (1 ≤ a1, a2, a3, a4 ≤ 106).
output: On the single line print without leading zeroes the answer to the problem — the minimum lucky number d such, that cnt(4) = a1, cnt(7) = a2, cnt(47) = a3, cnt(74) = a4. If such number does not exist, print the single number "-1" (without the quotes).

legend.ai: Petya 非常喜欢幸运数。众所周知，幸运数是十进制表示中只包含幸运数字 4 和 7 的正整数。例如，47、744、4 是幸运数，而 5、17、467 不是。

Petya 非常喜欢较长的幸运数。他对满足某些条件的最小幸运数 d 感兴趣。令 cnt(x) 表示数字 x 作为子串在数字 d 中出现的次数。例如，当 d = 747747 时，cnt(4) = 2，cnt(7) = 4，cnt(47) = 2，cnt(74) = 2。Petya 希望同时满足以下条件：cnt(4) = a1，cnt(7) = a2，cnt(47) = a3，cnt(74) = a4。Petya 对其他数字的出现次数不感兴趣。请帮助他完成这项任务。

input.ai: 一行包含四个整数 a1、a2、a3 和 a4（1 ≤ a1，a2，a3，a4 ≤ 106）。

output.ai: 在一行中输出本题的答案——不含前导零且满足 cnt(4) = a1、cnt(7) = a2、cnt(47) = a3、cnt(74) = a4 的最小幸运数 d。如果不存在这样的数字，则输出单独的数字“-1”（不含引号）。

problems.hint: The number of operations for each $(x,y)$ can be calculated.

legend: The first algorithm for detecting a face on the image working in realtime was developed by Paul Viola and Michael Jones in 2001. A part of the algorithm is a procedure that computes Haar features. As part of this task, we consider a simplified model of this concept.
Let's consider a rectangular image that is represented with a table of size n × m. The table elements are integers that specify the brightness of each pixel in the image.
A feature also is a rectangular table of size n × m. Each cell of a feature is painted black or white.

To calculate the value of the given feature at the given image, you must perform the following steps. First the table of the feature is put over the table of the image (without rotations or reflections), thus each pixel is entirely covered with either black or white cell. The value of a feature in the image is the value of W - B, where W is the total brightness of the pixels in the image, covered with white feature cells, and B is the total brightness of the pixels covered with black feature cells.
Some examples of the most popular Haar features are given below.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7b607f43d52a051b4a30ee0a9cc80a09135d83e4.png)
Your task is to determine the number of operations that are required to calculate the feature by using the so-called prefix rectangles.
A prefix rectangle is any rectangle on the image, the upper left corner of which coincides with the upper left corner of the image.
You have a variable value, whose value is initially zero. In one operation you can count the sum of pixel values ​​at any prefix rectangle, multiply it by any integer and add to variable value.

You are given a feature. It is necessary to calculate the minimum number of operations required to calculate the values of this attribute at an arbitrary image. For a better understanding of the statement, read the explanation of the first sample.
input: The first line contains two space-separated integers n and m (1 ≤ n, m ≤ 100) — the number of rows and columns in the feature.

Next n lines contain the description of the feature. Each line consists of m characters, the j-th character of the i-th line equals to "W", if this element of the feature is white and "B" if it is black.
output: Print a single number — the minimum number of operations that you need to make to calculate the value of the feature.
note: The first sample corresponds to feature B, the one shown in the picture. The value of this feature in an image of size 6 × 8 equals to the difference of the total brightness of the pixels in the lower and upper half of the image. To calculate its value, perform the following two operations:

add the sum of pixels in the prefix rectangle with the lower right corner in the 6-th row and 8-th column with coefficient 1 to the variable value (the rectangle is indicated by a red frame); ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b58310c85de9a0f17f6a1997100232c0c7481f84.png)

add the number of pixels in the prefix rectangle with the lower right corner in the 3-rd row and 8-th column with coefficient  - 2 and variable value. ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b38cf76c02a599fdaf334479e2b06a7d0f798d12.png)
Thus, all the pixels in the lower three rows of the image will be included with factor 1, and all pixels in the upper three rows of the image will be included with factor 1 - 2 =  - 1, as required.

legend.ai: 2001 年，Paul Viola 和 Michael Jones 开发了第一种能够实时在图像中检测人脸的算法。该算法的一部分是计算 Haar 特征的过程。作为本题的一部分，我们将考虑这一概念的简化模型。
考虑一个用大小为 n × m 的表格表示的矩形图像。表格元素为整数，表示图像中每个像素的亮度。
特征也是一个大小为 n × m 的矩形表格。特征的每个格子被涂成黑色或白色。
要计算给定特征在给定图像上的取值，需要执行以下步骤。首先将特征表格覆盖在图像表格上（不允许旋转或翻转），这样每个像素都完全被黑色或白色格子覆盖。特征在图像中的取值等于 W - B，其中 W 是被白色特征格子覆盖的像素的总亮度，B 是被黑色特征格子覆盖的像素的总亮度。
下面给出一些最常用的 Haar 特征的示例。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7b607f43d52a051b4a30ee0a9cc80a09135d83e4.png)
你的任务是确定使用所谓的前缀矩形来计算该特征所需的操作次数。
前缀矩形是图像上的任意一个矩形，其左上角与图像的左上角重合。
你有一个变量，其值初始为零。在一次操作中，你可以计算任意前缀矩形内像素值之和，将其乘以任意整数，并加到变量的值上。
给定一个特征。你需要计算在任意图像上计算该特征值所需的最少操作次数。为了更好地理解题意，请阅读第一个样例的解释。

input.ai: 第一行包含两个用空格分隔的整数 n 和 m（1 ≤ n，m ≤ 100）——特征的行数和列数。
接下来 n 行包含特征的描述。每行由 m 个字符组成。如果该特征的第 i 行第 j 个元素为白色，则第 i 行的第 j 个字符为“W”；如果为黑色，则为“B”。

output.ai: 输出一个整数——计算该特征的值所需进行的最少操作次数。

note.ai: 第一个样例对应于图中所示的特征 B。对于大小为 6 × 8 的图像，该特征的值等于图像下半部分与上半部分像素总亮度之差。要计算其值，执行以下两个操作：
将右下角位于第 6 行第 8 列的前缀矩形中像素的总和乘以系数 1，加到变量 value 上(该矩形用红框标出)；![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b58310c85de9a0f17f6a1997100232c0c7481f84.png)
将右下角位于第 3 行第 8 列的前缀矩形中像素的数量乘以系数  - 2，加到变量 value 上。![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b38cf76c02a599fdaf334479e2b06a7d0f798d12.png)
因此，图像下方三行中的所有像素都将以系数 1 计入，而图像上方三行中的所有像素都将以系数 1 - 2 =  - 1 计入，正如要求的那样。

legend: Bob recently read about bitwise operations used in computers: AND, OR and XOR. He have studied their properties and invented a new game.

Initially, Bob chooses integer m, bit depth of the game, which means that all numbers in the game will consist of m bits. Then he asks Peter to choose some m-bit number. After that, Bob computes the values of n variables. Each variable is assigned either a constant m-bit number or result of bitwise operation. Operands of the operation may be either variables defined before, or the number, chosen by Peter. After that, Peter's score equals to the sum of all variable values.

Bob wants to know, what number Peter needs to choose to get the minimum possible score, and what number he needs to choose to get the maximum possible score. In both cases, if there are several ways to get the same score, find the minimum number, which he can choose.
input: The first line contains two integers n and m, the number of variables and bit depth, respectively (1 ≤ n ≤ 5000; 1 ≤ m ≤ 1000).

The following n lines contain descriptions of the variables. Each line describes exactly one variable. Description has the following format: name of a new variable, space, sign ":=", space, followed by one of:
Binary number of exactly m bits.

The first operand, space, bitwise operation ("AND", "OR" or "XOR"), space, the second operand. Each operand is either the name of variable defined before or symbol '?', indicating the number chosen by Peter.
Variable names are strings consisting of lowercase Latin letters with length at most 10. All variable names are different.
output: In the first line output the minimum number that should be chosen by Peter, to make the sum of all variable values minimum possible, in the second line output the minimum number that should be chosen by Peter, to make the sum of all variable values maximum possible. Both numbers should be printed as m-bit binary numbers.
note: In the first sample if Peter chooses a number 0112, then a = 1012, b = 0112, c = 0002, the sum of their values is 8. If he chooses the number 1002, then a = 1012, b = 0112, c = 1112, the sum of their values is 15.
For the second test, the minimum and maximum sum of variables a, bb, cx, d and e is 2, and this sum doesn't depend on the number chosen by Peter, so the minimum Peter can choose is 0.

examples.input:
5 1
a := 1
bb := 0
cx := ? OR a
d := ? XOR ?
e := d AND bb

input.ai: 第一行包含两个整数 n 和 m，分别表示变量的数量和位数（1 ≤ n ≤ 5000；1 ≤ m ≤ 1000）。
接下来的 n 行包含变量的描述。每行恰好描述一个变量。描述格式如下：新变量的名称、空格、符号 :=、空格，后接以下内容之一：
一个恰好包含 m 位的二进制数。
第一个操作数、空格、按位运算（“AND”、“OR”或“XOR”）、空格、第二个操作数。每个操作数要么是之前定义的变量名，要么是符号 '?'，表示 Peter 选择的数字。
变量名是由小写拉丁字母组成的字符串，长度不超过 10。所有变量名互不相同。

output.ai: 第一行输出 Peter 为使得所有变量值之和尽可能小而应选择的最小的数；第二行输出 Peter 为使得所有变量值之和尽可能大而应选择的最小的数。两个数都应输出为 m 位二进制数。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，如果 Peter 选择数 0112，则 a = 1012, b = 0112, c = 0002，它们的值之和为 8。如果他选择数 1002，则 a = 1012, b = 0112, c = 1112，它们的值之和为 15。
对于第二个测试用例，变量 a、bb、cx、d 和 e 的和的最小值与最大值均为 2，并且这个和与 Peter 选择的数无关，所以 Peter 可以选择的最小数是 0。

legend.ai: Bob 最近读到了计算机中使用的按位运算：AND、OR 和 XOR。他研究了这些运算的性质，并发明了一种新游戏。
最初，Bob 选择整数 m 作为游戏的位数，这意味着游戏中的所有数字都由 m 位组成。然后他要求 Peter 选择一个 m 位数。之后，Bob 计算 n 个变量的值。每个变量要么被赋予一个常量 m 位数，要么被赋予一次按位运算的结果。运算的操作数可以是之前定义的变量，也可以是 Peter 选择的数字。之后，Peter 的得分等于所有变量值之和。
Bob 想知道 Peter 需要选择什么数字才能获得可能的最小得分，以及需要选择什么数字才能获得可能的最大得分。在这两种情况下，如果有多种选择可以得到相同的得分，则找出 Peter 可以选择的最小数字。

legend: A revolution took place on the Buka Island. New government replaced the old one. The new government includes n parties and each of them is entitled to some part of the island according to their contribution to the revolution. However, they can't divide the island.

The island can be conventionally represented as two rectangles a × b and c × d unit squares in size correspondingly. The rectangles are located close to each other. At that, one of the sides with the length of a and one of the sides with the length of c lie on one line. You can see this in more details on the picture.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c919851573257c51c49fd0bc2857509b3d8bc159.png)

The i-th party is entitled to a part of the island equal to xi unit squares. Every such part should fully cover several squares of the island (it is not allowed to cover the squares partially) and be a connected figure. A "connected figure" presupposes that from any square of this party one can move to any other square of the same party moving through edge-adjacent squares also belonging to that party.
Your task is to divide the island between parties.
input: The first line contains 5 space-separated integers — a, b, c, d and n (1 ≤ a, b, c, d ≤ 50, b ≠ d, 1 ≤ n ≤ 26). The second line contains n space-separated numbers. The i-th of them is equal to number xi (1 ≤ xi ≤ a × b + c × d). It is guaranteed that ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/35d7a672005b7ad5e3d4935e2cb8334465a0bee4.png).
output: If dividing the island between parties in the required manner is impossible, print "NO" (without the quotes). Otherwise, print "YES" (also without the quotes) and, starting from the next line, print max(b, d) lines each containing a + c characters. To mark what square should belong to what party, use lowercase Latin letters. For the party that is first in order in the input data, use "a", for the second one use "b" and so on. Use "." for the squares that belong to the sea. The first symbol of the second line of the output data should correspond to the square that belongs to the rectangle a × b. The last symbol of the second line should correspond to the square that belongs to the rectangle c × d.
If there are several solutions output any.

legend: A social network for dogs called DH (DogHouse) has k special servers to recompress uploaded videos of cute cats. After each video is uploaded, it should be recompressed on one (any) of the servers, and only after that it can be saved in the social network.
We know that each server takes one second to recompress a one minute fragment. Thus, any server takes m seconds to recompress a m minute video.

We know the time when each of the n videos were uploaded to the network (in seconds starting from the moment all servers started working). All videos appear at different moments of time and they are recompressed in the order they appear. If some video appeared at time s, then its recompressing can start at that very moment, immediately. Some videos can await recompressing when all the servers are busy. In this case, as soon as a server is available, it immediately starts recompressing another video. The videos that await recompressing go in a queue. If by the moment the videos started being recompressed some servers are available, then any of them starts recompressing the video.
For each video find the moment it stops being recompressed.
input: The first line of the input contains integers n and k (1 ≤ n, k ≤ 5·105) — the number of videos and servers, respectively.

Next n lines contain the descriptions of the videos as pairs of integers si, mi (1 ≤ si, mi ≤ 109), where si is the time in seconds when the i-th video appeared and mi is its duration in minutes. It is guaranteed that all the si's are distinct and the videos are given in the chronological order of upload, that is in the order of increasing si.
output: Print n numbers e1, e2, ..., en, where ei is the time in seconds after the servers start working, when the i-th video will be recompressed.

legend.ai: 一个名为 DH（DogHouse）的狗狗社交网络拥有 k 台专用服务器，用于重新压缩上传的可爱猫咪视频。每个视频上传后，都应在其中一台（任意一台）服务器上进行重新压缩，之后才能将其保存到社交网络中。
我们知道，每台服务器重新压缩一段一分钟的视频需要一秒。因此，任意服务器重新压缩一段 m 分钟的视频需要 m 秒。

我们知道 n 个视频上传到网络的时间（单位为秒，从所有服务器开始工作时刻起算）。所有视频的出现时刻互不相同，并且按照出现顺序进行重新压缩。如果某个视频在时刻 s 出现，那么其重新压缩可以恰好从该时刻立即开始。当所有服务器都忙碌时，部分视频可能需要等待重新压缩。此时，一旦某台服务器空闲，它就会立即开始重新压缩另一个视频。等待重新压缩的视频会进入队列。如果在视频开始重新压缩的时刻有服务器空闲，则其中任意一台都会开始重新压缩该视频。
对于每个视频，求它完成重新压缩的时刻。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含整数 n 和 k（1 ≤ n, k ≤ 5·10^5），分别表示视频数量和服务器数量。
接下来的 n 行包含视频的描述，每行是两个整数 s_i、m_i（1 ≤ s_i, m_i ≤ 10^9），其中 s_i 表示第 i 个视频出现的时间（单位为秒），m_i 表示其时长（单位为分钟）。保证所有 s_i 互不相同，且视频按照上传的时间顺序给出，即按照 s_i 递增的顺序给出。

output.ai: 输出 n 个数 e_1、e_2、…、e_n，其中 e_i 表示服务器开始工作后经过的时间（单位为秒），即第 i 个视频将被重新压缩的时刻。
