legend: Maxim has opened his own restaurant! The restaurant has got a huge table, the table's length is p meters.

Maxim has got a dinner party tonight, n guests will come to him. Let's index the guests of Maxim's restaurant from 1 to n. Maxim knows the sizes of all guests that are going to come to him. The i-th guest's size (ai) represents the number of meters the guest is going to take up if he sits at the restaurant table.

Long before the dinner, the guests line up in a queue in front of the restaurant in some order. Then Maxim lets the guests in, one by one. Maxim stops letting the guests in when there is no place at the restaurant table for another guest in the queue. There is no place at the restaurant table for another guest in the queue, if the sum of sizes of all guests in the restaurant plus the size of this guest from the queue is larger than p. In this case, not to offend the guest who has no place at the table, Maxim doesn't let any other guest in the restaurant, even if one of the following guests in the queue would have fit in at the table.

(2, 3, 1) — there will be one person in the restaurant;
(3, 1, 2) — there will be one person in the restaurant;
(3, 2, 1) — there will be one person in the restaurant.

legend.ai: Maxim 开了自己的餐厅！这家餐厅有一张很大的餐桌，餐桌的长度为 p 米。
今晚 Maxim 将举办晚宴，会有 n 位客人来参加。我们将 Maxim 餐厅的客人编号为 1 到 n。Maxim 知道所有即将到来的客人的大小。第 i 位客人的大小（ai）表示当该客人坐在餐桌旁时，他将占用的米数。

problems.hint: Classic shortest path problem.

legend: All of Slavic's friends are planning to travel from the place where they live to a party using their bikes. And they all have a bike except Slavic. There are n$$$n$$$ cities through which they can travel. They all live in the city 1$$$1$$$ and want to go to the party located in the city n$$$n$$$. The map of cities can be seen as an undirected graph with n$$$n$$$ nodes and m$$$m$$$ edges. Edge i$$$i$$$ connects cities ui$$$u_i$$$ and vi$$$v_i$$$ and has a length of wi$$$w_i$$$.

Slavic doesn't have a bike, but what he has is money. Every city has exactly one bike for sale. The bike in the i$$$i$$$-th city has a slowness factor of si$$$s_{i}$$$. Once Slavic buys a bike, he can use it whenever to travel from the city he is currently in to any neighboring city, by taking wi⋅sj$$$w_i \cdot s_j$$$ time, considering he is traversing edge i$$$i$$$ using a bike j$$$j$$$ he owns.

Slavic can buy as many bikes as he wants as money isn't a problem for him. Since Slavic hates traveling by bike, he wants to get from his place to the party in the shortest amount of time possible. And, since his informatics skills are quite rusty, he asks you for help.

What's the shortest amount of time required for Slavic to travel from city 1$$$1$$$ to city n$$$n$$$? Slavic can't travel without a bike. It is guaranteed that it is possible for Slavic to travel from city 1$$$1$$$ to any other city.
input: The first line contains a single integer t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤100$$$1 \leq t \leq 100$$$) — the number of test cases. The description of the test cases follows.

The first line of each test case contains two space-separated integers n$$$n$$$ and m$$$m$$$ (2≤n≤1000$$$2 \leq n \leq 1000$$$; n−1≤m≤1000$$$n - 1 \leq m \leq 1000$$$) — the number of cities and the number of roads, respectively.

The i$$$i$$$-th of the following m$$$m$$$ lines each contain three integers ui$$$u_i$$$, vi$$$v_i$$$, wi$$$w_i$$$ (1≤ui,vi≤n$$$1 \le u_i, v_i \le n$$$, ui≠vi$$$u_i \neq v_i$$$; 1≤wi≤105$$$1 \leq w_i \leq 10^5$$$), denoting that there is a road between cities ui$$$u_i$$$ and vi$$$v_i$$$ of length wi$$$w_i$$$. The same pair of cities can be connected by more than one road.
The next line contains n$$$n$$$ integers s1,…,sn$$$s_1, \ldots, s_n$$$ (1≤si≤1000$$$1 \leq s_i \leq 1000$$$) — the slowness factor of each bike.
The sum of n$$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed 1000$$$1000$$$, and the sum of m$$$m$$$ over all test cases does not exceed 1000$$$1000$$$.

legend: Advertising has become part of our routine. And now, in the era of progressive technologies, we need your ideas to make advertising better!

Single words in one line of the banner should be separated by spaces. You are allowed to insert more than one space at once. Note that you are not allowed to break the words, that is, each word in the text must occupy exactly one line in the banner. Besides, you cannot change the word order, that is, if you read the banner text consecutively, from top to bottom and from left to right, you should get some consecutive part of the advertisement text.

More formally, the statement can be written like that. Let's say that all words are indexed from 1 to n in the order in which they occur in the advertisement text. Then you have to choose all words, starting from some i-th one and ending with some j-th one (1 ≤ i ≤ j ≤ n), so that all of them could be written on the banner. legend: There is a long plate s containing n digits. Iahub wants to delete some digits (possibly none, but he is not allowed to delete all the digits) to form his "magic number" on the plate, a number that is divisible by 5. Note that, the resulting number may contain leading zeros.

If it is impossible to sort the given sequence, print the single number -1.

legend.ai: Petya 喜欢幸运数字。我们都知道，幸运数字是十进制表示中只包含幸运数字 4 和 7 的正整数。例如，47、744、4 是幸运数字，而 5、17、467 不是。
Petya 得到了一个由 n 个数字组成的数组，这是他的生日礼物。现在他想将其按非递减顺序排序。然而，进行普通的排序很无聊，因此 Petya 规定了如下限制：只有当两个数中至少有一个是幸运数时，才能交换这两个数。你的任务是根据这一限制对数组进行排序。请找出任意一种可行的交换序列（序列中的操作次数不应超过 2n）。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 105）——数组中元素的个数。第二行包含 n 个不超过 109 的正整数——需要按非递减顺序排序的数组。

output.ai: 第一行输出一个整数 k（0 ≤ k ≤ 2n）——排序所需的交换次数。接下来的 k 行中，每行输出一对不同的整数——表示需要交换的两个元素的下标。数组中的元素从 1 开始编号。如果无法对给定序列进行排序，则输出单独的一个数 -1。
如果存在多种方案，输出任意一种即可。注意，你不需要使 k 最小。只要交换次数不超过 2n，任何能够完成排序的方案都会被接受。

legend: Shaass has n books. He wants to make a bookshelf for all his books. He wants the bookshelf's dimensions to be as small as possible. The thickness of the i-th book is ti and its pages' width is equal to wi. The thickness of each book is either 1 or 2. All books have the same page heights.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a0717a4d638e90b96d21956ba5c63ca11ab4694d.png)

Shaass puts the books on the bookshelf in the following way. First he selects some of the books and put them vertically. Then he puts the rest of the books horizontally above the vertical books. The sum of the widths of the horizontal books must be no more than the total thickness of the vertical books. A sample arrangement of the books is depicted in the figure.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e4df5ef6413006729dc788d02b6e321e4a23b590.png)
Help Shaass to find the minimum total thickness of the vertical books that we can achieve.
input: The first line of the input contains an integer n, (1 ≤ n ≤ 100). Each of the next n lines contains two integers ti and wi denoting the thickness and width of the i-th book correspondingly, (1 ≤ ti ≤ 2, 1 ≤ wi ≤ 100).
output: On the only line of the output print the minimum total thickness of the vertical books that we can achieve.

legend.ai: Shaass 有 n 本书。他想为所有书制作一个书架。他希望书架的尺寸尽可能小。第 i 本书的厚度为 t_i，书页的宽度等于 w_i。每本书的厚度均为 1 或 2。所有书的页面高度都相同。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a0717a4d638e90b96d21956ba5c63ca11ab4694d.png)
Shaass 按如下方式将书放在书架上。首先，他选择一些书并将它们竖直放置。然后，他将其余的书水平放置在竖直放置的书上方。水平放置的书的宽度总和不得超过竖直放置的书的总厚度。图中展示了一种书籍摆放方式。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e4df5ef6413006729dc788d02b6e321e4a23b590.png)
请帮助 Shaass 求出我们能够达到的竖直放置的书的总厚度的最小值。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 100）。接下来的 n 行中，每行包含两个整数 ti 和 wi，分别表示第 i 本书的厚度和宽度（1 ≤ ti ≤ 2，1 ≤ wi ≤ 100）。

output.ai: 在输出的唯一一行中，输出我们能够达到的竖直放置的书的总厚度的最小值。

Each day, Harry walks a trail from the cabin where he currently is to Lake Geneva, and then from there he walks a trail to any of the m$$$m$$$ cabins (including the one he started in). However, as he has to finish the hike in a day, at least one of the two trails has to be short.
How many possible combinations of trails can Harry take if he starts in cabin 1 and walks for n$$$n$$$ days?

legend: Let A = {a1, a2, ..., an} be any permutation of the first n natural numbers {1, 2, ..., n}. You are given a positive integer k and another sequence B = {b1, b2, ..., bn}, where bi is the number of elements aj in A to the left of the element at = i such that aj ≥ (i + k).
For example, if n = 5, a possible A is {5, 1, 4, 2, 3}. For k = 2, B is given by {1, 2, 1, 0, 0}. But if k = 3, then B = {1, 1, 0, 0, 0}.

For two sequences X = {x1, x2, ..., xn} and Y = {y1, y2, ..., yn}, let i-th elements be the first elements such that xi ≠ yi. If xi < yi, then X is lexicographically smaller than Y, while if xi > yi, then X is lexicographically greater than Y.
Given n, k and B, you need to determine the lexicographically smallest A.
input: The first line contains two space separated integers n and k (1 ≤ n ≤ 1000, 1 ≤ k ≤ n). On the second line are n integers specifying the values of B = {b1, b2, ..., bn}.
output: Print on a single line n integers of A = {a1, a2, ..., an} such that A is lexicographically minimal. It is guaranteed that the solution exists.

input.ai: 第一行包含两个由空格分隔的整数 n 和 k（1 ≤ n ≤ 1000，1 ≤ k ≤ n）。第二行包含 n 个整数，表示 B = {b1, b2, ..., bn} 中的元素值。

output.ai: 请在一行中输出 n 个整数 A = {a1, a2, ..., an}，使得 A 在字典序上最小。保证解一定存在。

legend.ai: 令 A = {a1, a2, ..., an} 为前 n 个自然数 {1, 2, ..., n} 的任意一个排列。给定一个正整数 k 和另一个序列 B = {b1, b2, ..., bn}，其中 bi 表示 A 中位于值为 i 的元素左侧且满足 aj ≥ (i + k) 的元素 aj 的数量。
对于两个序列 X = {x1, x2, ..., xn} 和 Y = {y1, y2, ..., yn}，令第 i 个元素为满足 xi ≠ yi 的第一个元素。如果 xi < yi，则称 X 的字典序小于 Y；如果 xi > yi，则称 X 的字典序大于 Y。
给定 n、k 和 B，你需要确定字典序最小的 A。

legend: The Berland road network consists of n cities and of m bidirectional roads. The cities are numbered from 1 to n, where the main capital city has number n, and the culture capital — number 1. The road network is set up so that it is possible to reach any city from any other one by the roads. Moving on each road in any direction takes the same time.
All residents of Berland are very lazy people, and so when they want to get from city v to city u, they always choose one of the shortest paths (no matter which one).

The Berland government wants to make this country's road network safer. For that, it is going to put a police station in one city. The police station has a rather strange property: when a citizen of Berland is driving along the road with a police station at one end of it, the citizen drives more carefully, so all such roads are considered safe. The roads, both ends of which differ from the city with the police station, are dangerous.

Now the government wonders where to put the police station so that the average number of safe roads for all the shortest paths from the cultural capital to the main capital would take the maximum value.
input: The first input line contains two integers n and m (2 ≤ n ≤ 100, ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/830edae867a954b8b9fed8adb7a01c55020312a0.png)) — the number of cities and the number of roads in Berland, correspondingly. Next m lines contain pairs of integers vi, ui (1 ≤ vi, ui ≤ n, vi ≠ ui) — the numbers of cities that are connected by the i-th road. The numbers on a line are separated by a space.
It is guaranteed that each pair of cities is connected with no more than one road and that it is possible to get from any city to any other one along Berland roads.
output: Print the maximum possible value of the average number of safe roads among all shortest paths from the culture capital to the main one. The answer will be considered valid if its absolute or relative inaccuracy does not exceed 10 - 6.
note: In the first sample you can put a police station in one of the capitals, then each path will have exactly one safe road. If we place the station not in the capital, then the average number of safe roads will also make ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/8f23cc2cd3bef67bde56e16911c7af627da25d4d.png).

In the second sample we can obtain the maximum sought value if we put the station in city 4, then 6 paths will have 2 safe roads each, and one path will have 0 safe roads, so the answer will equal ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d7723df54e28c93b1c3b9d4c68b039b5071092af.png).

legend.ai: Berland 的道路网络由 n 座城市和 m 条双向道路组成。城市编号从 1 到 n，其中主要首都的编号为 n，文化首都的编号为 1。该道路网络保证任意城市都可以通过道路到达其他任意城市。在每条道路上向任意方向行驶所需的时间都相同。
Berland 的所有居民都非常懒惰，因此当他们想要从城市 v 到达城市 u 时，总会选择一条最短路径（无论是哪一条）。
Berland 政府希望让这个国家的道路网络更加安全。为此，他们计划在某座城市中设置一个警察局。警察局具有一种相当奇特的性质：当 Berland 的居民沿着一端设有警察局的道路行驶时，他们会更加小心，因此所有这类道路都被视为安全道路。两端都不是设有警察局的城市的道路则是危险的。
现在，政府想知道应将警察局设在哪里，才能使从文化首都到主首都的所有最短路径中，安全道路数量的平均值达到最大。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含两个整数 n 和 m(2 ≤ n ≤ 100， ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/830edae867a954b8b9fed8adb7a01c55020312a0.png))——分别表示 Berland 中城市和道路的数量。接下来的 m 行包含两个整数 vi、ui(1 ≤ vi，ui ≤ n，vi ≠ ui)——表示由第 i 条道路连接的城市编号。每行中的数字以空格分隔。
保证任意一对城市之间至多有一条道路，并且沿着 Berland 的道路可以从任意城市到达任意其他城市。

output.ai: 输出从文化首都到主首都的所有最短路径中，安全道路数量平均值的最大可能值。当答案的绝对误差或相对误差不超过 10 - 6 时，将被视为正确。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，可以将警察局设在其中一个首都，这样每条路径都恰好有一条安全道路。如果不将警察局设在首都，那么安全道路数量的平均值也会达到 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/8f23cc2cd3bef67bde56e16911c7af627da25d4d.png)。
在第二个样例中，如果将警察局设在城市 4，就可以得到所求的最大值。此时有 6 条路径各包含 2 条安全道路，另有 1 条路径包含 0 条安全道路，因此答案等于 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d7723df54e28c93b1c3b9d4c68b039b5071092af.png)。

legend: Jon Snow now has to fight with White Walkers. He has n rangers, each of which has his own strength. Also Jon Snow has his favourite number x. Each ranger can fight with a white walker only if the strength of the white walker equals his strength. He however thinks that his rangers are weak and need to improve. Jon now thinks that if he takes the bitwise XOR of strengths of some of rangers with his favourite number x, he might get soldiers of high strength. So, he decided to do the following operation k times:
Arrange all the rangers in a straight line in the order of increasing strengths.
Take the bitwise XOR (is written as ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c4b7092c0f7ce6535f2574569c98f7b3c2fe2c5f.png)) of the strength of each alternate ranger with x and update it's strength.
The strength of first ranger is updated to ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b989fec42185029adec488aa738b78d9de953aef.png), i.e. 7.
The strength of second ranger remains the same, i.e. 7.
The strength of third ranger is updated to ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/3c7c9436158c0744fffbc90f5dcf6769683b82c2.png), i.e. 11.
The strength of fourth ranger remains the same, i.e. 11.
The strength of fifth ranger is updated to ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/842bb4d07e058ad06611d99fc15455f0a936cb03.png), i.e. 13.
Now, Jon wants to know the maximum and minimum strength of the rangers after performing the above operations k times. He wants your help for this task. Can you help him?
input: First line consists of three integers n, k, x (1 ≤ n ≤ 105, 0 ≤ k ≤ 105, 0 ≤ x ≤ 103) — number of rangers Jon has, the number of times Jon will carry out the operation and Jon's favourite number respectively.
Second line consists of n integers representing the strengths of the rangers a1, a2, ..., an (0 ≤ ai ≤ 103).
output: Output two integers, the maximum and the minimum strength of the rangers after performing the operation k times.

legend.ai: 琼恩·雪诺现在必须与异鬼战斗。他有 n 名游骑兵，每名游骑兵都有自己的战斗力。此外，琼恩·雪诺还有他最喜欢的数字 x。每名游骑兵只有在异鬼的战斗力与自己的战斗力相等时，才能与异鬼战斗。然而，他认为自己的游骑兵太弱了，需要提升实力。琼恩现在想到，如果将一些游骑兵的战斗力与他最喜欢的数字 x 进行按位异或，或许能得到战斗力更强的士兵。因此，他决定执行以下操作 k 次：
按照战斗力递增的顺序，将所有游骑兵排成一条直线。
将每隔一名游骑兵的战斗力与 x 进行按位异或(记作 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c4b7092c0f7ce6535f2574569c98f7b3c2fe2c5f.png))，并更新其战斗力。
第一名游骑兵的战斗力更新为 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b989fec42185029adec488aa738b78d9de953aef.png)，即 7。
第二名游骑兵的战斗力保持不变，即 7。
第三个游骑兵的战斗力更新为 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/3c7c9436158c0744fffbc90f5dcf6769683b82c2.png)，即 11。
第四个游骑兵的战斗力保持不变，即 11。
第五个游骑兵的战斗力更新为 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/842bb4d07e058ad06611d99fc15455f0a936cb03.png)，即 13。
现在，Jon 想知道执行上述操作 k 次后游骑兵战斗力的最大值和最小值。他希望你帮助完成这项任务。你能帮他吗？

input.ai: 第一行包含三个整数 n、k、x（1 ≤ n ≤ 105，0 ≤ k ≤ 105，0 ≤ x ≤ 103）——Jon 拥有的游骑兵数量、Jon 将执行该操作的次数以及 Jon 最喜欢的数字。
第二行包含 n 个整数，表示游骑兵的战斗力 a1、a2、...、an（0 ≤ ai ≤ 103）。

output.ai: 输出两个整数，表示执行 k 次操作后游骑兵的最大战斗力和最小战斗力。

legend.ai: 最近，Mike 一直忙于准备考试和参加比赛。现在，他打算通过在城市里观光来放松一下。

城市由 n 个编号从 1 到 n 的路口组成。Mike 从位于 1 号路口的家出发，沿着某个路口序列行走。从编号为 i 的路口走到编号为 j 的路口需要消耗 |i - j| 单位的能量。Mike 访问路口序列 p1 = 1，p2，...，pk 所消耗的总能量等于 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b366a738332ae698b6ad24b23eec6b08a25a2fe9.png) 单位。

当然，如果没有捷径，走路会很无聊。捷径是一种特殊的路径，允许 Mike 从一个路口走到另一个路口，只需消耗 1 单位的能量。Mike 的城市中恰好有 n 条捷径，其中第 i 条允许从路口 i 走到路口 a_i（i ≤ a_i ≤ a_{i+1}）（但不能反向行走），因此每个路口恰好有一条以其为起点的捷径。形式化地说，若 Mike 选择了一个序列 p_1 = 1，p_2，…，p_k，那么对于每个满足 1 ≤ i < k、p_{i+1} = a_{p_i} 且 a_{p_i} ≠ p_i 的 i，Mike 从路口 p_i 走到路口 p_{i+1} 时只需消耗 1 单位的能量，而不是 |p_i - p_{i+1}|。例如，如果 Mike 选择序列 p_1 = 1，p_2 = a_{p_1}，p_3 = a_{p_2}，…，p_k = a_{p_{k-1}}，那么他在这些路口之间行走总共恰好消耗 k - 1 单位的能量。
在开始冒险之前，Mike 请你找出从他家到每个路口所需的最少能量。形式化地说，对于每个 1 ≤ i ≤ n，Mike 想知道某个序列 p_1 = 1，p_2，…，p_k = i 所需的可能的最小总能量。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 200 000）——Mike 的城市中路口的数量。
第二行包含 n 个整数 a_1，a_2，…，a_n(i ≤ a_i ≤ n，![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a0e0e50a93f8d64ea6c764b778e4071020d4ef96.png)，描述 Mike 城市中的捷径；这些捷径允许仅消耗 1 单位的能量从路口 i 走到路口 a_i。请注意，捷径不允许反向行走(从 a_i 到 i)。

output.ai: 仅一行输出 n 个整数 m_1，m_2，…，m_n，其中 m_i 表示从路口 1 走到路口 i 所需的最少总能量。

problems.hint: You can't really operate many number of times.

legend: Sereja has two sequences a1, a2, ..., an and b1, b2, ..., bm, consisting of integers. One day Sereja got bored and he decided two play with them. The rules of the game was very simple. Sereja makes several moves, in one move he can perform one of the following actions:

Choose several (at least one) first elements of sequence a (non-empty prefix of a), choose several (at least one) first elements of sequence b (non-empty prefix of b); the element of sequence a with the maximum index among the chosen ones must be equal to the element of sequence b with the maximum index among the chosen ones; remove the chosen elements from the sequences.
Remove all elements of both sequences.

The first action is worth e energy units and adds one dollar to Sereja's electronic account. The second action is worth the number of energy units equal to the number of elements Sereja removed from the sequences before performing this action. After Sereja performed the second action, he gets all the money that he earned on his electronic account during the game.
Initially Sereja has s energy units and no money on his account. What maximum number of money can Sereja get? Note, the amount of Seraja's energy mustn't be negative at any time moment.
input: The first line contains integers n, m, s, e (1 ≤ n, m ≤ 105; 1 ≤ s ≤ 3·105; 103 ≤ e ≤ 104). The second line contains n integers a1, a2, ..., an (1 ≤ ai ≤ 105). The third line contains m integers b1, b2, ..., bm (1 ≤ bi ≤ 105).
output: Print a single integer — maximum number of money in dollars that Sereja can get.

legend.ai: Sereja 有两个由整数构成的序列 a1, a2, ..., an 和 b1, b2, ..., bm。一天，Sereja 感到无聊，于是决定用它们玩一玩。游戏规则非常简单。Sereja 进行若干次操作，每次操作可以执行以下动作之一：
选择序列 a 的若干个（至少一个）首元素（即 a 的一个非空前缀），再选择序列 b 的若干个（至少一个）首元素（即 b 的一个非空前缀）；所选序列 a 中下标最大的元素必须等于所选序列 b 中下标最大的元素；从两个序列中删除所选元素。
删除两个序列中的所有元素。
第一个操作需要消耗 e 个能量单位，并向 Sereja 的电子账户中增加 1 美元。第二个操作需要消耗的能量单位数，等于 Sereja 在执行该操作前从序列中删除的元素数量。执行第二个操作后，Sereja 将获得游戏期间在电子账户中赚取的所有钱。
初始时，Sereja 拥有 s 个能量单位，账户中没有钱。Sereja 最多能获得多少钱？注意，在任何时刻，Sereja 的能量都不能为负。

input.ai: 第一行包含整数 n, m, s, e（1 ≤ n, m ≤ 105；1 ≤ s ≤ 3·105；103 ≤ e ≤ 104）。第二行包含 n 个整数 a1, a2, ..., an（1 ≤ ai ≤ 105）。第三行包含 m 个整数 b1, b2, ..., bm（1 ≤ bi ≤ 105）。

output.ai: 输出一个整数——Sereja 最多能获得的美元数。

problems.hint: Use the first few steps to make sure the tank is in some of the positions.

legend: Slava plays his favorite game "Peace Lightning". Now he is flying a bomber on a very specific map.

Formally, map is a checkered field of size 1 × n, the cells of which are numbered from 1 to n, in each cell there can be one or several tanks. Slava doesn't know the number of tanks and their positions, because he flies very high, but he can drop a bomb in any cell. All tanks in this cell will be damaged.

If a tank takes damage for the first time, it instantly moves to one of the neighboring cells (a tank in the cell n can only move to the cell n - 1, a tank in the cell 1 can only move to the cell 2). If a tank takes damage for the second time, it's counted as destroyed and never moves again. The tanks move only when they are damaged for the first time, they do not move by themselves.
Help Slava to destroy all tanks using as few bombs as possible.
input: The first line contains a single integer n (2 ≤ n ≤ 100 000) — the size of the map.
output: In the first line print m — the minimum number of bombs Slava needs to destroy all tanks.
In the second line print m integers k1, k2, ..., km. The number ki means that the i-th bomb should be dropped at the cell ki.
If there are multiple answers, you can print any of them.

legend.ai: Slava 正在玩他最喜欢的游戏“Peace Lightning”。现在他正驾驶一架轰炸机飞行在一张非常特殊的地图上。
形式化地说，地图是一个大小为 1 × n 的棋盘格场地，格子从 1 到 n 编号，每个格子中可以有一个或多个坦克。Slava 不知道坦克的数量和它们的位置，因为他飞得很高，但他可以向任意格子投下炸弹。该格子中的所有坦克都会受到伤害。
如果一辆坦克第一次受到伤害，它会立刻移动到相邻的格子之一（在格子 n 的坦克只能移动到格子 n - 1，在格子 1 的坦克只能移动到格子 2）。如果一辆坦克第二次受到伤害，它就被视为被摧毁，并且不会再移动。坦克只会在第一次受到伤害时移动，它们不会自行移动。
帮助 Slava 使用尽可能少的炸弹摧毁所有坦克。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n（2 ≤ n ≤ 100 000）——地图的大小。

output.ai: 第一行输出 m——Slava 摧毁所有坦克所需的最少炸弹数。
第二行输出 m 个整数 k1, k2, ..., km。数字 ki 表示第 i 枚炸弹应投放在编号为 ki 的单元格中。
如果有多个答案，可以输出其中任意一个。

problems.hint: Find out the rules.

legend: Before the start of the football season in Berland a strange magic ritual is held. The most experienced magicians have to find a magic matrix of the size n × n (n is even number). Gods will never allow to start the championship without it. Matrix should contain integers from 0 to n - 1, main diagonal should contain only zeroes and matrix should be symmetric. Moreover, all numbers in each row should be different. Magicians are very tired of the thinking process, so they ask you to write a program to find such matrix.
input: The first line contains one integer n (2 ≤ n ≤ 1000), n is even.
output: Output n lines with n numbers each — the required matrix. Separate numbers with spaces. If there are several solutions, output any.

legend.ai: 在 Berland 的足球赛季开始前，会举行一种奇怪的魔法仪式。最有经验的魔法师必须找到一个大小为 n × n 的魔法矩阵（n 为偶数）。没有它，众神绝不会允许锦标赛开始。矩阵应包含从 0 到 n - 1 的整数，主对角线上只能有 0，并且矩阵应为对称矩阵。此外，每一行中的所有数字都必须各不相同。魔法师们已经对思考过程感到厌倦，因此他们请你编写一个程序来寻找这样的矩阵。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n（2 ≤ n ≤ 1000），n 为偶数。

output.ai: 输出 n 行，每行包含 n 个数字，即所需的矩阵。数字之间用空格分隔。如果有多个解，输出任意一个即可。

problems.hint: If you have a minimum spanning tree of the graph, how can you add an edge to the graph without changing the MST?

legend: Student Vladislav came to his programming exam completely unprepared as usual. He got a question about some strange algorithm on a graph — something that will definitely never be useful in real life. He asked a girl sitting next to him to lend him some cheat papers for this questions and found there the following definition:
The minimum spanning tree T of graph G is such a tree that it contains all the vertices of the original graph G, and the sum of the weights of its edges is the minimum possible among all such trees.

Vladislav drew a graph with n vertices and m edges containing no loops and multiple edges. He found one of its minimum spanning trees and then wrote for each edge its weight and whether it is included in the found tree or not. Unfortunately, the piece of paper where the graph was painted is gone and the teacher is getting very angry and demands to see the original graph. Help Vladislav come up with a graph so that the information about the minimum spanning tree remains correct.
input: The first line of the input contains two integers n and m (![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ff8ab63d2234d30c36551ae9737f0ccd16b68b4c.png)) — the number of vertices and the number of edges in the graph.

Each of the next m lines describes an edge of the graph and consists of two integers aj and bj (1 ≤ aj ≤ 109, bj = {0, 1}). The first of these numbers is the weight of the edge and the second number is equal to 1 if this edge was included in the minimum spanning tree found by Vladislav, or 0 if it was not.
It is guaranteed that exactly n - 1 number {bj} are equal to one and exactly m - n + 1 of them are equal to zero.
output: If Vladislav has made a mistake and such graph doesn't exist, print  - 1.

Otherwise print m lines. On the j-th line print a pair of vertices (uj, vj) (1 ≤ uj, vj ≤ n, uj ≠ vj), that should be connected by the j-th edge. The edges are numbered in the same order as in the input. The graph, determined by these edges, must be connected, contain no loops or multiple edges and its edges with bj = 1 must define the minimum spanning tree. In case there are multiple possible solutions, print any of them.

legend.ai: 学生 Vladislav 像往常一样，毫无准备地来参加编程考试。他遇到了一道关于图上某种奇怪算法的问题——这种东西在现实生活中肯定永远派不上用场。他向坐在旁边的女生借了一些关于这道题的作弊纸条，并在那里找到了如下定义：
图 G 的最小生成树 T 是这样一棵树：它包含原图 G 的所有顶点，并且在所有这样的树中，其边的权重之和是可能的最小值。
Vladislav 画了一个包含 n 个顶点和 m 条边的图，其中没有自环和重边。他找到了其中一棵最小生成树，然后为每条边记录了它的权值以及该边是否包含在找到的树中。不幸的是，绘制该图的纸张丢失了，老师非常生气，要求查看原图。请帮助 Vladislav 构造出一个图，使关于这棵最小生成树的信息仍然正确。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含两个整数 n 和 m(![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ff8ab63d2234d30c36551ae9737f0ccd16b68b4c.png))——图中的顶点数和边数。
接下来的 m 行中的每一行描述图中的一条边，由两个整数 aj 和 bj 组成（1 ≤ aj ≤ 109，bj = {0，1}）。其中第一个数是边的权值，第二个数在该边被包含在 Vladislav 找到的最小生成树中时等于 1，否则等于 0。
保证恰有 n - 1 个数 {bj} 等于 1，恰有 m - n + 1 个数等于 0。

output.ai: 如果 Vladislav 犯了错误，不存在这样的图，则输出  - 1。
否则输出 m 行。第 j 行输出一对顶点（uj，vj）（1 ≤ uj，vj ≤ n，uj ≠ vj），表示第 j 条边应连接的两个顶点。边的编号与输入中的顺序相同。由这些边确定的图必须是连通图，不包含自环或重边，并且其中 bj = 1 的边必须构成该图的一棵最小生成树。如果有多个可行解，输出任意一个即可。

problems.hint: Take notice of the leading zeros.

legend: International Abbreviation Olympiad takes place annually starting from 1989. Each year the competition receives an abbreviation of form IAO'y, where y stands for some number of consequent last digits of the current year. Organizers always pick an abbreviation with non-empty string y that has never been used before. Among all such valid abbreviations they choose the shortest one and announce it to be the abbreviation of this year's competition.

For example, the first three Olympiads (years 1989, 1990 and 1991, respectively) received the abbreviations IAO'9, IAO'0 and IAO'1, while the competition in 2015 received an abbreviation IAO'15, as IAO'5 has been already used in 1995.
You are given a list of abbreviations. For each of them determine the year it stands for.
input: The first line of the input contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 1000) — the number of abbreviations to process.
Then n lines follow, each containing a single abbreviation. It's guaranteed that each abbreviation contains at most nine digits.
output: For each abbreviation given in the input, find the year of the corresponding Olympiad.

output.ai: 对于输入中给出的每个缩写，找出相应奥林匹克竞赛的年份。

legend.ai: 国际缩写奥林匹克竞赛自 1989 年起每年举办一次。每年，竞赛都会获得一个形如 IAO'y 的缩写，其中 y 表示当年的若干个连续末位数字。组织者总是选择一个此前从未使用过且 y 非空的缩写。在所有符合条件的缩写中，他们选择最短的一个，并宣布其为当年竞赛的缩写。
例如，前三届奥林匹克竞赛（分别于 1989 年、1990 年和 1991 年举办）的缩写为 IAO'9、IAO'0 和 IAO'1，而 2015 年的竞赛使用了缩写 IAO'15，因为 IAO'5 已在 1995 年使用过。
给定一个缩写列表。对于每个缩写，确定它所代表的年份。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 1000）——需要处理的缩写数量。
接下来 n 行，每行包含一个缩写。保证每个缩写至多包含 9 位数字。

titleZh.ai: D. 国际奥林匹克竞赛

problems.hint: It's a binary tree. Just operate from the leaves.

legend: Two pirates Polycarpus and Vasily play a very interesting game. They have n chests with coins, the chests are numbered with integers from 1 to n. Chest number i has ai coins.

Polycarpus and Vasily move in turns. Polycarpus moves first. During a move a player is allowed to choose a positive integer x (2·x + 1 ≤ n) and take a coin from each chest with numbers x, 2·x, 2·x + 1. It may turn out that some chest has no coins, in this case the player doesn't take a coin from this chest. The game finishes when all chests get emptied.

Polycarpus isn't a greedy scrooge. Polycarpys is a lazy slob. So he wonders in what minimum number of moves the game can finish. Help Polycarpus, determine the minimum number of moves in which the game can finish. Note that Polycarpus counts not only his moves, he also counts Vasily's moves.
input: The first line contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 100) — the number of chests with coins. The second line contains a sequence of space-separated integers: a1, a2, ..., an (1 ≤ ai ≤ 1000), where ai is the number of coins in the chest number i at the beginning of the game.
output: Print a single integer — the minimum number of moves needed to finish the game. If no sequence of turns leads to finishing the game, print -1.
note: In the first test case there isn't a single move that can be made. That's why the players won't be able to empty the chests.
In the second sample there is only one possible move x = 1. This move should be repeated at least 3 times to empty the third chest.

output.ai: 输出一个整数——完成游戏所需的最少步数。如果不存在能够完成游戏的回合序列，则输出 -1。

note.ai: 在第一个测试用例中，没有任何一步可以执行。因此，玩家无法清空这些宝箱。
在第二个样例中，只有一个可能的操作 x = 1。为了清空第三个宝箱，至少需要重复该操作 3 次。

legend.ai: 两名海盗 Polycarpus 和 Vasily 进行一个非常有趣的游戏。他们有 n 个装有硬币的箱子，箱子的编号为 1 到 n。第 i 个箱子中有 ai 枚硬币。
Polycarpus 和 Vasily 轮流行动。Polycarpus 先手。每次行动时，玩家可以选择一个正整数 x（2·x + 1 ≤ n），并从编号为 x、2·x、2·x + 1 的每个箱子中取出一枚硬币。如果某个箱子中没有硬币，则玩家不会从该箱子中取走硬币。当所有箱子都被清空时，游戏结束。
Polycarpus 不是一个贪婪的吝啬鬼。Polycarpys 是个懒惰的懒汉。因此，他想知道游戏最少可以进行多少次行动后结束。请帮助 Polycarpus 确定游戏结束所需的最少行动次数。注意，Polycarpus 计算的不仅是自己的行动次数，也包括 Vasily 的行动次数。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 100）——装有硬币的箱子数量。第二行包含一行由空格分隔的整数：a1、a2、...、an（1 ≤ ai ≤ 1000），其中 ai 表示游戏开始时编号为 i 的箱子中的硬币数量。

problems.hint: It's allowed to solve the problem in $\mathcal{O}(n^2)$ .

legend: The Berland Kingdom is a set of n cities connected with each other with n - 1 railways. Each road connects exactly two different cities. The capital is located in city 1. For each city there is a way to get from there to the capital by rail.

In the i-th city there is a soldier division number i, each division is characterized by a number of ai. It represents the priority, the smaller the number, the higher the priority of this division. All values of ai are different.

One day the Berland King Berl Great declared a general mobilization, and for that, each division should arrive in the capital. Every day from every city except the capital a train departs. So there are exactly n - 1 departing trains each day. Each train moves toward the capital and finishes movement on the opposite endpoint of the railway on the next day. It has some finite capacity of cj, expressed in the maximum number of divisions, which this train can transport in one go. Each train moves in the direction of reducing the distance to the capital. So each train passes exactly one railway moving from a city to the neighboring (where it stops) toward the capital.

In the first place among the divisions that are in the city, division with the smallest number of ai get on the train, then with the next smallest and so on, until either the train is full or all the divisions are be loaded. So it is possible for a division to stay in a city for a several days.

The duration of train's progress from one city to another is always equal to 1 day. All divisions start moving at the same time and end up in the capital, from where they don't go anywhere else any more. Each division moves along a simple path from its city to the capital, regardless of how much time this journey will take.
Your goal is to find for each division, in how many days it will arrive to the capital of Berland. The countdown begins from day 0.
input: The first line contains the single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 5000). It is the number of cities in Berland. The second line contains n space-separated integers a1, a2, ..., an, where ai represents the priority of the division, located in the city number i. All numbers a1, a2, ..., an are different (1 ≤ ai ≤ 109). Then n - 1 lines contain the descriptions of the railway roads. Each description consists of three integers vj, uj, cj, where vj, uj are number of cities connected by the j-th rail, and cj stands for the maximum capacity of a train riding on this road (1 ≤ vj, uj ≤ n, vj ≠ uj, 1 ≤ cj ≤ n).
output: Print sequence t1, t2, ..., tn, where ti stands for the number of days it takes for the division of city i to arrive to the capital. Separate numbers with spaces.

legend.ai: 伯兰王国由 n 个城市组成，这些城市通过 n - 1 条铁路相互连接。每条道路恰好连接两个不同的城市。首都位于城市 1。对于每个城市，都存在一条可以通过铁路从该城市到达首都的路径。
第 i 个城市中有一支编号为 i 的军队，每支军队都有一个 a_i 值。它表示该军队的优先级，数字越小，优先级越高。所有 a_i 的值都互不相同。

一天，伯兰国王 Berl Great 宣布进行全国动员，要求每个师都前往首都。每天，除首都外的每个城市都会发出一列火车。因此，每天恰好有 n - 1 列火车出发。每列火车都朝首都方向行驶，并在第二天抵达铁路的另一端。每列火车都有一个有限的容量 cj，表示这列火车一次最多可以运送的师的数量。每列火车都会沿着到首都的距离减小的方向行驶。因此，每列火车恰好经过一段铁路，从一个城市驶向朝向首都的相邻城市，并在那里停下。
首先，城市中 ai 最小的师登上火车，然后是 ai 次小的师，依此类推，直到火车装满或所有师都已登车。因此，一个师可能会在某个城市停留数天。
火车从一个城市行驶到另一个城市所需的时间始终为 1 天。所有师同时开始移动，并最终到达首都；到达首都后，它们不再前往其他地方。每个师都沿着从其所在城市到首都的一条简单路径移动，无论这段旅程需要多长时间。
你的任务是求出每个师需要多少天才能到达伯兰的首都。倒计时从第 0 天开始。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 5000），表示伯兰的城市数量。第二行包含 n 个空格分隔的整数 a1, a2, ..., an，其中 ai 表示位于编号为 i 的城市中的师的优先级。a1, a2, ..., an 互不相同（1 ≤ ai ≤ 109）。接下来 n - 1 行描述铁路。每行包含三个整数 vj、uj、cj，其中 vj 和 uj 表示由第 j 条铁路连接的城市编号，cj 表示在这条铁路上行驶的火车的最大容量（1 ≤ vj, uj ≤ n，vj ≠ uj，1 ≤ cj ≤ n）。

output.ai: 输出序列 t1, t2, ..., tn，其中 ti 表示城市 i 中的师到达首都所需的天数。相邻数字之间用空格分隔。

problems.hint: A greedy approach. But think carefully.

legend: Oleg the client and Igor the analyst are good friends. However, sometimes they argue over little things. Recently, they started a new company, but they are having trouble finding a name for the company.

To settle this problem, they've decided to play a game. The company name will consist of n letters. Oleg and Igor each have a set of n letters (which might contain multiple copies of the same letter, the sets can be different). Initially, the company name is denoted by n question marks. Oleg and Igor takes turns to play the game, Oleg moves first. In each turn, a player can choose one of the letters c in his set and replace any of the question marks with c. Then, a copy of the letter c is removed from his set. The game ends when all the question marks has been replaced by some letter.
For example, suppose Oleg has the set of letters {i, o, i} and Igor has the set of letters {i, m, o}. One possible game is as follows :
Initially, the company name is ???.
Oleg replaces the second question mark with 'i'. The company name becomes ?i?. The set of letters Oleg have now is {i, o}.
Igor replaces the third question mark with 'o'. The company name becomes ?io. The set of letters Igor have now is {i, m}.
Finally, Oleg replaces the first question mark with 'o'. The company name becomes oio. The set of letters Oleg have now is {i}.
In the end, the company name is oio.

Oleg wants the company name to be as lexicographically small as possible while Igor wants the company name to be as lexicographically large as possible. What will be the company name if Oleg and Igor always play optimally?
A string s = s1s2...sm is called lexicographically smaller than a string t = t1t2...tm (where s ≠ t) if si < ti where i is the smallest index such that si ≠ ti. (so sj = tj for all j < i)
input: The first line of input contains a string s of length n (1 ≤ n ≤ 3·105). All characters of the string are lowercase English letters. This string denotes the set of letters Oleg has initially.
The second line of input contains a string t of length n. All characters of the string are lowercase English letters. This string denotes the set of letters Igor has initially.
output: The output should contain a string of n lowercase English letters, denoting the company name if Oleg and Igor plays optimally.
note: One way to play optimally in the first sample is as follows :
Initially, the company name is ???????.
Oleg replaces the first question mark with 'f'. The company name becomes f??????.
Igor replaces the second question mark with 'z'. The company name becomes fz?????.
Oleg replaces the third question mark with 'f'. The company name becomes fzf????.
Igor replaces the fourth question mark with 's'. The company name becomes fzfs???.
Oleg replaces the fifth question mark with 'i'. The company name becomes fzfsi??.
Igor replaces the sixth question mark with 'r'. The company name becomes fzfsir?.
Oleg replaces the seventh question mark with 'k'. The company name becomes fzfsirk.
For the second sample, no matter how they play, the company name will always be xxxxxx.

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含一个长度为 n 的字符串 s（1 ≤ n ≤ 3·105）。字符串中的所有字符都是小写英文字母。该字符串表示 Oleg 初始拥有的字母集合。
输入的第二行包含一个长度为 n 的字符串 t。字符串中的所有字符均为小写英文字母。该字符串表示 Igor 初始拥有的字母集合。

output.ai: 输出应包含一个由 n 个小写英文字母组成的字符串，表示在 Oleg 和 Igor 均采取最优策略时的公司名称。

note.ai: 第一组样例中，一种最优的玩法如下：
最初，公司名称为 ???????。
Oleg 将第一个问号替换为 'f'。公司名称变为 f??????。
Igor 将第二个问号替换为 'z'。公司名称变为 fz?????。
Oleg 将第三个问号替换为“f”。公司名称变为 fzf????。
Igor 将第四个问号替换为“s”。公司名称变为 fzfs???。
Oleg 将第五个问号替换为“i”。公司名称变为 fzfsi??。
Igor 将第六个问号替换为“r”。公司名称变为 fzfsir?。
Oleg 将第七个问号替换为“k”。公司名称变为 fzfsirk。
对于第二个样例，无论他们如何操作，公司名称始终为 xxxxxx。

legend.ai: 客户 Oleg 和分析师 Igor 是好朋友。然而，他们有时会为一些小事争论。最近，他们创办了一家新公司，但他们在为公司取名时遇到了困难。

为了解决这个问题，他们决定玩一个游戏。公司名称由 n 个字母组成。Oleg 和 Igor 各自有一个包含 n 个字母的集合（其中可能包含同一个字母的多个副本，两个集合也可能不同）。最初，公司名称表示为 n 个问号。Oleg 和 Igor 轮流进行游戏，由 Oleg 先手。在每一回合中，一名玩家可以从自己的集合中选择一个字母 c，并用 c 替换任意一个问号。然后，从他的集合中移除一个字母 c 的副本。当所有问号都被某个字母替换后，游戏结束。
例如，假设 Oleg 的字母集合为 {i, o, i}，Igor 的字母集合为 {i, m, o}。一种可能的游戏过程如下：
最初，公司名称为 ???。
Oleg 将第二个问号替换为 'i'。公司名称变为 ?i?。此时 Oleg 的字母集合为 {i, o}。
Igor 将第三个问号替换为“o”。公司名变为 ?io。Igor 现在拥有的字母集合为 {i, m}。
最后，Oleg 将第一个问号替换为“o”。公司名变为 oio。Oleg 现在拥有的字母集合为 {i}。
最终，公司名为 oio。
Oleg 希望公司名的字典序尽可能小，而 Igor 希望公司名的字典序尽可能大。如果 Oleg 和 Igor 始终采取最优策略，公司名会是什么？
如果 s ≠ t，且 i 是满足 si ≠ ti 的最小下标，并且 si < ti，则称字符串 s = s1s2...sm 的字典序小于字符串 t = t1t2...tm。（即对于所有 j < i，都有 sj = tj。）

problems.hint: Note that the sequence is not nice now.

legend: The life goes up and down, just like nice sequences. Sequence t1, t2, ..., tn is called nice if the following two conditions are satisfied:
ti < ti + 1 for each odd i < n;
ti > ti + 1 for each even i < n.
For example, sequences (2, 8), (1, 5, 1) and (2, 5, 1, 100, 99, 120) are nice, while (1, 1), (1, 2, 3) and (2, 5, 3, 2) are not.

Bear Limak has a sequence of positive integers t1, t2, ..., tn. This sequence is not nice now and Limak wants to fix it by a single swap. He is going to choose two indices i < j and swap elements ti and tj in order to get a nice sequence. Count the number of ways to do so. Two ways are considered different if indices of elements chosen for a swap are different.
input: The first line of the input contains one integer n (2 ≤ n ≤ 150 000) — the length of the sequence.
The second line contains n integers t1, t2, ..., tn (1 ≤ ti ≤ 150 000) — the initial sequence. It's guaranteed that the given sequence is not nice.
output: Print the number of ways to swap two elements exactly once in order to get a nice sequence.
note: In the first sample, there are two ways to get a nice sequence with one swap:
Swap t2 = 8 with t4 = 7.
Swap t1 = 2 with t5 = 7.
In the second sample, there is only one way — Limak should swap t1 = 200 with t4 = 50.

legend.ai: 生活有起有落，就像优美的序列一样。序列 t₁, t₂, ..., tₙ 被称为优美序列，当且仅当满足以下两个条件：
对于每个满足 i < n 的奇数 i，都有 tᵢ < tᵢ₊₁；
对于每个满足 i < n 的偶数 i，都有 tᵢ > tᵢ₊₁。
熊 Limak 有一个由正整数组成的序列 t₁, t₂, ..., tₙ。现在这个序列并不优美，Limak 想通过一次交换将其修正。他将选择两个下标 i < j，并交换元素 tᵢ 和 tⱼ，从而得到一个优美序列。请计算完成这一操作的方法数。如果交换时选择的元素下标不同，则认为是不同的方法。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含一个整数 n（2 ≤ n ≤ 150000）——序列的长度。
第二行包含 n 个整数 t1、t2、...、tn（1 ≤ ti ≤ 150000）——初始序列。保证给定序列不是优美序列。

output.ai: 输出恰好交换一次两个元素后得到优美序列的方案数。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，有两种通过一次交换得到优美序列的方法：
交换 t2 = 8 和 t4 = 7。
交换 t1 = 2 和 t5 = 7。
在第二个样例中，只有一种方案——Limak 应该将 t1 = 200 与 t4 = 50 交换。

problems.hint: How many diamonds should you move if you take out one of them?

legend: It is nighttime and Joe the Elusive got into the country's main bank's safe. The safe has n cells positioned in a row, each of them contains some amount of diamonds. Let's make the problem more comfortable to work with and mark the cells with positive numbers from 1 to n from the left to the right.
Unfortunately, Joe didn't switch the last security system off. On the plus side, he knows the way it works.

Every minute the security system calculates the total amount of diamonds for each two adjacent cells (for the cells between whose numbers difference equals 1). As a result of this check we get an n - 1 sums. If at least one of the sums differs from the corresponding sum received during the previous check, then the security system is triggered.

Joe can move the diamonds from one cell to another between the security system's checks. He manages to move them no more than m times between two checks. One of the three following operations is regarded as moving a diamond: moving a diamond from any cell to any other one, moving a diamond from any cell to Joe's pocket, moving a diamond from Joe's pocket to any cell. Initially Joe's pocket is empty, and it can carry an unlimited amount of diamonds. It is considered that before all Joe's actions the system performs at least one check.

In the morning the bank employees will come, which is why Joe has to leave the bank before that moment. Joe has only k minutes left before morning, and on each of these k minutes he can perform no more than m operations. All that remains in Joe's pocket, is considered his loot.
Calculate the largest amount of diamonds Joe can carry with him. Don't forget that the security system shouldn't be triggered (even after Joe leaves the bank) and Joe should leave before morning.
input: The first line contains integers n, m and k (1 ≤ n ≤ 104, 1 ≤ m, k ≤ 109). The next line contains n numbers. The i-th number is equal to the amount of diamonds in the i-th cell — it is an integer from 0 to 105.
output: Print a single number — the maximum number of diamonds Joe can steal.
note: In the second sample Joe can act like this:
The diamonds' initial positions are 4 1 3.
During the first period of time Joe moves a diamond from the 1-th cell to the 2-th one and a diamond from the 3-th cell to his pocket.
By the end of the first period the diamonds' positions are 3 2 2. The check finds no difference and the security system doesn't go off.
During the second period Joe moves a diamond from the 3-rd cell to the 2-nd one and puts a diamond from the 1-st cell to his pocket.
By the end of the second period the diamonds' positions are 2 3 1. The check finds no difference again and the security system doesn't go off.
Now Joe leaves with 2 diamonds in his pocket.

legend.ai: 现在是夜晚，Joe the Elusive 潜入了这个国家的中央银行的金库。金库中有 n 个沿一行排列的格子，每个格子里都有一定数量的钻石。为了便于描述，我们从左到右用 1 到 n 的正整数给这些格子编号。
不幸的是，Joe 没有关闭最后一道安保系统。好在，他知道该系统的工作方式。
安保系统每分钟都会计算每一对相邻格子中的钻石总数（即两个格子的编号之差为 1）。每次检查会得到 n - 1 个和。如果这些和中至少有一个与上一次检查得到的对应总和不同，安保系统就会被触发。
Joe 可以在两次安保系统检查之间移动钻石。在两次检查之间，他至多能移动 m 次。以下三种操作中的任意一种都算作移动一颗钻石：将一颗钻石从任意格子移动到另一个任意格子，将一颗钻石从任意格子移动到 Joe 的口袋中，或将一颗钻石从 Joe 的口袋移动到任意格子中。最初 Joe 的口袋是空的，并且可以容纳无限数量的钻石。规定在 Joe 进行所有操作之前，系统至少会进行一次检查。
早上银行员工会来，因此 Joe 必须在那之前离开银行。距离早晨只剩下 k 分钟，在这 k 分钟中的每一分钟，他最多可以进行 m 次操作。Joe 口袋里剩下的所有东西都算作他的战利品。
计算 Joe 能带走的钻石数量的最大值。别忘了，安全系统不应被触发（即使在 Joe 离开银行之后也是如此），并且 Joe 必须在早晨到来之前离开。

input.ai: 第一行包含整数 n、m 和 k（1 ≤ n ≤ 10^4，1 ≤ m，k ≤ 10^9）。下一行包含 n 个数。第 i 个数表示第 i 个单元格中的钻石数量，是一个范围在 0 到 10^5 之间的整数。

output.ai: 输出一个数——Joe 能偷走的钻石数量的最大值。

note.ai: 在第二个样例中，Joe 可以进行如下操作：
钻石的初始位置为 4 1 3。
在第一个时间段内，Joe 将一颗钻石从第 1 个格子移到第 2 个格子，并将第 3 个格子中的一颗钻石放进口袋。
第一个时间段结束时，钻石的位置为 3 2 2。检查没有发现任何差异，安保系统没有触发。
在第二个时间段内，Joe 将一颗钻石从第 3 个格子移到第 2 个格子，并将第 1 个格子中的一颗钻石放进口袋。
第二个时间段结束时，钻石的位置为 2 3 1。检查再次没有发现任何差异，安保系统没有触发。
现在 Joe 带着口袋里的 2 颗钻石离开了。

problems.hint: If $v$ is the son of $u$ with the subtree of the largest size, the centroid of the subtree of $u$ is also an ancestor of the centroid of the subtree of $v$ .

legend: After the piece of a devilish mirror hit the Kay's eye, he is no longer interested in the beauty of the roses. Now he likes to watch snowflakes.

Once upon a time, he found a huge snowflake that has a form of the tree (connected acyclic graph) consisting of n nodes. The root of tree has index 1. Kay is very interested in the structure of this tree.
After doing some research he formed q queries he is interested in. The i-th query asks to find a centroid of the subtree of the node vi. Your goal is to answer all queries.

Subtree of a node is a part of tree consisting of this node and all it's descendants (direct or not). In other words, subtree of node v is formed by nodes u, such that node v is present on the path from u to root.

Centroid of a tree (or a subtree) is a node, such that if we erase it from the tree, the maximum size of the connected component will be at least two times smaller than the size of the initial tree (or a subtree).
input: The first line of the input contains two integers n and q (2 ≤ n ≤ 300 000, 1 ≤ q ≤ 300 000) — the size of the initial tree and the number of queries respectively.
The second line contains n - 1 integer p2, p3, ..., pn (1 ≤ pi ≤ n) — the indices of the parents of the nodes from 2 to n. Node 1 is a root of the tree. It's guaranteed that pi define a correct tree.
Each of the following q lines contain a single integer vi (1 ≤ vi ≤ n) — the index of the node, that define the subtree, for which we want to find a centroid.
output: For each query print the index of a centroid of the corresponding subtree. If there are many suitable nodes, print any of them. It's guaranteed, that each subtree has at least one centroid.
note: ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b6d1f35b3db16b3f662d8b452206abbdeb5d0aa4.png)
The first query asks for a centroid of the whole tree — this is node 3. If we delete node 3 the tree will split in four components, two of size 1 and two of size 2.
The subtree of the second node consists of this node only, so the answer is 2.
Node 3 is centroid of its own subtree.
The centroids of the subtree of the node 5 are nodes 5 and 6 — both answers are considered correct.

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含两个整数 n 和 q（2 ≤ n ≤ 300000，1 ≤ q ≤ 300000）——分别表示初始树的节点数和查询次数。
第二行包含 n-1 个整数 p2，p3，...，pn（1 ≤ pi ≤ n）——编号从 2 到 n 的节点的父节点编号。节点 1 是树的根。保证 pi 构成一棵正确的树。
接下来的 q 行中，每行包含一个整数 vi（1 ≤ vi ≤ n）——定义子树的节点编号，我们需要找到该子树的重心。

output.ai: 对于每个查询，输出相应子树的一个重心的编号。如果有多个符合条件的节点，输出其中任意一个即可。保证每棵子树至少有一个重心。

note.ai: ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b6d1f35b3db16b3f662d8b452206abbdeb5d0aa4.png)
第一个查询询问整棵树的重心——即节点 3。删除节点 3 后，树会分裂成四个连通分量，其中两个大小为 1，另外两个大小为 2。
第二个节点的子树仅由该节点自身组成，因此答案是 2。
节点 3 是其自身子树的重心。
节点 5 的子树的重心是节点 5 和节点 6——两个答案都被认为是正确的。

legend.ai: 一块恶魔镜子的碎片击中了 Kay 的眼睛后，他不再对玫瑰的美丽感兴趣。现在，他喜欢观察雪花。
从前，他发现了一片巨大的雪花，其形状是一棵由 n 个节点组成的树（连通无环图）。树的根节点编号为 1。Kay 对这棵树的结构非常感兴趣。
经过一番研究后，他提出了 q 个感兴趣的查询。第 i 个查询要求找到节点 vi 的子树的一个重心。你的任务是回答所有查询。
一个节点的子树是由该节点及其所有后代（无论直接还是间接）组成的树的一部分。换句话说，节点 v 的子树由所有满足以下条件的节点 u 构成：从 u 到根的路径上包含节点 v。
树（或子树）的重心是这样一个节点：如果将其从树中删除，所得连通分量中的最大大小将不超过初始树（或子树）大小的一半。

problems.hint: Don't use any kind of data structures..

legend: One day Squidward, Spongebob and Patrick decided to go to the beach. Unfortunately, the weather was bad, so the friends were unable to ride waves. However, they decided to spent their time building sand castles.

At the end of the day there were n castles built by friends. Castles are numbered from 1 to n, and the height of the i-th castle is equal to hi. When friends were about to leave, Squidward noticed, that castles are not ordered by their height, and this looks ugly. Now friends are going to reorder the castles in a way to obtain that condition hi ≤ hi + 1 holds for all i from 1 to n - 1.
Squidward suggested the following process of sorting castles:
Castles are split into blocks — groups of consecutive castles. Therefore the block from i to j will include castles i, i + 1, ..., j. A block may consist of a single castle.
The partitioning is chosen in such a way that every castle is a part of exactly one block.
Each block is sorted independently from other blocks, that is the sequence hi, hi + 1, ..., hj becomes sorted.
The partitioning should satisfy the condition that after each block is sorted, the sequence hi becomes sorted too. This may always be achieved by saying that the whole sequence is a single block.

Even Patrick understands that increasing the number of blocks in partitioning will ease the sorting process. Now friends ask you to count the maximum possible number of blocks in a partitioning that satisfies all the above requirements.
input: The first line of the input contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 100 000) — the number of castles Spongebob, Patrick and Squidward made from sand during the day.
The next line contains n integers hi (1 ≤ hi ≤ 109). The i-th of these integers corresponds to the height of the i-th castle.
output: Print the maximum possible number of blocks in a valid partitioning.
note: In the first sample the partitioning looks like that: [1][2][3].
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/982507039f7537a2dfca523fb24428b17f8bbe4c.png)
In the second sample the partitioning is: [2, 1][3, 2]

legend.ai: 一天，Squidward、Spongebob 和 Patrick 决定去海滩。不幸的是，天气很糟糕，所以朋友们无法冲浪。然而，他们决定把时间花在堆沙堡上。
一天结束时，朋友们一共建造了 n 座城堡。城堡的编号从 1 到 n，第 i 座城堡的高度等于 h_i。朋友们正要离开时，Squidward 注意到城堡的高度没有按顺序排列，这看起来很难看。现在，朋友们打算重新排列城堡，使得对于 i 从 1 到 n−1 的所有值，都满足 h_i ≤ h_{i+1}。
Squidward 提出了以下对城堡进行排序的过程：
城堡被分成若干块——每块由连续的城堡组成。因此，从 i 到 j 的块将包含城堡 i、i+1、...、j。一块可以只由一个城堡组成。
划分的方式应保证每座城堡恰好属于一个块。
每个块都独立于其他块进行排序，也就是说，序列 h_i、h_{i+1}、...、h_j 会变为有序序列。
划分应满足这样的条件：在每个块排序后，序列 h 也变得有序。这总是可以通过将整个序列视为一个块来实现。
甚至 Patrick 也明白，增加划分中的块数会使排序过程更加容易。现在，朋友们请你计算满足上述所有要求的划分中，块数的最大可能值。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 100000）——Spongebob、Patrick 和 Squidward 白天用沙子堆成的城堡数量。
下一行包含 n 个整数 h_i（1 ≤ h_i ≤ 10^9）。其中第 i 个整数表示第 i 座城堡的高度。

output.ai: 输出合法划分中块数的最大可能值。

legend: You have a grid with n rows and n columns. Each cell is either empty (denoted by '.') or blocked (denoted by 'X').

Two empty cells are directly connected if they share a side. Two cells (r1, c1) (located in the row r1 and column c1) and (r2, c2) are connected if there exists a sequence of empty cells that starts with (r1, c1), finishes with (r2, c2), and any two consecutive cells in this sequence are directly connected. A connected component is a set of empty cells such that any two cells in the component are connected, and there is no cell in this set that is connected to some cell not in this set.

Your friend Limak is a big grizzly bear. He is able to destroy any obstacles in some range. More precisely, you can choose a square of size k × k in the grid and Limak will transform all blocked cells there to empty ones. However, you can ask Limak to help only once.
The chosen square must be completely inside the grid. It's possible that Limak won't change anything because all cells are empty anyway.
You like big connected components. After Limak helps you, what is the maximum possible size of the biggest connected component in the grid?
input: The first line of the input contains two integers n and k (1 ≤ k ≤ n ≤ 500) — the size of the grid and Limak's range, respectively.
Each of the next n lines contains a string with n characters, denoting the i-th row of the grid. Each character is '.' or 'X', denoting an empty cell or a blocked one, respectively.
output: Print the maximum possible size (the number of cells) of the biggest connected component, after using Limak's help.
note: In the first sample, you can choose a square of size 2 × 2. It's optimal to choose a square in the red frame on the left drawing below. Then, you will get a connected component with 10 cells, marked blue in the right drawing.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/bc3be3998e7988930c7ec84634e6eadca7b7b172.png)

legend.ai: 给定一个有 n 行 n 列的网格。每个格子要么为空（用 '.' 表示），要么被阻挡（用 'X' 表示）。
如果两个空格子共用一条边，则它们直接相连。若存在一个由空格子组成的序列，以 (r1, c1)（位于第 r1 行、第 c1 列）开头，以 (r2, c2) 结尾，且序列中任意两个相邻格子都直接相连，则称格子 (r1, c1) 和 (r2, c2) 相连。连通块是一个空格子的集合，其中任意两个格子都相连，并且集合中不存在与集合外某个格子相连的格子。
你的朋友 Limak 是一只大灰熊。他能够摧毁某个范围内的所有障碍物。具体来说，你可以在网格中选择一个大小为 k × k 的正方形，Limak 会将其中所有被阻挡的格子变为空格子。不过，你只能求助 Limak 一次。
所选正方形必须完全位于网格内。即使所有格子本来就是空的，Limak 也可能什么都不改变。
你喜欢大的连通块。Limak 帮助你之后，网格中最大的连通块的大小最大能是多少？

接下来的 n 行中，每行包含一个长度为 n 的字符串，表示网格的第 i 行。每个字符都是“.”或“X”，分别表示空单元格或被阻塞的单元格。

output.ai: 输出在使用 Limak 的帮助后，最大的连通块的最大可能大小（单元格数量）。

legend: You are given a matrix consisting of digits zero and one, its size is n × m. You are allowed to rearrange its rows. What is the maximum area of the submatrix that only consists of ones and can be obtained in the given problem by the described operations?

Let's assume that the rows of matrix a are numbered from 1 to n from top to bottom and the columns are numbered from 1 to m from left to right. A matrix cell on the intersection of the i-th row and the j-th column can be represented as (i, j). Formally, a submatrix of matrix a is a group of four integers d, u, l, r (1 ≤ d ≤ u ≤ n; 1 ≤ l ≤ r ≤ m). We will assume that the submatrix contains cells (i, j) (d ≤ i ≤ u; l ≤ j ≤ r). The area of the submatrix is the number of cells it contains.
input: The first line contains two integers n and m (1 ≤ n, m ≤ 5000). Next n lines contain m characters each — matrix a. Matrix a only contains characters: "0" and "1". Note that the elements of the matrix follow without any spaces in the lines.
output: Print a single integer — the area of the maximum obtained submatrix. If we cannot obtain a matrix of numbers one, print 0.

legend.ai: 给定一个由数字 0 和 1 组成的 n × m 矩阵。你可以重新排列矩阵的行。通过题目所述的操作，能够得到的仅由 1 组成的子矩阵的最大面积是多少？

假设矩阵 a 的行从上到下编号为 1 到 n，列从左到右编号为 1 到 m。第 i 行与第 j 列交叉处的矩阵单元格可以表示为 (i, j)。形式化地说，矩阵 a 的一个子矩阵由四个整数 d、u、l、r 组成（1 ≤ d ≤ u ≤ n；1 ≤ l ≤ r ≤ m）。我们规定该子矩阵包含所有满足 (d ≤ i ≤ u；l ≤ j ≤ r) 的单元格 (i, j)。子矩阵的面积就是它所包含的单元格数量。

input.ai: 第一行包含两个整数 n 和 m（1 ≤ n，m ≤ 5000）。接下来的 n 行每行包含 m 个字符，即矩阵 a。矩阵 a 只包含字符“0”和“1”。注意，矩阵的元素在每行中连续给出，字符之间没有空格。

output.ai: 输出一个整数，即所能得到的最大子矩阵的面积。如果无法得到一个全部由 1 组成的矩阵，则输出 0。

legend: Each employee of the "Blake Techologies" company uses a special messaging app "Blake Messenger". All the stuff likes this app and uses it constantly. However, some important futures are missing. For example, many users want to be able to search through the message history. It was already announced that the new feature will appear in the nearest update, when developers faced some troubles that only you may help them to solve.

All the messages are represented as a strings consisting of only lowercase English letters. In order to reduce the network load strings are represented in the special compressed form. Compression algorithm works as follows: string is represented as a concatenation of n blocks, each block containing only equal characters. One block may be described as a pair (li, ci), where li is the length of the i-th block and ci is the corresponding letter. Thus, the string s may be written as the sequence of pairs ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/68dc87dc42fc8b5c9e100569fb0db6d0de6f0e20.png).

Your task is to write the program, that given two compressed string t and s finds all occurrences of s in t. Developers know that there may be many such occurrences, so they only ask you to find the number of them. Note that p is the starting position of some occurrence of s in t if and only if tptp + 1...tp + |s| - 1 = s, where ti is the i-th character of string t.

Note that the way to represent the string in compressed form may not be unique. For example string "aaaa" may be given as ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/939322623808439da25353cdf333633a2bd459d1.png), ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/1d6356300e6949063b637098187983ab4a94bdd0.png), ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/fe55bc3160319d1cb679fcb8d1a2d90686d4db05.png)...
input: The first line of the input contains two integers n and m (1 ≤ n, m ≤ 200 000) — the number of blocks in the strings t and s, respectively.
The second line contains the descriptions of n parts of string t in the format "li-ci" (1 ≤ li ≤ 1 000 000) — the length of the i-th part and the corresponding lowercase English letter.
The second line contains the descriptions of m parts of string s in the format "li-ci" (1 ≤ li ≤ 1 000 000) — the length of the i-th part and the corresponding lowercase English letter.
output: Print a single integer — the number of occurrences of s in t.
note: In the first sample, t = "aaabbccccaaacc", and string s = "aabbc". The only occurrence of string s in string t starts at position p = 2.
In the second sample, t = "aaabbbbbbaaaaaaacccceeeeeeeeaa", and s = "aaa". The occurrences of s in t start at positions p = 1, p = 10, p = 11, p = 12, p = 13 and p = 14.

legend.ai: “Blake Techologies”公司的每位员工都使用一款名为“Blake Messenger”的特殊即时通信应用。所有员工都喜欢这款应用，并且一直在使用它。然而，这款应用还缺少一些重要功能。例如，许多用户希望能够搜索消息历史记录。开发者已经宣布，新功能将在最近的一次更新中推出，但他们遇到了一些问题，只有你能帮助他们解决。

所有消息都表示为仅由小写英文字母组成的字符串。为了减少网络负载，字符串采用特殊的压缩形式表示。压缩算法如下：字符串表示为 n 个块的拼接，每个块中只包含相同的字符。一个块可以表示为一对 (li, ci)，其中 li 是第 i 个块的长度，ci 是对应的字母。因此，字符串 s 可以写成如下的序列 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/68dc87dc42fc8b5c9e100569fb0db6d0de6f0e20.png)。
你的任务是编写一个程序，给定两个压缩字符串 t 和 s，找出 s 在 t 中的所有出现位置。开发者知道这样的出现可能有很多，因此只要求你求出它们的数量。注意，当且仅当 tptp + 1...tp + |s| - 1 = s 时，p 才是 s 在 t 中某次出现的起始位置，其中 ti 是字符串 t 的第 i 个字符。

注意，同一个字符串的压缩表示方式可能不唯一。例如，字符串 "aaaa" 可以表示为 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/939322623808439da25353cdf333633a2bd459d1.png)、![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/1d6356300e6949063b637098187983ab4a94bdd0.png)、![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/fe55bc3160319d1cb679fcb8d1a2d90686d4db05.png)……

output.ai: 输出一个整数——s 在 t 中出现的次数。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，t = "aaabbccccaaacc"，字符串 s = "aabbc"。字符串 s 在字符串 t 中唯一一次出现的起始位置为 p = 2。
在第二个样例中，t = "aaabbbbbbaaaaaaacccceeeeeeeeaa"，s = "aaa"。s 在 t 中的出现位置为 p = 1、p = 10、p = 11、p = 12、p = 13 和 p = 14。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含两个整数 n 和 m（1 ≤ n，m ≤ 200 000），分别表示字符串 t 和 s 中块的数量。
第二行包含字符串 t 的 n 个部分的描述，格式为 "li-ci"（1 ≤ li ≤ 1 000 000），其中 li 是第 i 个部分的长度，ci 是对应的小写英文字母。
第二行包含字符串 s 的 m 个部分的描述，格式为 "li-ci"（1 ≤ li ≤ 1 000 000），其中 li 是第 i 个部分的长度，ci 是对应的小写英文字母。

legend: Nanami is an expert at playing games. This day, Nanami's good friend Hajime invited her to watch a game of baseball. Unwilling as she was, she followed him to the stadium. But Nanami had no interest in the game, so she looked around to see if there was something that might interest her. That's when she saw the digital board at one end of the stadium.

The digital board is n pixels in height and m pixels in width, every pixel is either light or dark. The pixels are described by its coordinate. The j-th pixel of the i-th line is pixel (i, j). The board displays messages by switching a combination of pixels to light, and the rest to dark. Nanami notices that the state of the pixels on the board changes from time to time. At certain times, certain pixels on the board may switch from light to dark, or from dark to light.

Nanami wonders, what is the area of the biggest light block such that a specific pixel is on its side. A light block is a sub-rectangle of the board, in which all pixels are light. Pixel (i, j) belongs to a side of sub-rectangle with (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) as its upper-left and lower-right vertex if and only if it satisfies the logical condition:
Nanami has all the history of changing pixels, also she has some questions of the described type, can you answer them?
input: The first line contains three space-separated integers n, m and q (1 ≤ n, m, q ≤ 1000) — the height and width of the digital board, and the number of operations.
Then follow n lines, each line containing m space-separated integers. The j-th integer of the i-th line is ai, j — the initial state of pixel (i, j).
If ai, j = 0, pixel (i, j) is initially dark.
If ai, j = 1, pixel (i, j) is initially light.
Then follow q lines, each line containing three space-separated integers op, x, and y (1 ≤ op ≤ 2; 1 ≤ x ≤ n; 1 ≤ y ≤ m), describing an operation.
If op = 1, the pixel at (x, y) changes its state (from light to dark or from dark to light).
If op = 2, Nanami queries the biggest light block with pixel (x, y) on its side.
output: For each query, print a single line containing one integer — the answer to Nanami's query.
note: Consider the first sample.
The first query specifies pixel (2, 2), which is dark itself, so there are no valid light blocks, thus the answer is 0.
The second query specifies pixel (1, 2). The biggest light block is the block with (1, 2) as its upper-left vertex and (1, 3) as its lower-right vertex.
The last query specifies pixel (2, 2), which became light in the third operation. The biggest light block is the block with (1, 2) as its upper-left vertex and (3, 3) as its lower-right vertex.

legend.ai: Nanami 是一位游戏高手。一天，Nanami 的好朋友 Hajime 邀请她去观看一场棒球比赛。尽管她并不情愿，她还是跟着他来到了体育场。但 Nanami 对比赛毫无兴趣，于是她环顾四周，看看是否有什么东西能引起她的兴趣。就在这时，她看到了体育场一端的数字板。
数字板的高度为 n 个像素，宽度为 m 个像素，每个像素要么是亮的，要么是暗的。像素由其坐标描述。第 i 行的第 j 个像素是像素 (i, j)。数字板通过将一部分像素切换为亮、其余像素切换为暗来显示消息。Nanami 注意到，数字板上像素的状态会随时间变化。在某些时刻，板上的某些像素可能会从亮变暗，或从暗变亮。
Nanami 想知道，包含某个指定像素且该像素位于其边界上的最大亮色块的面积是多少。亮色块是数字板的一个子矩形，其中所有像素都是亮的。当且仅当像素 (i, j) 满足以下逻辑条件时，它属于左上顶点为 (x1, y1)、右下顶点为 (x2, y2) 的子矩形的一条边：
Nanami 拥有所有像素变化的历史记录，她还有一些关于上述类型的问题，你能回答吗？

input.ai: 第一行包含三个以空格分隔的整数 n、m 和 q（1 ≤ n, m, q ≤ 1000）——数字面板的高度和宽度，以及操作次数。
接下来有 n 行，每行包含 m 个以空格分隔的整数。第 i 行的第 j 个整数是 aᵢ, ⱼ，表示像素 (i, j) 的初始状态。
如果 aᵢ, ⱼ = 0，则像素 (i, j) 初始为暗。
如果 aᵢ, ⱼ = 1，则像素 (i, j) 初始为亮。
接下来有 q 行，每行包含三个以空格分隔的整数 op、x 和 y（1 ≤ op ≤ 2；1 ≤ x ≤ n；1 ≤ y ≤ m），描述一次操作。
如果 op = 1，坐标为 (x, y) 的像素会改变其状态（由亮变暗或由暗变亮）。
如果 op = 2，Nanami 会查询像素 (x, y) 位于其边上的最大亮色块。

output.ai: 对于每次查询，输出一行，其中包含一个整数，即 Nanami 查询的答案。

note.ai: 考虑第一个样例。
第一次查询指定了像素 (2, 2)，该像素本身是暗的，因此不存在合法的亮色块，答案为 0。
