legend: PMP is getting a warrior. He is practicing a lot, but the results are not acceptable yet. This time instead of programming contests, he decided to compete in a car racing to increase the spirit of victory. He decides to choose a competition that also exhibits algorithmic features.

AlgoRace is a special league of car racing where different teams compete in a country of n cities. Cities are numbered 1 through n. Every two distinct cities in the country are connected with one bidirectional road. Each competing team should introduce one driver and a set of cars.

The competition is held in r rounds. In i-th round, drivers will start at city si and finish at city ti. Drivers are allowed to change their cars at most ki times. Changing cars can take place in any city in no time. One car can be used multiple times in one round, but total number of changes should not exceed ki. Drivers can freely choose their path to destination.
PMP has prepared m type of purpose-built cars. Beside for PMP’s driving skills, depending on properties of the car and the road, a car traverses each road in each direction in different times.

PMP Warriors wants to devise best strategies of choosing car and roads in each round to maximize the chance of winning the cup. For each round they want to find the minimum time required to finish it.
input: The first line contains three space-separated integers n, m, r (2 ≤ n ≤ 60, 1 ≤ m ≤ 60, 1 ≤ r ≤ 105) — the number of cities, the number of different types of cars and the number of rounds in the competition, correspondingly.

Next m sets of n × n matrices of integers between 0 to 106 (inclusive) will follow — describing the time one car requires to traverse different roads. The k-th integer in j-th line of the i-th set is the time that i-th car requires to traverse the road from j-th city to k-th city. These matrices are not necessarily symmetric, but their diagonal is always zero.

Next r lines contain description of the rounds. The i-th of these lines contains space-separated integers si, ti, ki (1 ≤ si, ti ≤ n, si ≠ ti, 0 ≤ ki ≤ 1000) — the number of starting city, finishing city and the number of possible car changes in i-th round, correspondingly.
output: For each round you should print the minimum required time to complete the round in a single line.
note: In the first sample, in all rounds PMP goes from city #1 to city #2, then city #3 and finally city #4. But the sequences of types of the cars he uses are (1, 2, 1) in the first round and (1, 2, 2) in the second round. In the third round, although he can change his car three times, he uses the same strategy as the first round which only needs two car changes.

legend.ai: PMP 正在成为一名勇士。他进行了大量训练，但目前取得的成绩仍不尽如人意。这一次，他没有参加编程竞赛，而是决定参加赛车比赛，以增强胜利的信念。他决定选择一项同样具有算法特色的比赛。
AlgoRace 是一个特殊的赛车联赛，不同队伍在一个拥有 n 座城市的国家中展开竞争。城市编号为 1 至 n。该国任意两个不同的城市之间都有一条双向道路相连。每支参赛队伍都应派出一名车手和一组汽车。
比赛分为 r 轮。在第 i 轮中，车手从城市 \(s_i\) 出发，在城市 \(t_i\) 结束。车手最多可以换车 \(k_i\) 次。换车可以在任意城市瞬间完成。一辆汽车在一轮比赛中可以被使用多次，但换车总次数不能超过 \(k_i\)。车手可以自由选择前往终点的路径。
PMP 准备了 m 种特制汽车。除 PMP 的驾驶技术外，根据汽车和道路的属性，汽车沿每条道路的不同方向行驶所需的时间也各不相同。
PMP Warriors 希望制定在每一轮中选择汽车和道路的最佳策略，以最大化赢得奖杯的概率。对于每一轮，他们希望求出完成该轮所需的最短时间。

input.ai: 第一行包含三个用空格分隔的整数 n、m、r（2 ≤ n ≤ 60，1 ≤ m ≤ 60，1 ≤ r ≤ 10^5），分别表示城市数量、不同类型汽车的数量以及比赛的轮数。
接下来给出 m 组 n × n 的整数矩阵，矩阵中的整数均在 0 到 10^6（含）之间——描述一辆汽车通过不同道路所需的时间。第 i 组矩阵第 j 行中的第 k 个整数，表示第 i 种汽车从第 j 个城市驶往第 k 个城市所需的时间。这些矩阵不一定对称，但其对角线上的元素始终为 0。
接下来 r 行描述各轮比赛。第 i 行包含三个用空格分隔的整数 si、ti、ki（1 ≤ si, ti ≤ n，si ≠ ti，0 ≤ ki ≤ 1000），分别表示第 i 轮的起始城市、终点城市以及允许更换汽车的次数。

output.ai: 对于每一轮，在单独一行中输出完成该轮所需的最短时间。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，每一轮 PMP 都从城市 #1 前往城市 #2，然后前往城市 #3，最后到达城市 #4。但他在第一轮和第二轮中使用的汽车类型序列分别为 (1, 2, 1) 和 (1, 2, 2)。在第三轮中，尽管他可以更换汽车三次，但他采用了与第一轮相同的策略，而该策略只需要更换两次汽车。

problems.hint: Distribute the numbers evenly.

legend: Valera has 2·n cubes, each cube contains an integer from 10 to 99. He arbitrarily chooses n cubes and puts them in the first heap. The remaining cubes form the second heap.

Valera decided to play with cubes. During the game he takes a cube from the first heap and writes down the number it has. Then he takes a cube from the second heap and write out its two digits near two digits he had written (to the right of them). In the end he obtained a single fourdigit integer — the first two digits of it is written on the cube from the first heap, and the second two digits of it is written on the second cube from the second heap.

Valera knows arithmetic very well. So, he can easily count the number of distinct fourdigit numbers he can get in the game. The other question is: how to split cubes into two heaps so that this number (the number of distinct fourdigit integers Valera can get) will be as large as possible?
input: The first line contains integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 100). The second line contains 2·n space-separated integers ai (10 ≤ ai ≤ 99), denoting the numbers on the cubes.
output: In the first line print a single number — the maximum possible number of distinct four-digit numbers Valera can obtain. In the second line print 2·n numbers bi (1 ≤ bi ≤ 2). The numbers mean: the i-th cube belongs to the bi-th heap in your division.
If there are multiple optimal ways to split the cubes into the heaps, print any of them.
note: In the first test case Valera can put the first cube in the first heap, and second cube — in second heap. In this case he obtain number 1099. If he put the second cube in the first heap, and the first cube in the second heap, then he can obtain number 9910. In both cases the maximum number of distinct integers is equal to one.
In the second test case Valera can obtain numbers 1313, 1345, 2413, 2445. Note, that if he put the first and the third cubes in the first heap, he can obtain only two numbers 1324 and 1345.

legend.ai: Valera 有 2·n 个立方体，每个立方体上都写着一个 10 到 99 之间的整数。他任意选择 n 个立方体放入第一个堆中，其余立方体组成第二个堆。
Valera 决定玩立方体游戏。在游戏过程中，他从第一个堆中取出一个立方体，并记下其上的数字。然后，他从第二个堆中取出一个立方体，将其上的两个数字写在之前写下的两个数字旁边（即右侧）。最终，他得到一个四位整数——它的前两位数字写在第一个堆取出的立方体上，后两位数字写在第二个堆取出的立方体上。
Valera 非常擅长数学。因此，他可以轻松计算出在游戏中能够得到的不同四位数的数量。现在的问题是：应当如何将立方体分成两个堆，使这个数量（Valera 能够得到的不同四位整数的数量）尽可能大？

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 100）。第二行包含 2·n 个以空格分隔的整数 a_i（10 ≤ a_i ≤ 99），表示立方体上的数字。

output.ai: 第一行输出一个数，即 Valera 能够得到的不同四位数的最大数量。第二行输出 2·n 个数 b_i（1 ≤ b_i ≤ 2）。这些数表示：第 i 个立方体在你的划分中属于第 b_i 个堆。
如果有多种将方块分配到各堆的最优方案，输出任意一种即可。

note.ai: 在第一组测试数据中，Valera 可以将第一个方块放入第一堆，将第二个方块放入第二堆。此时他得到数字 1099。如果将第二个方块放入第一堆，将第一个方块放入第二堆，那么他可以得到数字 9910。在这两种情况下，不同整数的最大数量都等于 1。
在第二组测试数据中，Valera 可以得到数字 1313、1345、2413 和 2445。注意，如果他将第一个和第三个方块放入第一堆，那么只能得到两个数字 1324 和 1345。

problems.hint: If you rotate the camera $x$ times, how far is it from being vertical?

legend: Vasya started working in a machine vision company of IT City. Vasya's team creates software and hardware for identification of people by their face.

One of the project's know-how is a camera rotating around its optical axis on shooting. People see an eye-catching gadget — a rotating camera — come up to it to see it better, look into it. And the camera takes their photo at that time. What could be better for high quality identification?

But not everything is so simple. The pictures from camera appear rotated too (on clockwise camera rotation frame the content becomes rotated counter-clockwise). But the identification algorithm can work only with faces that are just slightly deviated from vertical.

Vasya was entrusted to correct the situation — to rotate a captured image so that image would be minimally deviated from vertical. Requirements were severe. Firstly, the picture should be rotated only on angle divisible by 90 degrees to not lose a bit of information about the image. Secondly, the frames from the camera are so huge and FPS is so big that adequate rotation speed is provided by hardware FPGA solution only. And this solution can rotate only by 90 degrees clockwise. Of course, one can apply 90 degrees turn several times but for the sake of performance the number of turns should be minimized.

Help Vasya implement the program that by the given rotation angle of the camera can determine the minimum number of 90 degrees clockwise turns necessary to get a picture in which up direction deviation from vertical is minimum.
The next figure contains frames taken from an unrotated camera, then from rotated 90 degrees clockwise, then from rotated 90 degrees counter-clockwise. Arrows show direction to "true up".
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/f321c00fdcb688f9004c13173a743b06c2618db4.png)
The next figure shows 90 degrees clockwise turn by FPGA hardware.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/458a2dacc4bab8212a4a12b5ccd4fcd472e3daf1.png)
input: The only line of the input contains one integer x ( - 1018 ≤ x ≤ 1018) — camera angle in degrees. Positive value denotes clockwise camera rotation, negative — counter-clockwise.
output: Output one integer — the minimum required number of 90 degrees clockwise turns.
note: When the camera is rotated 60 degrees counter-clockwise (the second example), an image from it is rotated 60 degrees clockwise. One 90 degrees clockwise turn of the image result in 150 degrees clockwise total rotation and deviation from "true up" for one turn is 150 degrees. Two 90 degrees clockwise turns of the image result in 240 degrees clockwise total rotation and deviation from "true up" for two turns is 120 degrees because 240 degrees clockwise equal to 120 degrees counter-clockwise. Three 90 degrees clockwise turns of the image result in 330 degrees clockwise total rotation and deviation from "true up" for three turns is 30 degrees because 330 degrees clockwise equal to 30 degrees counter-clockwise.
From 60, 150, 120 and 30 degrees deviations the smallest is 30, and it it achieved in three 90 degrees clockwise turns.

legend.ai: Vasya 开始在 IT City 的一家机器视觉公司工作。Vasya 的团队开发用于通过人脸识别人们的软件和硬件。
该项目的一项独门技术是在拍摄时让摄像机绕其光轴旋转。人们看到这个引人注目的装置——一台旋转的摄像机——便会走近它，以便看得更清楚，并向镜头中看去。此时摄像机会拍下他们的照片。还有什么能比这更有利于高质量的人脸识别呢？
但并非一切都这么简单。摄像头拍摄的画面也会出现旋转（当摄像头顺时针旋转时，画面内容会逆时针旋转）。但识别算法只能处理那些与竖直方向偏差很小的面部。
Vasya 受委托来纠正这种情况——旋转捕获的图像，使图像与竖直方向的偏差最小。要求非常严格。首先，图像只能旋转 90 度的整数倍角度，以免丢失关于图像的任何信息。其次，摄像头输出的帧非常大，FPS 又很高，因此只有硬件 FPGA 方案才能提供足够的旋转速度，而该方案只能顺时针旋转 90 度。当然，可以多次施加 90 度旋转，但为了性能，旋转次数应尽可能少。
帮助 Vasya 实现一个程序：给定摄像头的旋转角度，计算最少需要进行多少次顺时针 90 度旋转，才能得到一幅“上方方向”与竖直方向偏差最小的图像。
下图展示了分别由未旋转的摄像头、顺时针旋转 90 度的摄像头、逆时针旋转 90 度的摄像头拍摄的帧。箭头指向“真正的上方”。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/f321c00fdcb688f9004c13173a743b06c2618db4.png)
下图展示了 FPGA 硬件执行的顺时针 90 度旋转。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/458a2dacc4bab8212a4a12b5ccd4fcd472e3daf1.png)

input.ai: 输入的唯一一行包含一个整数 x（-10^18 ≤ x ≤ 10^18）——以度为单位的相机角度。正值表示相机顺时针旋转，负值表示逆时针旋转。

output.ai: 输出一个整数——所需的最少 90 度顺时针旋转次数。

note.ai: 当相机逆时针旋转 60 度时（第二个样例），拍摄出的图像会顺时针旋转 60 度。将图像顺时针旋转 90 度一次后，总旋转角度为顺时针 150 度，此时相对于“正上方”的偏差为 150 度。将图像顺时针旋转 90 度两次后，总旋转角度为顺时针 240 度，此时相对于“正上方”的偏差为 120 度，因为顺时针旋转 240 度等价于逆时针旋转 120 度。将图像顺时针旋转 90 度三次后，总旋转角度为顺时针 330 度，此时相对于“正上方”的偏差为 30 度，因为顺时针旋转 330 度等价于逆时针旋转 30 度。
在 60、150、120 和 30 度的偏差中，最小的是 30 度，并且进行三次 90 度顺时针旋转即可达到这一偏差。

problems.hint: Group the numbers.

legend: There have recently been elections in the zoo. Overall there were 7 main political parties: one of them is the Little Elephant Political Party, 6 other parties have less catchy names.

Political parties find their number in the ballot highly important. Overall there are m possible numbers: 1, 2, ..., m. Each of these 7 parties is going to be assigned in some way to exactly one number, at that, two distinct parties cannot receive the same number.

The Little Elephant Political Party members believe in the lucky digits 4 and 7. They want to evaluate their chances in the elections. For that, they need to find out, how many correct assignments are there, such that the number of lucky digits in the Little Elephant Political Party ballot number is strictly larger than the total number of lucky digits in the ballot numbers of 6 other parties.
Help the Little Elephant Political Party, calculate this number. As the answer can be rather large, print the remainder from dividing it by 1000000007 (109 + 7).
input: A single line contains a single positive integer m (7 ≤ m ≤ 109) — the number of possible numbers in the ballot.
output: In a single line print a single integer — the answer to the problem modulo 1000000007 (109 + 7).

legend.ai: 最近动物园里举行了选举。总共有 7 个主要政党：其中一个是小象党，另外 6 个政党的名字没那么响亮。
各政党非常看重自己在选票上的编号。总共有 m 个可用的编号：1, 2, ..., m。这 7 个政党中的每一个都将以某种方式被分配到一个编号，而且两个不同的政党不能得到相同的编号。
小象党党员相信幸运数字 4 和 7。他们想评估自己在选举中的机会。为此，他们需要知道有多少种正确的分配方案，使得小象党选票编号中幸运数字的个数严格大于其他 6 个政党选票编号中幸运数字的总个数。
帮助小象党计算这个数量。由于答案可能很大，输出它对 1000000007 (10^9 + 7) 取模的余数。

input.ai: 单行包含一个正整数 m (7 ≤ m ≤ 10^9) — 选票上可用的编号数量。

output.ai: 单行输出一个整数 — 答案对 1000000007 (10^9 + 7) 取模的结果。

problems.hint: Consider the number of cars that are not moved.

legend: An infinitely long railway has a train consisting of n cars, numbered from 1 to n (the numbers of all the cars are distinct) and positioned in arbitrary order. David Blaine wants to sort the railway cars in the order of increasing numbers. In one move he can make one of the cars disappear from its place and teleport it either to the beginning of the train, or to the end of the train, at his desire. What is the minimum number of actions David Blaine needs to perform in order to sort the train?
input: The first line of the input contains integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 100 000) — the number of cars in the train.
The second line contains n integers pi (1 ≤ pi ≤ n, pi ≠ pj if i ≠ j) — the sequence of the numbers of the cars in the train.
output: Print a single integer — the minimum number of actions needed to sort the railway cars.
note: In the first sample you need first to teleport the 4-th car, and then the 5-th car to the end of the train.

legend.ai: 一条无限长的铁路上有一列由 n 节车厢组成的列车，车厢编号为 1 到 n（所有车厢的编号各不相同），并且车厢的排列顺序任意。David Blaine 想要将这些车厢按照编号递增的顺序排列。每次操作中，他可以让某一节车厢从当前位置消失，并根据自己的意愿将其传送到列车的开头或末尾。为了将列车排序，David Blaine 最少需要进行多少次操作？

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 100 000），表示列车中的车厢数。
第二行包含 n 个整数 p_i（1 ≤ p_i ≤ n，若 i ≠ j 则 p_i ≠ p_j），表示列车中车厢编号组成的序列。

output.ai: 输出一个整数，表示将铁路车厢排序所需的最少操作次数。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，你需要先将第 4 节车厢传送到列车末尾，然后将第 5 节车厢传送到列车末尾。

problems.hint: Pre-process the DP.

legend: Alice is a big fan of volleyball and especially of the very strong "Team A".

Volleyball match consists of up to five sets. During each set teams score one point for winning a ball. The first four sets are played until one of the teams scores at least 25 points and the fifth set is played until one of the teams scores at least 15 points. Moreover, if one of the teams scores 25 (or 15 in the fifth set) points while the other team scores 24 (or 14 in the fifth set), the set is played until the absolute difference between teams' points becomes two. The match ends when one of the teams wins three sets. The match score is the number of sets won by each team.

Alice found a book containing all the results of all matches played by "Team A". The book is old, and some parts of the book became unreadable. Alice can not read the information on how many sets each of the teams won, she can not read the information on how many points each of the teams scored in each set, she even does not know the number of sets played in a match. The only information she has is the total number of points scored by each of the teams in all the sets during a single match.

Alice wonders what is the best match score "Team A" could achieve in each of the matches. The bigger is the difference between the number of sets won by "Team A" and their opponent, the better is the match score. Find the best match score or conclude that no match could end like that. If there is a solution, then find any possible score for each set that results in the best match score.
input: The first line contains a single integer m$$$m$$$ (1≤m≤50000$$$1 \le m \le 50\,000$$$) — the number of matches found by Alice in the book.

Each of the next m$$$m$$$ lines contains two integers a$$$a$$$ and b$$$b$$$ (0≤a,b≤200$$$0 \le a, b \le 200$$$) — the number of points scored by "Team A" and the number of points scored by their opponents respectively.
output: Output the solution for every match in the same order as they are given in the input. If the teams could not score a$$$a$$$ and b$$$b$$$ points respectively, output "Impossible".
Otherwise, output the match score formatted as "x$$$x$$$:y$$$y$$$", where x$$$x$$$ is the number of sets won by "Team A" and y$$$y$$$ is the number of sets won by their opponent.

The next line should contain the set scores in the order they were played. Each set score should be printed in the same format as the match score, with x$$$x$$$ being the number of points scored by "Team A" in this set, and y$$$y$$$ being the number of points scored by their opponent.

legend.ai: Alice 是排球的忠实球迷，尤其是强队“Team A”的球迷。
排球比赛最多进行五局。每局比赛中，球队赢下一个球得 1 分。前四局先打到至少 25 分的球队获胜，第五局先打到至少 15 分的球队获胜。此外，如果一队得到 25 分（第五局为 15 分）而另一队得到 24 分（第五局为 14 分），则继续比赛直到两队分差的绝对值为 2。当一方赢下三局时比赛结束。比赛比分为双方各自赢得的局数。
Alice 找到了一本书，里面记录了“Team A”参加的所有比赛的结果。这本书已经很旧，部分内容变得无法辨认。Alice 无法读到双方各自赢得的局数，也无法读到每局中双方各自的得分，她甚至不知道一场比赛打了多少局。她唯一知道的信息是，在单独一场比赛的所有局中，双方各自的总得分数。
Alice 想知道在每个比赛中，“Team A”可能取得的最好局分是多少。“Team A”赢得的局数与对手赢得的局数之差越大，局分就越好。请找出最好的局分，或者判断不存在这样的比赛结果。如果存在解，还要给出任意一组能达成该最好局分的每局得分。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 m$$$m$$$(1≤m≤50000$$$1 \le m \le 50\,000$$$)——表示 Alice 在书中找到的比赛场数。
接下来的 m$$$m$$$ 行中的每一行包含两个整数 a$$$a$$$ 和 b$$$b$$$(0≤a,b≤200$$$0 \le a, b \le 200$$$)——分别表示“Team A”和其对手得到的分数。

output.ai: 按输入中给出的顺序输出每场比赛的方案。如果两队无法分别得到 a$$$a$$$ 分和 b$$$b$$$ 分，则输出 "Impossible"。
否则，按照 "x$$$x$$$:y$$$y$$$" 的格式输出比赛比分，其中 x$$$x$$$ 表示“Team A”赢得的局数，y$$$y$$$ 表示其对手赢得的局数。
下一行应按照各局进行的顺序包含每局的比分。每局比分都应使用与比赛比分相同的格式输出，其中 x$$$x$$$ 表示“Team A”在该局得到的分数，y$$$y$$$ 表示其对手得到的分数。

problems.hint: Which points can be swapped in the final sequence?

legend: Little Dima has two sequences of points with integer coordinates: sequence (a1, 1), (a2, 2), ..., (an, n) and sequence (b1, 1), (b2, 2), ..., (bn, n).

Now Dima wants to count the number of distinct sequences of points of length 2·n that can be assembled from these sequences, such that the x-coordinates of points in the assembled sequence will not decrease. Help him with that. Note that each element of the initial sequences should be used exactly once in the assembled sequence.
Dima considers two assembled sequences (p1, q1), (p2, q2), ..., (p2·n, q2·n) and (x1, y1), (x2, y2), ..., (x2·n, y2·n) distinct, if there is such i (1 ≤ i ≤ 2·n), that (pi, qi) ≠ (xi, yi).
As the answer can be rather large, print the remainder from dividing the answer by number m.
input: The first line contains integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 105). The second line contains n integers a1, a2, ..., an (1 ≤ ai ≤ 109). The third line contains n integers b1, b2, ..., bn (1 ≤ bi ≤ 109). The numbers in the lines are separated by spaces.
The last line contains integer m (2 ≤ m ≤ 109 + 7).
output: In the single line print the remainder after dividing the answer to the problem by number m.
note: In the first sample you can get only one sequence: (1, 1), (2, 1).
In the second sample you can get such sequences : (1, 1), (2, 2), (2, 1), (3, 2); (1, 1), (2, 1), (2, 2), (3, 2). Thus, the answer is 2.

legend.ai: 小 Dima 有两个点序列，点的坐标均为整数：序列 (a1, 1), (a2, 2), ..., (an, n) 和序列 (b1, 1), (b2, 2), ..., (bn, n)。
现在 Dima 想要计算由这些序列拼成的长度为 2·n 的互不相同的点序列的个数，使得拼成序列中各点的 x 坐标不递减。请帮助他完成。注意，初始序列中的每个元素在拼成的序列中必须恰好使用一次。
Dima 认为两个拼成的序列 (p1, q1), (p2, q2), ..., (p2·n, q2·n) 与 (x1, y1), (x2, y2), ..., (x2·n, y2·n) 是不同的，如果存在某个 i（1 ≤ i ≤ 2·n），使得 (pi, qi) ≠ (xi, yi)。
由于答案可能相当大，请输出答案除以 m 所得的余数。

input.ai: 第一行包含整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5）。第二行包含 n 个整数 a1, a2, ..., an（1 ≤ ai ≤ 10^9）。第三行包含 n 个整数 b1, b2, ..., bn（1 ≤ bi ≤ 10^9）。行内数字之间用空格分隔。
最后一行包含整数 m（2 ≤ m ≤ 10^9 + 7）。

output.ai: 在单行中输出本题答案除以 m 所得的余数。

problems.hint: If you know the original direction and the current direction of $i$ , you can decide that of $i + 1$ .

legend: A very tense moment: n cowboys stand in a circle and each one points his colt at a neighbor. Each cowboy can point the colt to the person who follows or precedes him in clockwise direction. Human life is worthless, just like in any real western.

The picture changes each second! Every second the cowboys analyse the situation and, if a pair of cowboys realize that they aim at each other, they turn around. In a second all such pairs of neighboring cowboys aiming at each other turn around. All actions happen instantaneously and simultaneously in a second.

We'll use character "A" to denote a cowboy who aims at his neighbour in the clockwise direction, and character "B" for a cowboy who aims at his neighbour in the counter clockwise direction. Then a string of letters "A" and "B" will denote the circle of cowboys, the record is made from the first of them in a clockwise direction.
For example, a circle that looks like "ABBBABBBA" after a second transforms into "BABBBABBA" and a circle that looks like "BABBA" transforms into "ABABB".
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/6538d918f52acb2f4601b4247aa86973f71fed72.png)

A second passed and now the cowboys' position is described by string s. Your task is to determine the number of possible states that lead to s in a second. Two states are considered distinct if there is a cowboy who aims at his clockwise neighbor in one state and at his counter clockwise neighbor in the other state.
input: The input data consists of a single string s. Its length is from 3 to 100 characters, inclusive. Line s consists of letters "A" and "B".
output: Print the sought number of states.
note: In the first sample the possible initial states are "ABBBABBAB" and "ABBBABBBA".
In the second sample the possible initial states are "AABBB" and "BABBA".

legend.ai: 一个非常紧张的时刻：n 名牛仔站成一圈，每个人都将手枪指向一名邻居。每名牛仔都可以将手枪指向顺时针方向上位于他之后或之前的人。人命一文不值，就像任何真正的西部片中一样。
局势每秒都会发生变化！每秒钟，牛仔们都会分析情况；如果一对牛仔发现他们正互相瞄准，就会转身。在一秒钟内，所有互相瞄准的相邻牛仔对都会转身。所有动作都会瞬间且同时发生。
我们用字符 “A” 表示将枪口指向顺时针方向邻居的牛仔，用字符 “B” 表示将枪口指向逆时针方向邻居的牛仔。于是，一个由字母 “A” 和 “B” 组成的字符串就表示这圈牛仔，记录从其中第一个牛仔开始，沿顺时针方向进行。
例如，一个看起来像“ABBBABBBA”的圆圈经过一秒后会变成“BABBBABBA”，而一个看起来像“BABBA”的圆圈会变成“ABABB”。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/6538d918f52acb2f4601b4247aa86973f71fed72.png)
一秒过去了，现在牛仔们的位置由字符串 s 描述。你的任务是确定一秒前能够变为 s 的可能状态数量。如果存在一名牛仔，在一种状态中瞄准其顺时针方向的邻居，而在另一种状态中瞄准其逆时针方向的邻居，则认为这两种状态不同。

input.ai: 输入数据包含一个字符串 s。其长度为 3 到 100 个字符（含端点）。字符串 s 由字母“A”和“B”组成。

output.ai: 输出所求的状态数量。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，可能的初始状态为“ABBBABBAB”和“ABBBABBBA”。
在第二个样例中，可能的初始状态是“AABBB”和“BABBA”。

problems.hint: If you decide to use some of the servers, re-distribute them between services.

legend: One department of some software company has n$$$n$$$ servers of different specifications. Servers are indexed with consecutive integers from 1$$$1$$$ to n$$$n$$$. Suppose that the specifications of the j$$$j$$$-th server may be expressed with a single integer number cj$$$c_j$$$ of artificial resource units.

In order for production to work, it is needed to deploy two services S1$$$S_1$$$ and S2$$$S_2$$$ to process incoming requests using the servers of the department. Processing of incoming requests of service Si$$$S_i$$$ takes xi$$$x_i$$$ resource units.

The described situation happens in an advanced company, that is why each service may be deployed using not only one server, but several servers simultaneously. If service Si$$$S_i$$$ is deployed using ki$$$k_i$$$ servers, then the load is divided equally between these servers and each server requires only xi/ki$$$x_i / k_i$$$ (that may be a fractional number) resource units.

Each server may be left unused at all, or be used for deploying exactly one of the services (but not for two of them simultaneously). The service should not use more resources than the server provides.
Determine if it is possible to deploy both services using the given servers, and if yes, determine which servers should be used for deploying each of the services.
input: The first line contains three integers n$$$n$$$, x1$$$x_1$$$, x2$$$x_2$$$ (2≤n≤300000$$$2 \leq n \leq 300\,000$$$, 1≤x1,x2≤109$$$1 \leq x_1, x_2 \leq 10^9$$$) — the number of servers that the department may use, and resource units requirements for each of the services.
The second line contains n$$$n$$$ space-separated integers c1,c2,…,cn$$$c_1, c_2, \ldots, c_n$$$ (1≤ci≤109$$$1 \leq c_i \leq 10^9$$$) — the number of resource units provided by each of the servers.
output: If it is impossible to deploy both services using the given servers, print the only word "No" (without the quotes).
Otherwise print the word "Yes" (without the quotes).
In the second line print two integers k1$$$k_1$$$ and k2$$$k_2$$$ (1≤k1,k2≤n$$$1 \leq k_1, k_2 \leq n$$$) — the number of servers used for each of the services.
In the third line print k1$$$k_1$$$ integers, the indices of the servers that will be used for the first service.
In the fourth line print k2$$$k_2$$$ integers, the indices of the servers that will be used for the second service.
No index may appear twice among the indices you print in the last two lines. If there are several possible answers, it is allowed to print any of them.
note: In the first sample test each of the servers 1, 2 and 6 will will provide 8/3=2.(6)$$$8 / 3 = 2.(6)$$$ resource units and each of the servers 5, 4 will provide 16/2=8$$$16 / 2 = 8$$$ resource units.
In the second sample test the first server will provide 20$$$20$$$ resource units and each of the remaining servers will provide 32/3=10.(6)$$$32 / 3 = 10.(6)$$$ resource units.

legend.ai: 某软件公司有一个部门，该部门拥有 n$$$n$$$ 台规格各不相同的服务器。服务器的编号是从 1$$$1$$$ 到 n$$$n$$$ 的连续整数。假设第 j$$$j$$$ 台服务器的规格可以用一个整数 cj$$$c_j$$$ 表示，该整数表示人造资源单位的数量。
为了使生产正常运行，需要使用该部门的服务器部署两个服务 S1$$$S_1$$$ 和 S2$$$S_2$$$，以处理传入的请求。处理服务 Si$$$S_i$$$ 的传入请求需要 xi$$$x_i$$$ 个资源单位。
上述情况发生在一家先进的公司中，因此每项服务不仅可以使用一台服务器部署，也可以同时使用多台服务器部署。如果服务 Si$$$S_i$$$ 使用 ki$$$k_i$$$ 台服务器部署，那么负载将在这些服务器之间平均分配，每台服务器只需 xi/ki$$$x_i / k_i$$$ 个资源单位(该数可以是分数)。
每台服务器可以完全闲置，也可以用于部署恰好一个服务（但不能同时用于两个服务）。服务使用的资源不应超过服务器所能提供的资源。
判断是否可以使用给定的服务器部署这两项服务；如果可以，确定应分别使用哪些服务器部署每项服务。

input.ai: 第一行包含三个整数 n$$$n$$$、x1$$$x_1$$$、x2$$$x_2$$$(2≤n≤300000$$$2 \leq n \leq 300\,000$$$，1≤x1,x2≤109$$$1 \leq x_1, x_2 \leq 10^9$$$)——该部门可以使用的服务器数量，以及两项服务各自所需的资源单位数。
第二行包含 n$$$n$$$ 个以空格分隔的整数 c1,c2,…,cn$$$c_1, c_2, \ldots, c_n$$$(1≤ci≤109$$$1 \leq c_i \leq 10^9$$$)——每台服务器提供的资源单位数。

output.ai: 如果无法使用给定的服务器部署这两项服务，输出唯一的单词“No”（不含引号）。
否则，输出单词“Yes”（不含引号）。
在第二行输出两个整数 k1$$$k_1$$$ 和 k2$$$k_2$$$(1≤k1,k2≤n$$$1 \leq k_1, k_2 \leq n$$$)——分别用于部署两项服务的服务器数量。
在第三行输出 k1$$$k_1$$$ 个整数，即将用于第一项服务的服务器编号。
在第四行输出 k2$$$k_2$$$ 个整数，即将用于第二项服务的服务器编号。
你在最后两行输出的编号中不能有任何重复。如果有多个可行答案，可以输出其中任意一个。

note.ai: 在第一个样例测试中，服务器 1、2 和 6 中的每一台将提供 8/3=2.(6)$$$8 / 3 = 2.(6)$$$ 个资源单位，而服务器 5、4 中的每一台将提供 16/2=8$$$16 / 2 = 8$$$ 个资源单位。
在第二个样例测试中，第一台服务器将提供 20$$$20$$$ 个资源单位，其余每台服务器将提供 32/3=10.(6)$$$32 / 3 = 10.(6)$$$ 个资源单位。

problems.hint: What's remaining for merging?

legend: The programmers from the R2 company love playing 2048. One day, they decided to invent their own simplified version of this game — 2k on a stripe.
Imagine an infinite in one direction stripe, consisting of unit squares (the side of each square is equal to the height of the stripe). Each square can either be empty or contain some number.

Initially, all squares are empty. Then at infinity one of the unit squares number 2 or 4 appears. Then the player presses a button once, and the appeared number begins to move towards the beginning of the stripe. Let's assume that some number x moves to the beginning of the stripe, then it will stop if:
it either gets in the first square of the stripe;

or it is in the square that is preceded by a square with number y (y ≠ x). But if number x at some point of time gets to the square with the same number then both numbers add to each other and result in 2x. The new number 2x continues moving to the beginning of the stripe by the same rules.
After the final stop of the number moving process, the infinity gets a new number 2 or 4 and the process repeats. Read the notes to the test samples to better understand the moving strategy.

I guess you've understood that the game progress fully depends on the order in which numbers 2 and 4 appear. Let's look at some sequence of numbers 2 and 4 in the game. We assume that the sequence is winning if it results in at least one square getting the number greater or equal than 2k.

The goal of the game is to make up a winning sequence of n numbers. But not everything is so simple, some numbers in the sequence are identified beforehand. You are given a sequence consisting of numbers 0, 2, 4. Count how many ways there are to replace each 0 of the sequence with 2 or 4 to get a winning sequence.
input: The first line contains two integers n and k (1 ≤ n ≤ 2000; 3 ≤ k ≤ 11). The next line contains sequence of n integers, each of them is either 0, or 2, or 4.
output: Print a single integer — the number of ways to replace zeroes by numbers 2 or 4 to get a winning sequence. As this number can be rather large, print it modulo 1000000007 (109 + 7).
note: Consider the first example. The beginning of the strip will look as follows:

To better understand the game, you can see the original game on http://gabrielecirulli.github.io/2048/. Please note that the game that is described on the strip is slightly different from the original game (when the two numbers add up in the original game, they do not keep moving). Be careful, the game is addictive, there isn't much time for the contest!

legend.ai: R2 公司的程序员们喜欢玩 2048。有一天，他们决定发明这个游戏的简化版本——在一条长条上的 2k。
想象一条沿一个方向无限延伸的长条，它由若干个单位正方形组成（每个正方形的边长等于长条的高度）。每个格子可以是空的，也可以包含某个数字。
初始时所有格子都是空的。然后在无穷远处会出现一个数字为 2 或 4 的方块。接着玩家按下一次按钮，出现的数字便开始向长条的起点移动。假设某个数字 x 向长条起点移动，那么它会在以下情况停下：
它进入了长条的第一个格子；
或者它所在的格子的前一个格子中有一个数字 y（y ≠ x）。但如果数字 x 在某一时刻到达了一个含有相同数字的格子，那么两个数字会相加并得到 2x。新的数字 2x 会按照同样的规则继续向长条起点移动。
在数字移动过程最终停止后，无穷远处会再次出现一个新的数字 2 或 4，然后该过程重复。请阅读测试样例的注释，以更好地理解移动策略。
我想你已经明白，游戏的进程完全取决于数字 2 和 4 出现的顺序。让我们来看看游戏中的某个由数字 2 和 4 组成的序列。如果该序列最终能使至少一个方格中的数字大于等于 2^k，我们就称该序列是获胜的。
游戏的目标是组成一个由 n 个数字构成的获胜序列。但事情并没有这么简单，序列中的一些数字已经预先确定。给定一个由数字 0、2 和 4 组成的序列，请计算将序列中的每个 0 替换为 2 或 4 后得到获胜序列的方案数。

note.ai: 考虑第一个样例。条带的开头如下所示：
为了更好地理解这个游戏，你可以在 http://gabrielecirulli.github.io/2048/. 查看原始游戏。请注意，漫画中描述的这个游戏与原始游戏略有不同(在原始游戏中，当两个数字相加时，它们不会继续移动)。小心，这个游戏很容易上瘾，比赛可没有太多时间！

input.ai: 第一行包含两个整数 n 和 k（1 ≤ n ≤ 2000；3 ≤ k ≤ 11）。下一行包含一个由 n 个整数组成的序列，其中每个数都是 0、2 或 4。

output.ai: 输出一个整数——将 0 替换为 2 或 4 后得到获胜序列的方案数。由于这个数可能很大，请输出它对 1000000007（10^9 + 7）取模后的结果。

problems.hint: Iterate over all possible combinations of hints.

legend: Have you ever played Hanabi? If not, then you've got to try it out! This problem deals with a simplified version of the game.

Overall, the game has 25 types of cards (5 distinct colors and 5 distinct values). Borya is holding n cards. The game is somewhat complicated by the fact that everybody sees Borya's cards except for Borya himself. Borya knows which cards he has but he knows nothing about the order they lie in. Note that Borya can have multiple identical cards (and for each of the 25 types of cards he knows exactly how many cards of this type he has).

The aim of the other players is to achieve the state when Borya knows the color and number value of each of his cards. For that, other players can give him hints. The hints can be of two types: color hints and value hints.
A color hint goes like that: a player names some color and points at all the cards of this color.
Similarly goes the value hint. A player names some value and points at all the cards that contain the value.
Determine what minimum number of hints the other players should make for Borya to be certain about each card's color and value.
input: The first line contains integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 100) — the number of Borya's cards. The next line contains the descriptions of n cards. The description of each card consists of exactly two characters. The first character shows the color (overall this position can contain five distinct letters — R, G, B, Y, W). The second character shows the card's value (a digit from 1 to 5). Borya doesn't know exact order of the cards they lie in.
output: Print a single integer — the minimum number of hints that the other players should make.
note: In the first sample Borya already knows for each card that it is a green three.
In the second sample we can show all fours and all red cards.
In the third sample you need to make hints about any four colors.

legend.ai: 你玩过 Hanabi 吗？如果没有，那你一定要试试！本题讨论的是该游戏的简化版本。
整个游戏共有 25 种牌（5 种不同颜色和 5 种不同数值）。Borya 手里拿着 n 张牌。游戏因这样一个事实而变得有些复杂：除了 Borya 本人，每个人都能看到 Borya 的牌。Borya 知道自己有哪些牌，但他完全不知道这些牌的排列顺序。注意，Borya 可以拥有多张完全相同的牌（并且对于 25 种牌中的每一种，他都知道自己拥有该种牌的确切张数）。
其他玩家的目标是让 Borya 知道他的每张牌的颜色和数值。为此，其他玩家可以给他提示。提示分为两种：颜色提示和数值提示。
颜色提示是这样的：一名玩家说出一种颜色，然后指向所有该颜色的牌。
数值提示同理。玩家说出某个数值，并指出所有包含该数值的牌。
确定其他玩家至少需要给出多少条提示，才能让 Borya 确定每张牌的颜色和数值。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，Borya 已经知道每张牌都是绿色的 3。
在第二个样例中，我们可以指出所有数字为 4 的牌和所有红色的牌。
在第三个样例中，你需要对任意四种颜色给出提示。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 100）——Borya 的牌数。下一行包含 n 张牌的描述。每张牌的描述恰好由两个字符组成。第一个字符表示颜色（这一位置总共可能出现五种不同的字母——R、G、B、Y、W）。第二个字符表示牌的数值（一个 1 到 5 的数字）。Borya 不知道这些牌的确切顺序。

output.ai: 输出一个整数——其他玩家应该给出的提示的最少数量。

problems.hint: If you are at $u$ , where should you go?

legend: Connected undirected graph without cycles is called a tree. Trees is a class of graphs which is interesting not only for people, but for ants too.

An ant stands at the root of some tree. He sees that there are n vertexes in the tree, and they are connected by n - 1 edges so that there is a path between any pair of vertexes. A leaf is a distinct from root vertex, which is connected with exactly one other vertex.

The ant wants to visit every vertex in the tree and return to the root, passing every edge twice. In addition, he wants to visit the leaves in a specific order. You are to find some possible route of the ant.
input: The first line contains integer n (3 ≤ n ≤ 300) — amount of vertexes in the tree. Next n - 1 lines describe edges. Each edge is described with two integers — indexes of vertexes which it connects. Each edge can be passed in any direction. Vertexes are numbered starting from 1. The root of the tree has number 1. The last line contains k integers, where k is amount of leaves in the tree. These numbers describe the order in which the leaves should be visited. It is guaranteed that each leaf appears in this order exactly once.
output: If the required route doesn't exist, output -1. Otherwise, output 2n - 1 numbers, describing the route. Every time the ant comes to a vertex, output it's index.

output.ai: 如果所需的路线不存在，输出 -1。否则，输出 2n - 1 个数字，用于描述这条路线。每当蚂蚁到达一个顶点时，输出该顶点的编号。

legend.ai: 无环的连通无向图被称为树。树是一类不仅对人类有趣、对蚂蚁也同样有趣的图。
一只蚂蚁站在某棵树的根节点上。它看到这棵树有 n 个顶点，并由 n−1 条边连接，使得任意一对顶点之间都存在一条路径。叶子是一个与根节点不同、且恰好与另一个顶点相连的顶点。
蚂蚁希望访问树中的每个顶点并返回根节点，同时每条边恰好经过两次。此外，它还希望按照指定的顺序访问叶子。请找出一条蚂蚁可能经过的路线。

input.ai: 第一行包含整数 n（3 ≤ n ≤ 300），表示树中顶点的数量。接下来的 n−1 行描述边。每条边由两个整数表示，即它所连接的顶点编号。每条边都可以沿任意方向经过。顶点编号从 1 开始。根节点的编号为 1。最后一行包含 k 个整数，其中 k 是树中叶子的数量。这些数字描述了访问叶子的顺序。保证每个叶子在该顺序中恰好出现一次。

problems.hint: Some are fixed. Others can be greedily distributed.

legend: The organizers of a programming contest have decided to present t-shirts to participants. There are six different t-shirts sizes in this problem: S, M, L, XL, XXL, XXXL (sizes are listed in increasing order). The t-shirts are already prepared. For each size from S to XXXL you are given the number of t-shirts of this size.

During the registration, the organizers asked each of the n participants about the t-shirt size he wants. If a participant hesitated between two sizes, he could specify two neighboring sizes — this means that any of these two sizes suits him.
Write a program that will determine whether it is possible to present a t-shirt to each participant of the competition, or not. Of course, each participant should get a t-shirt of proper size:
the size he wanted, if he specified one size;
any of the two neibouring sizes, if he specified two sizes.
If it is possible, the program should find any valid distribution of the t-shirts.
input: The first line of the input contains six non-negative integers — the number of t-shirts of each size. The numbers are given for the sizes S, M, L, XL, XXL, XXXL, respectively. The total number of t-shirts doesn't exceed 100 000.
The second line contains positive integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 100 000) — the number of participants.

The following n lines contain the sizes specified by the participants, one line per participant. The i-th line contains information provided by the i-th participant: single size or two sizes separated by comma (without any spaces). If there are two sizes, the sizes are written in increasing order. It is guaranteed that two sizes separated by comma are neighboring.
output: If it is not possible to present a t-shirt to each participant, print «NO» (without quotes).

Otherwise, print n + 1 lines. In the first line print «YES» (without quotes). In the following n lines print the t-shirt sizes the orginizers should give to participants, one per line. The order of the participants should be the same as in the input.
If there are multiple solutions, print any of them.

legend.ai: 编程竞赛的组织者决定向参赛者赠送 T 恤。本题中有六种不同的 T 恤尺码：S、M、L、XL、XXL、XXXL（尺码按递增顺序列出）。T 恤已经准备完毕。对于从 S 到 XXXL 的每种尺码，给出该尺码 T 恤的数量。
在报名期间，组织者询问了 n 位参赛者中的每一人想要的 T 恤尺码。如果某位参赛者在两个尺码之间犹豫，他可以指定两个相邻的尺码——这意味着这两个尺码中的任意一个都适合他。
编写一个程序，判断是否可以为竞赛的每位参赛者提供一件 T 恤。当然，每位参赛者都应得到合适尺码的 T 恤：
如果他指定了一个尺码，则为他想要的尺码；
如果他指定了两个尺码，则可以选择其中任意一个相邻尺码。
如果可能，程序应找出一种有效的 T 恤分配方案。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含六个非负整数，分别表示 S、M、L、XL、XXL、XXXL 各尺码的 T 恤数量。T 恤总数不超过 100 000。
第二行包含正整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 100 000），表示参与者的数量。
接下来的 n 行包含参与者指定的尺码，每位参与者占一行。第 i 行包含第 i 位参与者提供的信息：一个尺码，或由逗号分隔的两个尺码（不含空格）。如果有两个尺码，则尺码按递增顺序给出。保证由逗号分隔的两个尺码相邻。

output.ai: 如果无法为每位参与者分配一件 T 恤，则输出 «NO»（不含引号）。
否则，输出 n + 1 行。第一行输出「YES」（不含引号）。接下来的 n 行中，每行输出组织者应分发给参赛者的 T 恤尺码。参赛者的顺序应与输入中的顺序相同。
如果有多个解，输出其中任意一个即可。

problems.hint: There is exactly one `'@'` in each email.

legend: One of the most important products of the R1 company is a popular @r1.com mail service. The R1 mailboxes receive and send millions of emails every day.

Today, the online news thundered with terrible information. The R1 database crashed and almost no data could be saved except for one big string. The developers assume that the string contains the letters of some users of the R1 mail. Recovering letters is a tedious mostly manual work. So before you start this process, it was decided to estimate the difficulty of recovering. Namely, we need to calculate the number of different substrings of the saved string that form correct e-mail addresses.
We assume that valid addresses are only the e-mail addresses which meet the following criteria:
the address should begin with a non-empty sequence of letters, numbers, characters '_', starting with a letter;
then must go character '@';
then must go a non-empty sequence of letters or numbers;
then must go character '.';
the address must end with a non-empty sequence of letters.

You got lucky again and the job was entrusted to you! Please note that the substring is several consecutive characters in a string. Two substrings, one consisting of the characters of the string with numbers l1, l1 + 1, l1 + 2, ..., r1 and the other one consisting of the characters of the string with numbers l2, l2 + 1, l2 + 2, ..., r2, are considered distinct if l1 ≠ l2 or r1 ≠ r2.
input: The first and the only line contains the sequence of characters s1s2... sn (1 ≤ n ≤ 106) — the saved string. It is guaranteed that the given string contains only small English letters, digits and characters '.', '_', '@'.
output: Print in a single line the number of substrings that are valid e-mail addresses.
note: In the first test case all the substrings that are correct e-mail addresses begin from one of the letters of the word agapov and end in one of the letters of the word com.
In the second test case note that the e-mail x@x.x is considered twice in the answer. Note that in this example the e-mail entries overlap inside the string.

legend.ai: R1 公司最重要的产品之一是广受欢迎的 @r1.com 邮件服务。R1 邮箱每天都会接收和发送数百万封电子邮件。
今天，网上新闻传来了可怕的消息。R1 的数据库崩溃了，除了一个很长的字符串外，几乎没有任何数据能够保存下来。开发者推测，这个字符串中包含 R1 邮件服务中一些用户的邮件。恢复这些邮件是一项繁琐且主要依靠人工完成的工作。因此，在开始这一过程之前，人们决定先估计恢复工作的难度。具体来说，我们需要计算保存下来的字符串中，能够构成正确电子邮件地址的不同子串数量。
我们认为，只有满足以下条件的电子邮件地址才是有效的：
地址应以一个非空的字母、数字或字符“_”序列开头，且第一个字符必须是字母；
接下来必须是字符“@”；
接下来必须是一个非空的字母或数字序列；
接下来必须是字符“.”；
地址必须以一个非空的字母序列结尾。
你又一次走运了，这项工作交给了你！请注意，子串是字符串中的若干个连续字符。若两个子串分别由字符串中编号为 l1，l1 + 1，l1 + 2，...，r1 的字符和编号为 l2，l2 + 1，l2 + 2，...，r2 的字符组成，那么当 l1 ≠ l2 或 r1 ≠ r2 时，这两个子串被认为是不同的。

input.ai: 第一行也是唯一一行，包含由字符 s1s2...sn 组成的序列（1 ≤ n ≤ 10^6）——保存的字符串。保证给定字符串仅包含小写英文字母、数字以及字符“.”、“_”、“@”。

output.ai: 请在一行中输出合法电子邮件地址子串的数量。

note.ai: 在第一个测试用例中，所有合法电子邮件地址子串都以单词 agapov 中的某个字母开头，并以单词 com 中的某个字母结尾。
在第二个测试用例中，注意电子邮件地址 x@x.x 在答案中被计算了两次。还要注意，在这个例子中，字符串中的电子邮件地址彼此重叠。

problems.hint: Which round is it?

legend: There are n animals in the queue to Dr. Dolittle. When an animal comes into the office, the doctor examines him, gives prescriptions, appoints tests and may appoint extra examination. Doc knows all the forest animals perfectly well and therefore knows exactly that the animal number i in the queue will have to visit his office exactly ai times. We will assume that an examination takes much more time than making tests and other extra procedures, and therefore we will assume that once an animal leaves the room, it immediately gets to the end of the queue to the doctor. Of course, if the animal has visited the doctor as many times as necessary, then it doesn't have to stand at the end of the queue and it immediately goes home.

Doctor plans to go home after receiving k animals, and therefore what the queue will look like at that moment is important for him. Since the doctor works long hours and she can't get distracted like that after all, she asked you to figure it out.
input: The first line of input data contains two space-separated integers n and k (1 ≤ n ≤ 105, 0 ≤ k ≤ 1014). In the second line are given space-separated integers a1, a2, ..., an (1 ≤ ai ≤ 109).
Please do not use the %lld specificator to read or write 64-bit numbers in C++. It is recommended to use cin, cout streams (you can also use the %I64d specificator).
output: If the doctor will overall carry out less than k examinations, print a single number "-1" (without quotes). Otherwise, print the sequence of numbers — number of animals in the order in which they stand in the queue.
Note that this sequence may be empty. This case is present in pretests. You can just print nothing or print one "End of line"-character. Both will be accepted.
note: In the first sample test:
Before examination: {1, 2, 3}
After the first examination: {2, 3}
After the second examination: {3, 2}
After the third examination: {2}
In the second sample test:
Before examination: {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7}
After the first examination: {2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7}
After the second examination: {3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 2}
After the third examination: {4, 5, 6, 7, 2, 3}
After the fourth examination: {5, 6, 7, 2, 3}
After the fifth examination: {6, 7, 2, 3, 5}
After the sixth examination: {7, 2, 3, 5, 6}
After the seventh examination: {2, 3, 5, 6}
After the eighth examination: {3, 5, 6, 2}
After the ninth examination: {5, 6, 2, 3}
After the tenth examination: {6, 2, 3}

note.ai: 在第一个样例测试中：
第一次检查后：{2, 3}
第二次检查后：{3, 2}
第三次检查后：{2}
在第二个样例测试中：
第十次检查后：{6, 2, 3}

legend.ai: 有 n 只动物正在排队等待去 Dolittle 医生处就诊。当一只动物进入诊室时，医生会对它进行检查、开具处方、安排检查，并可能安排额外的检查。医生非常了解森林中的所有动物，因此他准确知道，队伍中编号为 i 的动物需要到他的诊室就诊恰好 ai 次。我们假设一次检查所需的时间远多于进行化验和其他额外操作所需的时间，因此假设一只动物离开诊室后，会立即回到医生处队伍的末尾。当然，如果该动物已经按所需次数就诊，那么它就不必排到队尾，而是立即回家。
医生计划在接收 k 只动物后回家，因此那一时刻队列的状态对她来说很重要。由于医生工作时间很长，毕竟不能因此分心，所以她请你计算出队列的状态。

input.ai: 输入数据的第一行包含两个用空格分隔的整数 n 和 k（1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5，0 ≤ k ≤ 10^14）。第二行包含 n 个用空格分隔的整数 a1，a2，...，an（1 ≤ ai ≤ 10^9）。
请不要在 C++ 中使用 %lld 说明符来读写 64 位数字。建议使用 cin、cout 流（也可以使用 %I64d 说明符）。

output.ai: 如果医生总共进行的检查次数少于 k 次，输出一个数字“-1”（不含引号）。否则，输出一个数字序列，即按照动物在队列中的顺序输出它们的编号。
注意，这个序列可能为空。预测试中包含这种情况。你可以什么都不输出，或者只输出一个换行符。两种方式都会被接受。

problems.hint: $p(x+1)\leq p(x)$ means something.
Consider what property the number should have before $\sqrt{}$ operation.

legend: ZS the Coder is playing a game. There is a number displayed on the screen and there are two buttons, ' + ' (plus) and '![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c77ded9b8209a8cb488cc2ec7b7fe1dae32a5309.png)' (square root). Initially, the number 2 is displayed on the screen. There are n + 1 levels in the game and ZS the Coder start at the level 1.
When ZS the Coder is at level k, he can :
Press the ' + ' button. This increases the number on the screen by exactly k. So, if the number on the screen was x, it becomes x + k.

Press the '![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c77ded9b8209a8cb488cc2ec7b7fe1dae32a5309.png)' button. Let the number on the screen be x. After pressing this button, the number becomes ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/dd68ff2d8e5b97302506ac32d308bb521ab84a26.png). After that, ZS the Coder levels up, so his current level becomes k + 1. This button can only be pressed when x is a perfect square, i.e. x = m2 for some positive integer m.

Additionally, after each move, if ZS the Coder is at level k, and the number on the screen is m, then m must be a multiple of k. Note that this condition is only checked after performing the press. For example, if ZS the Coder is at level 4 and current number is 100, he presses the '![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c77ded9b8209a8cb488cc2ec7b7fe1dae32a5309.png)' button and the number turns into 10. Note that at this moment, 10 is not divisible by 4, but this press is still valid, because after it, ZS the Coder is at level 5, and 10 is divisible by 5.

ZS the Coder needs your help in beating the game — he wants to reach level n + 1. In other words, he needs to press the '![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c77ded9b8209a8cb488cc2ec7b7fe1dae32a5309.png)' button n times. Help him determine the number of times he should press the ' + ' button before pressing the '![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c77ded9b8209a8cb488cc2ec7b7fe1dae32a5309.png)' button at each level.
Please note that ZS the Coder wants to find just any sequence of presses allowing him to reach level n + 1, but not necessarily a sequence minimizing the number of presses.
input: The first and only line of the input contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 100 000), denoting that ZS the Coder wants to reach level n + 1.
output: Print n non-negative integers, one per line. i-th of them should be equal to the number of times that ZS the Coder needs to press the ' + ' button before pressing the '![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c77ded9b8209a8cb488cc2ec7b7fe1dae32a5309.png)' button at level i.
Each number in the output should not exceed 1018. However, the number on the screen can be greater than 1018.
It is guaranteed that at least one solution exists. If there are multiple solutions, print any of them.
note: In the first sample case:

On the first level, ZS the Coder pressed the ' + ' button 14 times (and the number on screen is initially 2), so the number became 2 + 14·1 = 16. Then, ZS the Coder pressed the '![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c77ded9b8209a8cb488cc2ec7b7fe1dae32a5309.png)' button, and the number became ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c3d2663f5f74e9220fd5cbccbfaf4ca76ef7284f.png).

After that, on the second level, ZS pressed the ' + ' button 16 times, so the number becomes 4 + 16·2 = 36. Then, ZS pressed the '![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c77ded9b8209a8cb488cc2ec7b7fe1dae32a5309.png)' button, levelling up and changing the number into ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/49ab1d31f1435b7c7b96550d63a35be671d3d85a.png).

After that, on the third level, ZS pressed the ' + ' button 46 times, so the number becomes 6 + 46·3 = 144. Then, ZS pressed the '![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c77ded9b8209a8cb488cc2ec7b7fe1dae32a5309.png)' button, levelling up and changing the number into ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/499b57d4b7ba5e1e0957767cc182808ca48ef722.png).
Note that 12 is indeed divisible by 4, so ZS the Coder can reach level 4.

Also, note that pressing the ' + ' button 10 times on the third level before levelling up does not work, because the number becomes 6 + 10·3 = 36, and when the '![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c77ded9b8209a8cb488cc2ec7b7fe1dae32a5309.png)' button is pressed, the number becomes ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/49ab1d31f1435b7c7b96550d63a35be671d3d85a.png) and ZS the Coder is at Level 4. However, 6 is not divisible by 4 now, so this is not a valid solution.
In the second sample case:

On the first level, ZS the Coder pressed the ' + ' button 999999999999999998 times (and the number on screen is initially 2), so the number became 2 + 999999999999999998·1 = 1018. Then, ZS the Coder pressed the '![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c77ded9b8209a8cb488cc2ec7b7fe1dae32a5309.png)' button, and the number became ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/f07f2a60ab6cecbd2507861a0df57a16a015fd86.png).

After that, on the second level, ZS pressed the ' + ' button 44500000000 times, so the number becomes 109 + 44500000000·2 = 9·1010. Then, ZS pressed the '![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c77ded9b8209a8cb488cc2ec7b7fe1dae32a5309.png)' button, levelling up and changing the number into ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/4c4d8829d987a7bcfd597cd1aa101327a66c0eca.png).
Note that 300000 is a multiple of 3, so ZS the Coder can reach level 3.

legend.ai: ZS the Coder 正在玩一个游戏。屏幕上显示着一个数字，并且有两个按钮：“ + ”(加法)和“![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c77ded9b8209a8cb488cc2ec7b7fe1dae32a5309.png)”(平方根)。初始时，屏幕上显示的数字为 2。游戏中有 n + 1 个关卡，ZS the Coder 从第 1 关开始。
当 ZS the Coder 处于等级 k 时，他可以：
按下“+”按钮。屏幕上的数字恰好增加 k。因此，如果屏幕上的数字原来是 x，就会变为 x + k。

按下“![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c77ded9b8209a8cb488cc2ec7b7fe1dae32a5309.png)”按钮。设屏幕上的数字为 x。按下此按钮后，数字变为 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/dd68ff2d8e5b97302506ac32d308bb521ab84a26.png)。随后，ZS the Coder 升级，因此他的当前等级变为 k + 1。只有当 x 是完全平方数，即对于某个正整数 m，x = m² 时，才能按下此按钮。

此外，每次操作后，如果 ZS the Coder 处于等级 k，且屏幕上的数字为 m，那么 m 必须是 k 的倍数。注意，这一条件只会在执行按键操作后检查。例如，如果 ZS the Coder 处于 4 级，当前数字为 100，他按下“![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c77ded9b8209a8cb488cc2ec7b7fe1dae32a5309.png)”按钮，数字变为 10。注意，此时 10 不能被 4 整除，但这次按键操作仍然有效，因为操作后 ZS the Coder 处于 5 级，而 10 能被 5 整除。

ZS the Coder 需要你的帮助来赢得这场游戏——他想要达到 n + 1 级。换句话说，他需要按下“![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c77ded9b8209a8cb488cc2ec7b7fe1dae32a5309.png)”按钮 n 次。请帮助他确定在每个等级按下“![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c77ded9b8209a8cb488cc2ec7b7fe1dae32a5309.png)”按钮之前应该按下“+”按钮的次数。
请注意，ZS the Coder 只想找到任意一系列能够让他达到 n + 1 级的按键操作，而不一定要使按键总次数最少。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中：

在第一层，ZS the Coder 按下“ + ”按钮 14 次(屏幕上的数字初始为 2)，因此数字变为 2 + 14·1 = 16。然后，ZS the Coder 按下 “![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c77ded9b8209a8cb488cc2ec7b7fe1dae32a5309.png)” 按钮，数字变为 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c3d2663f5f74e9220fd5cbccbfaf4ca76ef7284f.png)。

此后，在第二级，ZS 按下了 16 次“ + ”按钮，因此数字变为 4 + 16·2 = 36。然后，ZS 按下“![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c77ded9b8209a8cb488cc2ec7b7fe1dae32a5309.png)”按钮，升级并将数字变为 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/49ab1d31f1435b7c7b96550d63a35be671d3d85a.png)。

此后，在第三级，ZS 按下了 46 次“ + ”按钮，因此数字变为 6 + 46·3 = 144。然后，ZS 按下“![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c77ded9b8209a8cb488cc2ec7b7fe1dae32a5309.png)”按钮，升级并将数字变为 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/499b57d4b7ba5e1e0957767cc182808ca48ef722.png)。
注意，12 确实能被 4 整除，因此 ZS the Coder 可以到达第 4 级。

此外，注意在升级前于第三级按下 10 次“ + ”按钮是不可行的，因为数字会变为 6 + 10·3 = 36，而按下“![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c77ded9b8209a8cb488cc2ec7b7fe1dae32a5309.png)”按钮后，数字会变为 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/49ab1d31f1435b7c7b96550d63a35be671d3d85a.png)，此时 ZS the Coder 处于第 4 级。然而，6 现在不能被 4 整除，因此这不是一个有效的方案。
在第二个样例中：

在第一级，ZS the Coder 按下了 999999999999999998 次“ + ”按钮(屏幕上的数字初始为 2)，因此数字变为 2 + 999999999999999998·1 = 1018。然后，ZS the Coder 按下“![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c77ded9b8209a8cb488cc2ec7b7fe1dae32a5309.png)”按钮，数字变为 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/f07f2a60ab6cecbd2507861a0df57a16a015fd86.png)。

legend: Every December, VK traditionally holds an event for its employees named "Secret Santa". Here's how it happens.

n$$$n$$$ employees numbered from 1$$$1$$$ to n$$$n$$$ take part in the event. Each employee i$$$i$$$ is assigned a different employee bi$$$b_i$$$, to which employee i$$$i$$$ has to make a new year gift. Each employee is assigned to exactly one other employee, and nobody is assigned to themselves (but two employees may be assigned to each other). Formally, all bi$$$b_i$$$ must be distinct integers between 1$$$1$$$ and n$$$n$$$, and for any i$$$i$$$, bi≠i$$$b_i \ne i$$$ must hold.

The assignment is usually generated randomly. This year, as an experiment, all event participants have been asked who they wish to make a gift to. Each employee i$$$i$$$ has said that they wish to make a gift to employee ai$$$a_i$$$.
Find a valid assignment b$$$b$$$ that maximizes the number of fulfilled wishes of the employees.
input: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤105$$$1 \le t \le 10^5$$$). Description of the test cases follows.
Each test case consists of two lines. The first line contains a single integer n$$$n$$$ (2≤n≤2⋅105$$$2 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of participants of the event.
The second line contains n$$$n$$$ integers a1,a2,…,an$$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ (1≤ai≤n$$$1 \le a_i \le n$$$; ai≠i$$$a_i \ne i$$$) — wishes of the employees in order from 1$$$1$$$ to n$$$n$$$.
It is guaranteed that the sum of n$$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed 2⋅105$$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output: For each test case, print two lines.
In the first line, print a single integer k$$$k$$$ (0≤k≤n$$$0 \le k \le n$$$) — the number of fulfilled wishes in your assignment.

In the second line, print n$$$n$$$ distinct integers b1,b2,…,bn$$$b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_n$$$ (1≤bi≤n$$$1 \le b_i \le n$$$; bi≠i$$$b_i \ne i$$$) — the numbers of employees assigned to employees 1,2,…,n$$$1, 2, \ldots, n$$$.
k$$$k$$$ must be equal to the number of values of i$$$i$$$ such that ai=bi$$$a_i = b_i$$$, and must be as large as possible. If there are multiple answers, print any.
note: In the first test case, two valid assignments exist: [3,1,2]$$$[3, 1, 2]$$$ and [2,3,1]$$$[2, 3, 1]$$$. The former assignment fulfills two wishes, while the latter assignment fulfills only one. Therefore, k=2$$$k = 2$$$, and the only correct answer is [3,1,2]$$$[3, 1, 2]$$$.

legend.ai: 每年十二月，VK 都会按照传统为其员工举办一项名为“Secret Santa”的活动。活动流程如下。

有 n$$$n$$$ 名编号从 1$$$1$$$ 到 n$$$n$$$ 的员工参加活动。每名员工 i$$$i$$$ 都被分配给一名不同的员工 bi$$$b_i$$$，员工 i$$$i$$$ 必须向该员工赠送新年礼物。每名员工恰好被分配给另一名员工，且没有人会被分配给自己(但两名员工可以互相分配给对方)。形式化地说，所有 bi$$$b_i$$$ 都必须是 1$$$1$$$ 到 n$$$n$$$ 之间的互不相同的整数，并且对于任意 i$$$i$$$，都必须满足 bi≠i$$$b_i \ne i$$$。
通常情况下，这种分配是随机生成的。今年，作为一次实验，活动的所有参与者都被询问了他们希望向谁赠送礼物。每名员工 i$$$i$$$ 都表示希望向员工 ai$$$a_i$$$ 赠送礼物。
寻找一个有效的分配 b$$$b$$$，使员工愿望得到满足的数量最大。

input.ai: 每个测试包含多个测试用例。第一行包含测试用例的数量 t$$$t$$$(1≤t≤105$$$1 \le t \le 10^5$$$)。下面给出测试用例的描述。

在第一行输出一个整数 k$$$k$$$(0≤k≤n$$$0 \le k \le n$$$)——你的分配方案中得到满足的愿望数量。

k$$$k$$$ 必须等于满足 ai=bi$$$a_i = b_i$$$ 的 i$$$i$$$ 的取值个数，并且应尽可能大。若有多个答案，输出任意一个。

legend: You are playing the following game. There are n points on a plane. They are the vertices of a regular n-polygon. Points are labeled with integer numbers from 1 to n. Each pair of distinct points is connected by a diagonal, which is colored in one of 26 colors. Points are denoted by lowercase English letters. There are three stones positioned on three distinct vertices. All stones are the same. With one move you can move the stone to another free vertex along some diagonal. The color of this diagonal must be the same as the color of the diagonal, connecting another two stones.

Your goal is to move stones in such way that the only vertices occupied by stones are 1, 2 and 3. You must achieve such position using minimal number of moves. Write a program which plays this game in an optimal way.
input: In the first line there is one integer n (3 ≤ n ≤ 70) — the number of points. In the second line there are three space-separated integer from 1 to n — numbers of vertices, where stones are initially located.

Each of the following n lines contains n symbols — the matrix denoting the colors of the diagonals. Colors are denoted by lowercase English letters. The symbol j of line i denotes the color of diagonal between points i and j. Matrix is symmetric, so j-th symbol of i-th line is equal to i-th symbol of j-th line. Main diagonal is filled with '*' symbols because there is no diagonal, connecting point to itself.
output: If there is no way to put stones on vertices 1, 2 and 3, print -1 on a single line. Otherwise, on the first line print minimal required number of moves and in the next lines print the description of each move, one move per line. To describe a move print two integers. The point from which to remove the stone, and the point to which move the stone. If there are several optimal solutions, print any of them.
note: In the first example we can move stone from point 4 to point 1 because this points are connected by the diagonal of color 'a' and the diagonal connection point 2 and 3, where the other stones are located, are connected by the diagonal of the same color. After that stones will be on the points 1, 2 and 3.

legend.ai: 你正在进行如下游戏。平面上有 n 个点，它们是一个正 n 边形的顶点。点被标上从 1 到 n 的整数编号。每一对不同的点之间都连接有一条对角线，该对角线被涂成 26 种颜色中的一种。点用小写英文字母表示。有三个棋子分别放置在三个不同的顶点上。所有棋子都完全相同。每次操作中，你可以沿某条对角线将一个棋子移动到另一个空闲的顶点。该对角线的颜色必须与连接另外两个棋子的对角线的颜色相同。
你的目标是以某种方式移动石子，使得被石子占据的顶点只有 1、2 和 3。你必须用最少的移动次数达到这种局面。请编写一个程序，以最优方式游玩这个游戏。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n（3 ≤ n ≤ 70），表示点的数量。第二行包含三个用空格分隔的 1 到 n 之间的整数，表示石子初始所在顶点的编号。
接下来的 n 行每行包含 n 个符号，构成表示对角线颜色的矩阵。颜色由小写英文字母表示。第 i 行第 j 个符号表示点 i 和点 j 之间对角线的颜色。矩阵是对称的，因此第 i 行第 j 个符号等于第 j 行第 i 个符号。主对角线用 '*' 填充，因为不存在连接点到自身的对角线。

output.ai: 如果无法将石子放到顶点 1、2 和 3 上，则输出一行 -1。否则，第一行输出所需的最少移动次数，接下来的每行输出一步移动的描述，每行描述一步移动。描述一步移动时输出两个整数：移除石子的点，以及移动石子的目标点。如果有多种最优方案，输出其中任意一种即可。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，我们可以将石子从点 4 移到点 1，因为这两个点由颜色为 'a' 的对角线连接，而连接另外两颗石子所在的点 2 和点 3 的对角线也是相同颜色。之后石子将位于点 1、2 和 3 上。

legend: Little Chris is very keen on his toy blocks. His teacher, however, wants Chris to solve more problems, so he decided to play a trick on Chris.

There are exactly s blocks in Chris's set, each block has a unique number from 1 to s. Chris's teacher picks a subset of blocks X and keeps it to himself. He will give them back only if Chris can pick such a non-empty subset Y from the remaining blocks, that the equality holds:
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/37b797b8afff1b78d9cef3602665323f470da659.png)

For example, consider a case where s = 8 and Chris's teacher took the blocks with numbers 1, 4 and 5. One way for Chris to choose a set is to pick the blocks with numbers 3 and 6, see figure. Then the required sums would be equal: (1 - 1) + (4 - 1) + (5 - 1) = (8 - 3) + (8 - 6) = 7.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/33225395a3670b19e14e3697714044c96b003500.png)
However, now Chris has exactly s = 106 blocks. Given the set X of blocks his teacher chooses, help Chris to find the required set Y!
input: The first line of input contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 5·105), the number of blocks in the set X. The next line contains n distinct space-separated integers x1, x2, ..., xn (1 ≤ xi ≤ 106), the numbers of the blocks in X.
Note: since the size of the input and output could be very large, don't use slow output techniques in your language. For example, do not use input and output streams (cin, cout) in C++.
output: In the first line of output print a single integer m (1 ≤ m ≤ 106 - n), the number of blocks in the set Y. In the next line output m distinct space-separated integers y1, y2, ..., ym (1 ≤ yi ≤ 106), such that the required equality holds. The sets X and Y should not intersect, i.e. xi ≠ yj for all i, j (1 ≤ i ≤ n; 1 ≤ j ≤ m). It is guaranteed that at least one solution always exists. If there are multiple solutions, output any of them.

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 5·10^5），表示集合 X 中块的数量。下一行包含 n 个互不相同的、以空格分隔的整数 x1、x2、...、xn（1 ≤ xi ≤ 10^6），表示 X 中各块的编号。
注意：由于输入和输出的规模可能非常大，请不要在所使用的语言中采用速度较慢的输入输出方式。例如，在 C++ 中不要使用输入输出流（cin、cout）。

output.ai: 在输出的第一行输出一个整数 m（1 ≤ m ≤ 10^6 - n），表示集合 Y 中块的数量。在下一行输出 m 个互不相同的、以空格分隔的整数 y1、y2、...、ym（1 ≤ yi ≤ 10^6），使得所要求的等式成立。集合 X 和 Y 不应有交集，即对于所有 i、j（1 ≤ i ≤ n；1 ≤ j ≤ m），均有 xi ≠ yj。保证至少存在一个解。如果有多个解，输出其中任意一个即可。

legend.ai: 小克里斯非常喜欢他的玩具积木。然而，他的老师希望克里斯多解决一些问题，于是决定捉弄一下克里斯。
克里斯的积木组中恰好有 s 块积木，每块积木都有一个从 1 到 s 的唯一编号。克里斯的老师选取了积木的一个子集 X，并将其藏了起来。只有当克里斯能从剩余的积木中选出一个非空子集 Y，使得下列等式成立时，老师才会把它们还给克里斯：
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/37b797b8afff1b78d9cef3602665323f470da659.png)
例如，考虑 s = 8 且克里斯的老师拿走了编号为 1、4 和 5 的积木的情况。克里斯可以选择编号为 3 和 6 的积木，见图。这样一来，所要求的两边之和相等：(1 - 1) + (4 - 1) + (5 - 1) = (8 - 3) + (8 - 6) = 7。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/33225395a3670b19e14e3697714044c96b003500.png)
然而，现在克里斯恰好有 s = 106 块积木。给定他的老师选择的积木集合 X，请帮助克里斯找出所要求的集合 Y！

problems.hint: How can you check whether a permutation satisfy the conditions?

legend: Let's suppose you have an array a, a stack s (initially empty) and an array b (also initially empty).
You may perform the following operations until both a and s are empty:
Take the first element of a, push it into s and remove it from a (if a is not empty);
Take the top element from s, append it to the end of array b and remove it from s (if s is not empty).
You can perform these operations in arbitrary order.
If there exists a way to perform the operations such that array b is sorted in non-descending order in the end, then array a is called stack-sortable.
For example, [3, 1, 2] is stack-sortable, because b will be sorted if we perform the following operations:
Remove 3 from a and push it into s;
Remove 1 from a and push it into s;
Remove 1 from s and append it to the end of b;
Remove 2 from a and push it into s;
Remove 2 from s and append it to the end of b;
Remove 3 from s and append it to the end of b.
After all these operations b = [1, 2, 3], so [3, 1, 2] is stack-sortable. [2, 3, 1] is not stack-sortable.

You are given k first elements of some permutation p of size n (recall that a permutation of size n is an array of size n where each integer from 1 to n occurs exactly once). You have to restore the remaining n - k elements of this permutation so it is stack-sortable. If there are multiple answers, choose the answer such that p is lexicographically maximal (an array q is lexicographically greater than an array p iff there exists some integer k such that for every i < k qi = pi, and qk > pk). You may not swap or change any of first k elements of the permutation.
Print the lexicographically maximal permutation p you can obtain.
If there exists no answer then output -1.
input: The first line contains two integers n and k (2 ≤ n ≤ 200000, 1 ≤ k < n) — the size of a desired permutation, and the number of elements you are given, respectively.
The second line contains k integers p1, p2, ..., pk (1 ≤ pi ≤ n) — the first k elements of p. These integers are pairwise distinct.
output: If it is possible to restore a stack-sortable permutation p of size n such that the first k elements of p are equal to elements given in the input, print lexicographically maximal such permutation.
Otherwise print -1.

legend.ai: 假设有一个数组 a、一个栈 s（初始为空）以及一个数组 b（同样初始为空）。
在 a 和 s 均为空之前，你可以执行以下操作：
取出 a 的第一个元素，将其压入 s，并从 a 中移除（如果 a 不为空）；
取出 s 的栈顶元素，将其追加到数组 b 的末尾，并从 s 中移除（如果 s 不为空）。
你可以按任意顺序执行这些操作。
如果存在一种执行操作的方式，使得最终数组 b 按非递减顺序排序，则称数组 a 是栈可排序的。
例如，[3, 1, 2] 是栈可排序的，因为如果我们执行以下操作，b 将被排序：
从 a 中移除 3 并将其压入 s；
从 a 中移除 1，并将其压入 s；
从 s 中移除 1，并将其追加到 b 的末尾；
从 a 中移除 2，并将其压入 s；
从 s 中移除 2，并将其追加到 b 的末尾；
从 s 中移除 3，并将其追加到 b 的末尾。
完成所有这些操作后，b = [1, 2, 3]，因此 [3, 1, 2] 是可栈排序的。[2, 3, 1] 不是可栈排序的。

给定某个大小为 n 的排列 p 的前 k 个元素（回忆一下，大小为 n 的排列是一个大小为 n 的数组，其中 1 到 n 的每个整数恰好出现一次）。你需要补全这个排列剩余的 n-k 个元素，使得它是一个栈可排序的排列。如果存在多个答案，选择使 p 字典序最大的答案（当且仅当存在某个整数 k，使得对所有 i<k 有 qi=pi，且 qk>pk 时，数组 q 的字典序大于数组 p）。你不能交换或修改排列的前 k 个元素。
输出你能得到的字典序最大的排列 p。
如果不存在答案，则输出 -1。

input.ai: 第一行包含两个整数 n 和 k（2≤n≤200000，1≤k<n），分别表示所需排列的大小和你被给定的元素个数。
第二行包含 k 个整数 p1, p2, ..., pk（1≤pi≤n），即 p 的前 k 个元素。这些整数两两互不相同。

output.ai: 如果能够补全一个大小为 n 的栈可排序排列 p，使得 p 的前 k 个元素与输入中给出的元素相等，则输出字典序最大的这样的排列。
否则输出 -1。

legend: Mahmoud wrote a message s of length n. He wants to send it as a birthday present to his friend Moaz who likes strings. He wrote it on a magical paper but he was surprised because some characters disappeared while writing the string. That's because this magical paper doesn't allow character number i in the English alphabet to be written on it in a string of length more than ai. For example, if a1 = 2 he can't write character 'a' on this paper in a string of length 3 or more. String "aa" is allowed while string "aaa" is not.

Mahmoud decided to split the message into some non-empty substrings so that he can write every substring on an independent magical paper and fulfill the condition. The sum of their lengths should be n and they shouldn't overlap. For example, if a1 = 2 and he wants to send string "aaa", he can split it into "a" and "aa" and use 2 magical papers, or into "a", "a" and "a" and use 3 magical papers. He can't split it into "aa" and "aa" because the sum of their lengths is greater than n. He can split the message into single string if it fulfills the conditions.

A substring of string s is a string that consists of some consecutive characters from string s, strings "ab", "abc" and "b" are substrings of string "abc", while strings "acb" and "ac" are not. Any string is a substring of itself.
While Mahmoud was thinking of how to split the message, Ehab told him that there are many ways to split it. After that Mahmoud asked you three questions:

How many ways are there to split the string into substrings such that every substring fulfills the condition of the magical paper, the sum of their lengths is n and they don't overlap? Compute the answer modulo 109 + 7.
What is the maximum length of a substring that can appear in some valid splitting?
What is the minimum number of substrings the message can be spit in?
Two ways are considered different, if the sets of split positions differ. For example, splitting "aa|a" and "a|aa" are considered different splittings of message "aaa".
input: The first line contains an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 103) denoting the length of the message.
The second line contains the message s of length n that consists of lowercase English letters.
The third line contains 26 integers a1, a2, ..., a26 (1 ≤ ax ≤ 103) — the maximum lengths of substring each letter can appear in.
output: Print three lines.
In the first line print the number of ways to split the message into substrings and fulfill the conditions mentioned in the problem modulo 109  +  7.
In the second line print the length of the longest substring over all the ways.
In the third line print the minimum number of substrings over all the ways.
note: In the first example the three ways to split the message are:
a|a|b
aa|b
a|ab
The longest substrings are "aa" and "ab" of length 2.
The minimum number of substrings is 2 in "a|ab" or "aa|b".
Notice that "aab" is not a possible splitting because the letter 'a' appears in a substring of length 3, while a1 = 2.

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，将消息划分的三种方案为：
a|a|b
aa|b
a|ab
最长的子串是长度为 2 的 "aa" 和 "ab"。
在 "a|ab" 或 "aa|b" 中，子串数量的最小值为 2。

legend.ai: Mahmoud 写了一条长度为 n 的消息 s。他想把它作为生日礼物送给喜欢字符串的朋友 Moaz。他把消息写在一张魔法纸上，但在书写字符串时，他惊讶地发现有些字符消失了。这是因为这张魔法纸不允许在长度大于 a_i 的字符串中写入英文字母表中的第 i 个字符。例如，如果 a_1=2，那么在长度为 3 或更长的字符串中，他就无法在这张纸上写字符 'a'。字符串 "aa" 是允许的，而字符串 "aaa" 不允许。

Mahmoud 决定将这条消息划分成若干个非空子串，这样他就能把每个子串分别写在一张独立的魔法纸上，并满足条件。所有子串的长度之和应为 n，且它们不能重叠。例如，如果 a_1=2，且他想发送字符串 "aaa"，那么他可以将其划分为 "a" 和 "aa"，使用 2 张魔法纸；也可以划分为 "a"、"a" 和 "a"，使用 3 张魔法纸。他不能将其划分为 "aa" 和 "aa"，因为它们的长度之和大于 n。如果整条消息满足条件，他也可以不进行划分。
字符串 s 的子串是由 s 中某些连续字符组成的字符串。字符串 "ab"、"abc" 和 "b" 是字符串 "abc" 的子串，而字符串 "acb" 和 "ac" 不是。任何字符串都是其自身的子串。
Mahmoud 正在思考如何划分这条消息时，Ehab 告诉他有许多种划分方式。于是 Mahmoud 向你提出了三个问题：
有多少种方法可以将字符串划分成若干子串，使得每个子串都满足魔法纸的条件、所有子串的长度之和为 n 且它们互不重叠？请计算答案对 109 + 7 取模的结果。
在某种合法划分中可能出现的子串的最大长度是多少？
这条消息最少可以被划分成多少个子串？
如果划分位置的集合不同，则认为两种划分不同。例如，将消息“aaa”划分为“aa|a”和“a|aa”被认为是两种不同的划分。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 10^3），表示消息的长度。

legend: One beautiful day Vasily the bear painted 2m circles of the same radius R on a coordinate plane. Naturally, the bear painted the circles for a simple experiment with a fly. The experiment continued for m2 days. Each day of the experiment got its own unique number from 0 to m2 - 1, inclusive.
On the day number i the following things happened:

The fly arrived at the coordinate plane at the center of the circle with number ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b3df97a98dd984c03bd53b2f4c4c7288bd321ddc.png) (![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/1d85d9be5f5d8cb39c28e7277ba0b39c3ccd4f0e.png) is the result of dividing number x by number y, rounded down to an integer).

The fly went along the coordinate plane to the center of the circle number ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ce2bb6c4a4ddae405ec27cce4e3cfeaee3958192.png) (![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/f58f159973d4609d919286c1821e69cd34d81118.png) is the remainder after dividing number x by number y). The bear noticed that the fly went from the center of circle v to the center of circle u along the shortest path with all points lying on the border or inside at least one of the 2m circles. After the fly reached the center of circle u, it flew away in an unknown direction.
Help Vasily, count the average distance the fly went along the coordinate plane during each of these m2 days.

legend: The Berland's capital has the form of a rectangle with sizes n × m quarters. All quarters are divided into three types:
regular (labeled with the character '.') — such quarters do not produce the noise but are not obstacles to the propagation of the noise;
sources of noise (labeled with an uppercase Latin letter from 'A' to 'Z') — such quarters are noise sources and are not obstacles to the propagation of the noise;
heavily built-up (labeled with the character '*') — such quarters are soundproofed, the noise does not penetrate into them and they themselves are obstacles to the propagation of noise.

A quarter labeled with letter 'A' produces q units of noise. A quarter labeled with letter 'B' produces 2·q units of noise. And so on, up to a quarter labeled with letter 'Z', which produces 26·q units of noise. There can be any number of quarters labeled with each letter in the city.

When propagating from the source of the noise, the noise level is halved when moving from one quarter to a quarter that shares a side with it (when an odd number is to be halved, it's rounded down). The noise spreads along the chain. For example, if some quarter is located at a distance 2 from the noise source, then the value of noise which will reach the quarter is divided by 4. So the noise level that comes from the source to the quarter is determined solely by the length of the shortest path between them. Heavily built-up quarters are obstacles, the noise does not penetrate into them.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/985e6cfcaf374bf2c1080c5819a7f73a7658a14d.png)

The noise level in quarter is defined as the sum of the noise from all sources. To assess the quality of life of the population of the capital of Berland, it is required to find the number of quarters whose noise level exceeds the allowed level p.

Each of the following n lines contains m characters — the description of the capital quarters, in the format that was described in the statement above. It is possible that in the Berland's capital there are no quarters of any type.

噪声从噪声源传播时，每移动到一个与当前街区共边的街区，噪声级就会减半（当一个奇数除以 2 时，向下取整）。噪声会沿着这条链传播。例如，如果某个街区与噪声源的距离为 2，那么传到该街区的噪声值会除以 4。因此，噪声源传播到某个街区的噪声级只取决于两者之间最短路径的长度。建筑密集的街区是障碍物，噪声无法穿透它们。

legend: Sereja loves number sequences very much. That's why he decided to make himself a new one following a certain algorithm.

Sereja takes a blank piece of paper. Then he starts writing out the sequence in m stages. Each time he either adds a new number to the end of the sequence or takes l first elements of the current sequence and adds them c times to the end. More formally, if we represent the current sequence as a1, a2, ..., an, then after we apply the described operation, the sequence transforms into a1, a2, ..., an[, a1, a2, ..., al] (the block in the square brackets must be repeated c times).
A day has passed and Sereja has completed the sequence. He wonders what are the values of some of its elements. Help Sereja.

Next m lines contain the description of the stages in the order they follow. The first number in the line is a type of stage (1 or 2). Type 1 means adding one number to the end of the sequence, in this case the line contains integer xi (1 ≤ xi ≤ 105) — the number to add. Type 2 means copying a prefix of length li to the end ci times, in this case the line further contains two integers li, ci (1 ≤ li ≤ 105, 1 ≤ ci ≤ 104), li is the length of the prefix, ci is the number of copyings. It is guaranteed that the length of prefix li is never larger than the current length of the sequence.

The next line contains integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 105) — the number of elements Sereja is interested in. The next line contains the numbers of elements of the final sequence Sereja is interested in. The numbers are given in the strictly increasing order. It is guaranteed that all numbers are strictly larger than zero and do not exceed the length of the resulting sequence. Consider the elements of the final sequence numbered starting from 1 from the beginning to the end of the sequence.
Please, do not use the %lld specifier to read or write 64-bit integers in С++. It is preferred to use the cin, cout streams or the %I64d specifier.
output: Print the elements that Sereja is interested in, in the order in which their numbers occur in the input.

legend.ai: 道馆馆主们对在 Felicity 营地发生的进化过程十分着迷。因此，他们想知道宝可梦进化背后的秘密。
营地的组织者给了道馆馆主们一个 PokeBlock，它是由 n 个成分组成的序列。每个成分的类型可以是 0 或 1。组织者告诉道馆馆主们，要使一只类型为 k（k ≥ 2）的宝可梦进化，他们需要在 PokeBlock 上进行 k 次有效切割，从而得到更小的方块。
假设给定的 PokeBlock 序列为 b₀b₁b₂...bₙ - ₁。你可以选择在 n + 1 个位置进行切割，即 b₀ 之前、b₀ 和 b₁ 之间、b₁ 和 b₂ 之间、……、bₙ - ₂ 和 bₙ - ₁ 之间，以及 bₙ - ₁ 之后。
n + 1 个可切割位置如下（其中 | 表示一个可能的切割位置）：
考虑一组 k 次切割。现在，每一对相邻切割之间都会包含一个由成分类型组成的二进制字符串。第一次切割之前和最后一次切割之后的成分会被浪费，也就是说它们不予考虑。因此，恰好会有 k - 1 个这样的二进制子串。每个子串都可以看作一个二进制数。令 m 为得到的这些数中的最大值。如果所有得到的数都是正数，并且得到的数的集合包含从 1 到 m 的所有整数，那么这组切割就称为一组有效切割。
例如，假设给定的 PokeBlock 序列为 101101001110，并按如下方式进行了 5 次切割：
因此得到的 4 个二进制子串为：11、010、01 和 1，它们分别对应数字 3、2、1 和 1。这里 m = 3，因为它是得到的数字中的最大值。并且所有得到的数字都是正数，我们得到了从 1 到 m 的所有整数。因此，这组切点是一个有效的 5 个切点集合。
类型为 k 的宝可梦只有在使用包含 k 个切点的有效集合切割 PokeBlock 时才会进化。相同大小的有效集合可能有很多个。如果一个集合中存在某个切点，而另一个集合中不存在，则这两个包含 k 个切点的有效集合被视为不同。
令 f(k) 表示包含 k 个切点的有效集合数量。求 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/1f553c10ee29622384beda9934a033e929407c9c.png) 的值。由于 s 的值可能非常大，请输出 s 对 109 + 7 取模的结果。

legend: Vasya and Kolya play a game with a string, using the following rules. Initially, Kolya creates a string s, consisting of small English letters, and uniformly at random chooses an integer k from a segment [0, len(s) - 1]. He tells Vasya this string s, and then shifts it k letters to the left, i. e. creates a new string t = sk + 1sk + 2... sns1s2... sk. Vasya does not know the integer k nor the string t, but he wants to guess the integer k. To do this, he asks Kolya to tell him the first letter of the new string, and then, after he sees it, open one more letter on some position, which Vasya can choose.
Vasya understands, that he can't guarantee that he will win, but he wants to know the probability of winning, if he plays optimally. He wants you to compute this probability.

Note that Vasya wants to know the value of k uniquely, it means, that if there are at least two cyclic shifts of s that fit the information Vasya knowns, Vasya loses. Of course, at any moment of the game Vasya wants to maximize the probability of his win.

legend: You are currently researching a graph traversal algorithm called the Breadth First Search (BFS). Suppose you have an input graph of N$$$N$$$ nodes (numbered from 1$$$1$$$ to N$$$N$$$). The graph is represented by an adjacency matrix M$$$M$$$, for which node u$$$u$$$ can traverse to node v$$$v$$$ if Mu,v$$$M_{u, v}$$$ is 1$$$1$$$, otherwise it is 0$$$0$$$. Your algorithm will output the order the nodes are visited in the BFS. The pseudocode of the algorithm is presented as follows.

legend.pre:
BFS(M[1..N][1..N]):
        let A be an empty array
        let Q be an empty queue

        append 1 to A
        push 1 to Q

        while Q is not empty:
            pop the front element of Q into u
            for v = 1 to N:
                if M[u][v] == 1 and v is not in A:
                    append v to A
                    push v to Q

        return A

problems.hint: We should find the first position after the decimal point which is no smaller than $5$ .

legend: Efim just received his grade for the last test. He studies in a special school and his grade can be equal to any positive decimal fraction. First he got disappointed, as he expected a way more pleasant result. Then, he developed a tricky plan. Each second, he can ask his teacher to round the grade at any place after the decimal point (also, he can ask to round to the nearest integer).

There are t seconds left till the end of the break, so Efim has to act fast. Help him find what is the maximum grade he can get in no more than t seconds. Note, that he can choose to not use all t seconds. Moreover, he can even choose to not round the grade at all.

In this problem, classic rounding rules are used: while rounding number to the n-th digit one has to take a look at the digit n + 1. If it is less than 5 than the n-th digit remain unchanged while all subsequent digits are replaced with 0. Otherwise, if the n + 1 digit is greater or equal to 5, the digit at the position n is increased by 1 (this might also change some other digits, if this one was equal to 9) and all subsequent digits are replaced with 0. At the end, all trailing zeroes are thrown away.

For example, if the number 1.14 is rounded to the first decimal place, the result is 1.1, while if we round 1.5 to the nearest integer, the result is 2. Rounding number 1.299996121 in the fifth decimal place will result in number 1.3.
input: The first line of the input contains two integers n and t (1 ≤ n ≤ 200 000, 1 ≤ t ≤ 109) — the length of Efim's grade and the number of seconds till the end of the break respectively.
The second line contains the grade itself. It's guaranteed that the grade is a positive number, containing at least one digit after the decimal points, and it's representation doesn't finish with 0.
output: Print the maximum grade that Efim can get in t seconds. Do not print trailing zeroes.
note: In the first two samples Efim initially has grade 10.245.
During the first second Efim can obtain grade 10.25, and then 10.3 during the next second. Note, that the answer 10.30 will be considered incorrect.
In the third sample the optimal strategy is to not perform any rounding at all.

note.ai: 在前两个样例中，Efim 初始成绩为 10.245。
在第一秒内，Efim 可以得到 10.25 的成绩，接着在下一秒内得到 10.3。注意，答案 10.30 将被判定为错误。
在第三个样例中，最优策略是完全不进行任何舍入。

legend.ai: Efim 刚刚收到了上次考试的成绩。他就读于一所特殊学校，他的成绩可以是任意正的十进制小数。起初他很失望，因为他原本期待一个愉快得多的结果。然后，他制定了一个巧妙的计划。每秒钟，他都可以请求老师将成绩在小数点后的任意位置进行四舍五入（也可以请求将其四舍五入到最接近的整数）。
距离休息结束还剩 t 秒，因此 Efim 必须迅速行动。请帮助他找出在不超过 t 秒内能够获得的最高成绩。注意，他可以选择不使用全部 t 秒。此外，他甚至可以选择完全不进行四舍五入。
本题使用经典的四舍五入规则：将一个数舍入到第 n 位时，需要查看第 n+1 位。如果它小于 5，则第 n 位保持不变，并将其后的所有位替换为 0。否则，如果第 n+1 位大于等于 5，则第 n 位加 1（如果该位原本为 9，这还可能导致其他位发生变化），并将其后的所有位替换为 0。最后，去掉所有末尾的 0。
例如，将数字 1.14 舍入到小数点后第一位时，结果为 1.1；而将 1.5 舍入到最接近的整数时，结果为 2。将数字 1.299996121 舍入到小数点后第五位，结果为 1.3。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含两个整数 n 和 t（1 ≤ n ≤ 200 000，1 ≤ t ≤ 109），分别表示 Efim 的成绩长度以及距离休息结束所剩的秒数。
第二行包含成绩本身。保证该成绩为正数，小数点后至少包含一位数字，且其表示形式不以 0 结尾。

output.ai: 输出 Efim 在 t 秒内能够获得的最高成绩。不要输出末尾的 0。
