problems.hint: Consider the problem in DFS. It's about checking the number of occurences of string $t$ in $s$ when adding or removing a last character.

legend: A rooted tree is a non-directed connected graph without any cycles with a distinguished vertex, which is called the tree root. Consider the vertices of a rooted tree, that consists of n vertices, numbered from 1 to n. In this problem the tree root is the vertex number 1.
Let's represent the length of the shortest by the number of edges path in the tree between vertices v and u as d(v, u).

A parent of vertex v in the rooted tree with the root in vertex r (v ≠ r) is vertex pv, such that d(r, pv) + 1 = d(r, v) and d(pv, v) = 1. For example, on the picture the parent of vertex v = 5 is vertex p5 = 2.

One day Polycarpus came across a rooted tree, consisting of n vertices. The tree wasn't exactly ordinary: it had strings written on its edges. Polycarpus positioned the tree on the plane so as to make all edges lead from top to bottom if you go from the vertex parent to the vertex (see the picture). For any edge that lead from vertex pv to vertex v (1 < v ≤ n), he knows string sv that is written on it. All strings are written on the edges from top to bottom. For example, on the picture s7="ba". The characters in the strings are numbered starting from 0.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/2358a87b1302583cb41f1d8aa514a32b02f411ec.png)

Polycarpus defines the position in this tree as a specific letter on a specific string. The position is written as a pair of integers (v, x) that means that the position is the x-th letter of the string sv (1 < v ≤ n, 0 ≤ x < |sv|), where |sv| is the length of string sv. For example, the highlighted letters are positions (2, 1) and (3, 1).

Let's consider the pair of positions (v, x) and (u, y) in Polycarpus' tree, such that the way from the first position to the second goes down on each step. We will consider that the pair of such positions defines string z. String z consists of all letters on the way from (v, x) to (u, y), written in the order of this path. For example, in the picture the highlighted positions define string "bacaba".

Polycarpus has a string t, he wants to know the number of pairs of positions that define string t. Note that the way from the first position to the second in the pair must go down everywhere. Help him with this challenging tree-string problem!
input: The first line contains integer n (2 ≤ n ≤ 105) — the number of vertices of Polycarpus's tree. Next n - 1 lines contain the tree edges. The i-th of them contains number pi + 1 and string si + 1 (1 ≤ pi + 1 ≤ n; pi + 1 ≠ (i + 1)). String si + 1 is non-empty and consists of lowercase English letters. The last line contains string t. String t consists of lowercase English letters, its length is at least 2.
It is guaranteed that the input contains at most 3·105 English letters.
output: Print a single integer — the required number.
Please, do not use the %lld specifier to read or write 64-bit integers in С++. It is preferred to use the cin, cout streams or the %I64d specifier.
note: In the first test case string "aba" is determined by the pairs of positions: (2, 0) and (5, 0); (5, 2) and (6, 1); (5, 2) and (3, 1); (4, 0) and (4, 2); (4, 4) and (4, 6); (3, 3) and (3, 5).
Note that the string is not defined by the pair of positions (7, 1) and (5, 0), as the way between them doesn't always go down.

1 ab
5 bacaba
1 abacaba
2 aca
5 ba

aba

1 abacaba
2 aca
5 ba

legend.ai: 有根树是一个无向连通且无环的图，其中有一个指定的顶点，称为树根。考虑一棵由 n 个顶点组成的有根树，其顶点编号为 1 到 n。在本题中，树根是编号为 1 的顶点。
将树中顶点 v 和 u 之间最短路径的边数记为 d(v, u)。
在根为顶点 r 的有根树中，对于 v ≠ r，顶点 v 的父节点是顶点 p_v，满足 d(r, p_v) + 1 = d(r, v) 且 d(p_v, v) = 1。例如，在图中，顶点 v = 5 的父节点是顶点 p_5 = 2。

一天，Polycarpus 遇到了一棵由 n 个顶点组成的有根树。这棵树并不完全普通：它的边上写有字符串。Polycarpus 将这棵树放置在平面上，使得从父节点走向子节点时，所有边都从上到下延伸（见图）。对于从顶点 p_v 到顶点 v 的任意一条边（1 < v ≤ n），他知道边上写着的字符串 s_v。所有字符串都沿着从上到下的方向写在边上。例如，在图中，s_7 = "ba"。字符串中的字符编号从 0 开始。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/2358a87b1302583cb41f1d8aa514a32b02f411ec.png)
Polycarpus 将树中的一个位置定义为某个字符串中的一个特定字符。位置表示为一对整数 (v, x)，表示该位置是字符串 s_v 中的第 x 个字符（1 < v ≤ n，0 ≤ x < |s_v|），其中 |s_v| 是字符串 s_v 的长度。例如，图中标出的字符对应的位置为 (2, 1) 和 (3, 1)。
考虑 Polycarpus 的树中的两个位置 (v, x) 和 (u, y)，并且从第一个位置到第二个位置的路径在每一步都向下。我们称这样的一对位置定义了字符串 z。字符串 z 由从 (v, x) 到 (u, y) 的路径上的所有字符组成，并按照路径经过的顺序排列。例如，在图中，标出的位置定义了字符串 "bacaba"。
Polycarpus 有一个字符串 t，他想知道有多少对位置能够定义字符串 t。注意，一对位置中从第一个位置到第二个位置的路径必须始终向下。请帮助他解决这个具有挑战性的树上字符串问题！

input.ai: 第一行包含整数 n（2 ≤ n ≤ 10^5）——Polycarpus 的树的顶点数。接下来的 n - 1 行包含树的边。其中第 i 行包含数字 p_{i+1} 和字符串 s_{i+1}（1 ≤ p_{i+1} ≤ n；p_{i+1} ≠ (i + 1)）。字符串 s_{i+1} 非空，由小写英文字母组成。最后一行包含字符串 t。字符串 t 由小写英文字母组成，长度至少为 2。
保证输入中至多包含 3·10^5 个英文字母。

output.ai: 输出一个整数——所求的数量。
请不要在 C++ 中使用 %lld 格式说明符来读写 64 位整数。建议使用 cin、cout 流，或使用 %I64d 格式说明符。

note.ai: 注意，位置对 (7, 1) 和 (5, 0) 并不能定义该字符串，因为它们之间的路径并不总是向下。

legend: In Berland there are n cities and n - 1 bidirectional roads. Each road connects some pair of cities, from any city you can get to any other one using only the given roads.

In each city there is exactly one repair brigade. To repair some road, you need two teams based in the cities connected by the road to work simultaneously for one day. Both brigades repair one road for the whole day and cannot take part in repairing other roads on that day. But the repair brigade can do nothing on that day.
Determine the minimum number of days needed to repair all the roads. The brigades cannot change the cities where they initially are.
input: The first line of the input contains a positive integer n (2 ≤ n ≤ 200 000) — the number of cities in Berland.
Each of the next n - 1 lines contains two numbers ui, vi, meaning that the i-th road connects city ui and city vi (1 ≤ ui, vi ≤ n, ui ≠ vi).
output: First print number k — the minimum number of days needed to repair all the roads in Berland.

In next k lines print the description of the roads that should be repaired on each of the k days. On the i-th line print first number di — the number of roads that should be repaired on the i-th day, and then di space-separated integers — the numbers of the roads that should be repaired on the i-th day. The roads are numbered according to the order in the input, starting from one.
If there are multiple variants, you can print any of them.
note: In the first sample you can repair all the roads in two days, for example, if you repair roads 1 and 2 on the first day and road 3 — on the second day.

legend.ai: 在 Berland 中有 n 个城市和 n−1 条双向道路。每条道路连接一对城市，仅使用给定的道路即可从任意城市到达任意其他城市。
每个城市恰好有一支维修队。要维修一条道路，需要道路两端城市的两支维修队同时工作一天。两支维修队需要花费一整天维修同一条道路，并且当天不能参与其他道路的维修。不过，维修队也可以在当天什么都不做。
请确定维修所有道路所需的最少天数。维修队不能更换它们最初所在的城市。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含一个正整数 n（2 ≤ n ≤ 200000）——Berland 的城市数。
接下来的 n−1 行中，每行包含两个数 u_i、v_i，表示第 i 条道路连接城市 u_i 和城市 v_i（1 ≤ u_i，v_i ≤ n，u_i ≠ v_i）。

output.ai: 首先输出整数 k——修复 Berland 中所有道路所需的最少天数。
接下来的 k 行中，输出每一天应修复的道路描述。第 i 行首先输出整数 d_i——第 i 天应修复的道路数量，然后输出 d_i 个以空格分隔的整数——第 i 天应修复的道路编号。道路按照输入中的顺序编号，从 1 开始。
如果有多种方案，你可以输出其中任意一种。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，你可以用两天修复所有道路。例如，第一天修复道路 1 和 2，第二天修复道路 3。

problems.hint: Solve the equation first.

legend: There is an old tradition of keeping 4 boxes of candies in the house in Cyberland. The numbers of candies are special if their arithmetic mean, their median and their range are all equal. By definition, for a set {x1, x2, x3, x4} (x1 ≤ x2 ≤ x3 ≤ x4) arithmetic mean is ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/daeb25d0b520beaea095158d4851903f527ffafc.png), median is ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7655b731471163052bb5fbb4c5414c495a2ca2e2.png) and range is x4 - x1. The arithmetic mean and median are not necessary integer. It is well-known that if those three numbers are same, boxes will create a "debugging field" and codes in the field will have no bugs.
For example, 1, 1, 3, 3 is the example of 4 numbers meeting the condition because their mean, median and range are all equal to 2.

Jeff has 4 special boxes of candies. However, something bad has happened! Some of the boxes could have been lost and now there are only n (0 ≤ n ≤ 4) boxes remaining. The i-th remaining box contains ai candies.
Now Jeff wants to know: is there a possible way to find the number of candies of the 4 - n missing boxes, meeting the condition above (the mean, median and range are equal)?
input: The first line of input contains an only integer n (0 ≤ n ≤ 4).
The next n lines contain integers ai, denoting the number of candies in the i-th box (1 ≤ ai ≤ 500).
output: In the first output line, print "YES" if a solution exists, or print "NO" if there is no solution.
If a solution exists, you should output 4 - n more lines, each line containing an integer b, denoting the number of candies in a missing box.

All your numbers b must satisfy inequality 1 ≤ b ≤ 106. It is guaranteed that if there exists a positive integer solution, you can always find such b's meeting the condition. If there are multiple answers, you are allowed to print any of them.
Given numbers ai may follow in any order in the input, not necessary in non-decreasing.
ai may have stood at any positions in the original set, not necessary on lowest n first positions.
note: For the first sample, the numbers of candies in 4 boxes can be 1, 1, 3, 3. The arithmetic mean, the median and the range of them are all 2.
For the second sample, it's impossible to find the missing number of candies.
In the third example no box has been lost and numbers satisfy the condition.
You may output b in any order.

output.ai: 如果存在解，在输出的第一行打印“YES”；如果不存在解，则打印“NO”。
如果存在解，你应该再输出 4 - n 行，每行包含一个整数 b，表示某个缺失盒子中的糖果数量。
你的所有数字 b 必须满足不等式 1 ≤ b ≤ 10^6。保证如果存在正整数解，你总能找到满足条件的这样的 b。如果有多组答案，你可以输出其中任意一组。
给定的数 ai 在输入中可能以任意顺序出现，不一定是非递减的。
ai 在原集合中可能位于任意位置，不一定在前 n 个最小的位置上。

note.ai: 对于第一个样例，4 个盒子中的糖果数量可以是 1, 1, 3, 3。它们的算术平均数、中位数和极差都为 2。
对于第二个样例，不可能找到缺失的糖果数量。
在第三个样例中，没有盒子丢失，并且数字满足条件。
你可以以任意顺序输出 b。

legend.ai: Cyberland 有一个古老的传统：在家中存放 4 盒糖果。如果糖果数量的算术平均数、中位数和极差都相等，那么这些糖果数量就是特殊的。根据定义，对于集合 {x1, x2, x3, x4}(x1 ≤ x2 ≤ x3 ≤ x4)，算术平均数为 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/daeb25d0b520beaea095158d4851903f527ffafc.png)，中位数为 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7655b731471163052bb5fbb4c5414c495a2ca2e2.png)，极差为 x4 - x1。算术平均数和中位数不一定是整数。众所周知，如果这三个数相同，这些盒子就会产生一个“调试场”，场中的代码将不会有任何错误。
例如，1、1、3、3 是满足条件的 4 个数的一个例子，因为它们的平均数、中位数和极差都等于 2。
Jeff 有 4 个装有糖果的特殊盒子。然而，发生了一件糟糕的事情！其中一些盒子可能丢失了，现在只剩下 n（0 ≤ n ≤ 4）个盒子。第 i 个剩余的盒子中有 ai 颗糖果。
现在 Jeff 想知道：是否存在一种方案，确定丢失的 4 − n 个盒子中的糖果数量，并满足上述条件（平均数、中位数和极差相等）？

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含一个整数 n（0 ≤ n ≤ 4）。
接下来的 n 行每行包含一个整数 ai，表示第 i 个盒子中糖果的数量（1 ≤ ai ≤ 500）。

problems.hint: When a vertex connects with its previous vertex in the shortest path, a tree is formed.

legend: Valera had an undirected connected graph without self-loops and multiple edges consisting of n vertices. The graph had an interesting property: there were at most k edges adjacent to each of its vertices. For convenience, we will assume that the graph vertices were indexed by integers from 1 to n.

One day Valera counted the shortest distances from one of the graph vertices to all other ones and wrote them out in array d. Thus, element d[i] of the array shows the shortest distance from the vertex Valera chose to vertex number i.
Then something irreparable terrible happened. Valera lost the initial graph. However, he still has the array d. Help him restore the lost graph.
input: The first line contains two space-separated integers n and k (1 ≤ k < n ≤ 105). Number n shows the number of vertices in the original graph. Number k shows that at most k edges were adjacent to each vertex in the original graph.
The second line contains space-separated integers d[1], d[2], ..., d[n] (0 ≤ d[i] < n). Number d[i] shows the shortest distance from the vertex Valera chose to the vertex number i.
output: If Valera made a mistake in his notes and the required graph doesn't exist, print in the first line number -1. Otherwise, in the first line print integer m (0 ≤ m ≤ 106) — the number of edges in the found graph.

In each of the next m lines print two space-separated integers ai and bi (1 ≤ ai, bi ≤ n; ai ≠ bi), denoting the edge that connects vertices with numbers ai and bi. The graph shouldn't contain self-loops and multiple edges. If there are multiple possible answers, print any of them.

legend.ai: Valera 有一个无向连通图，该图不含自环和重边，由 n 个顶点组成。这个图具有一个有趣的性质：与它的每个顶点相邻的边最多有 k 条。为方便起见，我们假设图中的顶点编号为 1 到 n 的整数。
一天，Valera 计算了图中某个顶点到所有其他顶点的最短距离，并将它们写在数组 d 中。因此，数组中的元素 d[i] 表示 Valera 所选顶点到编号为 i 的顶点的最短距离。
后来发生了一件可怕且无法挽回的事情。Valera 丢失了初始图。不过，他仍然有数组 d。请帮助他恢复丢失的图。

input.ai: 第一行包含两个用空格分隔的整数 n 和 k（1 ≤ k < n ≤ 10^5）。整数 n 表示原图中的顶点数。整数 k 表示原图中每个顶点至多与 k 条边相邻。
第二行包含用空格分隔的整数 d[1]、d[2]、...、d[n]（0 ≤ d[i] < n）。整数 d[i] 表示从 Valera 选择的顶点到编号为 i 的顶点的最短距离。

output.ai: 如果 Valera 在笔记中出错，所要求的图不存在，则在第一行输出 -1。否则，在第一行输出整数 m（0 ≤ m ≤ 10^6）——构造出的图中的边数。
接下来的 m 行中，每行输出两个用空格分隔的整数 ai 和 bi（1 ≤ ai, bi ≤ n；ai ≠ bi），表示连接编号为 ai 和 bi 的顶点的边。图中不应包含自环和重边。如果有多个可行答案，输出任意一个即可。

problems.hint: Turn $b$ all into $n$ , then each $a$ is not coprime to $n$ and sums up to $n-1$ .

legend: You are given a positive integer n$$$n$$$.
Find a sequence of fractions aibi$$$\frac{a_i}{b_i}$$$, i=1…k$$$i = 1 \ldots k$$$ (where ai$$$a_i$$$ and bi$$$b_i$$$ are positive integers) for some k$$$k$$$ such that:

{bi divides n, 1<bi<n for i=1…k1≤ai<bi for i=1…kk∑i=1aibi=1−1n$$ \begin{cases} \text{$b_i$ divides $n$, $1  \lt  b_i  \lt  n$ for $i = 1 \ldots k$} \\ \text{$1 \le a_i  \lt  b_i$ for $i = 1 \ldots k$} \\ \text{$\sum\limits_{i=1}^k \frac{a_i}{b_i} = 1 - \frac{1}{n}$} \end{cases} $$
input: The input consists of a single integer n$$$n$$$ (2≤n≤109$$$2 \le n \le 10^9$$$).
output: In the first line print "YES" if there exists such a sequence of fractions or "NO" otherwise.
If there exists such a sequence, next lines should contain a description of the sequence in the following format.

The second line should contain integer k$$$k$$$ (1≤k≤100000$$$1 \le k \le 100\,000$$$) — the number of elements in the sequence. It is guaranteed that if such a sequence exists, then there exists a sequence of length at most 100000$$$100\,000$$$.
Next k$$$k$$$ lines should contain fractions of the sequence with two integers ai$$$a_i$$$ and bi$$$b_i$$$ on each line.
note: In the second example there is a sequence 12,13$$$\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{3}$$$ such that 12+13=1−16$$$\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3} = 1 - \frac{1}{6}$$$.

legend.ai: 给定一个正整数 n$$$n$$$。
找到一个分数序列 aibi$$$\frac{a_i}{b_i}$$$，i=1…k$$$i = 1 \ldots k$$$(其中 ai$$$a_i$$$ 和 bi$$$b_i$$$ 为正整数)，对于某个 k$$$k$$$，满足：

{bi 整除 n，1<bi<n(i=1…k)；1≤ai<bi(i=1…k)；∑i=1aibi=1−1n$$ \begin{cases} \text{$b_i$ divides $n$, $1  \lt  b_i  \lt  n$ for $i = 1 \ldots k$} \\ \text{$1 \le a_i  \lt  b_i$ for $i = 1 \ldots k$} \\ \text{$\sum\limits_{i=1}^k \frac{a_i}{b_i} = 1 - \frac{1}{n}$} \end{cases} $$

output.ai: 如果存在这样的分数序列，第一行输出 "YES"；否则输出 "NO"。
如果存在这样的序列，接下来的若干行应按照以下格式描述该序列。
第二行应包含整数 k$$$k$$$(1≤k≤100000$$$1 \le k \le 100\,000$$$)——序列中元素的数量。保证如果存在这样的序列，则存在一个长度至多为 100000$$$100\,000$$$ 的序列。
接下来的 k$$$k$$$ 行应包含该序列中的分数，每行包含两个整数 ai$$$a_i$$$ 和 bi$$$b_i$$$。

problems.hint: Iterate over what flower is in the range of the first fountain. Special case: no flowers.

legend: A flowerbed has many flowers and two fountains.

You can adjust the water pressure and set any values r1(r1 ≥ 0) and r2(r2 ≥ 0), giving the distances at which the water is spread from the first and second fountain respectively. You have to set such r1 and r2 that all the flowers are watered, that is, for each flower, the distance between the flower and the first fountain doesn't exceed r1, or the distance to the second fountain doesn't exceed r2. It's OK if some flowers are watered by both fountains.
You need to decrease the amount of water you need, that is set such r1 and r2 that all the flowers are watered and the r12 + r22 is minimum possible. Find this minimum value.
input: The first line of the input contains integers n, x1, y1, x2, y2 (1 ≤ n ≤ 2000,  - 107 ≤ x1, y1, x2, y2 ≤ 107) — the number of flowers, the coordinates of the first and the second fountain.
Next follow n lines. The i-th of these lines contains integers xi and yi ( - 107 ≤ xi, yi ≤ 107) — the coordinates of the i-th flower.
It is guaranteed that all n + 2 points in the input are distinct.
output: Print the minimum possible value r12 + r22. Note, that in this problem optimal answer is always integer.
note: The first sample is (r12 = 5, r22 = 1): ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b22bc3b9d5e08270abeb227926f71a59c047471e.png) The second sample is (r12 = 1, r22 = 32): ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/52cff766dc5ed8406cad96178771df70a1edc042.png)

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含整数 n、x1、y1、x2、y2（1 ≤ n ≤ 2000，−10^7 ≤ x1、y1、x2、y2 ≤ 10^7）——花朵的数量，以及第一个和第二个喷泉的坐标。
接下来是 n 行。其中第 i 行包含整数 xi 和 yi（−10^7 ≤ xi、yi ≤ 10^7）——第 i 朵花的坐标。
保证输入中的全部 n + 2 个点互不相同。

output.ai: 输出 r₁² + r₂² 的可能的最小值。注意，在本题中最优答案总是整数。

note.ai: 第一个样例为(r₁² = 5，r₂² = 1)：![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b22bc3b9d5e08270abeb227926f71a59c047471e.png) 第二个样例为(r₁² = 1，r₂² = 32)：![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/52cff766dc5ed8406cad96178771df70a1edc042.png)

legend.ai: 一个花坛里有许多花，还有两个喷泉。
你可以调节水压，并将任意值 r1(r1 ≥ 0) 和 r2(r2 ≥ 0) 分别设置为水从第一个和第二个喷泉喷洒到的距离。你需要设置这样的 r1 和 r2，使所有的花都能被浇到，也就是说，对于每朵花，它到第一个喷泉的距离不超过 r1，或者到第二个喷泉的距离不超过 r2。某些花同时被两个喷泉浇到也是可以的。
你需要减少所需的水量，也就是设置这样的 r1 和 r2，使所有的花都能被浇到，并且 r12 + r22 尽可能小。求这个最小值。

problems.hint: If the orders are chosen, how should the chairperson choose? Sort the array so that this part comes easy.

legend: A student's life is fraught with complications. Some Berland University students know this only too well. Having studied for two years, they contracted strong antipathy towards the chairperson of some department. Indeed, the person in question wasn't the kindest of ladies to begin with: prone to reforming groups, banning automatic passes and other mean deeds. At last the students decided that she just can't get away with all this anymore...

The students pulled some strings on the higher levels and learned that the next University directors' meeting is going to discuss n orders about the chairperson and accept exactly p of them. There are two values assigned to each order: ai is the number of the chairperson's hairs that turn grey if she obeys the order and bi — the displeasement of the directors if the order isn't obeyed. The students may make the directors pass any p orders chosen by them. The students know that the chairperson will obey exactly k out of these p orders. She will pick the orders to obey in the way that minimizes first, the directors' displeasement and second, the number of hairs on her head that turn grey.

The students want to choose p orders in the way that maximizes the number of hairs on the chairperson's head that turn grey. If there are multiple ways to accept the orders, then the students are keen on maximizing the directors' displeasement with the chairperson's actions. Help them.
input: The first line contains three integers n (1 ≤ n ≤ 105), p (1 ≤ p ≤ n), k (1 ≤ k ≤ p) — the number of orders the directors are going to discuss, the number of orders to pass and the number of orders to be obeyed by the chairperson, correspondingly. Each of the following n lines contains two integers ai and bi (1 ≤ ai, bi ≤ 109), describing the corresponding order.
output: Print in an arbitrary order p distinct integers — the numbers of the orders to accept so that the students could carry out the revenge. The orders are indexed from 1 to n in the order they occur in the input. If there are multiple solutions, you can print any of them.
note: In the first sample one of optimal solutions is to pass orders 1, 2, 3. In this case the chairperson obeys orders number 1 and 2. She gets 10 new grey hairs in the head and the directors' displeasement will equal 3. Note that the same result can be achieved with order 4 instead of order 3.

In the second sample, the chairperson can obey all the orders, so the best strategy for the students is to pick the orders with the maximum sum of ai values. The chairperson gets 58 new gray hairs and the directors' displeasement will equal 0.

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，一种最优方案是通过第 1、2、3 条命令。在这种情况下，系主任会遵守第 1 条和第 2 条命令。她的头上会长出 10 根白发，而董事会的不满程度将等于 3。注意，将第 3 条命令替换为第 4 条命令也能达到相同的结果。
在第二个样例中，主席可以遵守所有命令，因此学生的最优策略是选择 ai 值之和最大的命令。主席会新增 58 根白发，而董事们的不满度将等于 0。

legend.ai: 学生的生活充满了麻烦。伯兰大学的一些学生对此深有体会。学习了两年后，他们对某个系的系主任产生了强烈的反感。事实上，这位女士本来就不怎么和善：她热衷于重组小组、禁止自动通过，以及做出其他刻薄的行为。最终，学生们决定她不能再这样逍遥法外了……

学生们通过上层关系得知，下一次大学董事会会议将讨论关于系主任的 n 条命令，并且恰好通过其中的 p 条。每条命令都有两个对应的数值：a_i 表示系主任遵守该命令后会变白的头发数量，b_i 表示该命令未被遵守时董事会的不满程度。学生们可以让董事会通过任意 p 条他们选定的命令。学生们知道，系主任恰好会遵守其中的 k 条命令。她会按照以下方式选择要遵守的命令：首先使董事会的不满程度最小，其次使她头上变白的头发数量最少。
学生们希望选择 p 条命令，使系主任头上变白的头发数量最大。如果有多种通过命令的方案，那么学生们还希望最大化董事会对系主任行为的不满程度。请帮助他们。

input.ai: 第一行包含三个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5）、p（1 ≤ p ≤ n）、k（1 ≤ k ≤ p），分别表示董事会将要讨论的命令数量、要通过的命令数量以及系主任将遵守的命令数量。接下来的 n 行中，每行包含两个整数 a_i 和 b_i（1 ≤ a_i, b_i ≤ 10^9），表示对应的命令。

output.ai: 以任意顺序输出 p 个互不相同的整数，表示学生们应当通过哪些命令来实施报复。命令按照它们在输入中出现的顺序编号为 1 至 n。如果有多种方案，输出其中任意一种即可。

problems.hint: You don't need to delete many characters.

legend: Furik loves math lessons very much, so he doesn't attend them, unlike Rubik. But now Furik wants to get a good mark for math. For that Ms. Ivanova, his math teacher, gave him a new task. Furik solved the task immediately. Can you?

You are given a set of digits, your task is to find the maximum integer that you can make from these digits. The made number must be divisible by 2, 3, 5 without a residue. It is permitted to use not all digits from the set, it is forbidden to use leading zeroes.
Each digit is allowed to occur in the number the same number of times it occurs in the set.
input: A single line contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 100000) — the number of digits in the set. The second line contains n digits, the digits are separated by a single space.
output: On a single line print the answer to the problem. If such number does not exist, then you should print -1.
note: In the first sample there is only one number you can make — 0. In the second sample the sought number is 5554443330. In the third sample it is impossible to make the required number.

legend.ai: Furik 非常喜欢数学课，所以他不像 Rubik 那样去上课。但现在 Furik 想在数学课上取得好成绩。为此，他的数学老师 Ivanova 女士给了他一道新题。Furik 立即解决了这道题。你能做到吗？
给定一个数字集合，你的任务是找出利用这些数字能够组成的最大整数。组成的数必须能被 2、3、5 整除且余数为 0。允许不使用集合中的所有数字，但禁止使用前导零。
每个数字在组成的数中出现的次数不能超过它在集合中出现的次数。

input.ai: 一行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 100000），表示集合中数字的个数。第二行包含 n 个数字，相邻数字之间用一个空格分隔。

output.ai: 请在一行中输出该问题的答案。如果不存在这样的数，则输出 -1。

note.ai: 第一个样例中，只有一个可以构造出的数——0。第二个样例中，所求的数是 5554443330。在第三个样例中，无法构造出所需的数。

problems.hint: If you can get to the destination in $t$ seconds, it's always possible to get there in $t'(t'\gt t)$ seconds.

legend: A team of furry rescue rangers was sitting idle in their hollow tree when suddenly they received a signal of distress. In a few moments they were ready, and the dirigible of the rescue chipmunks hit the road.
We assume that the action takes place on a Cartesian plane. The headquarters of the rescuers is located at point (x1, y1), and the distress signal came from the point (x2, y2).

Due to Gadget's engineering talent, the rescuers' dirigible can instantly change its current velocity and direction of movement at any moment and as many times as needed. The only limitation is: the speed of the aircraft relative to the air can not exceed ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/05a28aed63c92fafe8f32513b33646154faf8683.png) meters per second.

Of course, Gadget is a true rescuer and wants to reach the destination as soon as possible. The matter is complicated by the fact that the wind is blowing in the air and it affects the movement of the dirigible. According to the weather forecast, the wind will be defined by the vector (vx, vy) for the nearest t seconds, and then will change to (wx, wy). These vectors give both the direction and velocity of the wind. Formally, if a dirigible is located at the point (x, y), while its own velocity relative to the air is equal to zero and the wind (ux, uy) is blowing, then after ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c9148a5f77a39b4083611f2ac760c9479d17582c.png) seconds the new position of the dirigible will be ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/f42cccc4419e311f702830ad221b81f335011df6.png).

Gadget is busy piloting the aircraft, so she asked Chip to calculate how long will it take them to reach the destination if they fly optimally. He coped with the task easily, but Dale is convinced that Chip has given the random value, aiming only not to lose the face in front of Gadget. Dale has asked you to find the right answer.
It is guaranteed that the speed of the wind at any moment of time is strictly less than the maximum possible speed of the airship relative to the air.
input: The first line of the input contains four integers x1, y1, x2, y2 (|x1|,  |y1|,  |x2|,  |y2| ≤ 10 000) — the coordinates of the rescuers' headquarters and the point, where signal of the distress came from, respectively.

The second line contains two integers ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/05a28aed63c92fafe8f32513b33646154faf8683.png) and t (0 < v, t ≤ 1000), which are denoting the maximum speed of the chipmunk dirigible relative to the air and the moment of time when the wind changes according to the weather forecast, respectively.

Next follow one per line two pairs of integer (vx, vy) and (wx, wy), describing the wind for the first t seconds and the wind that will blow at all the remaining time, respectively. It is guaranteed that ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/4ddbd171d9061576ebb160327d6360a2129809aa.png) and ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e2970f5978fa0d3691dc2f7ae02f0c21a76e2d47.png).
output: Print a single real value — the minimum time the rescuers need to get to point (x2, y2). You answer will be considered correct if its absolute or relative error does not exceed 10 - 6.

Namely: let's assume that your answer is a, and the answer of the jury is b. The checker program will consider your answer correct, if ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c97ba2000ebfad962bff7ffd8d043594f5ae1086.png).

output.ai: 输出一个实数——救援人员到达点 (x2, y2) 所需的最短时间。如果你的答案的绝对误差或相对误差不超过 10^{-6}，则你的答案将被视为正确。
即：假设你的答案为 a，裁判的答案为 b。如果 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c97ba2000ebfad962bff7ffd8d043594f5ae1086.png)，检查程序将认为你的答案正确。

legend.ai: 一队毛茸茸的救援游骑兵正百无聊赖地坐在它们的空心树里，突然收到了一条求救信号。没过多久，它们就准备好了，救援花栗鼠们的飞艇出发了。
我们假设行动发生在直角坐标平面上。救援人员的总部位于点 (x1, y1)，而求救信号来自点 (x2, y2)。
由于 Gadget 的工程天赋，救援人员的飞艇可以在任意时刻、根据需要任意多次地瞬间改变当前速度和运动方向。唯一的限制是：飞行器相对于空气的速度不能超过 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/05a28aed63c92fafe8f32513b33646154faf8683.png) 米每秒。

当然，Gadget 是一名真正的救援者，她希望尽快抵达目的地。但空中吹着风，会影响飞艇的运动，使事情变得复杂。根据天气预报，接下来最近的 t 秒内，风由向量 (vx, vy) 表示，之后将变为 (wx, wy)。这些向量同时表示风的方向和速度。形式化地说，如果飞艇位于点 (x, y)，其相对于空气的自身速度为零，且正在刮着风 (ux, uy)，那么经过 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c9148a5f77a39b4083611f2ac760c9479d17582c.png) 秒后，飞艇的新位置将为 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/f42cccc4419e311f702830ad221b81f335011df6.png)。
Gadget 正忙于驾驶飞行器，因此她让 Chip 计算如果采取最优飞行方式，他们需要多长时间才能抵达目的地。他轻松地完成了任务，但 Dale 认为 Chip 给出的只是一个随机值，只是为了不在 Gadget 面前丢脸。Dale 请你求出正确答案。
保证在任意时刻，风速都严格小于飞艇相对于空气的最大可能速度。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含四个整数 x1、y1、x2、y2（|x1|、  |y1|、|x2|、|y2| ≤ 10 000），分别表示救援人员总部的坐标，以及发出求救信号的地点坐标。
第二行包含两个整数 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/05a28aed63c92fafe8f32513b33646154faf8683.png) 和 t(0 < v、t ≤ 1000)，分别表示花栗鼠飞艇相对于空气的最大速度，以及根据天气预报风向发生变化的时刻。

接下来每行包含两对整数 (vx, vy) 和 (wx, wy)，分别描述前 t 秒内的风，以及之后剩余时间内一直刮的风。保证 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/4ddbd171d9061576ebb160327d6360a2129809aa.png) 和 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e2970f5978fa0d3691dc2f7ae02f0c21a76e2d47.png)。

problems.hint: Let's see the weight of each character.

legend: Petya has n positive integers a1, a2, ..., an.

His friend Vasya decided to joke and replaced all digits in Petya's numbers with a letters. He used the lowercase letters of the Latin alphabet from 'a' to 'j' and replaced all digits 0 with one letter, all digits 1 with another letter and so on. For any two different digits Vasya used distinct letters from 'a' to 'j'.

Your task is to restore Petya's numbers. The restored numbers should be positive integers without leading zeros. Since there can be multiple ways to do it, determine the minimum possible sum of all Petya's numbers after the restoration. It is guaranteed that before Vasya's joke all Petya's numbers did not have leading zeros.
input: The first line contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 1 000) — the number of Petya's numbers.

Each of the following lines contains non-empty string si consisting of lowercase Latin letters from 'a' to 'j' — the Petya's numbers after Vasya's joke. The length of each string does not exceed six characters.
output: Determine the minimum sum of all Petya's numbers after the restoration. The restored numbers should be positive integers without leading zeros. It is guaranteed that the correct restore (without leading zeros) exists for all given tests.
note: In the first example, you need to replace the letter 'a' with the digit 1, the letter 'b' with the digit 0, the letter 'd' with the digit 2, the letter 'e' with the digit 3, and the letter 'j' with the digit 4. So after the restoration numbers will look like [10, 23, 14]. The sum of them is equal to 47, which is the minimum possible sum of the numbers after the correct restoration.
In the second example the numbers after the restoration can look like: [120468, 3579, 2468, 10024, 3].
In the second example the numbers after the restoration can look like: [11, 22, 11].

legend.ai: Petya 有 n 个正整数 a1, a2, ..., an。
他的朋友 Vasya 决定开个玩笑，把 Petya 的数中的所有数字都替换成了字母。他使用了拉丁字母表中小写字母 'a' 到 'j'，用其中一个字母替换所有数字 0，用另一个字母替换所有数字 1，以此类推。对于任意两个不同的数字，Vasya 都使用了 'a' 到 'j' 中不同的字母。
你的任务是恢复 Petya 的数。恢复后的数应为不含前导零的正整数。由于可能存在多种恢复方式，请确定恢复后 Petya 所有数之和的最小可能值。保证在 Vasya 开玩笑之前，Petya 的所有的数都没有前导零。

statement.title: D. Nene and the Mex Operator

legend: Nene gave you an array of integers a1,a2,…,an$$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ of length n$$$n$$$.
You can perform the following operation no more than 5⋅105$$$5\cdot 10^5$$$ times (possibly zero):

Choose two integers l$$$l$$$ and r$$$r$$$ such that 1≤l≤r≤n$$$1 \le l \le r \le n$$$, compute x$$$x$$$ as MEX({al,al+1,…,ar})$$$\operatorname{MEX}(\{a_l, a_{l+1}, \ldots, a_r\})$$$, and simultaneously set al:=x,al+1:=x,…,ar:=x$$$a_l:=x, a_{l+1}:=x, \ldots, a_r:=x$$$.
Here, MEX$$$\operatorname{MEX}$$$ of a set of integers {c1,c2,…,ck}$$$\{c_1, c_2, \ldots, c_k\}$$$ is defined as the smallest non-negative integer m$$$m$$$ which does not occur in the set c$$$c$$$.

Your goal is to maximize the sum of the elements of the array a$$$a$$$. Find the maximum sum and construct a sequence of operations that achieves this sum. Note that you don't need to minimize the number of operations in this sequence, you only should use no more than 5⋅105$$$5\cdot 10^5$$$ operations in your solution.
input: The first line contains an integer n$$$n$$$ (1≤n≤18$$$1 \le n \le 18$$$) — the length of the array a$$$a$$$.
The second line contains n$$$n$$$ integers a1,a2,…,an$$$a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n$$$ (0≤ai≤107$$$0\leq a_i \leq 10^7$$$) — the array a$$$a$$$.
output: In the first line, output two integers s$$$s$$$ and m$$$m$$$ (0≤m≤5⋅105$$$0\le m\le 5\cdot 10^5$$$) — the maximum sum of elements of the array a$$$a$$$ and the number of operations in your solution.
In the i$$$i$$$-th of the following m$$$m$$$ lines, output two integers l$$$l$$$ and r$$$r$$$ (1≤l≤r≤n$$$1 \le l \le r \le n$$$), representing the parameters of the i$$$i$$$-th operation.
It can be shown that the maximum sum of elements of the array a$$$a$$$ can always be obtained in no more than 5⋅105$$$5 \cdot 10^5$$$ operations.
note: In the first example, after the operation with l=1$$$l=1$$$ and r=2$$$r=2$$$ the array a$$$a$$$ becomes equal to [2,2]$$$[2,2]$$$. It can be shown that it is impossible to achieve a larger sum of the elements of a$$$a$$$, so the answer is 4$$$4$$$.
In the second example, the initial sum of elements is 13$$$13$$$ which can be shown to be the largest.
In the third example, the array a$$$a$$$ changes as follows:
after the first operation (l=3$$$l=3$$$, r=3$$$r=3$$$), the array a$$$a$$$ becomes equal to [1,100,0,1]$$$[1,100,0,1]$$$;
after the second operation (l=3$$$l=3$$$, r=4$$$r=4$$$), the array a$$$a$$$ becomes equal to [1,100,2,2]$$$[1,100,2,2]$$$.
It can be shown that it is impossible to achieve a larger sum of the elements of a$$$a$$$, so the answer is 105$$$105$$$.

legend.ai: Nene 给了你一个长度为 n$$$n$$$ 的整数数组 a1,a2,…,an$$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$。
你可以至多执行 5⋅105$$$5\cdot 10^5$$$ 次以下操作(也可以一次都不执行)：

选择两个整数 l$$$l$$$ 和 r$$$r$$$，满足 1≤l≤r≤n$$$1 \le l \le r \le n$$$，将 x$$$x$$$ 计算为 MEX({al,al+1,…,ar})$$$\operatorname{MEX}(\{a_l, a_{l+1}, \ldots, a_r\})$$$，并同时令 al:=x,al+1:=x,…,ar:=x$$$a_l:=x, a_{l+1}:=x, \ldots, a_r:=x$$$。
这里，整数集合 {c1,c2,…,ck}$$$\{c_1, c_2, \ldots, c_k\}$$$ 的 MEX$$$\operatorname{MEX}$$$ 定义为集合 c$$$c$$$ 中未出现的最小非负整数 m$$$m$$$。
你的目标是最大化数组 a$$$a$$$ 中所有元素的和。求出最大和，并构造一个能够达到该和的操作序列。注意，你无需最小化该序列中的操作次数，只需保证你的解中使用的操作次数不超过 5⋅105$$$5\cdot 10^5$$$。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n$$$n$$$(1≤n≤18$$$1 \le n \le 18$$$)——数组 a$$$a$$$ 的长度。

output.ai: 第一行输出两个整数 s$$$s$$$ 和 m$$$m$$$(0≤m≤5⋅105$$$0\le m\le 5\cdot 10^5$$$)——数组 a$$$a$$$ 中元素和的最大值，以及你的解法中的操作次数。
在接下来的 m$$$m$$$ 行中，第 i$$$i$$$ 行输出两个整数 l$$$l$$$ 和 r$$$r$$$(1≤l≤r≤n$$$1 \le l \le r \le n$$$)，表示第 i$$$i$$$ 次操作的参数。
可以证明，数组 a$$$a$$$ 中元素和的最大值总能在不超过 5⋅105$$$5 \cdot 10^5$$$ 次操作内得到。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，执行 l=1$$$l=1$$$ 且 r=2$$$r=2$$$ 的操作后，数组 a$$$a$$$ 变为 [2,2]$$$[2,2]$$$。可以证明，不可能使数组 a$$$a$$$ 中元素的和更大，因此答案为 4$$$4$$$。
在第二个样例中，元素的初始和为 13$$$13$$$，可以证明这是可能达到的最大值。

可以证明，无法使数组 a$$$a$$$ 中元素的和更大，因此答案为 105$$$105$$$。

legend: In order to win his toughest battle, Mircea came up with a great strategy for his army. He has n$$$n$$$ soldiers and decided to arrange them in a certain way in camps. Each soldier has to belong to exactly one camp, and there is one camp at each integer point on the x$$$x$$$-axis (at points ⋯,−2,−1,0,1,2,⋯$$$\cdots, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, \cdots$$$).

The strategy consists of m$$$m$$$ conditions. Condition i$$$i$$$ tells that soldier ai$$$a_i$$$ should belong to a camp that is situated di$$$d_i$$$ meters in front of the camp that person bi$$$b_i$$$ belongs to. (If di<0$$$d_i  \lt  0$$$, then ai$$$a_i$$$'s camp should be −di$$$-d_i$$$ meters behind bi$$$b_i$$$'s camp.)

Now, Mircea wonders if there exists a partition of soldiers that respects the condition and he asks for your help! Answer "YES" if there is a partition of the n$$$n$$$ soldiers that satisfies all of the m$$$m$$$ conditions and "NO" otherwise.
Note that two different soldiers may be placed in the same camp.

Then m$$$m$$$ lines follow, each of them containing 3$$$3$$$ integers: ai$$$a_i$$$, bi$$$b_i$$$, di$$$d_i$$$ (ai≠bi$$$a_i \neq b_i$$$; 1≤ai,bi≤n$$$1 \leq a_i, b_i \leq n$$$; −109≤di≤109$$$-10^9 \leq d_i \leq 10^9$$$) — denoting the conditions explained in the statement. Note that the sum of n$$$n$$$ over all test cases doesn't exceed 2⋅105$$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.

For the third test case, there is no partition that satisfies all the constraints since we get contradictory information about the same pair.

legend: ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c890509ce2af8567113a1a2d4b388e8763870e18.png)

Every student enrolled in the algorithms course is required to submit an assignment this week. The task is to implement an O(n2)$$$O(n^2)$$$-time algorithm to sort n$$$n$$$ given integers in non-decreasing order. Alice has already completed her assignment, and her implementation is shown below.

While you have access to Alice's code, you prefer not to simply copy it. Instead, you want to use Alice's sorting function as a building block for your own solution. There are two ways as listed below you can utilize her function, but each of them can be applied at most once. The order in which these two operations are invoked can be arbitrary.
Prefix sort: choose a length i∈{1,2,…,n}$$$i \in \{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$$$ and call alicesort(s,i)$$$\texttt{alicesort(}s, i\texttt{)}$$$. This sorts the first i$$$i$$$ elements in the array s$$$s$$$.

Suffix sort: choose a length i∈{1,2,…,n}$$$i \in \{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$$$ and call alicesort(s+n−i,i)$$$\texttt{alicesort(}s+n-i, i\texttt{)}$$$. This sorts the last i$$$i$$$ elements in the array s$$$s$$$.

Due to the time complexity of the sorting algorithm, the cost of performing either a prefix or suffix sort is i2$$$i^2$$$, where i$$$i$$$ is the length of the chosen subarray. Your goal is to determine the minimum cost to sort the input array s$$$s$$$ of n$$$n$$$ integers in non-decreasing order using Alice's function, following the rules mentioned above.

For example, Let s=[3,2,5,5,4,1]$$$s=[3,2,5,5,4,1]$$$. We can first perform a suffix sort of length 4$$$4$$$, and the array becomes [3,2,1,4,5,5]$$$[3,2,1,4,5,5]$$$. Then, we perform a prefix sort of length 3$$$3$$$, and the array becomes [1,2,3,4,5,5]$$$[1,2,3,4,5,5]$$$, which is a sorted array. The cost is 42+32=25$$$4^2+3^2=25$$$. Here is another example, let s=[4,3,2,1]$$$s=[4,3,2,1]$$$. We can complete the sorting by performing only a prefix sort of length 4$$$4$$$, and the cost is 42=16$$$4^2=16$$$.
input: The first line contains exactly one integer n$$$n$$$ which indicates the number of integers in the array s$$$s$$$. The second line contains the n$$$n$$$ integers in s=[s0,s1,…,sn−1]$$$s=[s_0, s_1, \ldots, s_{n-1}]$$$.
output: Output an integer on a line, indicating the minimum cost to sort the input array s$$$s$$$ of n$$$n$$$ integers in non-decreasing order using Alice's function, following the rules mentioned above.

legend.ai: ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c890509ce2af8567113a1a2d4b388e8763870e18.png)
每一名修读算法课程的学生都必须在本周提交一份作业。任务是实现一个运行时间为 O(n2)$$$O(n^2)$$$ 的算法，将给定的 n$$$n$$$ 个整数按非递减顺序排序。Alice 已经完成了她的作业，下面给出了她的实现。
虽然你可以访问 Alice 的代码，但你不愿意直接复制它。相反，你想将 Alice 的排序函数作为你自己解决方案的构建块。下面列出了两种可以利用她的函数的方式，但每种方式最多只能使用一次。这两个操作的调用顺序可以任意。
前缀排序：选择一个长度 i∈{1,2,…,n}$$$i \in \{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$$$ 并调用 alicesort(s,i)$$$\texttt{alicesort(}s, i\texttt{)}$$$。这会对数组 s$$$s$$$ 中前 i$$$i$$$ 个元素进行排序。
后缀排序：选择一个长度 i∈{1,2,…,n}$$$i \in \{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$$$ 并调用 alicesort(s+n−i,i)$$$\texttt{alicesort(}s+n-i, i\texttt{)}$$$。这会对数组 s$$$s$$$ 中后 i$$$i$$$ 个元素进行排序。
由于排序算法的时间复杂度，执行一次前缀排序或后缀排序的代价为 i2$$$i^2$$$，其中 i$$$i$$$ 是所选子数组的长度。你的目标是按照上述规则，使用 Alice 的函数将包含 n$$$n$$$ 个整数的输入数组 s$$$s$$$ 按非递减顺序排序，并确定最小代价。

input.ai: 第一行包含恰好一个整数 n$$$n$$$，表示数组 s$$$s$$$ 中整数的个数。第二行包含 s=[s0,s1,…,sn−1]$$$s=[s_0, s_1, \ldots, s_{n-1}]$$$ 中的 n$$$n$$$ 个整数。

output.ai: 在一行输出一个整数，表示按照上述规则使用 Alice 的函数将包含 n$$$n$$$ 个整数的输入数组 s$$$s$$$ 按非递减顺序排序所需的最小代价。

legend: Alice and Bob gathered in the evening to play an exciting game on a sequence of n$$$n$$$ integers, each integer of the sequence doesn't exceed 4$$$4$$$. The rules of the game are too complex to describe, so let's just describe the winning condition — Alice wins if the bitwise XOR of all the numbers in the sequence is non-zero; otherwise, Bob wins.

The guys invited Eve to act as a judge. Initially, Alice and Bob play with n$$$n$$$ numbers. After one game, Eve removes one of the numbers from the sequence, then Alice and Bob play with n−1$$$n-1$$$ numbers. Eve removes one number again, after which Alice and Bob play with n−2$$$n - 2$$$ numbers. This continues until the sequence of numbers is empty.

Eve seems to think that in such a game, Alice almost always wins, so she wants Bob to win as many times as possible. Determine the maximum number of times Bob can win against Alice if Eve removes the numbers optimally.
input: The first line contains an integer t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤104$$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases.

The first and only line of each test case contains four integers pi$$$p_i$$$ (0≤pi≤200$$$0 \le p_i \le 200$$$) — the number of ones, twos, threes, and fours in the sequence at the beginning of the game.
output: For each test case, print the maximum number of times Bob will win in a separate line, if Eve removes the numbers optimally.
note: In the first example, Bob wins when Eve has not removed any numbers yet.
In the second example, Bob wins if Eve removes one one and one three.

legend.ai: Alice 和 Bob 傍晚聚在一起，在一个包含 n$$$n$$$ 个整数的序列上玩一个激动人心的游戏，序列中的每个整数都不超过 4$$$4$$$。游戏规则过于复杂，无法描述，所以我们只描述获胜条件——如果序列中所有数字的按位异或结果不为零，则 Alice 获胜；否则 Bob 获胜。
他们邀请了 Eve 担任裁判。最初，Alice 和 Bob 用 n$$$n$$$ 个数玩游戏。一局之后，Eve 从序列中移除一个数，然后 Alice 和 Bob 用 n−1$$$n-1$$$ 个数玩游戏。Eve 再次移除一个数，之后 Alice 和 Bob 用 n−2$$$n - 2$$$ 个数玩游戏。如此继续，直到数列为空。
Eve似乎认为在这样的游戏中，Alice几乎总是获胜，因此她希望让Bob尽可能多地获胜。请确定如果Eve以最优方式移除数字，Bob最多能战胜Alice多少次。

legend: Wherever the destination is, whoever we meet, let's render this song together.

On a Cartesian coordinate plane lies a rectangular stage of size w × h, represented by a rectangle with corners (0, 0), (w, 0), (w, h) and (0, h). It can be seen that no collisions will happen before one enters the stage.
On the sides of the stage stand n dancers. The i-th of them falls into one of the following groups:
Vertical: stands at (xi, 0), moves in positive y direction (upwards);
Horizontal: stands at (0, yi), moves in positive x direction (rightwards).
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/8aba07adc75f9cf705def164ff858509481b54c7.png)

According to choreography, the i-th dancer should stand still for the first ti milliseconds, and then start moving in the specified direction at 1 unit per millisecond, until another border is reached. It is guaranteed that no two dancers have the same group, position and waiting time at the same time.
When two dancers collide (i.e. are on the same point at some time when both of them are moving), they immediately exchange their moving directions and go on.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a99291578f37557be4d80124c9bb6c84d22580a1.png)
Dancers stop when a border of the stage is reached. Find out every dancer's stopping position.
input: The first line of input contains three space-separated positive integers n, w and h (1 ≤ n ≤ 100 000, 2 ≤ w, h ≤ 100 000) — the number of dancers and the width and height of the stage, respectively.

The following n lines each describes a dancer: the i-th among them contains three space-separated integers gi, pi, and ti (1 ≤ gi ≤ 2, 1 ≤ pi ≤ 99 999, 0 ≤ ti ≤ 100 000), describing a dancer's group gi (gi = 1 — vertical, gi = 2 — horizontal), position, and waiting time. If gi = 1 then pi = xi; otherwise pi = yi. It's guaranteed that 1 ≤ xi ≤ w - 1 and 1 ≤ yi ≤ h - 1. It is guaranteed that no two dancers have the same group, position and waiting time at the same time.
output: Output n lines, the i-th of which contains two space-separated integers (xi, yi) — the stopping position of the i-th dancer in the input.
note: The first example corresponds to the initial setup in the legend, and the tracks of dancers are marked with different colours in the following figure.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/9af64013ccf58cb225463c40fd9f075bcf7ea913.png)
In the second example, no dancers collide.

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含三个用空格分隔的正整数 n、w 和 h（1 ≤ n ≤ 100 000，2 ≤ w, h ≤ 100 000）——舞者的数量以及舞台的宽度和高度。

接下来的 n 行分别描述一名舞者：其中第 i 行包含三个以空格分隔的整数 gi、pi 和 ti（1 ≤ gi ≤ 2，1 ≤ pi ≤ 99 999，0 ≤ ti ≤ 100 000），分别表示舞者所在的组 gi（gi = 1 表示竖直，gi = 2 表示水平）、位置和等待时间。如果 gi = 1，那么 pi = xi；否则 pi = yi。保证 1 ≤ xi ≤ w - 1 且 1 ≤ yi ≤ h - 1。保证不存在两名舞者的组别、位置和等待时间都相同。

output.ai: 输出 n 行，第 i 行包含两个以空格分隔的整数 (xi, yi)，表示输入中第 i 名舞者的停止位置。

note.ai: 第一个样例对应题面中的初始布局，以下图中用不同颜色标记了舞者的运动轨迹。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/9af64013ccf58cb225463c40fd9f075bcf7ea913.png)
在第二个样例中，没有舞者发生碰撞。

legend.ai: 无论目的地在哪里，无论我们遇见谁，让我们一起演奏这首歌吧。
在直角坐标平面上有一个大小为 w × h 的矩形舞台，其顶点为 (0, 0)、(w, 0)、(w, h) 和 (0, h)。可以看出，在进入舞台之前不会发生碰撞。
舞台的边上站着 n 名舞者。第 i 名舞者属于以下类别之一：
竖直：站在 (xi, 0) 处，沿 y 轴正方向（向上）移动；
水平：站在 (0, yi) 处，沿 x 轴正方向（向右）移动。

根据编舞安排，第 i 位舞者应在最初的 ti 毫秒内保持静止，然后以每毫秒 1 个单位的速度沿指定方向开始移动，直到到达另一侧边界。保证不会有两个舞者同时具有相同的组别、位置和等待时间。
当两位舞者发生碰撞时（即在某个时刻两人都在移动且位于同一点），他们会立即交换移动方向并继续前进。

舞者到达舞台边界时停止。请找出每位舞者的停止位置。

problems.hint: Let's maximize the $s_i'$ of each part.

legend: Mayor of city S just hates trees and lawns. They take so much space and there could be a road on the place they occupy!

The Mayor thinks that one of the main city streets could be considerably widened on account of lawn nobody needs anyway. Moreover, that might help reduce the car jams which happen from time to time on the street.
The street is split into n equal length parts from left to right, the i-th part is characterized by two integers: width of road si and width of lawn gi.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/1e351a64cc735b32c3ed5bd9304d0d528a12a83e.png)

For each of n parts the Mayor should decide the size of lawn to demolish. For the i-th part he can reduce lawn width by integer xi (0 ≤ xi ≤ gi). After it new road width of the i-th part will be equal to s'i = si + xi and new lawn width will be equal to g'i = gi - xi.

On the one hand, the Mayor wants to demolish as much lawn as possible (and replace it with road). On the other hand, he does not want to create a rapid widening or narrowing of the road, which would lead to car accidents. To avoid that, the Mayor decided that width of the road for consecutive parts should differ by at most 1, i.e. for each i (1 ≤ i < n) the inequation |s'i + 1 - s'i| ≤ 1 should hold. Initially this condition might not be true.
You need to find the the total width of lawns the Mayor will destroy according to his plan.
input: The first line contains integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·105) — number of parts of the street.
Each of the following n lines contains two integers si, gi (1 ≤ si ≤ 106, 0 ≤ gi ≤ 106) — current width of road and width of the lawn on the i-th part of the street.
output: In the first line print the total width of lawns which will be removed.
In the second line print n integers s'1, s'2, ..., s'n (si ≤ s'i ≤ si + gi) — new widths of the road starting from the first part and to the last.
If there is no solution, print the only integer -1 in the first line.

legend.ai: S 市市长简直讨厌树木和草坪。它们占据了太多空间，而这些地方本可以用来修路！
市长认为，城市的一条主干道可以利用反正无人需要的草坪进行大幅拓宽。此外，这或许还能缓解这条街道上不时发生的交通拥堵。
这条街道从左到右被划分为 n 个等长部分，第 i 个部分由两个整数表示：道路宽度 s_i 和草坪宽度 g_i。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/1e351a64cc735b32c3ed5bd9304d0d528a12a83e.png)
对于这 n 个部分中的每一个，市长都需要决定要拆除多少草坪。对于第 i 个部分，他可以将草坪宽度减少整数 x_i（0 ≤ x_i ≤ g_i）。调整后，第 i 个部分的新道路宽度为 s'_i = s_i + x_i，新草坪宽度为 g'_i = g_i - x_i。
一方面，市长希望尽可能多地拆除草坪（并将其替换为道路）。另一方面，他不希望道路出现突然的拓宽或变窄，因为这会导致交通事故。为避免这种情况，市长规定相邻部分的道路宽度之差最多为 1，即对于每个 i（1 ≤ i < n），都应满足不等式 |s'_{i + 1} - s'_i| ≤ 1。初始时，这一条件可能并不成立。
你需要求出市长根据其计划将摧毁的草坪总宽度。

input.ai: 第一行包含整数 n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·105) —— 街道的分段数。
接下来的 n 行中，每行包含两个整数 s_i, g_i (1 ≤ s_i ≤ 106, 0 ≤ g_i ≤ 106) —— 街道第 i 段当前的道路宽度和草坪宽度。

output.ai: 第一行输出将被移除的草坪总宽度。
第二行输出 n 个整数 s'1, s'2, ..., s'n (si ≤ s'i ≤ si + gi) —— 从第一段到最后一段的新道路宽度。
如果无解，则在第一行仅输出整数 -1。

problems.hint: Two kinds: whether LCM is $\max(a_i)$ or not.

legend: Nikita is a student passionate about number theory and algorithms. He faces an interesting problem related to an array of numbers.

Suppose Nikita has an array of integers $$$a$$$ of length $$$n$$$. He will call a subsequence$$$^\dagger$$$ of the array special if its least common multiple (LCM) is not contained in $$$a$$$. The LCM of an empty subsequence is equal to $$$0$$$.
Nikita wonders: what is the length of the longest special subsequence of $$$a$$$? Help him answer this question!

$$$^\dagger$$$ A sequence $$$b$$$ is a subsequence of $$$a$$$ if $$$b$$$ can be obtained from $$$a$$$ by the deletion of several (possibly, zero or all) elements, without changing the order of the remaining elements. For example, $$$[5,2,3]$$$ is a subsequence of $$$[1,5,7,8,2,4,3]$$$.
input: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line of input contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 2000$$$) — the number of test cases. The description of the test cases follows.
The first line of each test case contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 2000$$$) — the length of the array $$$a$$$.
The second line of each test case contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$) — the elements of the array $$$a$$$.
It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$2000$$$.
output: For each test case, output a single integer — the length of the longest special subsequence of $$$a$$$.
note: In the first test case, the LCM of any non-empty subsequence is contained in $$$a$$$, so the answer is $$$0$$$.
In the second test case, we can take the subsequence $$$[3, 2, 10, 1]$$$, its LCM is equal to $$$30$$$, which is not contained in $$$a$$$.
In the third test case, we can take the subsequence $$$[2, 3, 6, 100\,003]$$$, its LCM is equal to $$$600\,018$$$, which is not contained in $$$a$$$.

input.ai: 每个测试包含多个测试用例。输入的第一行包含一个整数 $$$t$$$($$$1 \le t \le 2000$$$)——测试用例的数量。接下来是各测试用例的描述。
每个测试用例的第一行包含一个整数 $$$n$$$($$$1 \le n \le 2000$$$)——数组 $$$a$$$ 的长度。
每个测试用例的第二行包含 $$$n$$$ 个整数 $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$($$$1 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$)——数组 $$$a$$$ 的元素。
保证所有测试用例中 $$$n$$$ 的总和不超过 $$$2000$$$。

output.ai: 对于每个测试用例，输出一个整数——$$$a$$$ 的最长特殊子序列的长度。

note.ai: 在第一个测试用例中，任意非空子序列的 LCM 都包含在 $$$a$$$ 中，因此答案为 $$$0$$$。
在第二个测试用例中，我们可以取子序列 $$$[3, 2, 10, 1]$$$，其 LCM 等于 $$$30$$$，而它不包含在 $$$a$$$ 中。
在第三个测试用例中，我们可以取子序列 $$$[2, 3, 6, 100\,003]$$$，其最小公倍数等于 $$$600\,018$$$，而它不包含在 $$$a$$$ 中。

legend.ai: Nikita 是一名热爱数论和算法的学生。他遇到了一个与数字数组有关的有趣问题。
假设 Nikita 有一个长度为 $$$n$$$ 的整数数组 $$$a$$$。如果数组的一个子序列$$$^\dagger$$$的最小公倍数(LCM)不在 $$$a$$$ 中，他就称其为特殊子序列。空子序列的 LCM 等于 $$$0$$$。
Nikita 想知道：$$$a$$$ 的最长特殊子序列的长度是多少？请帮助他回答这个问题！
$$$^\dagger$$$ 如果可以通过删除 $$$a$$$ 中的若干个元素(可能删除零个或全部元素)，且不改变剩余元素的顺序来得到 $$$b$$$，则称序列 $$$b$$$ 是 $$$a$$$ 的子序列。例如，$$$[5,2,3]$$$ 是 $$$[1,5,7,8,2,4,3]$$$ 的子序列。

legend: Pasha has recently bought a new phone jPager and started adding his friends' phone numbers there. Each phone number consists of exactly n digits.

Also Pasha has a number k and two sequences of length n / k (n is divisible by k) a1, a2, ..., an / k and b1, b2, ..., bn / k. Let's split the phone number into blocks of length k. The first block will be formed by digits from the phone number that are on positions 1, 2,..., k, the second block will be formed by digits from the phone number that are on positions k + 1, k + 2, ..., 2·k and so on. Pasha considers a phone number good, if the i-th block doesn't start from the digit bi and is divisible by ai if represented as an integer.
To represent the block of length k as an integer, let's write it out as a sequence c1, c2,...,ck. Then the integer is calculated as the result of the expression c1·10k - 1 + c2·10k - 2 + ... + ck.
Pasha asks you to calculate the number of good phone numbers of length n, for the given k, ai and bi. As this number can be too big, print it modulo 109 + 7.
input: The first line of the input contains two integers n and k (1 ≤ n ≤ 100 000, 1 ≤ k ≤ min(n, 9)) — the length of all phone numbers and the length of each block, respectively. It is guaranteed that n is divisible by k.
The second line of the input contains n / k space-separated positive integers — sequence a1, a2, ..., an / k (1 ≤ ai < 10k).
The third line of the input contains n / k space-separated positive integers — sequence b1, b2, ..., bn / k (0 ≤ bi ≤ 9).
output: Print a single integer — the number of good phone numbers of length n modulo 109 + 7.
note: In the first test sample good phone numbers are: 000000, 000098, 005600, 005698, 380000, 380098, 385600, 385698.

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含两个整数 n 和 k（1 ≤ n ≤ 100000，1 ≤ k ≤ min(n, 9)）——分别表示所有电话号码的长度和每个块的长度。保证 n 能被 k 整除。
输入的第二行包含 n / k 个由空格分隔的正整数——序列 a1、a2、...、a_{n/k}（1 ≤ ai < 10^k）。
输入的第三行包含 n / k 个由空格分隔的正整数——序列 b1、b2、...、b_{n/k}（0 ≤ bi ≤ 9）。

output.ai: 输出一个整数——长度为 n 的符合条件的电话号码数量对 10^9 + 7 取模后的结果。

legend.ai: Pasha 最近买了一部新手机 jPager，并开始在其中添加朋友们的电话号码。每个电话号码恰好由 n 位数字组成。

此外，Pasha 还有一个数 k，以及两个长度为 n / k 的序列 a1，a2，...，an / k 和 b1，b2，...，bn / k（n 能被 k 整除）。让我们将电话号码划分为长度为 k 的若干块。第一块由电话号码第 1、2、...、k 位上的数字组成，第二块由第 k + 1、k + 2、...、2·k 位上的数字组成，以此类推。如果第 i 个块的首位不是数字 bi，且将其视为整数后能被 ai 整除，那么 Pasha 就认为这个电话号码是好的。
为了将长度为 k 的块表示为整数，我们将其写成数字序列 c1，c2，...，ck。然后，该整数等于表达式 c1·10^{k − 1} + c2·10^{k − 2} + ... + ck 的值。
Pasha 请你计算对于给定的 k、ai 和 bi，长度为 n 的好的电话号码数量。由于这个数可能很大，请输出其对 10^9 + 7 取模的结果。

problems.hint: There are some basic rules for this graph.

legend: Olya has got a directed non-weighted graph, consisting of n vertexes and m edges. We will consider that the graph vertexes are indexed from 1 to n in some manner. Then for any graph edge that goes from vertex v to vertex u the following inequation holds: v < u.
Now Olya wonders, how many ways there are to add an arbitrary (possibly zero) number of edges to the graph so as the following conditions were met:
You can reach vertexes number i + 1, i + 2, ..., n from any vertex number i (i < n).
For any graph edge going from vertex v to vertex u the following inequation fulfills: v < u.
There is at most one edge between any two vertexes.
The shortest distance between the pair of vertexes i, j (i < j), for which j - i ≤ k holds, equals j - i edges.
The shortest distance between the pair of vertexes i, j (i < j), for which j - i > k holds, equals either j - i or j - i - k edges.
We will consider two ways distinct, if there is the pair of vertexes i, j (i < j), such that first resulting graph has an edge from i to j and the second one doesn't have it.
Help Olya. As the required number of ways can be rather large, print it modulo 1000000007 (109 + 7).
input: The first line contains three space-separated integers n, m, k (2 ≤ n ≤ 106, 0 ≤ m ≤ 105, 1 ≤ k ≤ 106).

The next m lines contain the description of the edges of the initial graph. The i-th line contains a pair of space-separated integers ui, vi (1 ≤ ui < vi ≤ n) — the numbers of vertexes that have a directed edge from ui to vi between them.

It is guaranteed that any pair of vertexes ui, vi has at most one edge between them. It also is guaranteed that the graph edges are given in the order of non-decreasing ui. If there are multiple edges going from vertex ui, then it is guaranteed that these edges are given in the order of increasing vi.
output: Print a single integer — the answer to the problem modulo 1000000007 (109 + 7).
note: In the first sample there are two ways: the first way is not to add anything, the second way is to add a single edge from vertex 2 to vertex 5.

legend.ai: Olya 有一个有向无带权图，包含 n 个顶点和 m 条边。我们假设图的顶点按某种方式从 1 到 n 编号。那么对于任意一条从顶点 v 到顶点 u 的图边，以下不等式成立：v < u。
现在 Olya 想知道，有多少种方式可以向图中添加任意（可能为零）数量的边，使得满足以下条件：
从任意编号为 i 的顶点（i < n）可以到达编号为 i + 1, i + 2, ..., n 的顶点。
对于任意一条从顶点 v 到顶点 u 的图边，以下不等式成立：v < u。
任意两个顶点之间至多有一条边。
对于满足 j - i ≤ k 的顶点对 i, j（i < j），它们之间的最短距离等于 j - i 条边。
对于满足 j-i>k 的顶点对 i、j（i<j），它们之间的最短距离等于 j-i 条边或 j-i-k 条边。
如果存在顶点对 i、j（i<j），使得第一个得到的图中有一条从 i 到 j 的边，而第二个图中没有这条边，则认为这两种方案不同。
帮助 Olya。由于所求方案数可能非常大，请输出其对 1000000007（10^9+7）取模的结果。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中有两种方式：第一种是什么也不添加，第二种是从顶点 2 到顶点 5 添加一条边。

input.ai: 第一行包含三个以空格分隔的整数 n、m、k（2≤n≤10^6，0≤m≤10^5，1≤k≤10^6）。
接下来的 m 行描述初始图中的边。第 i 行包含一对以空格分隔的整数 ui、vi（1≤ui<vi≤n），表示一条从 ui 指向 vi 的有向边的两个顶点编号。
保证任意一对顶点 ui、vi 之间至多有一条边。还保证图中的边按照 ui 非递减的顺序给出。如果有多条边从顶点 ui 出发，则保证这些边按照 vi 递增的顺序给出。

problems.hint: For each stone, find its perfect match.

legend: Kostya is a genial sculptor, he has an idea: to carve a marble sculpture in the shape of a sphere. Kostya has a friend Zahar who works at a career. Zahar knows about Kostya's idea and wants to present him a rectangular parallelepiped of marble from which he can carve the sphere.
Zahar has n stones which are rectangular parallelepipeds. The edges sizes of the i-th of them are ai, bi and ci. He can take no more than two stones and present them to Kostya.

If Zahar takes two stones, he should glue them together on one of the faces in order to get a new piece of rectangular parallelepiped of marble. Thus, it is possible to glue a pair of stones together if and only if two faces on which they are glued together match as rectangles. In such gluing it is allowed to rotate and flip the stones in any way.
Help Zahar choose such a present so that Kostya can carve a sphere of the maximum possible volume and present it to Zahar.
input: The first line contains the integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 105).

n lines follow, in the i-th of which there are three integers ai, bi and ci (1 ≤ ai, bi, ci ≤ 109) — the lengths of edges of the i-th stone. Note, that two stones may have exactly the same sizes, but they still will be considered two different stones.

You can print the stones in arbitrary order. If there are several answers print any of them.
note: In the first example we can connect the pairs of stones:
2 and 4, the size of the parallelepiped: 3 × 2 × 5, the radius of the inscribed sphere 1
2 and 5, the size of the parallelepiped: 3 × 2 × 8 or 6 × 2 × 4 or 3 × 4 × 4, the radius of the inscribed sphere 1, or 1, or 1.5 respectively.
2 and 6, the size of the parallelepiped: 3 × 5 × 4, the radius of the inscribed sphere 1.5
4 and 5, the size of the parallelepiped: 3 × 2 × 5, the radius of the inscribed sphere 1
5 and 6, the size of the parallelepiped: 3 × 4 × 5, the radius of the inscribed sphere 1.5
Or take only one stone:
1 the size of the parallelepiped: 5 × 5 × 5, the radius of the inscribed sphere 2.5
2 the size of the parallelepiped: 3 × 2 × 4, the radius of the inscribed sphere 1
3 the size of the parallelepiped: 1 × 4 × 1, the radius of the inscribed sphere 0.5
4 the size of the parallelepiped: 2 × 1 × 3, the radius of the inscribed sphere 0.5
5 the size of the parallelepiped: 3 × 2 × 4, the radius of the inscribed sphere 1
6 the size of the parallelepiped: 3 × 3 × 4, the radius of the inscribed sphere 1.5
It is most profitable to take only the first stone.

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，我们可以将石头两两连接：
2 和 4，平行六面体的尺寸为：3 × 2 × 5，内切球半径为 1
2 和 5，平行六面体的尺寸为：3 × 2 × 8、6 × 2 × 4 或 3 × 4 × 4，内切球半径分别为 1、1 和 1.5。
2 和 6，平行六面体的尺寸为：3 × 5 × 4，内切球半径为 1.5
4 和 5，平行六面体的尺寸为：3 × 2 × 5，内切球半径为 1

legend: Xenia likes puzzles very much. She is especially fond of the puzzles that consist of domino pieces. Look at the picture that shows one of such puzzles.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/eb51a91364aa18af4937d79e8dd11039eb9f5154.png)
A puzzle is a 3 × n table with forbidden cells (black squares) containing dominoes (colored rectangles on the picture). A puzzle is called correct if it meets the following conditions:
each domino occupies exactly two non-forbidden cells of the table;
no two dominoes occupy the same table cell;
exactly one non-forbidden cell of the table is unoccupied by any domino (it is marked by a circle in the picture).

To solve the puzzle, you need multiple steps to transport an empty cell from the starting position to some specified position. A move is transporting a domino to the empty cell, provided that the puzzle stays correct. The horizontal dominoes can be moved only horizontally, and vertical dominoes can be moved only vertically. You can't rotate dominoes. The picture shows a probable move.

Xenia has a 3 × n table with forbidden cells and a cell marked with a circle. Also, Xenia has very many identical dominoes. Now Xenia is wondering, how many distinct correct puzzles she can make if she puts dominoes on the existing table. Also, Xenia wants the circle-marked cell to be empty in the resulting puzzle. The puzzle must contain at least one move.
Help Xenia, count the described number of puzzles. As the described number can be rather large, print the remainder after dividing it by 1000000007 (109 + 7).
input: The first line contains integer n (3 ≤ n ≤ 104) — the puzzle's size. Each of the following three lines contains n characters — the description of the table. The j-th character of the i-th line equals "X" if the corresponding cell is forbidden; it equals ".", if the corresponding cell is non-forbidden and "O", if the corresponding cell is marked with a circle.
It is guaranteed that exactly one cell in the table is marked with a circle. It is guaranteed that all cells of a given table having at least one common point with the marked cell is non-forbidden.
output: Print a single number — the answer to the problem modulo 1000000007 (109 + 7).
note: Two puzzles are considered distinct if there is a pair of cells that contain one domino in one puzzle and do not contain it in the other one.

legend.ai: Xenia 非常喜欢谜题。她尤其喜欢由多米诺骨牌组成的谜题。请看展示了其中一个谜题的图片。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/eb51a91364aa18af4937d79e8dd11039eb9f5154.png)
一个谜题是一个 3 × n 的表格，其中有禁用单元格（黑色方格），并放置着多米诺骨牌（图中的彩色矩形）。如果一个谜题满足以下条件，则称其为正确：
每块多米诺骨牌恰好占据表格中的两个非禁用单元格；
没有两个多米诺骨牌占据同一个表格单元格；
表格中恰好有一个非禁用单元格未被任何多米诺骨牌占据（图中用圆圈标出）。
为了完成这个谜题，你需要经过多步操作，将一个空单元格从起始位置移动到某个指定位置。一次移动是将一个多米诺骨牌移到空单元格处，前提是移动后谜题仍然正确。横向多米诺骨牌只能水平移动，竖向多米诺骨牌只能竖直移动。你不能旋转多米诺骨牌。图中展示了一种可能的移动。

legend: Some time ago Leonid have known about idempotent functions. Idempotent function defined on a set {1, 2, ..., n} is such function ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/be90664fb67fc59aea0742746b0626ddab543582.png), that for any ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/75df05ed78f11fc97381dcb0cd5b104b9483ca8f.png) the formula g(g(x)) = g(x) holds.
Let's denote as f(k)(x) the function f applied k times to the value x. More formally, f(1)(x) = f(x), f(k)(x) = f(f(k - 1)(x)) for each k > 1.

You are given some function ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/58da889a2e5c65797055ac8eba57b4a01abee69c.png). Your task is to find minimum positive integer k such that function f(k)(x) is idempotent.
input: In the first line of the input there is a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 200) — the size of function f domain.
In the second line follow f(1), f(2), ..., f(n) (1 ≤ f(i) ≤ n for each 1 ≤ i ≤ n), the values of a function.
output: Output minimum k such that function f(k)(x) is idempotent.
note: In the first sample test function f(x) = f(1)(x) is already idempotent since f(f(1)) = f(1) = 1, f(f(2)) = f(2) = 2, f(f(3)) = f(3) = 2, f(f(4)) = f(4) = 4.
In the second sample test:
function f(x) = f(1)(x) isn't idempotent because f(f(1)) = 3 but f(1) = 2;
function f(x) = f(2)(x) is idempotent since for any x it is true that f(2)(x) = 3, so it is also true that f(2)(f(2)(x)) = 3.
In the third sample test:
function f(x) = f(1)(x) isn't idempotent because f(f(1)) = 3 but f(1) = 2;
function f(f(x)) = f(2)(x) isn't idempotent because f(2)(f(2)(1)) = 2 but f(2)(1) = 3;

function f(f(f(x))) = f(3)(x) is idempotent since it is identity function: f(3)(x) = x for any ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/46a8c73444c646004dfde04451775e7af924d108.png) meaning that the formula f(3)(f(3)(x)) = f(3)(x) also holds.

legend.ai: 前段时间，Leonid 了解了幂等函数。定义在集合 {1, 2, ..., n} 上的幂等函数是满足 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/be90664fb67fc59aea0742746b0626ddab543582.png) 的函数，即对于任意 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/75df05ed78f11fc97381dcb0cd5b104b9483ca8f.png)，等式 g(g(x)) = g(x) 成立。
将函数 f 对值 x 应用 k 次后的结果记为 f(k)(x)。更形式化地，f(1)(x) = f(x)，并且对于每个 k > 1，都有 f(k)(x) = f(f(k - 1)(x))。
给定函数 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/58da889a2e5c65797055ac8eba57b4a01abee69c.png)。你的任务是找出最小正整数 k，使得函数 f(k)(x) 是幂等函数。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 200）——函数 f 定义域的大小。
第二行包含 f(1)， f(2)， ...， f(n)（对于每个 1 ≤ f(i) ≤ n），即函数的各个值。

output.ai: 输出使函数 f(k)(x) 幂等的最小 k。

note.ai: 在第二个样例测试中：
函数 f(x) = f(1)(x) 不是幂等的，因为 f(f(1)) = 3，但 f(1) = 2；
函数 f(x) = f(2)(x) 是幂等的，因为对于任意 x，都有 f(2)(x) = 3，因此也有 f(2)(f(2)(x)) = 3。
在第三个样例测试中：
函数 f(x) = f(1)(x) 不是幂等的，因为 f(f(1)) = 3，但 f(1) = 2；
函数 f(f(f(x))) = f(3)(x) 是幂等的，因为它是恒等函数：对于任意 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/46a8c73444c646004dfde04451775e7af924d108.png)，f(3)(x) = x，这意味着公式 f(3)(f(3)(x)) = f(3)(x) 也成立。

problems.hint: It's about crossing lines. You can cross $2$ at a time.

legend: You are given an infinite checkered field. You should get from a square (x1; y1) to a square (x2; y2). Using the shortest path is not necessary. You can move on the field squares in four directions. That is, when you are positioned in any square, you can move to any other side-neighboring one.
A square (x; y) is considered bad, if at least one of the two conditions is fulfilled:
|x + y| ≡ 0 (mod 2a),
|x - y| ≡ 0 (mod 2b).
Your task is to find the minimum number of bad cells one will have to visit on the way from (x1; y1) to (x2; y2).
input: The only line contains integers a, b, x1, y1, x2 and y2 — the parameters of the bad squares, the coordinates of the initial and the final squares correspondingly (2 ≤ a, b ≤ 109 and |x1|,|y1|,|x2|,|y2| ≤ 109). It is guaranteed that the initial and the final square aren't bad.
output: Print a single number — the minimum number of bad cells that one will have to visit in order to travel from square (x1; y1) to square (x2; y2).

legend.ai: 给定一个无限的棋盘格。你需要从方格 (x1; y1) 到达方格 (x2; y2)。不必使用最短路径。你可以沿四个方向在棋盘格上移动。也就是说，当你位于任意一个方格时，你可以移动到与其共边相邻的任意另一个方格。
如果以下两个条件中至少一个成立，则称方格 (x; y) 是坏的：
|x + y| ≡ 0 (mod 2a),
|x - y| ≡ 0 (mod 2b).
你的任务是求出从 (x1; y1) 到 (x2; y2) 的路上必须经过的坏格子的最少数量。

input.ai: 唯一一行包含整数 a、b、x1、y1、x2 和 y2——坏方格的参数，以及初始方格和最终方格的坐标（2 ≤ a, b ≤ 109 且 |x1|,|y1|,|x2|,|y2| ≤ 109）。保证初始方格和最终方格都不是坏方格。

output.ai: 输出一个数——从方格 (x1; y1) 到方格 (x2; y2) 行进时必须经过的坏格子的最少数量。

problems.hint: There are only a few ways to put the balloons.

legend: A girl named Xenia has a cupboard that looks like an arc from ahead. The arc is made of a semicircle with radius r (the cupboard's top) and two walls of height h (the cupboard's sides). The cupboard's depth is r, that is, it looks like a rectangle with base r and height h + r from the sides. The figure below shows what the cupboard looks like (the front view is on the left, the side view is on the right).
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a0859d707114926c37a2a1fec2a9d1e5df510e60.png)

Xenia got lots of balloons for her birthday. The girl hates the mess, so she wants to store the balloons in the cupboard. Luckily, each balloon is a sphere with radius ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a4fcadf5554db1a524f8d91fc4f6fb6d9fa61718.png). Help Xenia calculate the maximum number of balloons she can put in her cupboard.

You can say that a balloon is in the cupboard if you can't see any part of the balloon on the left or right view. The balloons in the cupboard can touch each other. It is not allowed to squeeze the balloons or deform them in any way. You can assume that the cupboard's walls are negligibly thin.
input: The single line contains two integers r, h (1 ≤ r, h ≤ 107).
output: Print a single integer — the maximum number of balloons Xenia can put in the cupboard.

output.ai: 输出一个整数——Xenia 能放入橱柜中的气球的最大数量。

legend.ai: 一个名叫 Xenia 的女孩有一个柜子，从正面看起来像一段圆弧。这段圆弧由一个半径为 r 的半圆（柜子的顶部）和两面高度为 h 的墙（柜子的两侧）组成。柜子的深度为 r，也就是说，从侧面看它是一个底边长为 r、高为 h + r 的矩形。下图展示了柜子的样子（左边是正视图，右边是侧视图）。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a0859d707114926c37a2a1fec2a9d1e5df510e60.png)
Xenia 生日时得到了很多气球。这个女孩讨厌杂乱，因此她想把气球存放在柜子里。幸运的是，每个气球都是半径为 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a4fcadf5554db1a524f8d91fc4f6fb6d9fa61718.png) 的球体。请帮助 Xenia 计算她最多可以放入柜子中的气球数量。
如果从左视图或右视图中都看不到气球的任何部分，就可以认为气球在柜子里。柜子里的气球可以彼此接触。不允许挤压气球，也不允许以任何方式使它们变形。你可以假设柜子的墙壁厚度可以忽略不计。

input.ai: 一行包含两个整数 r、h（1 ≤ r，h ≤ 107）。

problems.hint: Find a rule of the parent node.

legend: During the programming classes Vasya was assigned a difficult problem. However, he doesn't know how to code and was unable to find the solution in the Internet, so he asks you to help.
You are given a sequence a$$$a$$$, consisting of n$$$n$$$ distinct integers, that is used to construct the binary search tree. Below is the formal description of the construction process.
First element a1$$$a_1$$$ becomes the root of the tree.

Elements a2,a3,…,an$$$a_2, a_3, \ldots, a_n$$$ are added one by one. To add element ai$$$a_i$$$ one needs to traverse the tree starting from the root and using the following rules:   The pointer to the current node is set to the root.
If ai$$$a_i$$$ is greater than the value in the current node, then its right child becomes the current node. Otherwise, the left child of the current node becomes the new current node.
If at some point there is no required child, the new node is created, it is assigned value ai$$$a_i$$$ and becomes the corresponding child of the current node.
input: The first line of the input contains a single integer n$$$n$$$ (2≤n≤100000$$$2 \leq n \leq 100\,000$$$) — the length of the sequence a$$$a$$$.
The second line contains n$$$n$$$ distinct integers ai$$$a_i$$$ (1≤ai≤109$$$1 \leq a_i \leq 10^9$$$) — the sequence a$$$a$$$ itself.
output: Output n−1$$$n - 1$$$ integers. For all i>1$$$i  \gt  1$$$ print the value written in the node that is the parent of the node with value ai$$$a_i$$$ in it.

legend.ai: 在编程课上，Vasya 被布置了一道难题。然而，他不会编程，也没能在互联网上找到解法，所以他请求你帮助。
给定一个序列 a$$$a$$$，它由 n$$$n$$$ 个互不相同的整数构成，用于构造二叉搜索树。下面给出构造过程的形式化描述。
第一个元素 a1$$$a_1$$$ 成为树的根。
元素 a2,a3,…,an$$$a_2, a_3, \ldots, a_n$$$ 依次加入。为了添加元素 ai$$$a_i$$$，需要从根开始按照以下规则遍历这棵树：   将指向当前节点的指针设置为根节点。
如果 ai$$$a_i$$$ 大于当前节点中的值，那么其右儿子就成为当前节点。否则，当前节点的左儿子成为新的当前节点。
如果在某一步不存在所需的儿子，则创建新节点，将其值赋为 ai$$$a_i$$$，并使其成为当前节点的相应儿子。

input.ai: 第二行包含 n$$$n$$$ 个互不相同的整数 ai$$$a_i$$$(1≤ai≤109$$$1 \leq a_i \leq 10^9$$$)——序列 a$$$a$$$ 本身。

output.ai: 输出 n−1$$$n - 1$$$ 个整数。对于所有 i>1$$$i  \gt  1$$$，输出值为 ai$$$a_i$$$ 的节点的父节点中记录的值。

problems.hint: It's just rounds of task completion.

legend: You are given a program you want to execute as a set of tasks organized in a dependency graph. The dependency graph is a directed acyclic graph: each task can depend on results of one or several other tasks, and there are no directed circular dependencies between tasks. A task can only be executed if all tasks it depends on have already completed.

Some of the tasks in the graph can only be executed on a coprocessor, and the rest can only be executed on the main processor. In one coprocessor call you can send it a set of tasks which can only be executed on it. For each task of the set, all tasks on which it depends must be either already completed or be included in the set. The main processor starts the program execution and gets the results of tasks executed on the coprocessor automatically.
Find the minimal number of coprocessor calls which are necessary to execute the given program.
input: The first line contains two space-separated integers N (1 ≤ N ≤ 105) — the total number of tasks given, and M (0 ≤ M ≤ 105) — the total number of dependencies between tasks.

The next line contains N space-separated integers ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b8ea124a4b6cdc09e444caafe74db01b7c444d1b.png). If Ei = 0, task i can only be executed on the main processor, otherwise it can only be executed on the coprocessor.

The next M lines describe the dependencies between tasks. Each line contains two space-separated integers T1 and T2 and means that task T1 depends on task T2 (T1 ≠ T2). Tasks are indexed from 0 to N - 1. All M pairs (T1, T2) are distinct. It is guaranteed that there are no circular dependencies between tasks.
output: Output one line containing an integer — the minimal number of coprocessor calls necessary to execute the program.
note: In the first test, tasks 1 and 3 can only be executed on the coprocessor. The dependency graph is linear, so the tasks must be executed in order 3 -> 2 -> 1 -> 0. You have to call coprocessor twice: first you call it for task 3, then you execute task 2 on the main processor, then you call it for for task 1, and finally you execute task 0 on the main processor.

In the second test, tasks 0, 1 and 2 can only be executed on the coprocessor. Tasks 1 and 2 have no dependencies, and task 0 depends on tasks 1 and 2, so all three tasks 0, 1 and 2 can be sent in one coprocessor call. After that task 3 is executed on the main processor.

legend.ai: 给定一个想要执行的程序，该程序由一组按照依赖图组织的任务组成。依赖图是有向无环图：每个任务可以依赖于其他一个或多个任务的结果，且任务之间不存在有向环依赖。只有当一个任务所依赖的所有任务都已完成时，才能执行该任务。
图中的一些任务只能在协处理器上执行，其余任务只能在主处理器上执行。在一次协处理器调用中，可以向协处理器发送一组只能在其上执行的任务。对于该集合中的每个任务，它所依赖的所有任务都必须已经完成，或者包含在该集合中。主处理器启动程序的执行，并自动获得在协处理器上执行的任务的结果。
求执行给定程序所必需的最少协处理器调用次数。

input.ai: 第一行包含两个由空格分隔的整数 N（1 ≤ N ≤ 10^5）——给定的任务总数，以及 M（0 ≤ M ≤ 10^5）——任务之间的依赖关系总数。
下一行包含 N 个由空格分隔的整数 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b8ea124a4b6cdc09e444caafe74db01b7c444d1b.png)。如果 E_i = 0，则任务 i 只能在主处理器上执行，否则只能在协处理器上执行。
接下来的 M 行描述任务之间的依赖关系。每行包含两个由空格分隔的整数 T1 和 T2，表示任务 T1 依赖于任务 T2（T1 ≠ T2）。任务编号从 0 到 N − 1。所有 M 对 (T1, T2) 互不相同。保证任务之间不存在循环依赖。

output.ai: 输出一行，其中包含一个整数——执行该程序所需的最少协处理器调用次数。

note.ai: 在第一个测试中，任务 1 和 3 只能在协处理器上执行。依赖图是线性的，因此任务必须按 3 -> 2 -> 1 -> 0 的顺序执行。你需要调用协处理器两次：首先为任务 3 调用协处理器，然后在主处理器上执行任务 2，接着为任务 1 调用协处理器，最后在主处理器上执行任务 0。
在第二个测试中，任务 0、1 和 2 只能在协处理器上执行。任务 1 和 2 没有依赖，而任务 0 依赖于任务 1 和 2，因此任务 0、1 和 2 可以在一次协处理器调用中全部发送。之后，任务 3 在主处理器上执行。

problems.hint: Iterate over the last ticket.

legend: A new innovative ticketing systems for public transport is introduced in Bytesburg. Now there is a single travel card for all transport. To make a trip a passenger scan his card and then he is charged according to the fare.
The fare is constructed in the following manner. There are three types of tickets:
a ticket for one trip costs 20 byteland rubles,
a ticket for 90 minutes costs 50 byteland rubles,
a ticket for one day (1440 minutes) costs 120 byteland rubles.
Note that a ticket for x minutes activated at time t can be used for trips started in time range from t to t + x - 1, inclusive. Assume that all trips take exactly one minute.

To simplify the choice for the passenger, the system automatically chooses the optimal tickets. After each trip starts, the system analyses all the previous trips and the current trip and chooses a set of tickets for these trips with a minimum total cost. Let the minimum total cost of tickets to cover all trips from the first to the current is a, and the total sum charged before is b. Then the system charges the passenger the sum a - b.
You have to write a program that, for given trips made by a passenger, calculates the sum the passenger is charged after each trip.
input: The first line of input contains integer number n (1 ≤ n ≤ 105) — the number of trips made by passenger.

Each of the following n lines contains the time of trip ti (0 ≤ ti ≤ 109), measured in minutes from the time of starting the system. All ti are different, given in ascending order, i. e. ti + 1 > ti holds for all 1 ≤ i < n.
output: Output n integers. For each trip, print the sum the passenger is charged after it.
note: In the first example, the system works as follows: for the first and second trips it is cheaper to pay for two one-trip tickets, so each time 20 rubles is charged, after the third trip the system understands that it would be cheaper to buy a ticket for 90 minutes. This ticket costs 50 rubles, and the passenger had already paid 40 rubles, so it is necessary to charge 10 rubles only.

legend.ai: Bytesburg 引入了一种用于公共交通的新型创新售票系统。现在，所有交通工具共用一张旅行卡。乘客出行时扫描自己的卡片，然后按照票价收费。
票价按以下方式确定。票有三种类型：
单次乘车票的价格为 20 拜特兰卢布，
90 分钟乘车票的价格为 50 拜特兰卢布，
一日（1440 分钟）乘车票的价格为 120 拜特兰卢布。
注意，在时间 t 激活的一张 x 分钟乘车票可用于在从 t 到 t + x - 1（含）的时间范围内开始的行程。假设每次行程恰好持续一分钟。
为了方便乘客选择，系统会自动选择最优的乘车票。每次行程开始后，系统会分析之前的所有行程和当前行程，并为这些行程选择一组总费用最低的乘车票。设覆盖从第一次行程到当前行程的乘车票最低总费用为 a，之前已收取的总金额为 b。那么系统会向乘客收取 a - b。
你需要编写一个程序，根据乘客的行程，计算每次行程后向乘客收取的金额。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5）——乘客乘坐的行程数。
接下来的 n 行中的每一行包含一次行程的时间 t_i（0 ≤ t_i ≤ 10^9），该时间以系统启动时刻起经过的分钟数表示。所有 t_i 互不相同，并按升序给出，即对于所有 1 ≤ i < n，均有 t_{i+1} > t_i。

output.ai: 输出 n 个整数。对于每次行程，输出乘客在该次行程后被收取的费用总额。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，系统的运行过程如下：对于第一次和第二次行程，购买两张单程票更便宜，因此每次收取 20 卢布；在第三次行程后，系统发现购买一张 90 分钟的车票更加便宜。这张车票的价格为 50 卢布，而乘客已经支付了 40 卢布，因此只需再收取 10 卢布。

problems.hint: Fix $(j_1,j_2)$ to find the possible $(i_1,i_2)$.

legend: Sonya had a birthday recently. She was presented with the matrix of size n×m$$$n\times m$$$ and consist of lowercase Latin letters. We assume that the rows are numbered by integers from 1$$$1$$$ to n$$$n$$$ from bottom to top, and the columns are numbered from 1$$$1$$$ to m$$$m$$$ from left to right.

Let's call a submatrix (i1,j1,i2,j2)$$$(i_1, j_1, i_2, j_2)$$$ (1≤i1≤i2≤n;1≤j1≤j2≤m)$$$(1\leq i_1\leq i_2\leq n; 1\leq j_1\leq j_2\leq m)$$$ elements aij$$$a_{ij}$$$ of this matrix, such that i1≤i≤i2$$$i_1\leq i\leq i_2$$$ and j1≤j≤j2$$$j_1\leq j\leq j_2$$$. Sonya states that a submatrix is beautiful if we can independently reorder the characters in each row (not in column) so that all rows and columns of this submatrix form palidroms.

Let's recall that a string is called palindrome if it reads the same from left to right and from right to left. For example, strings abacaba,bcaacb,a$$$abacaba, bcaacb, a$$$ are palindromes while strings abca,acbba,ab$$$abca, acbba, ab$$$ are not.
Help Sonya to find the number of beautiful submatrixes. Submatrixes are different if there is an element that belongs to only one submatrix.

Each of the next n$$$n$$$ lines contains m$$$m$$$ lowercase Latin letters.
output: Print one integer — the number of beautiful submatrixes.
note: The submatrix ((1,1),(3,5))$$$((1, 1), (3, 5))$$$ is beautiful since it can be reordered as:

legend.ai: Sonya 最近过生日。她收到了一个大小为 n×m$$$n\times m$$$ 的矩阵，矩阵由小写拉丁字母组成。我们规定，行从下到上依次编号为 1$$$1$$$ 到 n$$$n$$$，列从左到右依次编号为 1$$$1$$$ 到 m$$$m$$$。

我们称一个子矩阵 (i1,j1,i2,j2)$$$(i_1, j_1, i_2, j_2)$$$ (1≤i1≤i2≤n;1≤j1≤j2≤m)$$$(1\leq i_1\leq i_2\leq n; 1\leq j_1\leq j_2\leq m)$$$ 由该矩阵的元素 aij$$$a_{ij}$$$ 构成，当 i1≤i≤i2$$$i_1\leq i\leq i_2$$$ 且 j1≤j≤j2$$$j_1\leq j\leq j_2$$$ 时成立。Sonya 声称，如果我们可以独立地重新排列每一行中的字符(不能重新排列列中的字符)，使得该子矩阵的所有行和所有列都构成回文串，那么这个子矩阵就是美丽的。
我们知道，如果一个字符串从左到右和从右到左读起来相同，那么它就是回文串。例如，字符串 abacaba,bcaacb,a$$$abacaba, bcaacb, a$$$ 是回文串，而字符串 abca,acbba,ab$$$abca, acbba, ab$$$ 不是。
请帮助 Sonya 求出美丽子矩阵的数量。如果存在一个元素只属于两个子矩阵中的一个，则这两个子矩阵不同。

input.ai: 第一行包含两个整数 n$$$n$$$ 和 m$$$m$$$(1≤n,m≤250)$$$(1\leq n, m\leq 250)$$$——矩阵的行数和列数。
接下来的 n$$$n$$$ 行中，每行包含 m$$$m$$$ 个小写拉丁字母。

output.ai: 输出一个整数——美丽子矩阵的数量。

note.ai: 在这样的矩阵中，每一行和每一列都构成回文。

problems.hint: The MEX of the array changes only a few times.

legend: You are given an array of n$$$n$$$ nonnegative integers a1,a2,…,an$$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$.
Let m$$$m$$$ be a variable that is initialized to 0$$$0$$$, Jellyfish will perform the following operation n$$$n$$$ times:

legend: Denis, after buying flowers and sweets (you will learn about this story in the next task), went to a date with Nastya to ask her to become a couple. Now, they are sitting in the cafe and finally... Denis asks her to be together, but ... Nastya doesn't give any answer.

The poor boy was very upset because of that. He was so sad that he punched some kind of scoreboard with numbers. The numbers are displayed in the same way as on an electronic clock: each digit position consists of 7$$$7$$$ segments, which can be turned on or off to display different numbers. The picture shows how all 10$$$10$$$ decimal digits are displayed:
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/19e4ae06aceef4b9326d2ef6bca3339f5c84ed91.png)

After the punch, some segments stopped working, that is, some segments might stop glowing if they glowed earlier. But Denis remembered how many sticks were glowing and how many are glowing now. Denis broke exactly k$$$k$$$ segments and he knows which sticks are working now. Denis came up with the question: what is the maximum possible number that can appear on the board if you turn on exactly k$$$k$$$ sticks (which are off now)?
It is allowed that the number includes leading zeros.
input: The first line contains integer n$$$n$$$ (1≤n≤2000)$$$(1 \leq n \leq 2000)$$$  — the number of digits on scoreboard and k$$$k$$$ (0≤k≤2000)$$$(0 \leq k \leq 2000)$$$  — the number of segments that stopped working.
The next n$$$n$$$ lines contain one binary string of length 7$$$7$$$, the i$$$i$$$-th of which encodes the i$$$i$$$-th digit of the scoreboard.

Each digit on the scoreboard consists of 7$$$7$$$ segments. We number them, as in the picture below, and let the i$$$i$$$-th place of the binary string be 0$$$0$$$ if the i$$$i$$$-th stick is not glowing and 1$$$1$$$ if it is glowing. Then a binary string of length 7$$$7$$$ will specify which segments are glowing now.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/21dfa922ece26c6a6c647e0fc4f7a87cfb4db36f.png)
output: Output a single number consisting of n$$$n$$$ digits  — the maximum number that can be obtained if you turn on exactly k$$$k$$$ sticks or −1$$$-1$$$, if it is impossible to turn on exactly k$$$k$$$ sticks so that a correct number appears on the scoreboard digits.
note: In the first test, we are obliged to include all 7$$$7$$$ sticks and get one 8$$$8$$$ digit on the scoreboard.

In the second test, we have sticks turned on so that units are formed. For 5$$$5$$$ of additionally included sticks, you can get the numbers 07$$$07$$$, 18$$$18$$$, 34$$$34$$$, 43$$$43$$$, 70$$$70$$$, 79$$$79$$$, 81$$$81$$$ and 97$$$97$$$, of which we choose the maximum  — 97$$$97$$$.
In the third test, it is impossible to turn on exactly 5$$$5$$$ sticks so that a sequence of numbers appears on the scoreboard.
