可怜的男孩因此非常难过。他悲伤至极，竟然一拳打在了某个显示数字的记分板上。数字的显示方式与电子钟相同：每个数位由 7$$$7$$$ 段组成，可以通过点亮或熄灭不同的段来显示不同的数字。图片展示了全部 10$$$10$$$ 个十进制数字的显示方式：

拳击之后，一些数码管段停止工作，也就是说，之前发光的某些段可能不再发光。但是丹尼斯记得之前有多少根灯条在发光，以及现在有多少根在发光。丹尼斯弄坏了恰好 k$$$k$$$ 段，并且他知道现在哪些灯条仍然可以工作。丹尼斯想出了这样一个问题：如果恰好点亮 k$$$k$$$ 根(当前处于熄灭状态的)灯条，显示板上可能出现的最大数字是多少？

legend: Jill loves having good grades in university, so she never misses deadlines for her homework assignments. But even more, she loves watching the series and discussing it with her best friend Johnny. And unfortunately, today she needs to choose between these two activities!

Jill needs to complete n$$$n$$$ homework tasks. The i$$$i$$$-th task would require ai$$$a_i$$$ minutes to complete and needs to be submitted to the teacher at most di$$$d_i$$$ minutes from now. Also, there are m$$$m$$$ new episodes of the series that Johnny and Jill want to discuss. The j$$$j$$$-th episode lasts lj$$$l_j$$$ minutes. Jill can complete tasks in any order, but she needs to watch the episodes in the order they come. Neither completing a homework task nor watching an episode can be interrupted after starting.

Johnny and Jill need to agree on a time tk$$$t_k$$$ when they would have a call to discuss the series. They are not sure yet which time to choose. For each possible time, compute the maximum number of episodes Jill could watch before that time while still being able to complete all n$$$n$$$ homework tasks in time.

Note that for the purpose of this problem we assume that discussing the series with Johnny at time tk$$$t_k$$$ does not consume significant time from Jill and can happen even if she is in the middle of completing any of her homework tasks.

statement.title: C. Devu and Partitioning of the Array

legend: Devu being a small kid, likes to play a lot, but he only likes to play with arrays. While playing he came up with an interesting question which he could not solve, can you please solve it for him?

Given an array consisting of distinct integers. Is it possible to partition the whole array into k disjoint non-empty parts such that p of the parts have even sum (each of them must have even sum) and remaining k - p have odd sum? (note that parts need not to be continuous).
If it is possible to partition the array, also give any possible way of valid partitioning.
input: The first line will contain three space separated integers n, k, p (1 ≤ k ≤ n ≤ 105; 0 ≤ p ≤ k). The next line will contain n space-separated distinct integers representing the content of array a: a1, a2, ..., an (1 ≤ ai ≤ 109).
output: In the first line print "YES" (without the quotes) if it is possible to partition the array in the required way. Otherwise print "NO" (without the quotes).

If the required partition exists, print k lines after the first line. The ith of them should contain the content of the ith part. Print the content of the part in the line in the following way: firstly print the number of elements of the part, then print all the elements of the part in arbitrary order. There must be exactly p parts with even sum, each of the remaining k - p parts must have odd sum.
As there can be multiple partitions, you are allowed to print any valid partition.

output.ai: 在第一行输出 "YES"（不带引号），如果能够按要求划分数组。否则输出 "NO"（不带引号）。
如果所需的划分存在，在第一行之后输出 k 行。第 i 行应包含第 i 部分的内容。按如下方式在一行中输出该部分的内容：首先输出该部分的元素个数，然后以任意顺序输出该部分的所有元素。必须恰好有 p 个部分的和为偶数，其余 k - p 个部分的和都必须为奇数。
由于可能存在多种划分，你可以输出任意一种合法划分。

legend.ai: Devu 是个小孩子，喜欢玩耍，但他只喜欢玩数组。玩耍时，他想出了一个有趣的问题，却无法解决，你能帮他解决吗？

如果可以划分，还需给出任意一种有效的划分方案。

legend: Zart PMP is qualified for ICPC World Finals in Harbin, China. After team excursion to Sun Island Park for snow sculpture art exposition, PMP should get back to buses before they leave. But the park is really big and he does not know how to find them.

The park has n intersections numbered 1 through n. There are m bidirectional roads that connect some pairs of these intersections. At k intersections, ICPC volunteers are helping the teams and showing them the way to their destinations. Locations of volunteers are fixed and distinct.

When PMP asks a volunteer the way to bus station, he/she can tell him the whole path. But the park is fully covered with ice and snow and everywhere looks almost the same. So PMP can only memorize at most q intersections after each question (excluding the intersection they are currently standing). He always tells volunteers about his weak memory and if there is no direct path of length (in number of roads) at most q that leads to bus station, the volunteer will guide PMP to another volunteer (who is at most q intersections away, of course). ICPC volunteers know the area very well and always tell PMP the best way. So if there exists a way to bus stations, PMP will definitely find it.

PMP's initial location is intersection s and the buses are at intersection t. There will always be a volunteer at intersection s. Your job is to find out the minimum q which guarantees that PMP can find the buses.
input: The first line contains three space-separated integers n, m, k (2 ≤ n ≤ 105, 0 ≤ m ≤ 2·105, 1 ≤ k ≤ n) — the number of intersections, roads and volunteers, respectively. Next line contains k distinct space-separated integers between 1 and n inclusive — the numbers of cities where volunteers are located.

Next m lines describe the roads. The i-th of these lines contains two space-separated integers ui, vi (1 ≤ ui, vi ≤ n, ui ≠ vi) — two intersections that i-th road connects. There will be at most one road between any two intersections.
Last line of input contains two space-separated integers s, t (1 ≤ s, t ≤ n, s ≠ t) — the initial location of PMP and the location of the buses. It might not always be possible to reach t from s.
It is guaranteed that there is always a volunteer at intersection s.
output: Print on the only line the answer to the problem — the minimum value of q which guarantees that PMP can find the buses. If PMP cannot reach the buses at all, output -1 instead.
note: The first sample is illustrated below. Blue intersections are where volunteers are located. If PMP goes in the path of dashed line, it can reach the buses with q = 3:
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a1f626be4f756a007133181452aa752498ded077.png)
In the second sample, PMP uses intersection 6 as an intermediate intersection, thus the answer is 3.

output.ai: 在唯一一行输出问题的答案——保证 PMP 能找到公交车的最小值 q。如果 PMP 根本无法到达公交车，则输出 -1。

note.ai: 第一个样例说明如下。蓝色交叉路口是志愿者所在的位置。如果 PMP 沿着虚线路径前进，则在 q=3 时可以到达公交车：
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a1f626be4f756a007133181452aa752498ded077.png)
在第二个样例中，PMP 将交叉路口 6 作为中间交叉路口，因此答案为 3。

legend.ai: Zart PMP 获得了参加在中国哈尔滨举行的 ICPC 世界总决赛的资格。团队游览太阳岛公园的雪雕艺术展之后，PMP 必须在大巴车离开之前回到车旁。但公园真的很大，他不知道该如何找到它们。
公园有 n 个路口，编号为 1 到 n。有 m 条双向道路连接其中的一些路口。在 k 个路口处，ICPC 志愿者正在帮助参赛队伍，为他们指明前往目的地的道路。志愿者的位置是固定且互不相同的。

当 PMP 向一名志愿者询问前往公交车站的路线时，志愿者可以告诉他整条路径。然而，公园完全被冰雪覆盖，四处看起来几乎一模一样。因此，PMP 每次询问后最多只能记住 q 个路口（不包括他当前所在的路口）。他总会告诉志愿者自己的记忆力很差；如果不存在一条长度（以道路数量计）不超过 q、通往公交车站的路径，志愿者就会引导 PMP 去找另一名志愿者（当然，这名志愿者距离他不超过 q 个路口）。ICPC 志愿者非常熟悉这片区域，并且总会告诉 PMP 最优路线。因此，只要存在通往公交车站的路径，PMP 就一定能找到它。
PMP 的初始位置是路口 s，公交车位于路口 t。你的任务是求出能够保证 PMP 找到公交车的最小 q。

input.ai: 第一行包含三个用空格分隔的整数 n、m、k（2 ≤ n ≤ 10^5，0 ≤ m ≤ 2·10^5，1 ≤ k ≤ n）——路口、道路和志愿者的数量。下一行包含 k 个互不相同的、介于 1 和 n（含）之间的用空格分隔的整数——志愿者所在路口的编号。
接下来的 m 行描述道路。第 i 行包含两个用空格分隔的整数 u_i、v_i（1 ≤ u_i, v_i ≤ n，u_i ≠ v_i）——第 i 条道路连接的两个路口。任意两个路口之间至多有一条道路。
输入的最后一行包含两个用空格分隔的整数 s、t（1 ≤ s、t ≤ n，s ≠ t）——PMP 的初始位置和公交车所在的位置。从 s 不一定总能到达 t。
保证路口 s 处始终有一名志愿者。

legend: Alice has a very important message M consisting of some non-negative integers that she wants to keep secret from Eve. Alice knows that the only theoretically secure cipher is one-time pad. Alice generates a random key K of the length equal to the message's length. Alice computes the bitwise xor of each element of the message and the key (![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/0c01d57961927bc12eb51d8197470990daaaa8de.png), where ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c4b7092c0f7ce6535f2574569c98f7b3c2fe2c5f.png) denotes the bitwise XOR operation) and stores this encrypted message A. Alice is smart. Be like Alice.
For example, Alice may have wanted to store a message M = (0, 15, 9, 18). She generated a key K = (16, 7, 6, 3). The encrypted message is thus A = (16, 8, 15, 17).
Alice realised that she cannot store the key with the encrypted message. Alice sent her key K to Bob and deleted her own copy. Alice is smart. Really, be like Alice.

Bob realised that the encrypted message is only secure as long as the key is secret. Bob thus randomly permuted the key before storing it. Bob thinks that this way, even if Eve gets both the encrypted message and the key, she will not be able to read the message. Bob is not smart. Don't be like Bob.
In the above example, Bob may have, for instance, selected a permutation (3, 4, 1, 2) and stored the permuted key P = (6, 3, 16, 7).

One year has passed and Alice wants to decrypt her message. Only now Bob has realised that this is impossible. As he has permuted the key randomly, the message is lost forever. Did we mention that Bob isn't smart?

Bob wants to salvage at least some information from the message. Since he is not so smart, he asks for your help. You know the encrypted message A and the permuted key P. What is the lexicographically smallest message that could have resulted in the given encrypted text?

More precisely, for given A and P, find the lexicographically smallest message O, for which there exists a permutation π such that ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a13e05dbed3e9a47b9d8d6d0f07297a940549234.png) for every i.
Note that the sequence S is lexicographically smaller than the sequence T, if there is an index i such that Si < Ti and for all j < i the condition Sj = Tj holds.
input: The first line contains a single integer N (1 ≤ N ≤ 300000), the length of the message.
The second line contains N integers A1, A2, ..., AN (0 ≤ Ai < 230) representing the encrypted message.
The third line contains N integers P1, P2, ..., PN (0 ≤ Pi < 230) representing the permuted encryption key.
output: Output a single line with N integers, the lexicographically smallest possible message O. Note that all its elements should be non-negative.
note: In the first case, the solution is (10, 3, 28), since ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a896b30a69636d1bfbfa981eae10650f5fee843c.png), ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e383e4333ea37c4652ce2ac1ccfc2cfcf96e0896.png) and ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c24ed3c6f88805eb3710487b3fe07ff64034151a.png). Other possible permutations of key yield messages (25, 6, 10), (25, 3, 15), (10, 21, 10), (15, 21, 15) and (15, 6, 28), which are all lexicographically larger than the solution.

legend.ai: 爱丽丝有一条非常重要的消息 M，由一些非负整数组成，她想对 Eve 保密。爱丽丝知道唯一在理论上安全的加密方式是一次性密码本。爱丽丝生成了一个与消息长度相等的随机密钥 K。爱丽丝将消息和密钥中每个元素进行按位异或(![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/0c01d57961927bc12eb51d8197470990daaaa8de.png)，其中 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c4b7092c0f7ce6535f2574569c98f7b3c2fe2c5f.png) 表示按位异或运算)，并存储加密后的消息 A。爱丽丝很聪明。要像爱丽丝一样。
例如，Alice 可能想要存储一条消息 M = (0, 15, 9, 18)。她生成了一个密钥 K = (16, 7, 6, 3)。因此，加密后的消息为 A = (16, 8, 15, 17)。
Alice 意识到，她无法将密钥和加密后的消息存储在一起。于是 Alice 将她的密钥 K 发送给 Bob，并删除了自己手中的副本。Alice 很聪明。真的，要像 Alice 一样。
Bob 意识到，只要密钥是保密的，加密后的消息就是安全的。因此，Bob 在存储密钥之前随机打乱了密钥的顺序。Bob 认为这样一来，即使 Eve 同时获得了加密后的消息和密钥，她也无法读出消息。Bob 不聪明。不要学 Bob。
在上面的例子中，Bob 例如可以选择排列 (3, 4, 1, 2)，并存储打乱顺序后的密钥 P = (6, 3, 16, 7)。
一年过去了，Alice 想要解密她的消息。直到这时 Bob 才意识到这是不可能的。由于他随机打乱了密钥的顺序，这条消息永远丢失了。我们提过 Bob 不聪明吗？
Bob 想从这条消息中至少挽救一些信息。由于他没那么聪明，所以向你求助。你知道加密后的消息 A 和打乱顺序后的密钥 P。对于给定的加密文本，可能得到的消息中字典序最小的是哪一个？
更准确地说，给定 A 和 P，请找出字典序最小的消息 O，使得存在一个排列 π，对于每个 i 都有 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a13e05dbed3e9a47b9d8d6d0f07297a940549234.png)。
注意，如果存在一个下标 i，使得 Si < Ti，且对于所有 j < i 都满足 Sj = Tj，则序列 S 在字典序上小于序列 T。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 N（1 ≤ N ≤ 300000），表示消息的长度。
第二行包含 N 个整数 A1、A2、...、AN（0 ≤ Ai < 230），表示加密后的消息。
第三行包含 N 个整数 P1、P2、...、PN（0 ≤ Pi < 230），表示置换后的加密密钥。

output.ai: 输出一行，包含 N 个整数，即字典序最小的可能消息 O。注意，其所有元素都应为非负数。

note.ai: 在第一种情况下，答案是 (10, 3, 28)，因为 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a896b30a69636d1bfbfa981eae10650f5fee843c.png)、![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e383e4333ea37c4652ce2ac1ccfc2cfcf96e0896.png) 和 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c24ed3c6f88805eb3710487b3fe07ff64034151a.png)。密钥的其他可能排列会得到消息 (25, 6, 10)、(25, 3, 15)、(10, 21, 10)、(15, 21, 15) 和 (15, 6, 28)，它们在字典序上都大于该答案。

legend: The only difference with E1 is the question of the problem.

Vlad built a maze out of n$$$n$$$ rooms and n−1$$$n-1$$$ bidirectional corridors. From any room u$$$u$$$ any other room v$$$v$$$ can be reached through a sequence of corridors. Thus, the room system forms an undirected tree.
Vlad invited k$$$k$$$ friends to play a game with them.

Vlad starts the game in the room 1$$$1$$$ and wins if he reaches a room other than 1$$$1$$$, into which exactly one corridor leads. Friends are placed in the maze: the friend with number i$$$i$$$ is in the room xi$$$x_i$$$, and no two friends are in the same room (that is, xi≠xj$$$x_i \neq x_j$$$ for all i≠j$$$i \neq j$$$). Friends win if one of them meets Vlad in any room or corridor before he wins.
For one unit of time, each participant of the game can go through one corridor. All participants move at the same time. Participants may not move. Each room can fit all participants at the same time.

Friends know the plan of a maze and intend to win. They don't want to waste too much energy. They ask you to determine if they can win and if they can, what minimum number of friends must remain in the maze so that they can always catch Vlad.
In other words, you need to determine the size of the minimum (by the number of elements) subset of friends who can catch Vlad or say that such a subset does not exist.
input: The first line of the input contains an integer t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤104$$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases in the input. The input contains an empty string before each test case.
The first line of the test case contains two numbers n$$$n$$$ and k$$$k$$$ (1≤k<n≤2⋅105$$$1 \le k  \lt  n \le 2\cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of rooms and friends, respectively.
The next line of the test case contains k$$$k$$$ integers x1,x2,…,xk$$$x_1, x_2, \dots, x_k$$$ (2≤xi≤n$$$2 \le x_i \le n$$$) — numbers of rooms with friends. All xi$$$x_i$$$ are different.

The next n−1$$$n-1$$$ lines contain descriptions of the corridors, two numbers per line vj$$$v_j$$$ and uj$$$u_j$$$ (1≤uj,vj≤n$$$1 \le u_j, v_j \le n$$$) — numbers of rooms that connect the j$$$j$$$ corridor. All corridors are bidirectional. From any room, you can go to any other by moving along the corridors.
It is guaranteed that the sum of the values n$$$n$$$ over all test cases in the test is not greater than 2⋅105$$$2\cdot10^5$$$.
output: Print t$$$t$$$ lines, each line containing the answer to the corresponding test case. The answer to a test case should be −1$$$-1$$$ if Vlad wins anyway and a minimal number of friends otherwise.
note: In the first set of inputs, even if all the friends stay in the maze, Vlad can still win. Therefore, the answer is "-1".
In the second set of inputs it is enough to leave friends from rooms 6$$$6$$$ and 7$$$7$$$. Then Vlad will not be able to win. The answer is "2".
In the third and fourth sets of inputs Vlad cannot win only if all his friends stay in the maze. Therefore the answers are "1" and "2".

legend.ai: 与 E1 的唯一不同之处在于题目所提出的问题。
Vlad 用 n$$$n$$$ 个房间和 n−1$$$n-1$$$ 条双向走廊建造了一个迷宫。从任意房间 u$$$u$$$ 都可以通过一系列走廊到达任意其他房间 v$$$v$$$。因此，房间系统构成一棵无向树。
Vlad 邀请了 k$$$k$$$ 位朋友来和他一起玩游戏。

Vlad 从房间 1$$$1$$$ 开始游戏；如果他到达一个不是 1$$$1$$$ 且恰好有一条走廊通向它的房间，就获胜。朋友们被安置在迷宫中：编号为 i$$$i$$$ 的朋友位于房间 xi$$$x_i$$$，并且没有两个朋友位于同一个房间(也就是说，对于所有 i≠j$$$i \neq j$$$，都有 xi≠xj$$$x_i \neq x_j$$$)。如果在 Vlad 获胜之前，其中一人在任意房间或走廊中遇到 Vlad，朋友们就获胜。
在一个时间单位内，游戏中的每位参与者都可以通过一条走廊。所有参与者同时移动。参与者也可以选择不移动。每个房间可以同时容纳所有参与者。
朋友们了解迷宫的布局，并打算获胜。他们不想浪费太多体力。他们请你判断他们是否能够获胜；如果能，确定为了始终抓住 Vlad，迷宫中至少需要留下多少名朋友。
换句话说，你需要确定能够抓住 Vlad 的朋友子集的最小大小（按元素个数计算），或者说明不存在这样的子集。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含一个整数 t$$$t$$$(1≤t≤104$$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$)——输入中的测试用例数量。每个测试用例之前都有一个空行。
测试用例的第一行包含两个数 n$$$n$$$ 和 k$$$k$$$(1≤k<n≤2⋅105$$$1 \le k  \lt  n \le 2\cdot 10^5$$$)——分别表示房间数和朋友数。
测试用例的下一行包含 k$$$k$$$ 个整数 x1,x2,…,xk$$$x_1, x_2, \dots, x_k$$$(2≤xi≤n$$$2 \le x_i \le n$$$)——表示有朋友所在的房间编号。所有 xi$$$x_i$$$ 均不相同。
接下来的 n−1$$$n-1$$$ 行包含对各条走廊的描述，每行有两个数字 vj$$$v_j$$$ 和 uj$$$u_j$$$(1≤uj,vj≤n$$$1 \le u_j, v_j \le n$$$)——表示与第 j$$$j$$$ 条走廊相连的房间编号。所有走廊都是双向的。从任意房间出发，都可以沿着走廊到达其他任意房间。
保证所有测试用例中的 n$$$n$$$ 之和不超过 2⋅105$$$2\cdot10^5$$$。

output.ai: 输出 t$$$t$$$ 行，每行包含对应测试用例的答案。如果 Vlad 无论如何都会获胜，则该测试用例的答案应为 −1$$$-1$$$；否则为最少需要的朋友数。

note.ai: 在第一组输入中，即使所有朋友都留在迷宫中，Vlad 仍然可以获胜。因此，答案为“-1”。
在第二组输入中，只需让 6$$$6$$$ 号和 7$$$7$$$ 号房间的朋友离开即可。这样 Vlad 就无法获胜。答案为“2”。
在第三组和第四组输入中，只有当他的所有朋友都留在迷宫中时，Vlad 才无法获胜。因此答案分别为“1”和“2”。

legend: There is unrest in the Galactic Senate. Several thousand solar systems have declared their intentions to leave the Republic. Master Heidi needs to select the Jedi Knights who will go on peacekeeping missions throughout the galaxy. It is well-known that the success of any peacekeeping mission depends on the colors of the lightsabers of the Jedi who will go on that mission.

Heidi has n Jedi Knights standing in front of her, each one with a lightsaber of one of m possible colors. She knows that for the mission to be the most effective, she needs to select some contiguous interval of knights such that there are exactly k1 knights with lightsabers of the first color, k2 knights with lightsabers of the second color, ..., km knights with lightsabers of the m-th color.

However, since the last time, she has learned that it is not always possible to select such an interval. Therefore, she decided to ask some Jedi Knights to go on an indefinite unpaid vacation leave near certain pits on Tatooine, if you know what I mean. Help Heidi decide what is the minimum number of Jedi Knights that need to be let go before she is able to select the desired interval from the subsequence of remaining knights.
input: The first line of the input contains n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·105) and m (1 ≤ m ≤ n). The second line contains n integers in the range {1, 2, ..., m} representing colors of the lightsabers of the subsequent Jedi Knights. The third line contains m integers k1, k2, ..., km (with ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/028ad21fa922d9cfdf096d658a7e651e74feddcf.png)) – the desired counts of Jedi Knights with lightsabers of each color from 1 to m.
output: Output one number: the minimum number of Jedi Knights that need to be removed from the sequence so that, in what remains, there is an interval with the prescribed counts of lightsaber colors. If this is not possible, output  - 1.

legend.ai: 银河共和国参议院陷入动荡。数千个星系已经宣布打算脱离共和国。海蒂大师需要挑选出将前往整个银河系执行维和任务的绝地武士。众所周知，任何维和任务的成功都取决于执行该任务的绝地武士们所使用的光剑颜色。
海蒂面前站着 n 名绝地武士，每人都有一把 m 种可能颜色之一的光剑。她知道，为了使任务最有效，她需要选出一段连续的骑士区间，使其中恰好有 k1 名绝地武士使用第一种颜色的光剑，k2 名使用第二种颜色的光剑，……，km 名使用第 m 种颜色的光剑。
然而，自上次事件以来，她了解到并非总能选出这样的区间。因此，她决定让一些绝地武士前往塔图因的某些深坑附近进行无限期无薪休假，如果你明白我的意思的话。请帮助海蒂确定，在她能够从剩余骑士组成的子序列中选出所需区间之前，最少需要让多少名绝地武士离开。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含 n(1 ≤ n ≤ 2·105)和 m(1 ≤ m ≤ n)。第二行包含 n 个整数，范围为 {1, 2，...，m}，表示这些绝地武士依次使用的光剑颜色。第三行包含 m 个整数 k1，k2，……，km(满足 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/028ad21fa922d9cfdf096d658a7e651e74feddcf.png))——表示每种颜色(从 1 到 m)的光剑所需的绝地武士数量。

output.ai: 输出一个数：从序列中移除的绝地武士的最少数量，使得剩余序列中存在一个包含规定数量的各种光剑颜色的区间。如果无法做到，输出 -1。

legend: You are playing a game where your character should overcome different obstacles. The current problem is to come down from a cliff. The cliff has height h$$$h$$$, and there is a moving platform on each height x$$$x$$$ from 1$$$1$$$ to h$$$h$$$.

Each platform is either hidden inside the cliff or moved out. At first, there are n$$$n$$$ moved out platforms on heights p1,p2,…,pn$$$p_1, p_2, \dots, p_n$$$. The platform on height h$$$h$$$ is moved out (and the character is initially standing there).

If you character is standing on some moved out platform on height x$$$x$$$, then he can pull a special lever, which switches the state of two platforms: on height x$$$x$$$ and x−1$$$x - 1$$$. In other words, the platform you are currently standing on will hide in the cliff and the platform one unit below will change it state: it will hide if it was moved out or move out if it was hidden. In the second case, you will safely land on it. Note that this is the only way to move from one platform to another.

Your character is quite fragile, so it can safely fall from the height no more than 2$$$2$$$. In other words falling from the platform x$$$x$$$ to platform x−2$$$x - 2$$$ is okay, but falling from x$$$x$$$ to x−3$$$x - 3$$$ (or lower) is certain death.

Sometimes it's not possible to come down from the cliff, but you can always buy (for donate currency) several magic crystals. Each magic crystal can be used to change the state of any single platform (except platform on height h$$$h$$$, which is unaffected by the crystals). After being used, the crystal disappears.
What is the minimum number of magic crystal you need to buy to safely land on the 0$$$0$$$ ground level?
input: The first line contains one integer q$$$q$$$ (1≤q≤100$$$1 \le q \le 100$$$) — the number of queries. Each query contains two lines and is independent of all other queries.

The first line of each query contains two integers h$$$h$$$ and n$$$n$$$ (1≤h≤109$$$1 \le h \le 10^9$$$, 1≤n≤min(h,2⋅105)$$$1 \le n \le \min(h, 2 \cdot 10^5)$$$) — the height of the cliff and the number of moved out platforms.

The second line contains n$$$n$$$ integers p1,p2,…,pn$$$p_1, p_2, \dots, p_n$$$ (h=p1>p2>⋯>pn≥1$$$h = p_1  \gt  p_2  \gt  \dots  \gt  p_n \ge 1$$$) — the corresponding moved out platforms in the descending order of their heights.
The sum of n$$$n$$$ over all queries does not exceed 2⋅105$$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output: For each query print one integer — the minimum number of magic crystals you have to spend to safely come down on the ground level (with height 0$$$0$$$).

legend.ai: 你在玩一个游戏，你的角色需要克服各种障碍。当前的问题是让他从悬崖上下来。悬崖高度为 h$$$h$$$，并且每个高度 x$$$x$$$(从 1$$$1$$$ 到 h$$$h$$$)都有一个移动平台。
每个平台要么藏在悬崖内部，要么伸出来。开始时，有 n$$$n$$$ 个伸出的平台，位于高度 p1,p2,…,pn$$$p_1, p_2, \dots, p_n$$$。高度 h$$$h$$$ 的平台是伸出的(角色初始就站在上面)。
如果你的角色正站在某个高度为 x$$$x$$$ 的伸出平台上，他可以拉动一个特殊拉杆，这会切换两个平台的状态：即位于高度 x$$$x$$$ 和 x−1$$$x - 1$$$ 的两个平台。换句话说，你当前站立的平台会藏进悬崖，而下方一层的平台会改变状态：如果它原本是伸出的，则会隐藏；如果它原本是隐藏的，则会伸出。在后一种情况下，你会安全地落在上面。注意，这是从一个平台移动到另一个平台的唯一方式。
你的角色非常脆弱，因此从高度不超过 2$$$2$$$ 的地方落下是安全的。换句话说，从平台 x$$$x$$$ 落到平台 x−2$$$x - 2$$$ 没有问题，但从 x$$$x$$$ 落到 x−3$$$x - 3$$$(或更低)则必死无疑。
有时无法从悬崖上下来，但你总是可以用捐赠货币购买若干魔法水晶。每颗魔法水晶都可以用来改变任意单个平台的状态(高度为 h$$$h$$$ 的平台除外，它不受水晶影响)。水晶使用后就会消失。
你需要购买多少颗魔法水晶，才能安全落到高度为 0$$$0$$$ 的地面？

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 q$$$q$$$(1≤q≤100$$$1 \le q \le 100$$$)——查询的数量。每个查询包含两行，且与其他所有查询相互独立。
每个查询的第一行包含两个整数 h$$$h$$$ 和 n$$$n$$$(1≤h≤109$$$1 \le h \le 10^9$$$，1≤n≤min(h,2⋅105)$$$1 \le n \le \min(h, 2 \cdot 10^5)$$$)——悬崖高度和突出的平台数量。
第二行包含 n$$$n$$$ 个整数 p1,p2,…,pn$$$p_1, p_2, \dots, p_n$$$(h=p1>p2>⋯>pn≥1$$$h = p_1  \gt  p_2  \gt  \dots  \gt  p_n \ge 1$$$)——对应突出的平台，按高度降序排列。
所有查询中 n$$$n$$$ 的总和不超过 2⋅105$$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$。

output.ai: 对于每个查询，输出一个整数——为了安全降落到地面(高度为 0$$$0$$$)，你必须消耗的魔法水晶的最少数量。

problems.hint: Once you leave a column / row, it means nothing to you.

legend: You are at the top left cell (1,1)$$$(1, 1)$$$ of an n×m$$$n \times m$$$ labyrinth. Your goal is to get to the bottom right cell (n,m)$$$(n, m)$$$. You can only move right or down, one cell per step. Moving right from a cell (x,y)$$$(x, y)$$$ takes you to the cell (x,y+1)$$$(x, y + 1)$$$, while moving down takes you to the cell (x+1,y)$$$(x + 1, y)$$$.

Some cells of the labyrinth contain rocks. When you move to a cell with rock, the rock is pushed to the next cell in the direction you're moving. If the next cell contains a rock, it gets pushed further, and so on.
The labyrinth is surrounded by impenetrable walls, thus any move that would put you or any rock outside of the labyrinth is illegal.

Count the number of different legal paths you can take from the start to the goal modulo 109+7$$$10^9 + 7$$$. Two paths are considered different if there is at least one cell that is visited in one path, but not visited in the other.
input: The first line contains two integers n,m$$$n, m$$$ — dimensions of the labyrinth (1≤n,m≤2000$$$1 \leq n, m \leq 2000$$$).

Next n$$$n$$$ lines describe the labyrinth. Each of these lines contains m$$$m$$$ characters. The j$$$j$$$-th character of the i$$$i$$$-th of these lines is equal to "R" if the cell (i,j)$$$(i, j)$$$ contains a rock, or "." if the cell (i,j)$$$(i, j)$$$ is empty.
It is guaranteed that the starting cell (1,1)$$$(1, 1)$$$ is empty.
output: Print a single integer — the number of different legal paths from (1,1)$$$(1, 1)$$$ to (n,m)$$$(n, m)$$$ modulo 109+7$$$10^9 + 7$$$.
note: In the first sample case we can't (and don't have to) move, hence the only path consists of a single cell (1,1)$$$(1, 1)$$$.
In the second sample case the goal is blocked and is unreachable.
Illustrations for the third sample case can be found here: https://assets.codeforces.com/rounds/1225/index.html

legend.ai: 你位于一个 n×m$$$n \times m$$$ 迷宫的左上角单元格 (1,1)$$$(1, 1)$$$。你的目标是到达右下角单元格 (n,m)$$$(n, m)$$$。你只能向右或向下移动，每次移动一个单元格。从单元格 (x,y)$$$(x, y)$$$ 向右移动会到达单元格 (x,y+1)$$$(x, y + 1)$$$，而向下移动会到达单元格 (x+1,y)$$$(x + 1, y)$$$。
迷宫中的一些单元格里有岩石。当你移动到一个有岩石的单元格时，岩石会沿你移动的方向被推到下一个单元格。如果下一个单元格中有岩石，它会被继续向前推动，依此类推。
迷宫被无法穿透的墙包围，因此任何会使你或任何岩石移出迷宫的移动都是非法的。
计算从起点到终点可以经过的不同合法路径数量，对 109+7$$$10^9 + 7$$$ 取模。如果至少存在一个单元格在一条路径中被访问、但在另一条路径中未被访问，则认为这两条路径不同。

input.ai: 第一行包含两个整数 n,m$$$n, m$$$——迷宫的尺寸(1≤n,m≤2000$$$1 \leq n, m \leq 2000$$$)。
接下来 n$$$n$$$ 行描述迷宫。每行包含 m$$$m$$$ 个字符。这些行中第 i$$$i$$$ 行的第 j$$$j$$$ 个字符，如果单元格 (i,j)$$$(i, j)$$$ 中有岩石，则等于 "R"；如果单元格 (i,j)$$$(i, j)$$$ 为空，则等于 "."。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，我们无法(也无需)移动，因此唯一的路径只包含一个单元格 (1,1)$$$(1, 1)$$$。

第三个样例的示意图可以在这里找到：https://assets.codeforces.com/rounds/1225/index.html

legend: There is a robot on a checkered field that is endless in all directions. Initially, the robot is located in the cell with coordinates (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$. He will execute commands which are described by a string of capital Latin letters 'L', 'R', 'D', 'U'. When a command is executed, the robot simply moves in the corresponding direction:
'L': one cell to the left (the x$$$x$$$-coordinate of the current cell decreases by 1$$$1$$$);
'R': one cell to the right (the x$$$x$$$-coordinate of the current cell is increased by 1$$$1$$$);
'D': one cell down (the y$$$y$$$-coordinate of the current cell decreases by 1$$$1$$$);
'U': one cell up (the y$$$y$$$-coordinate of the current cell is increased by 1$$$1$$$).

Your task is to put an obstacle in one cell of the field so that after executing the commands, the robot will return to the original cell of its path (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$. Of course, an obstacle cannot be placed in the starting cell (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$. It is guaranteed that if the obstacle is not placed, then the robot will not return to the starting cell.

An obstacle affects the movement of the robot in the following way: if it tries to go in a certain direction, and there is an obstacle, then it simply remains in place (the obstacle also remains, that is, it does not disappear).

Find any such cell of the field (other than (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$) that if you put an obstacle there, the robot will return to the cell (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$ after the execution of all commands. If there is no solution, then report it.
input: The first line contains one integer t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤500$$$1 \le t \le 500$$$) — the number of test cases.

Each test case consists of a single line containing s$$$s$$$ — the sequence of commands, which are uppercase Latin letters 'L', 'R', 'D', 'U' only. The length of s$$$s$$$ is between 1$$$1$$$ and 5000$$$5000$$$, inclusive. Additional constraint on s$$$s$$$: executing this sequence of commands leads the robot to some cell other than (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$, if there are no obstacles.
The sum of lengths of all s$$$s$$$ in a test doesn't exceed 5000$$$5000$$$.
output: For each test case print a single line:

if there is a solution, print two integers x$$$x$$$ and y$$$y$$$ (−109≤x,y≤109$$$-10^9 \le x,y \le 10^9$$$) such that an obstacle in (x,y)$$$(x, y)$$$ will force the robot to return back to the cell (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$;
otherwise, print two zeroes (i. e. 0 0).
If there are multiple answers, you can print any of them.

legend.ai: 有一个机器人位于一块向所有方向无限延伸的方格场地上。起初，机器人位于坐标为 (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$ 的格子中。它将执行由大写拉丁字母 'L'、'R'、'D'、'U' 组成的字符串所描述的指令。执行一条指令时，机器人只会向相应的方向移动：
'L'：向左移动一个格子(当前格子的 x$$$x$$$ 坐标减小 1$$$1$$$)；
'R'：向右移动一个格子(当前格子的 x$$$x$$$ 坐标增加 1$$$1$$$)；
'D'：向下移动一格(当前单元格的 y$$$y$$$ 坐标减少 1$$$1$$$)。
'U'：向上移动一格(当前单元格的 y$$$y$$$ 坐标增加 1$$$1$$$)。
你的任务是在场地的一个单元格中放置障碍物，使得执行完这些命令后，机器人会回到其路径的起始单元格 (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$。当然，障碍物不能放在起始单元格 (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$。保证如果不放置障碍物，机器人不会回到起始单元格。
障碍物按如下方式影响机器人的移动：如果它试图朝某个方向移动，而该处有障碍物，那么它就会停留在原地（障碍物也仍然存在，即不会消失）。
请找出场地上任意一个这样的单元格(除 (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$ 外)：如果将障碍物放在那里，机器人在执行完所有命令后会回到单元格 (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$。如果无解，请报告无解。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤500$$$1 \le t \le 500$$$)——测试用例的数量。
每个测试用例包含一行，其中包含 s$$$s$$$ —— 仅由大写拉丁字母 'L'、'R'、'D'、'U' 组成的指令序列。s$$$s$$$ 的长度在 1$$$1$$$ 到 5000$$$5000$$$ 之间(包括端点)。对 s$$$s$$$ 的额外约束是：如果没有障碍物，执行这列指令会使机器人到达某个不同于 (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$ 的格子。
在一个测试中，所有 s$$$s$$$ 的长度之和不超过 5000$$$5000$$$。

output.ai: 对于每个测试用例，输出一行：
如果存在解，输出两个整数 x$$$x$$$ 和 y$$$y$$$(−109≤x,y≤109$$$-10^9 \le x,y \le 10^9$$$)，使得在 (x,y)$$$(x, y)$$$ 处放置一个障碍物后，机器人将被迫返回格子 (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$；
否则，输出两个零（即 0 0）。
如果有多个答案，可以输出任意一个。

legend: Karl is developing a key storage service. Each user has a positive integer key.

Karl knows that storing keys in plain text is bad practice. So, instead of storing a key, he decided to store a fingerprint of a key. However, using some existing fingerprint algorithm looked too boring to him, so he invented his own one.

Karl's fingerprint is calculated by the following process: divide the given integer by 2, then divide the result by 3, then divide the result by 4, and so on, until we get a result that equals zero (we are speaking about integer division each time). The fingerprint is defined as the multiset of the remainders of these divisions.

For example, this is how Karl's fingerprint algorithm is applied to the key 11: 11 divided by 2 has remainder 1 and result 5, then 5 divided by 3 has remainder 2 and result 1, and 1 divided by 4 has remainder 1 and result 0. Thus, the key 11 produces the sequence of remainders [1,2,1]$$$[1, 2, 1]$$$ and has the fingerprint multiset {1,1,2}$$$\{1, 1, 2\}$$$.

Ksenia wants to prove that Karl's fingerprint algorithm is not very good. For example, she found that both keys 178800 and 123456 produce the fingerprint of {0,0,0,0,2,3,3,4}$$$\{0, 0, 0, 0, 2, 3, 3, 4\}$$$. Thus, users are at risk of fingerprint collision with some commonly used and easy to guess keys like 123456.

Ksenia wants to make her words more persuasive. She wants to calculate the number of other keys that have the same fingerprint as the keys in the given list of some commonly used keys. Your task is to help her.
input: The first line contains an integer t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤50000$$$1 \le t \le 50\,000$$$) — the number of commonly used keys to examine. Each of the next t$$$t$$$ lines contains one integer ki$$$k_i$$$ (1≤ki≤1018$$$1 \le k_i \le 10^{18}$$$) — the key itself.
output: For each of the keys print one integer — the number of other keys that have the same fingerprint.
note: The other key with the same fingerprint as 11 is 15. 15 produces a sequence of remainders [1,1,2]$$$[1, 1, 2]$$$. So both numbers have the fingerprint multiset {1,1,2}$$$\{1, 1, 2\}$$$.

legend.ai: Karl 正在开发一项密钥存储服务。每个用户都有一个正整数密钥。
Karl 知道以明文形式存储密钥并不是好的做法。因此，他不直接存储密钥，而是决定存储密钥的指纹。然而，使用某种现有的指纹算法在他看来太无聊了，于是他发明了自己的算法。
Karl 的指纹通过以下过程计算：将给定整数除以 2，然后将结果除以 3，再将结果除以 4，依此类推，直到得到结果为 0（这里每次都是指整数除法）。指纹定义为这些除法所得余数的多重集。
例如，Karl 的指纹算法应用于密钥 11 的过程如下：11 除以 2 的余数为 1，结果为 5；然后 5 除以 3 的余数为 2，结果为 1；最后 1 除以 4 的余数为 1，结果为 0。因此，密钥 11 产生余数序列 [1,2,1]$$$[1, 2, 1]$$$，其指纹多重集为 {1,1,2}$$$\{1, 1, 2\}$$$。
Ksenia 想要证明 Karl 的指纹算法并不怎么好。例如，她发现密钥 178800 和 123456 都产生指纹 {0,0,0,0,2,3,3,4}$$$\{0, 0, 0, 0, 2, 3, 3, 4\}$$$。因此，用户面临指纹碰撞的风险，可能与某些常用且容易被猜到的密钥(如 123456)发生碰撞。
Ksenia 想让自己的话更有说服力。她希望计算出与给定的常用键列表中的键具有相同指纹的其他键的数量。请帮助她完成这项任务。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 t$$$t$$$(1≤t≤50000$$$1 \le t \le 50\,000$$$)——需要检查的常用键数量。接下来的 t$$$t$$$ 行中，每行包含一个整数 ki$$$k_i$$$(1≤ki≤1018$$$1 \le k_i \le 10^{18}$$$)——键本身。

output.ai: 对于每个键，输出一个整数——具有相同指纹的其他键的数量。

problems.hint: If $X_i$ is fixed, find out about $X_{i-1}$ .

legend: Alice and Bob begin their day with a quick game. They first choose a starting number X0 ≥ 3 and try to reach one million by the process described below.

Alice goes first and then they take alternating turns. In the i-th turn, the player whose turn it is selects a prime number smaller than the current number, and announces the smallest multiple of this prime number that is not smaller than the current number.

Formally, he or she selects a prime p < Xi - 1 and then finds the minimum Xi ≥ Xi - 1 such that p divides Xi. Note that if the selected prime p already divides Xi - 1, then the number does not change.

Eve has witnessed the state of the game after two turns. Given X2, help her determine what is the smallest possible starting number X0. Note that the players don't necessarily play optimally. You should consider all possible game evolutions.
input: The input contains a single integer X2 (4 ≤ X2 ≤ 106). It is guaranteed that the integer X2 is composite, that is, is not prime.
output: Output a single integer — the minimum possible X0.
note: In the first test, the smallest possible starting number is X0 = 6. One possible course of the game is as follows:
Alice picks prime 5 and announces X1 = 10
Bob picks prime 7 and announces X2 = 14.
In the second case, let X0 = 15.
Alice picks prime 2 and announces X1 = 16
Bob picks prime 5 and announces X2 = 20.

note.ai: 在第一个测试用例中，可能的最小初始数字为 X0 = 6。游戏的一种可能过程如下：
Alice 选择素数 5 并宣布 X1 = 10
Bob 选择素数 7 并宣布 X2 = 14。
在第二种情况中，令 X0 = 15。
Alice 选择素数 2 并宣布 X1 = 16
Bob 选择素数 5 并宣布 X2 = 20。

legend.ai: Alice 和 Bob 以一场快速游戏开始他们的一天。他们首先选择一个起始数字 X0 ≥ 3，并尝试通过下面描述的过程达到一百万。
Alice 先手，随后双方轮流进行。在第 i 回合，轮到的玩家选择一个小于当前数字的素数，并宣布这个素数的不小于当前数字的最小倍数。
严格地说，他或她选择一个素数 p < X_i - 1，然后找到满足 X_i ≥ X_i - 1 且 p 能整除 X_i 的最小 X_i。注意，如果所选素数 p 已经能整除 X_i - 1，那么数字不会改变。
Eve 见证了游戏进行两回合后的状态。给定 X2，请帮助她确定可能的最小初始数字 X0。注意，玩家不一定会采取最优策略。你需要考虑所有可能的游戏过程。

input.ai: 输入包含一个整数 X2（4 ≤ X2 ≤ 10^6）。保证整数 X2 是合数，即不是素数。

output.ai: 输出一个整数——可能的最小 X0。

problems.hint: If you study $k$ maps, what is the probability to play one of them?

legend: Little Johnny Bubbles enjoys spending hours in front of his computer playing video games. His favorite game is Bubble Strike, fast-paced bubble shooting online game for two players.

Each game is set in one of the N maps, each having different terrain configuration. First phase of each game decides on which map the game will be played. The game system randomly selects three maps and shows them to the players. Each player must pick one of those three maps to be discarded. The game system then randomly selects one of the maps that were not picked by any of the players and starts the game.

Johnny is deeply enthusiastic about the game and wants to spend some time studying maps, thus increasing chances to win games played on those maps. However, he also needs to do his homework, so he does not have time to study all the maps. That is why he asked himself the following question: "What is the minimum number of maps I have to study, so that the probability to play one of those maps is at least P$$$P$$$"?
Can you help Johnny find the answer for this question? You can assume Johnny's opponents do not know him, and they will randomly pick maps.
input: The first line contains two integers N$$$N$$$ (3$$$3$$$ ≤$$$\leq$$$ N$$$N$$$ ≤$$$\leq$$$ 103$$$10^{3}$$$) and P$$$P$$$ (0$$$0$$$ ≤$$$\leq$$$ P$$$P$$$ ≤$$$\leq$$$ 1$$$1$$$) – total number of maps in the game and probability to play map Johnny has studied. P$$$P$$$ will have at most four digits after the decimal point.
output: Output contains one integer number – minimum number of maps Johnny has to study.

legend.ai: 小约翰尼·Bubbles 喜欢花费数小时坐在电脑前玩电子游戏。他最喜欢的游戏是 Bubble Strike，这是一款节奏明快的双人在线泡泡射击游戏。
每局游戏都在 N 张地图中的一张上进行，每张地图都有不同的地形配置。每局游戏的第一阶段会决定游戏在哪张地图上进行。游戏系统会随机选出三张地图并展示给玩家。每名玩家都必须选择其中一张地图将其弃用。随后，游戏系统会从没有被任一玩家选中的地图中随机选出一张，并开始游戏。
Johnny 对这款游戏十分热衷，希望花时间研究地图，从而提高在这些地图上进行游戏时的获胜概率。然而，他还需要完成家庭作业，因此没有时间研究所有地图。这就是为什么他问自己这样一个问题：“我至少需要研究多少张地图，才能使玩到其中一张地图的概率至少为 P$$$P$$$？”
你能帮助 Johnny 找到这个问题的答案吗？你可以假设 Johnny 的对手并不了解他，并且会随机选择地图。

input.ai: 第一行包含两个整数 N$$$N$$$(3$$$3$$$ ≤$$$\leq$$$ N$$$N$$$ ≤$$$\leq$$$ 103$$$10^{3}$$$)和 P$$$P$$$(0$$$0$$$ ≤$$$\leq$$$ P$$$P$$$ ≤$$$\leq$$$ 1$$$1$$$)——分别表示游戏中的地图总数，以及玩到 Johnny 学习过的地图的概率。P$$$P$$$ 的小数点后最多有四位数字。

output.ai: 输出一个整数——Johnny 必须研究的最少地图数量。

legend: The map of Bertown can be represented as a set of n$$$n$$$ intersections, numbered from 1$$$1$$$ to n$$$n$$$ and connected by m$$$m$$$ one-way roads. It is possible to move along the roads from any intersection to any other intersection. The length of some path from one intersection to another is the number of roads that one has to traverse along the path. The shortest path from one intersection v$$$v$$$ to another intersection u$$$u$$$ is the path that starts in v$$$v$$$, ends in u$$$u$$$ and has the minimum length among all such paths.

Polycarp lives near the intersection s$$$s$$$ and works in a building near the intersection t$$$t$$$. Every day he gets from s$$$s$$$ to t$$$t$$$ by car. Today he has chosen the following path to his workplace: p1$$$p_1$$$, p2$$$p_2$$$, ..., pk$$$p_k$$$, where p1=s$$$p_1 = s$$$, pk=t$$$p_k = t$$$, and all other elements of this sequence are the intermediate intersections, listed in the order Polycarp arrived at them. Polycarp never arrived at the same intersection twice, so all elements of this sequence are pairwise distinct. Note that you know Polycarp's path beforehand (it is fixed), and it is not necessarily one of the shortest paths from s$$$s$$$ to t$$$t$$$.

Polycarp's car has a complex navigation system installed in it. Let's describe how it works. When Polycarp starts his journey at the intersection s$$$s$$$, the system chooses some shortest path from s$$$s$$$ to t$$$t$$$ and shows it to Polycarp. Let's denote the next intersection in the chosen path as v$$$v$$$. If Polycarp chooses to drive along the road from s$$$s$$$ to v$$$v$$$, then the navigator shows him the same shortest path (obviously, starting from v$$$v$$$ as soon as he arrives at this intersection). However, if Polycarp chooses to drive to another intersection w$$$w$$$ instead, the navigator rebuilds the path: as soon as Polycarp arrives at w$$$w$$$, the navigation system chooses some shortest path from w$$$w$$$ to t$$$t$$$ and shows it to Polycarp. The same process continues until Polycarp arrives at t$$$t$$$: if Polycarp moves along the road recommended by the system, it maintains the shortest path it has already built; but if Polycarp chooses some other path, the system rebuilds the path by the same rules.
Here is an example. Suppose the map of Bertown looks as follows, and Polycarp drives along the path [1,2,3,4]$$$[1, 2, 3, 4]$$$ (s=1$$$s = 1$$$, t=4$$$t = 4$$$):
Check the picture by the link http://tk.codeforces.com/a.png
When Polycarp starts at 1$$$1$$$, the system chooses some shortest path from 1$$$1$$$ to 4$$$4$$$. There is only one such path, it is [1,5,4]$$$[1, 5, 4]$$$;

Polycarp chooses to drive to 2$$$2$$$, which is not along the path chosen by the system. When Polycarp arrives at 2$$$2$$$, the navigator rebuilds the path by choosing some shortest path from 2$$$2$$$ to 4$$$4$$$, for example, [2,6,4]$$$[2, 6, 4]$$$ (note that it could choose [2,3,4]$$$[2, 3, 4]$$$);

Polycarp chooses to drive to 3$$$3$$$, which is not along the path chosen by the system. When Polycarp arrives at 3$$$3$$$, the navigator rebuilds the path by choosing the only shortest path from 3$$$3$$$ to 4$$$4$$$, which is [3,4]$$$[3, 4]$$$;
Polycarp arrives at 4$$$4$$$ along the road chosen by the navigator, so the system does not have to rebuild anything.

Overall, we get 2$$$2$$$ rebuilds in this scenario. Note that if the system chose [2,3,4]$$$[2, 3, 4]$$$ instead of [2,6,4]$$$[2, 6, 4]$$$ during the second step, there would be only 1$$$1$$$ rebuild (since Polycarp goes along the path, so the system maintains the path [3,4]$$$[3, 4]$$$ during the third step).

The example shows us that the number of rebuilds can differ even if the map of Bertown and the path chosen by Polycarp stays the same. Given this information (the map and Polycarp's path), can you determine the minimum and the maximum number of rebuilds that could have happened during the journey?
input: The first line contains two integers n$$$n$$$ and m$$$m$$$ (2≤n≤m≤2⋅105$$$2 \le n \le m \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of intersections and one-way roads in Bertown, respectively.

Then m$$$m$$$ lines follow, each describing a road. Each line contains two integers u$$$u$$$ and v$$$v$$$ (1≤u,v≤n$$$1 \le u, v \le n$$$, u≠v$$$u \ne v$$$) denoting a road from intersection u$$$u$$$ to intersection v$$$v$$$. All roads in Bertown are pairwise distinct, which means that each ordered pair (u,v)$$$(u, v)$$$ appears at most once in these m$$$m$$$ lines (but if there is a road (u,v)$$$(u, v)$$$, the road (v,u)$$$(v, u)$$$ can also appear).
The following line contains one integer k$$$k$$$ (2≤k≤n$$$2 \le k \le n$$$) — the number of intersections in Polycarp's path from home to his workplace.

The last line contains k$$$k$$$ integers p1$$$p_1$$$, p2$$$p_2$$$, ..., pk$$$p_k$$$ (1≤pi≤n$$$1 \le p_i \le n$$$, all these integers are pairwise distinct) — the intersections along Polycarp's path in the order he arrived at them. p1$$$p_1$$$ is the intersection where Polycarp lives (s=p1$$$s = p_1$$$), and pk$$$p_k$$$ is the intersection where Polycarp's workplace is situated (t=pk$$$t = p_k$$$). It is guaranteed that for every i∈[1,k−1]$$$i \in [1, k - 1]$$$ the road from pi$$$p_i$$$ to pi+1$$$p_{i + 1}$$$ exists, so the path goes along the roads of Bertown.
output: Print two integers: the minimum and the maximum number of rebuilds that could have happened during the journey.

legend.ai: Bertown 的地图可以表示为由 n$$$n$$$ 个路口组成的集合，这些路口编号从 1$$$1$$$ 到 n$$$n$$$，并由 m$$$m$$$ 条单向道路连接。沿着道路可以从任意一个路口到达任意另一个路口。从一个路口到另一个路口的某条路径的长度，是沿该路径需要经过的道路数量。从一个路口 v$$$v$$$ 到另一个路口 u$$$u$$$ 的最短路径，是一条从 v$$$v$$$ 出发、在 u$$$u$$$ 结束，并且在所有此类路径中长度最小的路径。

Polycarp 住在路口 s$$$s$$$ 附近，并在路口 t$$$t$$$ 附近的一栋楼里工作。他每天开车从 s$$$s$$$ 前往 t$$$t$$$。今天他选择了如下路线前往工作地点：p1$$$p_1$$$, p2$$$p_2$$$, ..., pk$$$p_k$$$，其中 p1=s$$$p_1 = s$$$，pk=t$$$p_k = t$$$，序列中的其他所有元素都是中间路口，按照 Polycarp 到达它们的顺序列出。Polycarp 从未两次到达同一个路口，因此该序列中的所有元素都两两不同。注意，你事先知道 Polycarp 的路线(它是固定的)，并且它不一定是从 s$$$s$$$ 到 t$$$t$$$ 的最短路径之一。

Polycarp 的汽车中安装了一个复杂的导航系统。下面介绍它的工作方式。当 Polycarp 在路口 s$$$s$$$ 开始行程时，系统会选择一条从 s$$$s$$$ 到 t$$$t$$$ 的最短路径并将其显示给 Polycarp。设所选路径中的下一个路口为 v$$$v$$$。如果 Polycarp 选择沿着从 s$$$s$$$ 到 v$$$v$$$ 的道路行驶，那么导航器会向他显示同一条最短路径(显然，在他到达该路口后，路径从 v$$$v$$$ 开始)。但是，如果 Polycarp 选择前往另一个路口 w$$$w$$$，导航器就会重新规划路径：Polycarp 一到达 w$$$w$$$，导航系统就会选择一条从 w$$$w$$$ 到 t$$$t$$$ 的最短路径并将其显示给他。这个过程会一直持续，直到 Polycarp 到达 t$$$t$$$：如果 Polycarp 沿着系统推荐的道路行驶，系统就会保留已经规划好的最短路径；但如果 Polycarp 选择了其他道路，系统就会按照相同的规则重新规划路径。
下面给出一个例子。假设 Bertown 的地图如下所示，并且 Polycarp 沿着路径 [1,2,3,4]$$$[1, 2, 3, 4]$$$ 行驶(s=1$$$s = 1$$$，t=4$$$t = 4$$$)：
请通过链接 http://tk.codeforces.com/a.png 查看图片
当 Polycarp 从 1$$$1$$$ 出发时，系统会选择一条从 1$$$1$$$ 到 4$$$4$$$ 的最短路径。这样的路径只有一条，即 [1,5,4]$$$[1, 5, 4]$$$；
Polycarp 选择驾车前往 2$$$2$$$，这不在系统所选的路径上。当 Polycarp 到达 2$$$2$$$ 时，导航器通过选择一条从 2$$$2$$$ 到 4$$$4$$$ 的最短路径来重建路径，例如 [2,6,4]$$$[2, 6, 4]$$$(注意，它也可能选择 [2,3,4]$$$[2, 3, 4]$$$)；
Polycarp 选择驾车前往 3$$$3$$$，这不在系统所选的路径上。当 Polycarp 到达 3$$$3$$$ 时，导航器通过选择从 3$$$3$$$ 到 4$$$4$$$ 的唯一最短路径来重建路径，该路径为 [3,4]$$$[3, 4]$$$；
Polycarp 沿着导航器选择的道路到达 4$$$4$$$，因此系统无需重建任何内容。
总的来说，在这种情况下我们需要重建 2$$$2$$$ 次。注意，如果系统在第二步选择了 [2,3,4]$$$[2, 3, 4]$$$ 而不是 [2,6,4]$$$[2, 6, 4]$$$，那么只需要重建 1$$$1$$$ 次(因为 Polycarp 会沿着该路径行驶，所以在第三步中系统会保留路径 [3,4]$$$[3, 4]$$$)。
这个例子告诉我们，即使 Bertown 的地图和 Polycarp 选择的路径保持不变，重建次数也可能不同。给定这些信息（地图和 Polycarp 的路径），你能确定这次旅途中可能发生的最少和最多重建次数吗？

input.ai: 第一行包含两个整数 n$$$n$$$ 和 m$$$m$$$(2≤n≤m≤2⋅105$$$2 \le n \le m \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$)——分别表示 Bertown 中的路口数量和单向道路数量。

接下来有 m$$$m$$$ 行，每行描述一条道路。每行包含两个整数 u$$$u$$$ 和 v$$$v$$$(1≤u,v≤n$$$1 \le u, v \le n$$$，u≠v$$$u \ne v$$$)，表示一条从路口 u$$$u$$$ 到路口 v$$$v$$$ 的道路。Bertown 中的所有道路两两不同，这意味着每个有序对 (u,v)$$$(u, v)$$$ 在这 m$$$m$$$ 行中最多出现一次(但如果存在道路 (u,v)$$$(u, v)$$$，道路 (v,u)$$$(v, u)$$$ 也可能出现)。
下面一行包含一个整数 k$$$k$$$(2≤k≤n$$$2 \le k \le n$$$)——Polycarp 从家到工作地点的路径上包含的路口数量。

最后一行包含 k$$$k$$$ 个整数 p1$$$p_1$$$、p2$$$p_2$$$、...、pk$$$p_k$$$(1≤pi≤n$$$1 \le p_i \le n$$$，这些整数两两不同)——按照 Polycarp 到达它们的顺序给出其路径上的路口。p1$$$p_1$$$ 是 Polycarp 居住的路口(s=p1$$$s = p_1$$$)，而 pk$$$p_k$$$ 是 Polycarp 工作地点所在的路口(t=pk$$$t = p_k$$$)。保证对于每个 i∈[1,k−1]$$$i \in [1, k - 1]$$$，从 pi$$$p_i$$$ 到 pi+1$$$p_{i + 1}$$$ 的道路都存在，因此这条路径沿着 Bertown 的道路行进。

output.ai: 输出两个整数：旅途中可能发生的重建次数的最小值和最大值。

problems.hint: Where can you go from $(i, j)$ ? How can you calculate the number of moves?

legend: Dima and Inna are doing so great! At the moment, Inna is sitting on the magic lawn playing with a pink pony. Dima wanted to play too. He brought an n × m chessboard, a very tasty candy and two numbers a and b.

Dima put the chessboard in front of Inna and placed the candy in position (i, j) on the board. The boy said he would give the candy if it reaches one of the corner cells of the board. He's got one more condition. There can only be actions of the following types:
move the candy from position (x, y) on the board to position (x - a, y - b);
move the candy from position (x, y) on the board to position (x + a, y - b);
move the candy from position (x, y) on the board to position (x - a, y + b);
move the candy from position (x, y) on the board to position (x + a, y + b).
Naturally, Dima doesn't allow to move the candy beyond the chessboard borders.

Inna and the pony started shifting the candy around the board. They wonder what is the minimum number of allowed actions that they need to perform to move the candy from the initial position (i, j) to one of the chessboard corners. Help them cope with the task!
input: The first line of the input contains six integers n, m, i, j, a, b (1 ≤ n, m ≤ 106; 1 ≤ i ≤ n; 1 ≤ j ≤ m; 1 ≤ a, b ≤ 106).

You can assume that the chessboard rows are numbered from 1 to n from top to bottom and the columns are numbered from 1 to m from left to right. Position (i, j) in the statement is a chessboard cell on the intersection of the i-th row and the j-th column. You can consider that the corners are: (1, m), (n, 1), (n, m), (1, 1).
output: In a single line print a single integer — the minimum number of moves needed to get the candy.
If Inna and the pony cannot get the candy playing by Dima's rules, print on a single line "Poor Inna and pony!" without the quotes.
note: Note to sample 1:

Inna and the pony can move the candy to position (1 + 2, 3 + 2) = (3, 5), from there they can move it to positions (3 - 2, 5 + 2) = (1, 7) and (3 + 2, 5 + 2) = (5, 7). These positions correspond to the corner squares of the chess board. Thus, the answer to the test sample equals two.

legend.ai: Dima 和 Inna 玩得非常开心！此时，Inna 正坐在魔法草坪上和一只粉色小马玩耍。Dima 也想一起玩。他带来了一块 n × m 的棋盘、一颗非常美味的糖果以及两个数 a 和 b。
Dima 把棋盘放在 Inna 面前，并将糖果放在棋盘上的位置 (i, j)。男孩说，如果糖果能够到达棋盘的某个角落格子，他就会把糖果给她。他还有一个条件：只能进行以下几种操作：
将棋盘上位于位置 (x, y) 的糖果移动到位置 (x - a, y - b)；
将棋盘上位于位置 (x, y) 的糖果移动到位置 (x + a, y - b)；
将棋盘上位于位置 (x, y) 的糖果移动到位置 (x - a, y + b)；
将棋盘上位于位置 (x, y) 的糖果移动到位置 (x + a, y + b)。
当然，Dima 不允许将糖果移出棋盘边界。
Inna 和小马开始在棋盘上移动糖果。他们想知道，将糖果从初始位置 (i, j) 移动到棋盘的某个角所需执行的允许操作的最少次数。请帮助他们完成这个任务！

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含六个整数 n、m、i、j、a、b（1 ≤ n, m ≤ 10^6；1 ≤ i ≤ n；1 ≤ j ≤ m；1 ≤ a, b ≤ 10^6）。
你可以认为棋盘的行从上到下编号为 1 到 n，列从左到右编号为 1 到 m。题目中的位置 (i, j) 表示第 i 行与第 j 列交叉处的棋盘格。你可以认为棋盘的四个角分别为：(1, m)、(n, 1)、(n, m) 和 (1, 1)。

output.ai: 请在一行中输出一个整数——获得糖果所需的最少移动次数。
如果 Inna 和小马无法按照 Dima 的规则获得糖果，请在一行中输出不带引号的 “Poor Inna and pony!”。

note.ai: 样例 1 注：
Inna 和小马可以将糖果移动到位置 (1 + 2, 3 + 2) = (3, 5)，从那里可以将其移动到位置 (3 - 2, 5 + 2) = (1, 7) 和 (3 + 2, 5 + 2) = (5, 7)。这些位置对应于棋盘的角落格子。因此，测试样例的答案为 2。

problems.hint: What should the final length be?

legend: Vector Willman and Array Bolt are the two most famous athletes of Byteforces. They are going to compete in a race with a distance of L meters today.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/82594a062484dab96b57c9680122b88727c533e3.png)
Willman and Bolt have exactly the same speed, so when they compete the result is always a tie. That is a problem for the organizers because they want a winner.

While watching previous races the organizers have noticed that Willman can perform only steps of length equal to w meters, and Bolt can perform only steps of length equal to b meters. Organizers decided to slightly change the rules of the race. Now, at the end of the racetrack there will be an abyss, and the winner will be declared the athlete, who manages to run farther from the starting point of the the racetrack (which is not the subject to change by any of the athletes).

Note that none of the athletes can run infinitely far, as they both will at some moment of time face the point, such that only one step further will cause them to fall in the abyss. In other words, the athlete will not fall into the abyss if the total length of all his steps will be less or equal to the chosen distance L.

Since the organizers are very fair, the are going to set the length of the racetrack as an integer chosen randomly and uniformly in range from 1 to t (both are included). What is the probability that Willman and Bolt tie again today?
input: The first line of the input contains three integers t, w and b (1 ≤ t, w, b ≤ 5·1018) — the maximum possible length of the racetrack, the length of Willman's steps and the length of Bolt's steps respectively.
output: Print the answer to the problem as an irreducible fraction ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/cb0172a656698061aefa8eb30b2dbcd1e31f508e.png). Follow the format of the samples output.

The fraction ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/cb0172a656698061aefa8eb30b2dbcd1e31f508e.png) (p and q are integers, and both p ≥ 0 and q > 0 holds) is called irreducible, if there is no such integer d > 1, that both p and q are divisible by d.
note: In the first sample Willman and Bolt will tie in case 1, 6 or 7 are chosen as the length of the racetrack.

legend.ai: Vector Willman 和 Array Bolt 是 Byteforces 最著名的两位运动员。他们今天将参加一场距离为 L 米的赛跑。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/82594a062484dab96b57c9680122b88727c533e3.png)
Willman 和 Bolt 的速度完全相同，因此他们比赛时结果总是平局。这给组织者带来了问题，因为他们希望决出一名获胜者。
在观看之前的比赛时，组织者注意到，Willman 只能迈出长度为 w 米的步子，而 Bolt 只能迈出长度为 b 米的步子。组织者决定稍微改变比赛规则。现在，跑道尽头将会有一个深渊，能够从跑道起点跑得更远的运动员将获胜（跑道起点不会被任何运动员改变）。
注意，两名运动员都不可能无限远地奔跑，因为在某个时刻，他们都会到达这样一个位置：只要再向前迈出一步，就会掉入深渊。换句话说，当运动员所有步子的总长度小于或等于所选距离 L 时，他不会掉入深渊。
由于组织者非常公平，他们将把跑道长度设为一个从 1 到 t（包括 1 和 t）中随机均匀选取的整数。求今天 Willman 和 Bolt 再次平局的概率。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，当赛道长度选为 1、6 或 7 时，Willman 和 Bolt 将打成平手。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含三个整数 t、w 和 b（1 ≤ t，w，b ≤ 5·10^18），分别表示跑道长度的最大可能值、Willman 的步长以及 Bolt 的步长。

output.ai: 请将答案以不可约分数 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/cb0172a656698061aefa8eb30b2dbcd1e31f508e.png) 的形式输出。请遵循输出样例的格式。
如果不存在整数 d>1，使得 p 和 q 都能被 d 整除，则称分数 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/cb0172a656698061aefa8eb30b2dbcd1e31f508e.png)(p 和 q 为整数，且满足 p ≥ 0、q > 0)为不可约分数。

problems.hint: How can you check if the current result can be formed with all intervals containing one integer?

statement.title: C. Teodor is not a liar!

legend: Young Teodor enjoys drawing. His favourite hobby is drawing segments with integer borders inside his huge [1;m] segment. One day Teodor noticed that picture he just drawn has one interesting feature: there doesn't exist an integer point, that belongs each of segments in the picture. Having discovered this fact, Teodor decided to share it with Sasha.

Sasha knows that Teodor likes to show off so he never trusts him. Teodor wants to prove that he can be trusted sometimes, so he decided to convince Sasha that there is no such integer point in his picture, which belongs to each segment. However Teodor is lazy person and neither wills to tell Sasha all coordinates of segments' ends nor wills to tell him their amount, so he suggested Sasha to ask him series of questions 'Given the integer point xi, how many segments in Fedya's picture contain that point?', promising to tell correct answers for this questions.

Both boys are very busy studying and don't have much time, so they ask you to find out how many questions can Sasha ask Teodor, that having only answers on his questions, Sasha can't be sure that Teodor isn't lying to him. Note that Sasha doesn't know amount of segments in Teodor's picture. Sure, Sasha is smart person and never asks about same point twice.
input: First line of input contains two integer numbers: n and m (1 ≤ n, m ≤ 100 000) — amount of segments of Teodor's picture and maximal coordinate of point that Sasha can ask about.
ith of next n lines contains two integer numbers li and ri (1 ≤ li ≤ ri ≤ m) — left and right ends of ith segment in the picture. Note that that left and right ends of segment can be the same point.
It is guaranteed that there is no integer point, that belongs to all segments.
output: Single line of output should contain one integer number k – size of largest set (xi, cnt(xi)) where all xi are different, 1 ≤ xi ≤ m, and cnt(xi) is amount of segments, containing point with coordinate xi, such that one can't be sure that there doesn't exist point, belonging to all of segments in initial picture, if he knows only this set(and doesn't know n).
note: First example shows situation where Sasha can never be sure that Teodor isn't lying to him, because even if one knows cnt(xi) for each point in segment [1;4], he can't distinguish this case from situation Teodor has drawn whole [1;4] segment.

In second example Sasha can ask about 5 points e.g. 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, still not being sure if Teodor haven't lied to him. But once he knows information about all points in [1;6] segment, Sasha can be sure that Teodor haven't lied to him.

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含两个整数 n 和 m（1 ≤ n，m ≤ 100 000）——Teodor 的图中线段的数量，以及 Sasha 可以询问的点的最大坐标。
接下来的 n 行中的第 i 行包含两个整数 li 和 ri（1 ≤ li ≤ ri ≤ m）——图中第 i 条线段的左端点和右端点。注意，线段的左端点和右端点可以是同一个点。
保证不存在属于所有线段的整数点。

output.ai: 输出一行应包含一个整数 k——集合 (xi, cnt(xi)) 的最大大小，其中所有 xi 互不相同，1 ≤ xi ≤ m，cnt(xi) 表示包含坐标为 xi 的点的线段数量；如果某人只知道这个集合（且不知道 n），就无法确定初始图中不存在一个属于所有线段的点。

note.ai: 第一个样例展示了这样一种情况：Sasha 永远无法确定 Teodor 没有对他撒谎，因为即使知道线段 [1;4] 中每个点的 cnt(xi)，他也无法将这种情况与 Teodor 画出了整条 [1;4] 线段的情况区分开来。
在第二个样例中，Sasha 可以询问 5 个点，例如 1、2、3、5、6，但仍然无法确定 Teodor 是否对他撒了谎。不过，一旦他知道了 [1;6] 线段中所有点的信息，Sasha 就能确定 Teodor 没有对他撒谎。

legend.ai: 年轻的 Teodor 喜欢画画。他最喜欢的爱好是在他巨大的 [1;m] 线段内画端点为整数的线段。一天，Teodor 注意到自己刚画的图有一个有趣的特点：不存在一个属于图中每条线段的整数点。发现这一事实后，Teodor 决定把它告诉 Sasha。

Sasha 知道 Teodor 喜欢炫耀，因此从不相信他。Teodor 想证明自己有时是值得信任的，于是决定说服 Sasha 相信他的图中不存在属于每条线段的整数点。然而，Teodor 很懒，既不愿意告诉 Sasha 所有线段端点的坐标，也不愿意告诉他线段的数量，因此他建议 Sasha 向自己提出一系列问题：“给定整数点 xi，Fedya 的图中有多少条线段包含该点？”，并承诺回答这些问题时都会如实作答。
两个男孩都忙于学习，没有太多时间，因此他们请你求出 Sasha 可以向 Teodor 提出多少个问题，使得仅凭这些问题的答案，Sasha 无法确定 Teodor 没有对他说谎。注意，Sasha 不知道 Teodor 的图中有多少条线段。当然，Sasha 很聪明，从不会两次询问同一个点。

legend: To confuse the opponents, the Galactic Empire represents fractions in an unusual format. The fractions are represented as two sets of integers. The product of numbers from the first set gives the fraction numerator, the product of numbers from the second set gives the fraction denominator. However, it turned out that the programs that work with fractions in this representations aren't complete, they lack supporting the operation of reducing fractions. Implement this operation and the Empire won't forget you.
input: The first input line contains two space-separated integers n, m (1 ≤ n, m ≤ 105) that show how many numbers the first set (the numerator) and the second set (the denominator) contain, correspondingly.
The second line contains n space-separated integers: a1, a2, ..., an (1 ≤ ai ≤ 107) — the numbers that are multiplied to produce the numerator.
The third line contains m space-separated integers: b1, b2, ..., bm (1 ≤ bi ≤ 107) — the numbers that are multiplied to produce the denominator.
output: Print the answer to the problem in the form, similar to the form of the input data. The number of values in the sets you print nout, mout must satisfy the inequality 1 ≤ nout, mout ≤ 105, and the actual values in the sets aout, i and bout, i must satisfy the inequality 1 ≤ aout, i, bout, i ≤ 107.

Separate the values in the lines by spaces. The printed fraction must be reduced, that is, there mustn't be such integer x (x > 1), that the numerator and the denominator of the printed fraction are divisible by x. If there are several matching answers, print any of them.
note: In the first test sample the numerator equals 1000, the denominator equals 500. If we reduce fraction 1000/500 by the greatest common divisor of the numerator and the denominator (by 500), we obtain fraction 2/1.

In the second test sample the numerator equals 2000, the denominator equals 300. If we reduce fraction 2000/300 by the greatest common divisor of the numerator and the denominator (by 100), we obtain fraction 20/3.

legend.ai: 为了迷惑对手，银河帝国使用一种不寻常的格式表示分数。分数表示为两个整数集合。第一个集合中所有数的乘积作为分数的分子，第二个集合中所有数的乘积作为分数的分母。然而，事实证明，使用这种表示法处理分数的程序并不完善，它们不支持约分操作。请实现这一操作，这样帝国就不会忘记你。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含两个用空格分隔的整数 n、m（1 ≤ n，m ≤ 10^5），分别表示第一个集合（分子）和第二个集合（分母）中包含的数字个数。
第二行包含 n 个用空格分隔的整数：a1，a2，...，an（1 ≤ ai ≤ 10^7）——这些数相乘得到分子。
第三行包含 m 个用空格分隔的整数：b1，b2，...，bm（1 ≤ bi ≤ 10^7）——这些数相乘得到分母。

output.ai: 请按照与输入数据类似的格式输出答案。输出的集合中元素的个数 nout、mout 必须满足不等式 1 ≤ nout，mout ≤ 10^5，集合中的实际值 aout，i 和 bout，i 必须满足不等式 1 ≤ aout，i、bout，i ≤ 10^7。
每行中的数值之间用空格分隔。输出的分数必须是最简分数，即不存在这样的整数 x（x > 1），使得输出分数的分子和分母都能被 x 整除。如果有多个符合条件的答案，输出任意一个即可。

note.ai: 在第一个测试样例中，分子等于 1000，分母等于 500。如果我们用分子和分母的最大公约数（即 500）将分数 1000/500 约分，得到分数 2/1。
在第二个测试样例中，分子等于 2000，分母等于 300。如果我们用分子和分母的最大公约数（即 100）将分数 2000/300 约分，得到分数 20/3。

legend: Lena is a beautiful girl who likes logical puzzles.
As a gift for her birthday, Lena got a matrix puzzle!

The matrix consists of n$$$n$$$ rows and m$$$m$$$ columns, and each cell is either black or white. The coordinates (i,j)$$$(i,j)$$$ denote the cell which belongs to the i$$$i$$$-th row and j$$$j$$$-th column for every 1≤i≤n$$$1\leq i \leq n$$$ and 1≤j≤m$$$1\leq j \leq m$$$. To solve the puzzle, Lena has to choose a cell that minimizes the Manhattan distance to the farthest black cell from the chosen cell.

More formally, let there be k≥1$$$k \ge 1$$$ black cells in the matrix with coordinates (xi,yi)$$$(x_i,y_i)$$$ for every 1≤i≤k$$$1\leq i \leq k$$$. Lena should choose a cell (a,b)$$$(a,b)$$$ that minimizes kmaxi=1(|a−xi|+|b−yi|).$$\max_{i=1}^{k}(|a-x_i|+|b-y_i|).$$
As Lena has no skill, she asked you for help. Will you tell her the optimal cell to choose?
input: There are several test cases in the input data. The first line contains a single integer t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤10000$$$1\leq t\leq 10\,000$$$) — the number of test cases. This is followed by the test cases description.
The first line of each test case contains two integers n$$$n$$$ and m$$$m$$$ (2≤n,m≤1000$$$2\leq n,m \leq 1000$$$)  — the dimensions of the matrix.

The following n$$$n$$$ lines contain m$$$m$$$ characters each, each character is either 'W' or 'B'. The j$$$j$$$-th character in the i$$$i$$$-th of these lines is 'W' if the cell (i,j)$$$(i,j)$$$ is white, and 'B' if the cell (i,j)$$$(i,j)$$$ is black.
It is guaranteed that at least one black cell exists.
It is guaranteed that the sum of n⋅m$$$n\cdot m$$$ does not exceed 106$$$10^6$$$.
output: For each test case, output the optimal cell (a,b)$$$(a,b)$$$ to choose. If multiple answers exist, output any.
note: In the first test case the two black cells have coordinates (1,1)$$$(1,1)$$$ and (3,2)$$$(3,2)$$$. The four optimal cells are (1,2)$$$(1,2)$$$, (2,1)$$$(2,1)$$$, (2,2)$$$(2,2)$$$ and (3,1)$$$(3,1)$$$. It can be shown that no other cell minimizes the maximum Manhattan distance to every black cell.

矩阵由 n$$$n$$$ 行和 m$$$m$$$ 列组成，每个单元格要么是黑色，要么是白色。对于每个 1≤i≤n$$$1\leq i \leq n$$$ 且 1≤j≤m$$$1\leq j \leq m$$$，坐标 (i,j)$$$(i,j)$$$ 表示属于第 i$$$i$$$ 行、第 j$$$j$$$ 列的单元格。为了解决这个谜题，Lena 必须选择一个单元格，使其到距所选单元格最远的黑色单元格的曼哈顿距离最小。

legend: Mikhail walks on a Cartesian plane. He starts at the point (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$, and in one move he can go to any of eight adjacent points. For example, if Mikhail is currently at the point (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$, he can go to any of the following points in one move:
If Mikhail goes from the point (x1,y1)$$$(x1, y1)$$$ to the point (x2,y2)$$$(x2, y2)$$$ in one move, and x1≠x2$$$x1 \ne x2$$$ and y1≠y2$$$y1 \ne y2$$$, then such a move is called a diagonal move.

Mikhail has q$$$q$$$ queries. For the i$$$i$$$-th query Mikhail's target is to go to the point (ni,mi)$$$(n_i, m_i)$$$ from the point (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$ in exactly ki$$$k_i$$$ moves. Among all possible movements he want to choose one with the maximum number of diagonal moves. Your task is to find the maximum number of diagonal moves or find that it is impossible to go from the point (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$ to the point (ni,mi)$$$(n_i, m_i)$$$ in ki$$$k_i$$$ moves.
Note that Mikhail can visit any point any number of times (even the destination point!).
input: The first line of the input contains one integer q$$$q$$$ (1≤q≤104$$$1 \le q \le 10^4$$$) — the number of queries.

Then q$$$q$$$ lines follow. The i$$$i$$$-th of these q$$$q$$$ lines contains three integers ni$$$n_i$$$, mi$$$m_i$$$ and ki$$$k_i$$$ (1≤ni,mi,ki≤1018$$$1 \le n_i, m_i, k_i \le 10^{18}$$$) — x$$$x$$$-coordinate of the destination point of the query, y$$$y$$$-coordinate of the destination point of the query and the number of moves in the query, correspondingly.
output: Print q$$$q$$$ integers. The i$$$i$$$-th integer should be equal to -1 if Mikhail cannot go from the point (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$ to the point (ni,mi)$$$(n_i, m_i)$$$ in exactly ki$$$k_i$$$ moves described above. Otherwise the i$$$i$$$-th integer should be equal to the the maximum number of diagonal moves among all possible movements.
note: One of the possible answers to the first test case: (0,0)→(1,0)→(1,1)→(2,2)$$$(0, 0) \to (1, 0) \to (1, 1) \to (2, 2)$$$.
In the third test case Mikhail cannot reach the point (10,1)$$$(10, 1)$$$ in 9 moves.

legend.ai: Mikhail 在笛卡尔平面上行走。他从点 (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$ 出发，每次移动可以走到八个相邻点中的任意一个。例如，如果 Mikhail 当前在点 (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$，他可以在一次移动中到达以下任意一个点：
如果 Mikhail 在一次移动中从点 (x1,y1)$$$(x1, y1)$$$ 移动到点 (x2,y2)$$$(x2, y2)$$$，且 x1≠x2$$$x1 \ne x2$$$ 且 y1≠y2$$$y1 \ne y2$$$，那么这种移动称为对角移动。

Mikhail 有 q$$$q$$$ 个查询。在第 i$$$i$$$ 个查询中，Mikhail 的目标是从点 (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$ 出发，恰好经过 ki$$$k_i$$$ 次移动到达点 (ni,mi)$$$(n_i, m_i)$$$。在所有可能的移动方案中，他希望选择对角移动次数最多的方案。你的任务是求出对角移动的最大次数，或者判定无法在 ki$$$k_i$$$ 次移动内从点 (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$ 到达点 (ni,mi)$$$(n_i, m_i)$$$。
注意，Mikhail 可以访问任意点任意多次（甚至包括终点！）。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含一个整数 q$$$q$$$(1≤q≤104$$$1 \le q \le 10^4$$$)——查询的数量。
接下来是 q$$$q$$$ 行。其中这 q$$$q$$$ 行中的第 i$$$i$$$ 行包含三个整数 ni$$$n_i$$$、mi$$$m_i$$$ 和 ki$$$k_i$$$(1≤ni,mi,ki≤1018$$$1 \le n_i, m_i, k_i \le 10^{18}$$$)，分别表示查询目标点的 x$$$x$$$ 坐标、查询目标点的 y$$$y$$$ 坐标以及查询中的移动次数。

output.ai: 输出 q$$$q$$$ 个整数。如果 Mikhail 无法在上述定义的恰好 ki$$$k_i$$$ 步内从点 (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$ 到达点 (ni,mi)$$$(n_i, m_i)$$$，则第 i$$$i$$$ 个整数应为 -1。否则，第 i$$$i$$$ 个整数应等于所有可能移动方案中对角移动次数的最大值。

problems.hint: Each burned tree turned into a square.

legend: The Berland Forest can be represented as an infinite cell plane. Every cell contains a tree. That is, contained before the recent events.

A destructive fire raged through the Forest, and several trees were damaged by it. Precisely speaking, you have a $$$n \times m$$$ rectangle map which represents the damaged part of the Forest. The damaged trees were marked as "X" while the remaining ones were marked as ".". You are sure that all burnt trees are shown on the map. All the trees outside the map are undamaged.

The firemen quickly extinguished the fire, and now they are investigating the cause of it. The main version is that there was an arson: at some moment of time (let's consider it as $$$0$$$) some trees were set on fire. At the beginning of minute $$$0$$$, only the trees that were set on fire initially were burning. At the end of each minute, the fire spread from every burning tree to each of $$$8$$$ neighboring trees. At the beginning of minute $$$T$$$, the fire was extinguished.

The firemen want to find the arsonists as quickly as possible. The problem is, they know neither the value of $$$T$$$ (how long the fire has been raging) nor the coordinates of the trees that were initially set on fire. They want you to find the maximum value of $$$T$$$ (to know how far could the arsonists escape) and a possible set of trees that could be initially set on fire.
Note that you'd like to maximize value $$$T$$$ but the set of trees can be arbitrary.
input: The first line contains two integer $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$1 \le n, m \le 10^6$$$, $$$1 \le n \cdot m \le 10^6$$$) — the sizes of the map.

Next $$$n$$$ lines contain the map. The $$$i$$$-th line corresponds to the $$$i$$$-th row of the map and contains $$$m$$$-character string. The $$$j$$$-th character of the $$$i$$$-th string is "X" if the corresponding tree is burnt and "." otherwise.
It's guaranteed that the map contains at least one "X".
output: In the first line print the single integer $$$T$$$ — the maximum time the Forest was on fire. In the next $$$n$$$ lines print the certificate: the map ($$$n \times m$$$ rectangle) where the trees that were set on fire are marked as "X" and all other trees are marked as ".".

input.ai: 第一行包含两个整数 $$$n$$$ 和 $$$m$$$($$$1 \le n, m \le 10^6$$$、$$$1 \le n \cdot m \le 10^6$$$)——地图的大小。
接下来的 $$$n$$$ 行包含地图。第 $$$i$$$ 行对应地图的第 $$$i$$$ 行，并包含一个长度为 $$$m$$$ 的字符串。第 $$$i$$$ 个字符串中的第 $$$j$$$ 个字符，如果对应的树被烧毁，则为“X”，否则为“.”。
保证地图中至少包含一个“X”。

output.ai: 第一行输出一个整数 $$$T$$$ —— 森林着火的最长时间。接下来的 $$$n$$$ 行输出证书：一个 $$$n \times m$$$ 矩形地图，其中被点燃的树标记为“X”，所有其他树标记为“.”。

legend.ai: 贝尔兰德森林可以表示为一个无限的网格平面。每个格子中都包含一棵树。也就是说，在最近发生的事件之前是这样的。
一场毁灭性的火灾席卷了森林，许多树因此受损。准确地说，你有一张 $$$n \times m$$$ 的矩形地图，表示森林中受损的部分。受损的树被标记为“X”，其余树被标记为“.”。你可以确定所有被烧毁的树都显示在地图上。地图之外的所有树都未受损。
消防员很快扑灭了火灾，现在他们正在调查火灾的原因。最有可能的情况是有人纵火：在某个时刻(记为 $$$0$$$)，一些树被点燃。在第 $$$0$$$ 分钟开始时，只有最初被点燃的树正在燃烧。在每分钟结束时，火焰会从每一棵正在燃烧的树蔓延到其 $$$8$$$ 棵相邻树中的每一棵。在第 $$$T$$$ 分钟开始时，火灾被扑灭。
消防员希望尽快找到纵火犯。问题在于，他们既不知道 $$$T$$$ 的值(火灾持续了多久)，也不知道最初被点燃的树的坐标。他们希望你找出 $$$T$$$ 的最大值(以了解纵火犯最远可以逃出多远)，并找出一组可能最初被点燃的树。
注意，你需要最大化 $$$T$$$，但树的集合可以任意选择。
