problems.hint: How does the swap of two elements change the total number of inversions?

legend: Petya is a beginner programmer. He has already mastered the basics of the C++ language and moved on to learning algorithms. The first algorithm he encountered was insertion sort. Petya has already written the code that implements this algorithm and sorts the given integer zero-indexed array a of size n in the non-decreasing order.

Petya uses this algorithm only for sorting of arrays that are permutations of numbers from 0 to n - 1. He has already chosen the permutation he wants to sort but he first decided to swap some two of its elements. Petya wants to choose these elements in such a way that the number of times the sorting executes function swap, was minimum. Help Petya find out the number of ways in which he can make the swap and fulfill this requirement.
It is guaranteed that it's always possible to swap two elements of the input permutation in such a way that the number of swap function calls decreases.
input: The first line contains a single integer n (2 ≤ n ≤ 5000) — the length of the permutation. The second line contains n different integers from 0 to n - 1, inclusive — the actual permutation.
output: Print two integers: the minimum number of times the swap function is executed and the number of such pairs (i, j) that swapping the elements of the input permutation with indexes i and j leads to the minimum number of the executions.
note: In the first sample the appropriate pairs are (0, 3) and (0, 4).
In the second sample the appropriate pairs are (0, 4), (1, 4), (2, 4) and (3, 4).

legend.ai: Petya 是一名编程初学者。他已经掌握了 C++ 语言的基础知识，并开始学习算法。他遇到的第一个算法是插入排序。Petya 已经编写了实现该算法的代码，可以将给定的大小为 n、下标从 0 开始的整数数组 a 按非递减顺序排序。
Petya 仅使用该算法对由 0 到 n−1 的数构成的排列进行排序。他已经选定了要排序的排列，但决定先交换其中的某两个元素。Petya 希望以一种使排序过程中执行 swap 函数的次数最少的方式选择这两个元素。请帮助 Petya 求出他可以进行这种交换并满足要求的方案数。
保证总能交换输入排列中的两个元素，使 swap 函数的调用次数减少。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n（2 ≤ n ≤ 5000），表示排列的长度。第二行包含 n 个互不相同的整数，范围为 0 到 n−1（包含边界），表示实际的排列。

output.ai: 输出两个整数：swap 函数执行的最少次数，以及满足以下条件的数对 (i, j) 的数量：交换输入排列中下标为 i 和 j 的元素后，swap 函数的执行次数达到最少。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，符合条件的数对为 (0, 3) 和 (0, 4)。
在第二个样例中，符合条件的数对为 (0, 4)、(1, 4)、(2, 4) 和 (3, 4)。

legend: As a tradition, every year before IOI all the members of Natalia Fan Club are invited to Malek Dance Club to have a fun night together. Malek Dance Club has 2n members and coincidentally Natalia Fan Club also has 2n members. Each member of MDC is assigned a unique id i from 0 to 2n - 1. The same holds for each member of NFC.

One of the parts of this tradition is one by one dance, where each member of MDC dances with a member of NFC. A dance pair is a pair of numbers (a, b) such that member a from MDC dances with member b from NFC.
The complexity of a pairs' assignment is the number of pairs of dancing pairs (a, b) and (c, d) such that a < c and b > d.

You are given a binary number of length n named x. We know that member i from MDC dances with member ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/064f62f758022f9f352d238ee5ed93ec9a92138b.png) from NFC. Your task is to calculate the complexity of this assignment modulo 1000000007 (109 + 7).

Expression ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b364f2e04c665b78b924ec10666327a4ef4635bc.png) denotes applying «XOR» to numbers x and y. This operation exists in all modern programming languages, for example, in C++ and Java it denotes as «^», in Pascal — «xor».
input: The first line of input contains a binary number x of lenght n, (1 ≤ n ≤ 100).
This number may contain leading zeros.
output: Print the complexity of the given dance assignent modulo 1000000007 (109 + 7).

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含一个长度为 n 的二进制数 x（1 ≤ n ≤ 100）。
这个数可能包含前导零。

output.ai: 输出给定舞蹈安排的复杂度对 1000000007（10⁹ + 7）取模后的结果。

legend.ai: 作为一项传统，每年在 IOI 之前，Natalia 粉丝俱乐部的所有成员都会受邀来到 Malek 舞蹈俱乐部，共度一个欢乐的夜晚。Malek 舞蹈俱乐部有 2^n 名成员，巧合的是，Natalia 粉丝俱乐部也有 2^n 名成员。MDC 的每位成员都被分配了一个从 0 到 2^n - 1 的唯一编号 i。NFC 的每位成员也是如此。
这项传统的一部分是一对一跳舞，即 MDC 的每位成员都与 NFC 的一位成员跳舞。舞蹈配对是一个数对 (a, b)，表示 MDC 中的成员 a 与 NFC 中的成员 b 跳舞。
配对方案的复杂度是满足 a < c 且 b > d 的舞蹈配对对 (a, b) 和 (c, d) 的数量。
给定一个长度为 n、名为 x 的二进制数。已知 MDC 中编号为 i 的成员与 NFC 中编号为 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/064f62f758022f9f352d238ee5ed93ec9a92138b.png) 的成员跳舞。你的任务是计算该配对方案的复杂度，并对 1000000007(10^9 + 7)取模。
表达式 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b364f2e04c665b78b924ec10666327a4ef4635bc.png) 表示对数字 x 和 y 进行“异或”运算。所有现代编程语言都支持该运算，例如在 C++ 和 Java 中表示为“^”，在 Pascal 中表示为“xor”。

problems.hint: There is a pattern that the remaining fools should follow.

legend: One fine morning, n fools lined up in a row. After that, they numbered each other with numbers from 1 to n, inclusive. Each fool got a unique number. The fools decided not to change their numbers before the end of the fun.
Every fool has exactly k bullets and a pistol. In addition, the fool number i has probability of pi (in percent) that he kills the fool he shoots at.

The fools decided to have several rounds of the fun. Each round of the fun looks like this: each currently living fool shoots at another living fool with the smallest number (a fool is not stupid enough to shoot at himself). All shots of the round are perfomed at one time (simultaneously). If there is exactly one living fool, he does not shoot.

Let's define a situation as the set of numbers of all the living fools at the some time. We say that a situation is possible if for some integer number j (0 ≤ j ≤ k) there is a nonzero probability that after j rounds of the fun this situation will occur.
Valera knows numbers p1, p2, ..., pn and k. Help Valera determine the number of distinct possible situations.
input: The first line contains two integers n, k (1 ≤ n, k ≤ 3000) — the initial number of fools and the number of bullets for each fool.
The second line contains n integers p1, p2, ..., pn (0 ≤ pi ≤ 100) — the given probabilities (in percent).
output: Print a single number — the answer to the problem.
note: In the first sample, any situation is possible, except for situation {1, 2}.
In the second sample there is exactly one fool, so he does not make shots.
In the third sample the possible situations are {1, 2} (after zero rounds) and the "empty" situation {} (after one round).
In the fourth sample, the only possible situation is {1, 2, 3}.

legend.ai: 一个晴朗的早晨，n 个傻瓜排成一排。随后，他们互相分配了从 1 到 n（含）之间的编号。每个傻瓜得到一个唯一的编号。他们决定在欢乐结束前不更改自己的编号。
每个傻瓜恰好有 k 发子弹和一把手枪。此外，编号为 i 的傻瓜有 pi% 的概率杀死他射击的目标。
这些傻瓜决定进行若干轮游戏。每一轮游戏如下：每个当前存活的傻瓜都会向编号最小的另一个存活傻瓜射击（傻瓜不会傻到朝自己射击）。这一轮中的所有射击同时进行。如果恰好只有一个存活的傻瓜，他不会射击。
我们将某一时刻所有存活傻瓜的编号集合定义为一种局面。如果存在某个整数 j（0 ≤ j ≤ k），使得进行 j 轮游戏后出现这种局面的概率非零，则称这种局面是可能的。
Valera 知道数字 p1、p2、...、pn 和 k。请帮助 Valera 确定不同可能局面的数量。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，除了情况 {1, 2} 之外，任何情况都有可能。
在第二个样例中恰好有一个傻瓜，因此他不会开枪。
在第三个样例中，可能的情况是 {1, 2}（经过 0 轮后）以及“空”情况 {}（经过 1 轮后）。
在第四个样例中，唯一可能的情况是 {1, 2, 3}。

input.ai: 第一行包含两个整数 n、k（1 ≤ n，k ≤ 3000）——初始傻瓜数量和每个傻瓜的子弹数量。
第二行包含 n 个整数 p1、p2、...、pn（0 ≤ pi ≤ 100）——给定的概率（以百分比表示）。

output.ai: 输出一个数——问题的答案。

problems.hint: Find a way to calculate the sum of the submatrix quickly.

legend: You have a string of decimal digits s. Let's define bij = si·sj. Find in matrix b the number of such rectangles that the sum bij for all cells (i, j) that are the elements of the rectangle equals a in each rectangle.
A rectangle in a matrix is a group of four integers (x, y, z, t) (x ≤ y, z ≤ t). The elements of the rectangle are all cells (i, j) such that x ≤ i ≤ y, z ≤ j ≤ t.

legend.ai: 给定一个十进制数字字符串 s。定义 b_ij = s_i·s_j。请在矩阵 b 中找出这样的矩形数量：对于每个矩形，矩形内所有单元格 (i, j) 的 b_ij 之和都等于 a。
矩阵中的一个矩形是由四个整数组成的组 (x, y, z, t)（x ≤ y，z ≤ t）。矩形中的元素是所有满足 x ≤ i ≤ y，z ≤ j ≤ t 的单元格 (i, j)。

legend.ai: 给定一个无向图，其中每条边有两种颜色之一：黑色或红色。

problems.hint: You just care about how many rows and columns remain after operations.

legend: User ainta decided to paint a wall. The wall consists of n2 tiles, that are arranged in an n × n table. Some tiles are painted, and the others are not. As he wants to paint it beautifully, he will follow the rules below.
Firstly user ainta looks at the wall. If there is at least one painted cell on each row and at least one painted cell on each column, he stops coloring. Otherwise, he goes to step 2.
User ainta choose any tile on the wall with uniform probability.
If the tile he has chosen is not painted, he paints the tile. Otherwise, he ignores it.
Then he takes a rest for one minute even if he doesn't paint the tile. And then ainta goes to step 1.

However ainta is worried if it would take too much time to finish this work. So he wants to calculate the expected time needed to paint the wall by the method above. Help him find the expected time. You can assume that choosing and painting any tile consumes no time at all.
input: The first line contains two integers n and m (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·103; 0 ≤ m ≤ min(n2, 2·104)) — the size of the wall and the number of painted cells.

Next m lines goes, each contains two integers ri and ci (1 ≤ ri, ci ≤ n) — the position of the painted cell. It is guaranteed that the positions are all distinct. Consider the rows of the table are numbered from 1 to n. Consider the columns of the table are numbered from 1 to n.
output: In a single line print the expected time to paint the wall in minutes. Your answer will be considered correct if it has at most 10 - 4 absolute or relative error.

legend.ai: 用户 ainta 决定粉刷一面墙壁。墙壁由 n2 块瓷砖组成，排列成一个 n × n 的表格。有些瓷砖已被粉刷，其余未粉刷。他希望把墙壁刷得漂亮，因此会遵循以下规则。
首先，用户 ainta 观察墙壁。如果每一行都至少有一个已粉刷的格子，并且每一列都至少有一个已粉刷的格子，他就停止涂色。否则，他进入第 2 步。
用户 ainta 从墙壁上等概率地随机选择任意一块瓷砖。
如果他选择的格子尚未涂色，就将其涂色；否则，他忽略它。
然后他休息一分钟，即使他没有涂那个格子。接着 ainta 回到步骤 1。
然而 ainta 担心完成这项工作会花费太多时间。因此他想计算用上述方法涂完整面墙所需的期望时间。帮他求出这个期望时间。你可以假设选择格子以及给任何格子涂色都不消耗时间。

input.ai: 第一行包含两个整数 n 和 m（1 ≤ n ≤ 2·10^3；0 ≤ m ≤ min(n^2, 2·10^4)）——墙的尺寸和已涂色格子的数量。
接下来有 m 行，每行包含两个整数 ri 和 ci（1 ≤ ri, ci ≤ n）——已涂色格子的位置。保证所有位置互不相同。注意表格的行从 1 到 n 编号，表格的列也从 1 到 n 编号。

output.ai: 在一行中输出涂完整面墙所需的期望时间，单位为分钟。答案的绝对误差或相对误差不超过 10^-4 即视为正确。

legend: Yet another education system reform has been carried out in Berland recently. The innovations are as follows:

An academic year now consists of n days. Each day pupils study exactly one of m subjects, besides, each subject is studied for no more than one day. After the lessons of the i-th subject pupils get the home task that contains no less than ai and no more than bi exercises. Besides, each subject has a special attribute, the complexity (ci). A school can make its own timetable, considering the following conditions are satisfied:
the timetable should contain the subjects in the order of the complexity's strict increasing;

each day, except for the first one, the task should contain either k times more exercises, or more by k compared to the previous day (more formally: let's call the number of home task exercises in the i-th day as xi, then for each i (1 < i ≤ n): either xi = k + xi - 1 or xi = k·xi - 1 must be true);
the total number of exercises in all home tasks should be maximal possible.
All limitations are separately set for each school.

It turned out that in many cases ai and bi reach 1016 (however, as the Berland Minister of Education is famous for his love to half-measures, the value of bi - ai doesn't exceed 100). That also happened in the Berland School №256. Nevertheless, you as the school's principal still have to work out the timetable for the next academic year...
input: The first line contains three integers n, m, k (1 ≤ n ≤ m ≤ 50, 1 ≤ k ≤ 100) which represent the number of days in an academic year, the number of subjects and the k parameter correspondingly. Each of the following m lines contains the description of a subject as three integers ai, bi, ci (1 ≤ ai ≤ bi ≤ 1016, bi - ai ≤ 100, 1 ≤ ci ≤ 100) — two limitations to the number of exercises on the i-th subject and the complexity of the i-th subject, correspondingly. Distinct subjects can have the same complexity. The subjects are numbered with integers from 1 to m.
Please do not use the %lld specificator to read or write 64-bit numbers in С++. It is preferred to use the cin stream or the %I64d specificator.
output: If no valid solution exists, print the single word "NO" (without the quotes). Otherwise, the first line should contain the word "YES" (without the quotes) and the next n lines should contain any timetable that satisfies all the conditions. The i + 1-th line should contain two positive integers: the number of the subject to study on the i-th day and the number of home task exercises given for this subject. The timetable should contain exactly n subjects.

legend.ai: 然而，最近 Berland 又进行了一次教育系统改革。改革内容如下：
现在，一个学年由 n 天组成。每天学生恰好学习 m 门科目中的一门，并且每门科目学习的天数不超过一天。学习第 i 门科目后，学生会得到一份包含不少于 a_i 且不多于 b_i 道习题的家庭作业。此外，每门科目都有一个特殊属性，即复杂度 c_i。学校可以自行制定课表，但必须满足以下条件：
课表中的科目应按照复杂度严格递增的顺序排列；
除第一天外，每天的作业中都应包含比前一天多 k 道习题，或包含前一天作业中习题数量的 k 倍（更正式地说，设第 i 天家庭作业中的习题数为 x_i，则对于每个 i（1 < i ≤ n），必须满足 x_i = k + x_{i-1} 或 x_i = k·x_{i-1}）；
所有家庭作业中的习题总数应尽可能大。
所有限制条件均针对每所学校分别设定。
事实证明，在许多情况下，ai 和 bi 会达到 10^16（不过，由于 Berland 教育部长以喜欢折中方案而闻名，bi - ai 的值不会超过 100）。Berland 第 256 号学校也遇到了这种情况。然而，作为该校校长，你仍然必须制定下一学年的课程表……

input.ai: 第一行包含三个整数 n、m、k（1 ≤ n ≤ m ≤ 50，1 ≤ k ≤ 100），分别表示一个学年的天数、科目数量以及参数 k。接下来的 m 行中，每行包含一个科目的描述，由三个整数 ai、bi、ci（1 ≤ ai ≤ bi ≤ 10^16，bi - ai ≤ 100，1 ≤ ci ≤ 100）组成，分别表示第 i 个科目习题数量的两个限制，以及第 i 个科目的难度。不同科目可以具有相同的难度。科目的编号为 1 到 m。
请不要在 C++ 中使用 %lld 格式说明符来读写 64 位数字。建议使用 cin 流或 %I64d 格式说明符。

output.ai: 如果不存在有效方案，请输出一个单词“NO”（不含引号）。否则，第一行应输出单词“YES”（不含引号），接下来的 n 行应输出任意一个满足所有条件的课程表。第 i+1 行应包含两个正整数：第 i 天学习的科目编号，以及为该科目布置的家庭作业习题数量。课程表中应恰好安排 n 个科目。

statement.title: C. Polo the Penguin and XOR operation

legend: Little penguin Polo likes permutations. But most of all he likes permutations of integers from 0 to n, inclusive.
For permutation p = p0, p1, ..., pn, Polo has defined its beauty — number ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/0c51fe5d835015fdb8b8dbb056e9a83c439c83dc.png).

Expression ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b364f2e04c665b78b924ec10666327a4ef4635bc.png) means applying the operation of bitwise excluding "OR" to numbers x and y. This operation exists in all modern programming languages, for example, in language C++ and Java it is represented as "^" and in Pascal — as "xor".
Help him find among all permutations of integers from 0 to n the permutation with the maximum beauty.
input: The single line contains a positive integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 106).
output: In the first line print integer m the maximum possible beauty. In the second line print any permutation of integers from 0 to n with the beauty equal to m.
If there are several suitable permutations, you are allowed to print any of them.

legend.ai: 小企鹅 Polo 喜欢排列。但他最喜欢的是从 0 到 n（含两端）的整数排列。
对于排列 p = p0, p1, ..., pn，Polo 定义了它的美丽值——数 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/0c51fe5d835015fdb8b8dbb056e9a83c439c83dc.png)。
表达式 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b364f2e04c665b78b924ec10666327a4ef4635bc.png) 表示对数字 x 和 y 进行按位异或运算。该运算存在于所有现代编程语言中，例如在 C++ 和 Java 中表示为 "^"，在 Pascal 中表示为 "xor"。
请帮助他在从 0 到 n 的所有整数排列中，找出美丽值最大的那个排列。

input.ai: 输入只有一行，包含一个正整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 10^6）。

output.ai: 第一行输出整数 m，表示可能的最大美丽值。第二行输出一个从 0 到 n 的整数排列，使其美丽值等于 m。
如果有多个合适的排列，你可以输出其中任意一个。

legend: Monocarp is a tutor of a group of n$$$n$$$ students. He communicates with them using a conference in a popular messenger.

Today was a busy day for Monocarp — he was asked to forward a lot of posts and announcements to his group, that's why he had to write a very large number of messages in the conference. Monocarp knows the students in the group he is tutoring quite well, so he understands which message should each student read: Monocarp wants the student i$$$i$$$ to read the message mi$$$m_i$$$.

Of course, no one's going to read all the messages in the conference. That's why Monocarp decided to pin some of them. Monocarp can pin any number of messages, and if he wants anyone to read some message, he should pin it — otherwise it will definitely be skipped by everyone.

Unfortunately, even if a message is pinned, some students may skip it anyway. For each student i$$$i$$$, Monocarp knows that they will read at most ki$$$k_i$$$ messages. Suppose Monocarp pins t$$$t$$$ messages; if t≤ki$$$t \le k_i$$$, then the i$$$i$$$-th student will read all the pinned messages; but if t>ki$$$t  \gt  k_i$$$, the i$$$i$$$-th student will choose exactly ki$$$k_i$$$ random pinned messages (all possible subsets of pinned messages of size ki$$$k_i$$$ are equiprobable) and read only the chosen messages.

Monocarp wants to maximize the expected number of students that read their respective messages (i.e. the number of such indices i$$$i$$$ that student i$$$i$$$ reads the message mi$$$m_i$$$). Help him to choose how many (and which) messages should he pin!
input: The first line contains one integer n$$$n$$$ (1≤n≤2⋅105$$$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of students in the conference.

Then n$$$n$$$ lines follow. The i$$$i$$$-th line contains two integers mi$$$m_i$$$ and ki$$$k_i$$$ (1≤mi≤2⋅105$$$1 \le m_i \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$; 1≤ki≤20$$$1 \le k_i \le 20$$$) — the index of the message which Monocarp wants the i$$$i$$$-th student to read and the maximum number of messages the i$$$i$$$-th student will read, respectively.
output: In the first line, print one integer t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤2⋅105$$$1 \le t \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of messages Monocarp should pin. In the second line, print t$$$t$$$ distinct integers c1$$$c_1$$$, c2$$$c_2$$$, ..., ct$$$c_t$$$ (1≤ci≤2⋅105$$$1 \le c_i \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the indices of the messages Monocarp should pin. The messages can be listed in any order.
If there are multiple answers, print any of them.
note: Let's consider the examples from the statement.

In the first example, Monocarp pins the messages 5$$$5$$$ and 10$$$10$$$.  if the first student reads the message 5$$$5$$$, the second student reads the messages 5$$$5$$$ and 10$$$10$$$, and the third student reads the messages 5$$$5$$$ and 10$$$10$$$, the number of students which have read their respective messages will be 2$$$2$$$;

if the first student reads the message 10$$$10$$$, the second student reads the messages 5$$$5$$$ and 10$$$10$$$, and the third student reads the messages 5$$$5$$$ and 10$$$10$$$, the number of students which have read their respective messages will be 3$$$3$$$.
So, the expected number of students which will read their respective messages is 52$$$\frac{5}{2}$$$.

In the second example, Monocarp pins the message 10$$$10$$$.  if the first student reads the message 10$$$10$$$, the second student reads the message 10$$$10$$$, and the third student reads the message 10$$$10$$$, the number of students which have read their respective messages will be 2$$$2$$$.

So, the expected number of students which will read their respective messages is 2$$$2$$$. If Monocarp had pinned both messages 5$$$5$$$ and 10$$$10$$$, the expected number of students which read their respective messages would have been 2$$$2$$$ as well.
In the third example, the expected number of students which will read their respective messages is 83$$$\frac{8}{3}$$$.
In the fourth example, the expected number of students which will read their respective messages is 2$$$2$$$.

legend.ai: Monocarp 是一个有 n$$$n$$$ 名学生的小组的辅导老师。他通过一款流行的即时通信软件中的群聊与他们交流。
今天对 Monocarp 来说是忙碌的一天——有人要求他将许多帖子和公告转发给他的小组，因此他不得不在群聊中发送大量消息。Monocarp 很了解自己辅导的小组中的学生，所以他知道每个学生应该阅读哪条消息：Monocarp 希望学生 i$$$i$$$ 阅读消息 mi$$$m_i$$$。
当然，没有人会阅读群聊中的所有消息。因此，Monocarp 决定将其中一些消息置顶。Monocarp 可以置顶任意数量的消息；如果他希望某人阅读某条消息，就应该将其置顶——否则这条消息肯定会被所有人跳过。

遗憾的是，即使一条消息被置顶，一些学生仍可能跳过它。对于每个学生 i$$$i$$$，Monocarp 知道他们至多会阅读 ki$$$k_i$$$ 条消息。假设 Monocarp 将 t$$$t$$$ 条消息置顶；如果 t≤ki$$$t \le k_i$$$，那么第 i$$$i$$$ 个学生会阅读所有置顶消息；但如果 t>ki$$$t  \gt  k_i$$$，第 i$$$i$$$ 个学生会从置顶消息中随机选择恰好 ki$$$k_i$$$ 条(所有大小为 ki$$$k_i$$$ 的置顶消息子集被选中的概率相同)，并且只阅读被选中的消息。
Monocarp 想要最大化阅读了各自消息的学生人数的期望值(也就是满足学生 i$$$i$$$ 阅读消息 mi$$$m_i$$$ 的下标 i$$$i$$$ 的数量)。请帮助他选择应该置顶多少条消息，以及置顶哪些消息！

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n$$$n$$$(1≤n≤2⋅105$$$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$)——会议中的学生人数。

接下来有 n$$$n$$$ 行。第 i$$$i$$$ 行包含两个整数 mi$$$m_i$$$ 和 ki$$$k_i$$$(1≤mi≤2⋅105$$$1 \le m_i \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$；1≤ki≤20$$$1 \le k_i \le 20$$$)——分别表示 Monocarp 希望第 i$$$i$$$ 个学生阅读的消息编号，以及第 i$$$i$$$ 个学生将阅读的消息数量上限。

output.ai: 第一行输出一个整数 t$$$t$$$(1≤t≤2⋅105$$$1 \le t \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$)——Monocarp 应该置顶的消息数量。第二行输出 t$$$t$$$ 个互不相同的整数 c1$$$c_1$$$、c2$$$c_2$$$、...、ct$$$c_t$$$(1≤ci≤2⋅105$$$1 \le c_i \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$)——Monocarp 应该置顶的消息编号。消息可以按任意顺序列出。
如果有多个答案，输出其中任意一个。

note.ai: 让我们来看题面中的样例。
在第一个样例中，Monocarp 置顶了消息 5$$$5$$$ 和 10$$$10$$$。如果第一个学生阅读消息 5$$$5$$$，第二个学生阅读消息 5$$$5$$$ 和 10$$$10$$$，第三个学生阅读消息 5$$$5$$$ 和 10$$$10$$$，那么阅读了各自对应消息的学生人数为 2$$$2$$$；
如果第一个学生阅读消息 10$$$10$$$，第二个学生阅读消息 5$$$5$$$ 和 10$$$10$$$，第三个学生阅读消息 5$$$5$$$ 和 10$$$10$$$，那么阅读了各自对应消息的学生人数为 3$$$3$$$。
因此，阅读各自对应消息的学生人数的期望值为 52$$$\frac{5}{2}$$$。
在第二个样例中，Monocarp 置顶了消息 10$$$10$$$。如果第一个学生阅读消息 10$$$10$$$，第二个学生阅读消息 10$$$10$$$，第三个学生阅读消息 10$$$10$$$，那么阅读了各自对应消息的学生人数为 2$$$2$$$。
因此，阅读各自对应消息的学生人数的期望值为 2$$$2$$$。如果 Monocarp 同时置顶了消息 5$$$5$$$ 和 10$$$10$$$，那么阅读各自对应消息的学生人数的期望值也会是 2$$$2$$$。
在第三个样例中，阅读各自对应消息的学生人数的期望值为 83$$$\frac{8}{3}$$$。
在第四个样例中，将阅读各自消息的学生的期望数量为 2$$$2$$$。

legend: Polycarpus is an amateur programmer. Now he is analyzing a friend's program. He has already found there the function rangeIncrement(l, r), that adds 1 to each element of some array a for all indexes in the segment [l, r]. In other words, this function does the following:

Polycarpus knows the state of the array a after a series of function calls. He wants to determine the minimum number of function calls that lead to such state. In addition, he wants to find what function calls are needed in this case. It is guaranteed that the required number of calls does not exceed 105.
Before calls of function rangeIncrement(l, r) all array elements equal zero.
input: The first input line contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 105) — the length of the array a[1... n].
The second line contains its integer space-separated elements, a[1], a[2], ..., a[n] (0 ≤ a[i] ≤ 105) after some series of function calls rangeIncrement(l, r).
It is guaranteed that at least one element of the array is positive. It is guaranteed that the answer contains no more than 105 calls of function rangeIncrement(l, r).
output: Print on the first line t — the minimum number of calls of function rangeIncrement(l, r), that lead to the array from the input data. It is guaranteed that this number will turn out not more than 105.

Then print t lines — the descriptions of function calls, one per line. Each line should contain two integers li, ri (1 ≤ li ≤ ri ≤ n) — the arguments of the i-th call rangeIncrement(l, r). Calls can be applied in any order.
If there are multiple solutions, you are allowed to print any of them.
note: The first sample requires a call for the entire array, and four additional calls:
one for the segment [2,2] (i.e. the second element of the array),
three for the segment [5,5] (i.e. the fifth element of the array).

note.ai: 第一个样例需要对整个数组进行一次调用，另外还需要四次调用：
对于区间 [2,2]（即数组的第二个元素），一个，
对于区间 [5,5]（即数组的第五个元素），三个。

input.ai: 第一行输入包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5）——数组 a[1... n] 的长度。
第二行包含在若干次函数 rangeIncrement(l, r) 调用后得到的、以空格分隔的整数元素 a[1]、a[2]、...、a[n]（0 ≤ a[i] ≤ 10^5）。
保证数组中至少有一个元素为正数。保证答案中调用函数 rangeIncrement(l, r) 的次数不超过 10^5。

output.ai: 第一行输出 t——使输入数据中的数组得到的函数 rangeIncrement(l, r) 调用次数的最小值。保证该数不超过 10^5。
然后输出 t 行——函数调用的描述，每行一个。每行应包含两个整数 l_i、r_i（1 ≤ l_i ≤ r_i ≤ n），表示第 i 次调用 rangeIncrement(l, r) 时的参数。调用可以按任意顺序进行。
如果存在多种解，允许输出其中任意一种。

legend.ai: Polycarpus 是一名业余程序员。现在，他正在分析一位朋友的程序。他已经在其中找到了函数 rangeIncrement(l, r)：对于区间 [l, r] 中的所有下标，该函数会将数组 a 的每个元素加 1。换句话说，该函数执行以下操作：
Polycarpus 知道数组 a 在一系列函数调用后的状态。他希望确定得到这种状态所需的最少函数调用次数。此外，他还希望找出在这种情况下需要进行哪些函数调用。保证所需的调用次数不超过 10^5。
调用函数 rangeIncrement(l, r) 之前，数组中的所有元素都等于 0。

legend: You've got an array a, consisting of n integers. The array elements are indexed from 1 to n. Let's determine a two step operation like that:

First we build by the array a an array s of partial sums, consisting of n elements. Element number i (1 ≤ i ≤ n) of array s equals ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/cdc22b6f0de971f5a4a64b6f9e22d76a719ec5b7.png). The operation x mod y means that we take the remainder of the division of number x by number y.
Then we write the contents of the array s to the array a. Element number i (1 ≤ i ≤ n) of the array s becomes the i-th element of the array a (ai = si).
You task is to find array a after exactly k described operations are applied.
input: The first line contains two space-separated integers n and k (1 ≤ n ≤ 2000, 0 ≤ k ≤ 109). The next line contains n space-separated integers a1, a2, ..., an — elements of the array a (0 ≤ ai ≤ 109).
output: Print n integers  — elements of the array a after the operations are applied to it. Print the elements in the order of increasing of their indexes in the array a. Separate the printed numbers by spaces.

legend.ai: 给定一个由 n 个整数构成的数组 a。数组元素的下标从 1 到 n。现在我们来定义如下的两步操作：
首先根据数组 a 构造一个由 n 个元素组成的部分和数组 s。数组 s 的第 i 个元素(1 ≤ i ≤ n)等于 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/cdc22b6f0de971f5a4a64b6f9e22d76a719ec5b7.png)。运算 x mod y 表示取 x 除以 y 的余数。
然后将数组 s 的内容写入数组 a。数组 s 的第 i 个元素（1 ≤ i ≤ n）变为数组 a 的第 i 个元素（ai = si）。
你的任务是求出在恰好进行 k 次所描述的操作后得到的数组 a。

input.ai: 第一行包含两个以空格分隔的整数 n 和 k（1 ≤ n ≤ 2000，0 ≤ k ≤ 10^9）。下一行包含 n 个以空格分隔的整数 a1，a2，...，an——数组 a 的元素（0 ≤ ai ≤ 10^9）。

legend: Even the most successful company can go through a crisis period when you have to make a hard decision — to restructure, discard and merge departments, fire employees and do other unpleasant stuff. Let's consider the following model of a company.

There are n people working for the Large Software Company. Each person belongs to some department. Initially, each person works on his own project in his own department (thus, each company initially consists of n departments, one person in each).

However, harsh times have come to the company and the management had to hire a crisis manager who would rebuild the working process in order to boost efficiency. Let's use team(person) to represent a team where person person works. A crisis manager can make decisions of two types:

Merge departments team(x) and team(y) into one large department containing all the employees of team(x) and team(y), where x and y (1 ≤ x, y ≤ n) — are numbers of two of some company employees. If team(x) matches team(y), then nothing happens.
Merge departments team(x), team(x + 1), ..., team(y), where x and y (1 ≤ x ≤ y ≤ n) — the numbers of some two employees of the company.
At that the crisis manager can sometimes wonder whether employees x and y (1 ≤ x, y ≤ n) work at the same department.
Help the crisis manager and answer all of his queries.

If type = 1 or type = 2, then the query represents the decision of a crisis manager about merging departments of the first and second types respectively. If type = 3, then your task is to determine whether employees x and y work at the same department. Note that x can be equal to y in the query of any type.

legend.ai: 即使是最成功的公司也可能遭遇危机，此时你不得不做出艰难的决定——进行重组、裁撤并合并部门、解雇员工，以及采取其他令人不快的措施。让我们考虑下面这个公司的模型。

将部门 team(x) 和 team(y) 合并为一个大部门，其中包含 team(x) 和 team(y) 的所有员工；其中 x 和 y（1 ≤ x，y ≤ n）是公司某两名员工的编号。如果 team(x) 与 team(y) 相同，则什么也不会发生。
合并部门 team(x)、team(x + 1)、...、team(y)，其中 x 和 y（1 ≤ x ≤ y ≤ n）是公司某两名员工的编号。
此外，危机管理者有时会询问员工 x 和 y（1 ≤ x，y ≤ n）是否在同一个部门工作。
请帮助危机管理者回答他的所有询问。

接下来的 q 行包含危机管理者的查询。每个查询形如 type x y，其中 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e566753f0340e5050e00bfbdcfeac4c7abd6a7d5.png)。如果 type = 1 或 type = 2，则该查询分别表示危机管理者关于合并第一类部门和第二类部门的决定。如果 type = 3，则你的任务是判断员工 x 和 y 是否在同一个部门工作。注意，在任何类型的查询中，x 都可能等于 y。

legend: Manao is taking part in a quiz. The quiz consists of n consecutive questions. A correct answer gives one point to the player. The game also has a counter of consecutive correct answers. When the player answers a question correctly, the number on this counter increases by 1. If the player answers a question incorrectly, the counter is reset, that is, the number on it reduces to 0. If after an answer the counter reaches the number k, then it is reset, and the player's score is doubled. Note that in this case, first 1 point is added to the player's score, and then the total score is doubled. At the beginning of the game, both the player's score and the counter of consecutive correct answers are set to zero.

Manao remembers that he has answered exactly m questions correctly. But he does not remember the order in which the questions came. He's trying to figure out what his minimum score may be. Help him and compute the remainder of the corresponding number after division by 1000000009 (109 + 9).
input: The single line contains three space-separated integers n, m and k (2 ≤ k ≤ n ≤ 109; 0 ≤ m ≤ n).
output: Print a single integer — the remainder from division of Manao's minimum possible score in the quiz by 1000000009 (109 + 9).
note: Sample 1. Manao answered 3 questions out of 5, and his score would double for each two consecutive correct answers. If Manao had answered the first, third and fifth questions, he would have scored as much as 3 points.
Sample 2. Now Manao answered 4 questions. The minimum possible score is obtained when the only wrong answer is to the question 4.

Also note that you are asked to minimize the score and not the remainder of the score modulo 1000000009. For example, if Manao could obtain either 2000000000 or 2000000020 points, the answer is 2000000000 mod 1000000009, even though 2000000020 mod 1000000009 is a smaller number.

output.ai: 输出一个整数——Manao 在测验中可能获得的最低分除以 1000000009（109 + 9）所得的余数。

note.ai: 样例 1。Manao 在 5 道题中答对了 3 道题，每连续答对两道题，他的分数就会翻倍。如果 Manao 答对的是第 1、3、5 题，他将获得 3 分。
样例 2。现在 Manao 答对了 4 道题。唯一答错的是第 4 题时，他能获得最低分。
另请注意，你需要最小化的是分数，而不是分数对 1000000009 取模后的余数。例如，如果 Manao 可能获得 2000000000 分或 2000000020 分，那么答案是 2000000000 mod 1000000009，尽管 2000000020 mod 1000000009 的结果更小。

legend.ai: Manao 正在参加一场问答比赛。比赛由 n 道连续的问题组成。答对一题会给玩家加 1 分。游戏中还有一个连续答对题数的计数器。当玩家答对一道题时，该计数器上的数字增加 1。如果玩家答错一道题，计数器被重置，即其上的数字变为 0。如果某次作答后计数器达到 k，则它被重置，并且玩家的得分翻倍。注意，在这种情况下，首先给玩家的得分加 1 分，然后将总分翻倍。游戏开始时，玩家的得分和连续答对题数的计数器都置为 0。
Manao 记得他恰好答对了 m 道题。但他不记得这些题目的出现顺序。他想知道自己的最低得分可能是多少。请帮助他，并计算相应数字除以 1000000009（10^9 + 9）后的余数。

legend: Ivan is playing a strange game.

He has a matrix a with n rows and m columns. Each element of the matrix is equal to either 0 or 1. Rows and columns are 1-indexed. Ivan can replace any number of ones in this matrix with zeroes. After that, his score in the game will be calculated as follows:
Initially Ivan's score is 0;
In each column, Ivan will find the topmost 1 (that is, if the current column is j, then he will find minimum i such that ai, j = 1). If there are no 1's in the column, this column is skipped;
Ivan will look at the next min(k, n - i + 1) elements in this column (starting from the element he found) and count the number of 1's among these elements. This number will be added to his score.

Of course, Ivan wants to maximize his score in this strange game. Also he doesn't want to change many elements, so he will replace the minimum possible number of ones with zeroes. Help him to determine the maximum possible score he can get and the minimum possible number of replacements required to achieve that score.
input: The first line contains three integer numbers n, m and k (1 ≤ k ≤ n ≤ 100, 1 ≤ m ≤ 100).

note: In the first example Ivan will replace the element a1, 2.

input.ai: 第一行包含三个整数 n、m 和 k（1 ≤ k ≤ n ≤ 100，1 ≤ m ≤ 100）。

legend: A non-empty string s is called binary, if it consists only of characters "0" and "1". Let's number the characters of binary string s from 1 to the string's length and let's denote the i-th character in string s as si.
Binary string s with length n is periodical, if there is an integer 1 ≤ k < n such that:
k is a divisor of number n
for all 1 ≤ i ≤ n - k, the following condition fulfills: si = si + k
For example, binary strings "101010" and "11" are periodical and "10" and "10010" are not.
A positive integer x is periodical, if its binary representation (without leading zeroes) is a periodic string.
Your task is to calculate, how many periodic numbers are in the interval from l to r (both ends are included).
input: The single input line contains two integers l and r (1 ≤ l ≤ r ≤ 1018). The numbers are separated by a space.
Please, do not use the %lld specifier to read or write 64-bit integers in С++. It is preferred to use the cin, cout streams or the %I64d specifier.
output: Print a single integer, showing how many periodic numbers are in the interval from l to r (both ends are included).
note: In the first sample periodic numbers are 3, 7 and 10.
In the second sample periodic numbers are 31 and 36.

legend.ai: 如果一个非空字符串 s 仅由字符“0”和“1”组成，则称其为 01 串。将 01 串 s 中的字符从 1 开始编号，直到字符串长度，并将 s 中第 i 个字符记作 s_i。
长度为 n 的二进制字符串 s 是周期性的，当且仅当存在一个整数 1 ≤ k < n，使得：
k 是 n 的一个约数
对于所有 1 ≤ i ≤ n - k，以下条件均成立：s_i = s_{i+k}
例如，二进制字符串“101010”和“11”是周期性的，而“10”和“10010”不是。
如果正整数 x 的二进制表示（不含前导零）是一个周期性字符串，则称 x 是周期性的。
你的任务是计算区间 l 到 r（包括两个端点）内有多少个周期性数。

input.ai: 单行输入包含两个整数 l 和 r（1 ≤ l ≤ r ≤ 10^18）。这两个数之间用空格分隔。
请不要在 C++ 中使用 %lld 格式说明符读写 64 位整数。建议使用 cin、cout 流或 %I64d 格式说明符。

output.ai: 输出一个整数，表示区间 l 到 r 中（包括两端）有多少个周期数。

note.ai: 第一个样例中的周期数是 3、7 和 10。
第二个样例中的周期数是 31 和 36。

legend: Ivan is a novice painter. He has n$$$n$$$ dyes of different colors. He also knows exactly m$$$m$$$ pairs of colors which harmonize with each other.

Ivan also enjoy playing chess. He has 5000$$$5000$$$ rooks. He wants to take k$$$k$$$ rooks, paint each of them in one of n$$$n$$$ colors and then place this k$$$k$$$ rooks on a chessboard of size 109×109$$$10^{9} \times 10^{9}$$$.

Let's call the set of rooks on the board connected if from any rook we can get to any other rook in this set moving only through cells with rooks from this set. Assume that rooks can jump over other rooks, in other words a rook can go to any cell which shares vertical and to any cell which shares horizontal.
Ivan wants his arrangement of rooks to have following properties:
For any color there is a rook of this color on a board;
For any color the set of rooks of this color is connected;
For any two different colors a$$$a$$$ b$$$b$$$ union of set of rooks of color a$$$a$$$ and set of rooks of color b$$$b$$$ is connected if and only if this two colors harmonize with each other.
Please help Ivan find such an arrangement.

In the first line of block print one number ai$$$a_{i}$$$ (1≤ai≤5000$$$1 \le a_{i} \le 5000$$$) — number of rooks of color i$$$i$$$. In each of next ai$$$a_{i}$$$ lines print two integers x$$$x$$$ and y$$$y$$$ (1≤x,y≤109$$$1 \le x, \,\, y \le 10^{9}$$$) — coordinates of the next rook.

legend: One Big Software Company has n employees numbered from 1 to n. The director is assigned number 1. Every employee of the company except the director has exactly one immediate superior. The director, of course, doesn't have a superior.

We will call person a a subordinates of another person b, if either b is an immediate supervisor of a, or the immediate supervisor of a is a subordinate to person b. In particular, subordinates of the head are all other employees of the company.

To solve achieve an Important Goal we need to form a workgroup. Every person has some efficiency, expressed by a positive integer ai, where i is the person's number. The efficiency of the workgroup is defined as the total efficiency of all the people included in it.

The employees of the big software company are obsessed with modern ways of work process organization. Today pair programming is at the peak of popularity, so the workgroup should be formed with the following condition. Each person entering the workgroup should be able to sort all of his subordinates who are also in the workgroup into pairs. In other words, for each of the members of the workgroup the number of his subordinates within the workgroup should be even.
Your task is to determine the maximum possible efficiency of the workgroup formed at observing the given condition. Any person including the director of company can enter the workgroup.
input: The first line contains integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·105) — the number of workers of the Big Software Company.

Then n lines follow, describing the company employees. The i-th line contains two integers pi, ai (1 ≤ ai ≤ 105) — the number of the person who is the i-th employee's immediate superior and i-th employee's efficiency. For the director p1 =  - 1, for all other people the condition 1 ≤ pi < i is fulfilled.
output: Print a single integer — the maximum possible efficiency of the workgroup.
note: In the sample test the most effective way is to make a workgroup from employees number 1, 2, 4, 5, 6.

legend.ai: 一家大型软件公司有 n 名员工，编号为 1 到 n。主管的编号为 1。除主管外，公司的每名员工都恰好有一个直接上级。当然，主管没有上级。
如果 b 是 a 的直接上级，或者 a 的直接上级是 b 的下属，则称 a 是 b 的下属。特别地，主管的下属是公司所有其他员工。
为了实现一个重要目标，我们需要组建一个工作组。每个人都有一定的效率，用一个正整数 ai 表示，其中 i 是员工的编号。工作组的效率定义为所有成员效率之和。
这家大型软件公司的员工痴迷于现代的工作流程组织方式。如今结对编程正处于流行巅峰，因此工作组需要满足以下条件：进入工作组的每个人都能将他所有也在工作组中的下属分成若干对。换言之，对于工作组的每个成员，他在工作组内的下属数量应为偶数。
你的任务是在满足给定条件的情况下，确定所组成工作组的最大可能效率。包括公司董事在内的任何人都可以加入工作组。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 2·10^5）——大软件公司的员工数量。
接下来 n 行描述公司的员工。第 i 行包含两个整数 p_i、a_i（1 ≤ a_i ≤ 10^5）——分别表示第 i 名员工的直属上司编号和第 i 名员工的效率。对于董事，p_1＝-1；对于其他所有人，均满足 1 ≤ p_i < i。

output.ai: 输出一个整数——工作组的最大可能效率。

note.ai: 在样例中，最有效的方法是由编号为 1、2、4、5、6 的员工组成一个工作组。

legend: Amr bought a new video game "Guess Your Way Out!". The goal of the game is to find an exit from the maze that looks like a perfect binary tree of height h. The player is initially standing at the root of the tree and the exit from the tree is located at some leaf node.
Let's index all the leaf nodes from the left to the right from 1 to 2h. The exit is located at some node n where 1 ≤ n ≤ 2h, the player doesn't know where the exit is so he has to guess his way out!

Amr follows simple algorithm to choose the path. Let's consider infinite command string "LRLRLRLRL..." (consisting of alternating characters 'L' and 'R'). Amr sequentially executes the characters of the string using following rules:
Character 'L' means "go to the left child of the current node";
Character 'R' means "go to the right child of the current node";
If the destination node is already visited, Amr skips current command, otherwise he moves to the destination node;
If Amr skipped two consecutive commands, he goes back to the parent of the current node before executing next command;
If he reached a leaf node that is not the exit, he returns to the parent of the current node;
If he reaches an exit, the game is finished.
Now Amr wonders, if he follows this algorithm, how many nodes he is going to visit before reaching the exit?
input: Input consists of two integers h, n (1 ≤ h ≤ 50, 1 ≤ n ≤ 2h).
output: Output a single integer representing the number of nodes (excluding the exit node) Amr is going to visit before reaching the exit by following this algorithm.
note: A perfect binary tree of height h is a binary tree consisting of h + 1 levels. Level 0 consists of a single node called root, level h consists of 2h nodes called leaves. Each node that is not a leaf has exactly two children, left and right one.
Following picture illustrates the sample test number 3. Nodes are labeled according to the order of visit.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/98ce18ee21285de525052fcfb3749bc60465e96d.png)

note.ai: 高度为 h 的完美二叉树由 h+1 层组成。第 0 层包含一个称为根的节点，第 h 层包含 2h 个称为叶子的节点。每个不是叶子的节点都恰好有两个子节点：左子节点和右子节点。
下图展示了样例测试 3。节点按照访问顺序标记。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/98ce18ee21285de525052fcfb3749bc60465e96d.png)

legend.ai: Amr 买了一款新电子游戏《Guess Your Way Out!》。游戏目标是在一个形如高度为 h 的满二叉树的迷宫中找到出口。玩家初始站在树的根节点，树的出口位于某个叶节点。
我们将所有叶节点从左到右编号为 1 到 2^h。出口位于编号为 n 的某个节点，其中 1 ≤ n ≤ 2^h。玩家不知道出口的位置，因此他必须猜出一条逃生路线！
Amr 遵循一个简单的算法来选择路径。考虑无限的指令字符串“LRLRLRLRL...”（由交替出现的字符“L”和“R”组成）。Amr 按顺序执行字符串中的字符，规则如下：
字符“L”表示“前往当前节点的左子节点”；
字符“R”表示“前往当前节点的右子节点”；
如果目标节点已经访问过，Amr 就跳过当前指令；否则，他移动到目标节点；
如果 Amr 连续跳过了两条命令，那么他会在执行下一条命令前返回当前节点的父节点；
如果他到达了一个不是出口的叶节点，那么他会返回当前节点的父节点；
如果他到达了出口，游戏就结束。
现在 Amr 想知道，如果他遵循这一算法，那么在到达出口之前将访问多少个节点？

input.ai: 输入包含两个整数 h、n（1 ≤ h ≤ 50，1 ≤ n ≤ 2h）。

output.ai: 输出一个整数，表示 Amr 遵循这一算法到达出口之前将访问的节点数（不包括出口节点）。

problems.hint: Transform the string into an array. Its prefix sum is almost consecutive.

legend: Having read half of the book called "Storm and Calm" on the IT lesson, Innocentius was absolutely determined to finish the book on the maths lessons. All was fine until the math teacher Ms. Watkins saw Innocentius reading fiction books instead of solving equations of the fifth degree. As during the last maths class Innocentius suggested the algorithm of solving equations of the fifth degree in the general case, Ms. Watkins had no other choice but to give him a new task.

The teacher asked to write consecutively (without spaces) all words from the "Storm and Calm" in one long string s. She thought that a string is good if the number of vowels in the string is no more than twice more than the number of consonants. That is, the string with v vowels and c consonants is good if and only if v ≤ 2c.
The task Innocentius had to solve turned out to be rather simple: he should find the number of the longest good substrings of the string s.
input: The only input line contains a non-empty string s consisting of no more than 2·105 uppercase and lowercase Latin letters. We shall regard letters "a", "e", "i", "o", "u" and their uppercase variants as vowels.
output: Print on a single line two numbers without a space: the maximum length of a good substring and the number of good substrings with this length. If no good substring exists, print "No solution" without the quotes.
Two substrings are considered different if their positions of occurrence are different. So if some string occurs more than once, then it should be counted more than once.
note: In the first sample there is only one longest good substring: "Abo" itself. The other good substrings are "b", "Ab", "bo", but these substrings have shorter length.
In the second sample there is only one longest good substring: "EIS". The other good substrings are: "S", "IS".

legend.ai: 在 IT 课上读了《Storm and Calm》这本书的一半后，Innocentius 下定决心要在数学课上把它读完。一切都很顺利，直到数学老师 Watkins 女士看到 Innocentius 没有在解五次方程，而是在读小说。由于在上一次数学课上，Innocentius 提出了在一般情况下求解五次方程的算法，Watkins 女士别无选择，只能给他一个新任务。
老师要求把《Storm and Calm》中的所有单词连续地（不加空格）写成一个长字符串 s。她认为，如果一个字符串中元音字母的数量不超过辅音字母数量的两倍，那么这个字符串就是好的。也就是说，一个有 v 个元音字母和 c 个辅音字母的字符串是好的，当且仅当 v ≤ 2c。
Innocentius 需要完成的任务其实相当简单：他应当求出字符串 s 中最长好子串的数量。

input.ai: 唯一的输入行包含一个非空字符串 s，其长度不超过 2·10^5，由大小写拉丁字母组成。我们将字母 “a”、“e”、“i”、“o”、“u” 及其大写形式视为元音。

output.ai: 在单独一行中输出两个数，中间不留空格：好子串的最大长度，以及具有该长度的好子串数量。如果不存在好子串，则输出 “No solution”（不含引号）。
如果两个子串的出现位置不同，则认为它们不同。因此，如果某个串出现多次，则应被计数多次。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，只有一个最长好子串：“Abo” 本身。其他好子串为 “b”、“Ab”、“bo”，但这些子串的长度较短。
在第二个样例中，只有一个最长好子串：“EIS”。其他好子串为 “S”、“IS”。

legend: A widely known among some people Belarusian sport programmer Yura possesses lots of information about cars. That is why he has been invited to participate in a game show called "Guess That Car!".

The game show takes place on a giant parking lot, which is 4n meters long from north to south and 4m meters wide from west to east. The lot has n + 1 dividing lines drawn from west to east and m + 1 dividing lines drawn from north to south, which divide the parking lot into n·m 4 by 4 meter squares. There is a car parked strictly inside each square. The dividing lines are numbered from 0 to n from north to south and from 0 to m from west to east. Each square has coordinates (i, j) so that the square in the north-west corner has coordinates (1, 1) and the square in the south-east corner has coordinates (n, m). See the picture in the notes for clarifications.

Before the game show the organizers offer Yura to occupy any of the (n + 1)·(m + 1) intersection points of the dividing lines. After that he can start guessing the cars. After Yura chooses a point, he will be prohibited to move along the parking lot before the end of the game show. As Yura is a car expert, he will always guess all cars he is offered, it's just a matter of time. Yura knows that to guess each car he needs to spend time equal to the square of the euclidean distance between his point and the center of the square with this car, multiplied by some coefficient characterizing the machine's "rarity" (the rarer the car is, the harder it is to guess it). More formally, guessing a car with "rarity" c placed in a square whose center is at distance d from Yura takes c·d2 seconds. The time Yura spends on turning his head can be neglected.
It just so happened that Yura knows the "rarity" of each car on the parking lot in advance. Help him choose his point so that the total time of guessing all cars is the smallest possible.
input: The first line contains two integers n and m (1 ≤ n, m ≤ 1000) — the sizes of the parking lot. Each of the next n lines contains m integers: the j-th number in the i-th line describes the "rarity" cij (0 ≤ cij ≤ 100000) of the car that is located in the square with coordinates (i, j).
output: In the first line print the minimum total time Yura needs to guess all offered cars. In the second line print two numbers li and lj (0 ≤ li ≤ n, 0 ≤ lj ≤ m) — the numbers of dividing lines that form a junction that Yura should choose to stand on at the beginning of the game show. If there are multiple optimal starting points, print the point with smaller li. If there are still multiple such points, print the point with smaller lj.
Please do not use the %lld specifier to read or write 64-bit integers in С++. It is preferred to use the cin, cout streams or the %I64d specifier.
note: In the first test case the total time of guessing all cars is equal to 3·8 + 3·8 + 4·8 + 9·8 + 5·40 + 1·40 = 392.
The coordinate system of the field:
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/137d495792e419abf638b48dd0c1e5d79fc5b4ca.png)

output.ai: 第一行输出 Yura 猜出所有提供的汽车所需的最短总时间。第二行输出两个数 li 和 lj（0 ≤ li ≤ n，0 ≤ lj ≤ m）——构成 Yura 应在游戏节目开始时选择站立的交点的两条分界线的编号。如果有多个最优起点，输出 li 较小的点。如果仍有多个这样的点，输出 lj 较小的点。
请不要在 C++ 中使用 %lld 格式说明符来读写 64 位整数。建议使用 cin、cout 流或 %I64d 格式说明符。

note.ai: 在第一个测试用例中，猜出所有汽车的总时间等于 3·8 + 3·8 + 4·8 + 9·8 + 5·40 + 1·40 = 392。

legend.ai: 在某些人群中广为人知的白俄罗斯竞赛程序员 Yura 掌握着大量关于汽车的信息。因此，他受邀参加名为“猜猜这辆车！”的游戏节目。

游戏节目在一个巨大的停车场中举行，该停车场从北到南长 4n 米，从西到东宽 4m 米。停车场中有 n + 1 条从西向东绘制的分界线，以及 m + 1 条从北向南绘制的分界线，它们将停车场划分为 n·m 个 4×4 米的方格。每个方格内（严格不在边界上）都停放着一辆汽车。分界线从北到南编号为 0 至 n，从西到东编号为 0 至 m。每个方格都有坐标 (i, j)，其中西北角的方格坐标为 (1, 1)，东南角的方格坐标为 (n, m)。具体说明请参见题目注释中的图片。

在游戏节目开始前，主办方允许 Yura 占据分界线交点中的任意一个，即 (n + 1)·(m + 1) 个交点中的任意一个。之后，他就可以开始猜车了。Yura 选定一个点后，在游戏节目结束前都不允许在停车场内移动。由于 Yura 是汽车专家，他总能猜出节目提供的所有汽车，只是需要一定的时间。Yura 知道，猜出每辆汽车所需的时间等于他所在点与该汽车所在方格中心之间的欧几里得距离的平方，再乘以一个表示汽车“稀有度”的系数（汽车越稀有，就越难猜出）。更正式地说，对于一辆“稀有度”为 c、停放在中心到 Yura 的距离为 d 的方格中的汽车，猜出它所需的时间为 c·d² 秒。Yura 转头所花费的时间可以忽略不计。
碰巧，Yura 事先知道停车场中每辆汽车的“稀有度”。请帮助他选择一个点，使猜出所有汽车所需的总时间尽可能短。

input.ai: 第一行包含两个整数 n 和 m（1 ≤ n, m ≤ 1000），表示停车场的大小。接下来的 n 行中，每行包含 m 个整数：第 i 行中的第 j 个数描述了坐标为 (i, j) 的方格中汽车的“稀有度” cij（0 ≤ cij ≤ 100000）。

legend: The semester is already ending, so Danil made an effort and decided to visit a lesson on harmony analysis to know how does the professor look like, at least. Danil was very bored on this lesson until the teacher gave the group a simple task: find 4 vectors in 4-dimensional space, such that every coordinate of every vector is 1 or  - 1 and any two vectors are orthogonal. Just as a reminder, two vectors in n-dimensional space are considered to be orthogonal if and only if their scalar product is equal to zero, that is:
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/9209cd1e676116390c8a0e27584fa6eda10b80e3.png)

Danil quickly managed to come up with the solution for this problem and the teacher noticed that the problem can be solved in a more general case for 2k vectors in 2k-dimensinoal space. When Danil came home, he quickly came up with the solution for this problem. Can you cope with it?
input: The only line of the input contains a single integer k (0 ≤ k ≤ 9).
output: Print 2k lines consisting of 2k characters each. The j-th character of the i-th line must be equal to ' * ' if the j-th coordinate of the i-th vector is equal to  - 1, and must be equal to ' + ' if it's equal to  + 1. It's guaranteed that the answer always exists.
If there are many correct answers, print any.

legend.ai: 学期已经快结束了，所以 Danil 努力了一把，决定去上一节和声分析课，至少看看教授长什么样。Danil 在这节课上一直觉得很无聊，直到老师给全班布置了一道简单的题：在四维空间中找出 4 个向量，使得每个向量的每个坐标都是 1 或 −1，并且任意两个向量都正交。提醒一下，n 维空间中的两个向量正交，当且仅当它们的点积等于零，也就是说：
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/9209cd1e676116390c8a0e27584fa6eda10b80e3.png)
Danil 很快就想出了这个问题的解法，老师也注意到，这个问题可以推广到 2k 个向量位于 2k 维空间中的更一般情形。Danil 回家后，很快也想出了这个问题的解法。你能解决它吗？

input.ai: 输入的唯一一行包含一个整数 k（0 ≤ k ≤ 9）。

output.ai: 输出 2k 行，每行由 2k 个字符组成。第 i 行的第 j 个字符必须为 '*'，当第 i 个向量的第 j 个坐标等于 −1 时；若该坐标等于 +1，则必须为 '+'。保证答案总是存在。

problems.hint: How can you decide the outcome of a Nim game? How does this status change?

legend: Dexterina and Womandark have been arch-rivals since they’ve known each other. Since both are super-intelligent teenage girls, they’ve always been trying to solve their disputes in a peaceful and nonviolent way. After god knows how many different challenges they’ve given to one another, their score is equal and they’re both desperately trying to best the other in various games of wits. This time, Dexterina challenged Womandark to a game of Nim.

Nim is a two-player game in which players take turns removing objects from distinct heaps. On each turn, a player must remove at least one object, and may remove any number of objects from a single heap. The player who can't make a turn loses. By their agreement, the sizes of piles are selected randomly from the range [0, x]. Each pile's size is taken independently from the same probability distribution that is known before the start of the game.

Womandark is coming up with a brand new and evil idea on how to thwart Dexterina’s plans, so she hasn’t got much spare time. She, however, offered you some tips on looking fabulous in exchange for helping her win in Nim. Your task is to tell her what is the probability that the first player to play wins, given the rules as above.
input: The first line of the input contains two integers n (1 ≤ n ≤ 109) and x (1 ≤ x ≤ 100) — the number of heaps and the maximum number of objects in a heap, respectively. The second line contains x + 1 real numbers, given with up to 6 decimal places each: P(0), P(1), ... , P(X). Here, P(i) is the probability of a heap having exactly i objects in start of a game. It's guaranteed that the sum of all P(i) is equal to 1.
output: Output a single real number, the probability that the first player wins. The answer will be judged as correct if it differs from the correct answer by at most 10 - 6.

legend.ai: Dexterina 和 Womandark 自从相识以来就是势均力敌的宿敌。由于两人都是超级聪明的少女，她们一直试图以和平且非暴力的方式解决争端。在她们互相发起了天知道多少种不同挑战之后，双方比分相同，而她们都在各种智力游戏中拼命想胜过对方。这一次，Dexterina 向 Womandark 挑战进行一局 Nim 游戏。
Nim 是一款双人游戏，玩家轮流从不同的堆中移除物品。每回合，玩家必须至少移除一个物品，并且可以从单个堆中移除任意数量的物品。无法行动的玩家输掉游戏。根据双方的约定，堆的大小从区间 [0, x] 中随机选取。每个堆的大小都独立地服从相同的概率分布，该分布在游戏开始前已知。
Womandark 正在构思一个全新且邪恶的想法，打算阻挠 Dexterina 的计划，因此没有太多空闲时间。不过，为了换取你帮助她在 Nim 中获胜，她向你提供了一些让自己看起来光彩照人的建议。你的任务是告诉她，在上述规则下，先手获胜的概率是多少。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含两个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 109）和 x（1 ≤ x ≤ 100），分别表示堆的数量和一堆中物品数量的最大值。第二行包含 x + 1 个实数，每个数最多有 6 位小数：P(0)、P(1)、...、P(X)。其中，P(i) 表示游戏开始时一个堆恰好有 i 个物品的概率。保证所有 P(i) 之和等于 1。

output.ai: 输出一个实数，表示先手获胜的概率。如果答案与正确答案的误差不超过 10⁻⁶，则会被判为正确。

problems.hint: "Differ by at most one". Note that the points chosen by an interval are consecutive.

legend: Iahub isn't well prepared on geometry problems, but he heard that this year there will be a lot of geometry problems on the IOI selection camp. Scared, Iahub locked himself in the basement and started thinking of new problems of this kind. One of them is the following.

Iahub wants to draw n distinct points and m segments on the OX axis. He can draw each point with either red or blue. The drawing is good if and only if the following requirement is met: for each segment [li, ri] consider all the red points belong to it (ri points), and all the blue points belong to it (bi points); each segment i should satisfy the inequality |ri - bi| ≤ 1.
Iahub thinks that point x belongs to segment [l, r], if inequality l ≤ x ≤ r holds.
Iahub gives to you all coordinates of points and segments. Please, help him to find any good drawing.
input: The first line of input contains two integers: n (1 ≤ n ≤ 100) and m (1 ≤ m ≤ 100). The next line contains n space-separated integers x1, x2, ..., xn (0 ≤ xi ≤ 100) — the coordinates of the points. The following m lines contain the descriptions of the m segments. Each line contains two integers li and ri (0 ≤ li ≤ ri ≤ 100) — the borders of the i-th segment.
It's guaranteed that all the points are distinct.
output: If there is no good drawing for a given test, output a single integer -1. Otherwise output n integers, each integer must be 0 or 1. The i-th number denotes the color of the i-th point (0 is red, and 1 is blue).
If there are multiple good drawings you can output any of them.

input.ai: 输入第一行包含两个整数：n（1 ≤ n ≤ 100）和 m（1 ≤ m ≤ 100）。下一行包含 n 个空格分隔的整数 x1, x2, ..., xn（0 ≤ xi ≤ 100）——这些点的坐标。接下来的 m 行包含 m 条线段的描述。每行包含两个整数 li 和 ri（0 ≤ li ≤ ri ≤ 100）——第 i 条线段的边界。
保证所有点互不相同。

output.ai: 如果某个测试数据不存在合法的画法，则输出单个整数 -1。否则输出 n 个整数，每个整数必须是 0 或 1。第 i 个数表示第 i 个点的颜色（0 表示红色，1 表示蓝色）。
如果存在多种合法的画法，你可以输出其中任意一种。

legend.ai: Iahub 不擅长几何题，但他听说今年 IOI 选拔集训营会有很多几何题。Iahub 很害怕，于是把自己锁在地下室里，开始思考这类新题目。其中一道题如下。
Iahub 想在 OX 轴上画 n 个互不相同的点和 m 条线段。每个点可以涂成红色或蓝色。当且仅当满足以下条件时，这幅图才是好的：对于每条线段 [l_i, r_i]，设其中红点的数量为 r_i，蓝点的数量为 b_i；每条线段 i 都必须满足不等式 |r_i - b_i| ≤ 1。
如果不等式 l ≤ x ≤ r 成立，Iahub 就认为点 x 属于线段 [l, r]。
Iahub 给出了所有点和线段的坐标。请帮他找到任意一种好的画法。

legend: You are given a node of the tree with index 1 and with weight 0. Let cnt be the number of nodes in the tree at any instant (initially, cnt is set to 1). Support Q queries of following two types:
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/3c53d1886cd6252f58663221e2b5768b1981acff.png) Add a new node (index cnt + 1) with weight W and add edge between node R and this node.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/3ca7b8a948d44b13bf24c54f54602fe3dbc94f6d.png) Output the maximum length of sequence of nodes which   starts with R.
Every node in the sequence is an ancestor of its predecessor.
Sum of weight of nodes in sequence does not exceed X.
For some nodes i, j that are consecutive in the sequence if i is an ancestor of j then w[i] ≥ w[j] and there should not exist a node k on simple path from i to j such that w[k] ≥ w[j]
The tree is rooted at node 1 at any instant.
Note that the queries are given in a modified way.
input: First line containing the number of queries Q (1 ≤ Q ≤ 400000).
Let last be the answer for previous query of type 2 (initially last equals 0).
Each of the next Q lines contains a query of following form:

1 p q (1 ≤ p, q ≤ 1018): This is query of first type where ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/23caaf5370a4d35b830e404cf70088925e1a9749.png) and ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/92f7f390372274897cb1fbe68b8e5fcbbbd9710c.png). It is guaranteed that 1 ≤ R ≤ cnt and 0 ≤ W ≤ 109.

2 p q (1 ≤ p, q ≤ 1018): This is query of second type where ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/23caaf5370a4d35b830e404cf70088925e1a9749.png) and ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/07ae7521dbc6857c85e4d6cc6df38a9db5a96d28.png). It is guaranteed that 1 ≤ R ≤ cnt and 0 ≤ X ≤ 1015.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/5f9a3eda18f3a09bbf898be93ace22143cf6584a.png) denotes bitwise XOR of a and b.
It is guaranteed that at least one query of type 2 exists.
output: Output the answer to each query of second type in separate line.
note: In the first example,
last = 0
- Query 1: 1 1 1, Node 2 with weight 1 is added to node 1.
- Query 2: 2 2 0, No sequence of nodes starting at 2 has weight less than or equal to 0. last = 0
- Query 3: 2 2 1, Answer is 1 as sequence will be {2}. last = 1
- Query 4: 1 2 1, Node 3 with weight 1 is added to node 2.
- Query 5: 2 3 1, Answer is 1 as sequence will be {3}. Node 2 cannot be added as sum of weights cannot be greater than 1. last = 1
- Query 6: 2 3 3, Answer is 2 as sequence will be {3, 2}. last = 2

input.ai: 第一行包含查询数量 Q (1 ≤ Q ≤ 400000)。
设 last 为上一次类型 2 查询的答案（初始时 last 等于 0）。
接下来的 Q 行每行包含一个如下形式的查询：

1 p q (1 ≤ p, q ≤ 10^18)：这是第一种类型的查询，其中 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/23caaf5370a4d35b830e404cf70088925e1a9749.png) 和 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/92f7f390372274897cb1fbe68b8e5fcbbbd9710c.png)。保证 1 ≤ R ≤ cnt 且 0 ≤ W ≤ 10^9。

2 p q (1 ≤ p, q ≤ 10^18)：这是第二种类型的查询，其中 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/23caaf5370a4d35b830e404cf70088925e1a9749.png) 和 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/07ae7521dbc6857c85e4d6cc6df38a9db5a96d28.png)。保证 1 ≤ R ≤ cnt 且 0 ≤ X ≤ 10^15。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/5f9a3eda18f3a09bbf898be93ace22143cf6584a.png) 表示 a 和 b 的按位异或。
保证至少存在一个类型 2 的查询。

output.ai: 将每个类型 2 查询的答案分别输出在单独一行。

last = 0
- 查询 1：1 1 1，将权值为 1 的节点 2 添加到节点 1。
- 查询 2：2 2 0，不存在从节点 2 开始且权值小于或等于 0 的节点序列。last = 0
- 查询 3：2 2 1，答案为 1，因为序列将为 {2}。last = 1

legend.ai: 给定树中编号为 1 且权值为 0 的一个节点。设 cnt 为任意时刻树中的节点数（初始时 cnt 为 1）。支持 Q 次以下两种类型的查询：
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/3c53d1886cd6252f58663221e2b5768b1981acff.png) 添加一个权值为 W 的新节点(编号为 cnt + 1)，并在节点 R 与该节点之间添加一条边。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/3ca7b8a948d44b13bf24c54f54602fe3dbc94f6d.png) 输出以 R 开头的节点序列的最大长度。

对于序列中相邻的节点 i、j，若 i 是 j 的祖先，则 w[i] ≥ w[j]，并且从 i 到 j 的简单路径上不存在满足 w[k] ≥ w[j] 的节点 k。
在任意时刻，树都以节点 1 为根。
注意，查询以修改后的方式给出。

legend: Valera has array a, consisting of n integers a0, a1, ..., an - 1, and function f(x), taking an integer from 0 to 2n - 1 as its single argument. Value f(x) is calculated by formula ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/eba4794e67d3b5ce144adcffa5217705a92db70f.png), where value bit(i) equals one if the binary representation of number x contains a 1 on the i-th position, and zero otherwise.
For example, if n = 4 and x = 11 (11 = 20 + 21 + 23), then f(x) = a0 + a1 + a3.
Help Valera find the maximum of function f(x) among all x, for which an inequality holds: 0 ≤ x ≤ m.
input: The first line contains integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 105) — the number of array elements. The next line contains n space-separated integers a0, a1, ..., an - 1 (0 ≤ ai ≤ 104) — elements of array a.

The third line contains a sequence of digits zero and one without spaces s0s1... sn - 1 — the binary representation of number m. Number m equals ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/77407fd65d8594ac862f8de69093d5a75e54d3c5.png).

note: In the first test case m = 20 = 1, f(0) = 0, f(1) = a0 = 3.
In the second sample m = 20 + 21 + 23 = 11, the maximum value of function equals f(5) = a0 + a2 = 17 + 10 = 27.

legend.ai: Valera 有一个包含 n 个整数 a0, a1, ..., an-1 的数组 a，以及一个函数 f(x)，它接受从 0 到 2^n - 1 的整数作为唯一参数。f(x) 的值由公式 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/eba4794e67d3b5ce144adcffa5217705a92db70f.png) 计算，其中当数字 x 的二进制表示在第 i 位为 1 时，bit(i) 等于 1，否则等于 0。
帮助 Valera 在满足不等式 0 ≤ x ≤ m 的所有 x 中找出函数 f(x) 的最大值。

第三行包含一个由数字 0 和 1 组成的、无空格的序列 s0s1...sn-1——数字 m 的二进制表示。数字 m 等于 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/77407fd65d8594ac862f8de69093d5a75e54d3c5.png)。

output.ai: 输出一个整数——对于满足 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/82bfd78b9ec5ce07767875a86696eb7b2eb3031c.png) 的 x，函数 f(x) 的最大值。

legend: Anton came to a chocolate factory. There he found a working conveyor and decided to run on it from the beginning to the end.

The conveyor is a looped belt with a total length of 2l meters, of which l meters are located on the surface and are arranged in a straight line. The part of the belt which turns at any moment (the part which emerges from under the floor to the surface and returns from the surface under the floor) is assumed to be negligibly short.

The belt is moving uniformly at speed v1 meters per second. Anton will be moving on it in the same direction at the constant speed of v2 meters per second, so his speed relatively to the floor will be v1 + v2 meters per second. Anton will neither stop nor change the speed or the direction of movement.

Here and there there are chocolates stuck to the belt (n chocolates). They move together with the belt, and do not come off it. Anton is keen on the chocolates, but he is more keen to move forward. So he will pick up all the chocolates he will pass by, but nothing more. If a chocolate is at the beginning of the belt at the moment when Anton starts running, he will take it, and if a chocolate is at the end of the belt at the moment when Anton comes off the belt, he will leave it.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7fcbe21ac233256be6e14c9e08608208248d66ce.png)

You are given the positions of the chocolates relative to the initial start position of the belt 0 ≤ a1 < a2 < ... < an < 2l. The positions on the belt from 0 to l correspond to the top, and from l to 2l — to the the bottom half of the belt (see example). All coordinates are given in meters.

Anton begins to run along the belt at a random moment of time. This means that all possible positions of the belt at the moment he starts running are equiprobable. For each i from 0 to n calculate the probability that Anton will pick up exactly i chocolates.
input: The first line contains space-separated integers n, l, v1 and v2 (1 ≤ n ≤ 105, 1 ≤ l, v1, v2 ≤ 109) — the number of the chocolates, the length of the conveyor's visible part, the conveyor's speed and Anton's speed.
The second line contains a sequence of space-separated integers a1, a2, ..., an (0 ≤ a1 < a2 < ... < an < 2l) — the coordinates of the chocolates.
output: Print n + 1 numbers (one per line): the probabilities that Anton picks up exactly i chocolates, for each i from 0 (the first line) to n (the last line). The answer will be considered correct if each number will have absolute or relative error of at most than 10 - 9.
note: In the first sample test Anton can pick up a chocolate if by the moment he starts running its coordinate is less than 0.5; but if by the moment the boy starts running the chocolate's coordinate is greater than or equal to 0.5, then Anton won't be able to pick it up. As all positions of the belt are equiprobable, the probability of picking up the chocolate equals ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/55d1d7955c1e59f407eb6baa7601582a54eeac4f.png), and the probability of not picking it up equals ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/0e79ad74cc0314b318cc094369c845c55b37c9ef.png).

legend.ai: Anton 来到一家巧克力工厂。他在那里发现一条正在运转的传送带，并决定从起点跑到终点。
传送带是一条总长为 2l 米的环形带，其中 l 米位于地面上，且排列成一条直线。传送带在任意时刻转弯的部分（即从地板下方升到地面、再从地面返回地板下方的部分）可视为长度极短。
传送带以 v1 米/秒的速度匀速运动。Anton 将以 v2 米/秒的恒定速度沿同一方向在传送带上移动，因此他相对于地面的速度是 v1 + v2 米/秒。Anton 既不会停下来，也不会改变速度或移动方向。
传送带上零散地粘着一些巧克力（共 n 块）。它们会随传送带一起移动，不会从传送带上掉下来。Anton 很喜欢巧克力，但他更想继续向前移动。因此，他会拿走所有经过的巧克力，但不会多拿。如果 Anton 开始跑动时，某块巧克力正好位于传送带的起点，他会拿走它；如果 Anton 离开传送带时，某块巧克力正好位于传送带的末端，他就会留下它。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7fcbe21ac233256be6e14c9e08608208248d66ce.png)
给定巧克力相对于传送带初始起点的位置 0 ≤ a1 < a2 < ... < an < 2l。传送带上从 0 到 l 的位置对应上半部分，从 l 到 2l 的位置对应下半部分（见样例）。所有坐标均以米为单位。
Anton 会在随机时刻开始沿传送带跑动。这意味着，他开始跑动时传送带的所有可能位置出现的概率均相等。对于每个 i（0 到 n），计算 Anton 恰好拿走 i 块巧克力的概率。

input.ai: 第一行包含以空格分隔的整数 n、l、v1 和 v2（1 ≤ n ≤ 105，1 ≤ l, v1, v2 ≤ 109）——巧克力的数量、传送带可见部分的长度、传送带的速度以及 Anton 的速度。
第二行包含以空格分隔的整数序列 a1, a2, ..., an（0 ≤ a1 < a2 < ... < an < 2l）——巧克力的坐标。

output.ai: 输出 n + 1 个数（每行一个）：对于每个 i（从 0（第一行）到 n（最后一行）），Anton 恰好捡起 i 块巧克力的概率。如果每个数的绝对误差或相对误差至多为 10 - 9，则答案将被认为正确。

legend: Polycarpus enjoys studying Berland hieroglyphs. Once Polycarp got hold of two ancient Berland pictures, on each of which was drawn a circle of hieroglyphs. We know that no hieroglyph occurs twice in either the first or the second circle (but in can occur once in each of them).

Polycarpus wants to save these pictures on his laptop, but the problem is, laptops do not allow to write hieroglyphs circles. So Polycarp had to break each circle and write down all of its hieroglyphs in a clockwise order in one line. A line obtained from the first circle will be called a, and the line obtained from the second one will be called b.

There are quite many ways to break hieroglyphic circles, so Polycarpus chooses the method, that makes the length of the largest substring of string a, which occurs as a subsequence in string b, maximum.
Help Polycarpus — find the maximum possible length of the desired substring (subsequence) if the first and the second circles are broken optimally.
The length of string s is the number of characters in it. If we denote the length of string s as |s|, we can write the string as s = s1s2... s|s|.
A substring of s is a non-empty string x = s[a... b] = sasa + 1... sb (1 ≤ a ≤ b ≤ |s|). For example, "code" and "force" are substrings of "codeforces", while "coders" is not.
A subsequence of s is a non-empty string y = s[p1p2... p|y|] = sp1sp2... sp|y| (1 ≤ p1 < p2 < ... < p|y| ≤ |s|). For example, "coders" is a subsequence of "codeforces".
input: The first line contains two integers la and lb (1 ≤ la, lb ≤ 1000000) — the number of hieroglyphs in the first and second circles, respectively.
Below, due to difficulties with encoding of Berland hieroglyphs, they are given as integers from 1 to 106.
The second line contains la integers — the hieroglyphs in the first picture, in the clockwise order, starting with one of them.
The third line contains lb integers — the hieroglyphs in the second picture, in the clockwise order, starting with one of them.
It is guaranteed that the first circle doesn't contain a hieroglyph, which occurs twice. The second circle also has this property.
output: Print a single number — the maximum length of the common substring and subsequence. If at any way of breaking the circles it does not exist, print 0.
note: In the first test Polycarpus picks a string that consists of hieroglyphs 5 and 1, and in the second sample — from hieroglyphs 1, 3 and 5.

legend.ai: Polycarpus 喜欢研究 Berland 象形文字。一天，Polycarpus 得到了两幅古老的 Berland 图画，每幅图画上都画着一个由象形文字组成的圆圈。我们知道，在第一个或第二个圆圈中，任何象形文字都不会出现两次（但同一个象形文字可以分别在两个圆圈中各出现一次）。
Polycarpus 想把这些图画保存到他的笔记本电脑上，但问题是，笔记本电脑不允许写下由象形文字组成的圆圈。因此，Polycarpus 不得不拆开每个圆圈，并按照顺时针顺序将其中的所有象形文字写成一行。由第一个圆圈得到的这一行称为 a，由第二个圆圈得到的这一行称为 b。
拆开象形文字圆圈的方法有很多，因此 Polycarpus 选择一种方法，使得字符串 a 中同时作为字符串 b 的子序列出现的最长子串的长度最大。
请帮助 Polycarpus：如果以最优方式拆开第一个和第二个圆圈，求所需子串（子序列）的最大可能长度。
字符串 s 的长度是其中字符的数量。如果将字符串 s 的长度记为 |s|，则可以将字符串写作 s = s_1s_2...s_|s|。
s 的子串是一个非空字符串 x = s[a...b] = s_a s_{a+1}...s_b（1 ≤ a ≤ b ≤ |s|）。例如，“code”和“force”是“codeforces”的子串，而“coders”不是。
s 的子序列是一个非空字符串 y = s[p_1p_2...p_|y|] = s_{p_1}s_{p_2}...s_{p_|y|}（1 ≤ p_1 < p_2 < ... < p_|y| ≤ |s|）。例如，“coders”是“codeforces”的子序列。

input.ai: 第一行包含两个整数 la 和 lb（1 ≤ la, lb ≤ 1000000）——分别表示第一个和第二个圆中的象形文字数量。
下面，由于 Berland 象形文字的编码存在困难，它们用 1 到 10^6 之间的整数表示。
第二行包含 la 个整数——第一幅图中的象形文字，按顺时针顺序排列，并以其中一个为起点。
第三行包含 lb 个整数——第二幅图片中的象形文字，按顺时针顺序排列，从其中一个开始。
保证第一个圆中不存在出现两次的象形文字。第二个圆也满足这一性质。

output.ai: 输出一个数——公共子串和子序列的最大长度。如果无论以何种方式切割这些圆都不存在这样的结果，则输出 0。

note.ai: 在第一组测试中，Polycarpus 选择了一个由象形文字 5 和 1 组成的字符串，而在第二个样例中，他选择了由象形文字 1、3 和 5 组成的字符串。

problems.hint: How can you check if a vertex $x$ is on the path from $u$ to $v$ ?

legend: The main characters have been omitted to be short.

You are given a directed unweighted graph without loops with n$$$n$$$ vertexes and a path in it (that path is not necessary simple) given by a sequence p1,p2,…,pm$$$p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_m$$$ of m$$$m$$$ vertexes; for each 1≤i<m$$$1 \leq i  \lt  m$$$ there is an arc from pi$$$p_i$$$ to pi+1$$$p_{i+1}$$$.

Define the sequence v1,v2,…,vk$$$v_1, v_2, \ldots, v_k$$$ of k$$$k$$$ vertexes as good, if v$$$v$$$ is a subsequence of p$$$p$$$, v1=p1$$$v_1 = p_1$$$, vk=pm$$$v_k = p_m$$$, and p$$$p$$$ is one of the shortest paths passing through the vertexes v1$$$v_1$$$, …$$$\ldots$$$, vk$$$v_k$$$ in that order.

A sequence a$$$a$$$ is a subsequence of a sequence b$$$b$$$ if a$$$a$$$ can be obtained from b$$$b$$$ by deletion of several (possibly, zero or all) elements. It is obvious that the sequence p$$$p$$$ is good but your task is to find the shortest good subsequence.
If there are multiple shortest good subsequences, output any of them.
input: The first line contains a single integer n$$$n$$$ (2≤n≤100$$$2 \le n \le 100$$$) — the number of vertexes in a graph.

The next n$$$n$$$ lines define the graph by an adjacency matrix: the j$$$j$$$-th character in the i$$$i$$$-st line is equal to 1$$$1$$$ if there is an arc from vertex i$$$i$$$ to the vertex j$$$j$$$ else it is equal to 0$$$0$$$. It is guaranteed that the graph doesn't contain loops.
The next line contains a single integer m$$$m$$$ (2≤m≤106$$$2 \le m \le 10^6$$$) — the number of vertexes in the path.

The next line contains m$$$m$$$ integers p1,p2,…,pm$$$p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_m$$$ (1≤pi≤n$$$1 \le p_i \le n$$$) — the sequence of vertexes in the path. It is guaranteed that for any 1≤i<m$$$1 \leq i  \lt  m$$$ there is an arc from pi$$$p_i$$$ to pi+1$$$p_{i+1}$$$.
output: In the first line output a single integer k$$$k$$$ (2≤k≤m$$$2 \leq k \leq m$$$) — the length of the shortest good subsequence. In the second line output k$$$k$$$ integers v1$$$v_1$$$, …$$$\ldots$$$, vk$$$v_k$$$ (1≤vi≤n$$$1 \leq v_i \leq n$$$) — the vertexes in the subsequence. If there are multiple shortest subsequences, print any. Any two consecutive numbers should be distinct.
note: Below you can see the graph from the first example:
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/3e0af0adb4ab1272fc9152aae8708228c6014c45.png)

The given path is passing through vertexes 1$$$1$$$, 2$$$2$$$, 3$$$3$$$, 4$$$4$$$. The sequence 1−2−4$$$1-2-4$$$ is good because it is the subsequence of the given path, its first and the last elements are equal to the first and the last elements of the given path respectively, and the shortest path passing through vertexes 1$$$1$$$, 2$$$2$$$ and 4$$$4$$$ in that order is 1−2−3−4$$$1-2-3-4$$$. Note that subsequences 1−4$$$1-4$$$ and 1−3−4$$$1-3-4$$$ aren't good because in both cases the shortest path passing through the vertexes of these sequences is 1−3−4$$$1-3-4$$$.
In the third example, the graph is full so any sequence of vertexes in which any two consecutive elements are distinct defines a path consisting of the same number of vertexes.
In the fourth example, the paths 1−2−4$$$1-2-4$$$ and 1−3−4$$$1-3-4$$$ are the shortest paths passing through the vertexes 1$$$1$$$ and 4$$$4$$$.

problems.hint: Another minimization problem. If the time is fixed, how can you check if all of the asterisks can be eaten? Note that you should let the left Packmen eat the left asterisks.

legend: A game field is a strip of 1 × n square cells. In some cells there are Packmen, in some cells — asterisks, other cells are empty.
Packman can move to neighboring cell in 1 time unit. If there is an asterisk in the target cell then Packman eats it. Packman doesn't spend any time to eat an asterisk.

In the initial moment of time all Packmen begin to move. Each Packman can change direction of its move unlimited number of times, but it is not allowed to go beyond the boundaries of the game field. Packmen do not interfere with the movement of other packmen; in one cell there can be any number of packmen moving in any directions.
Your task is to determine minimum possible time after which Packmen can eat all the asterisks.
input: The first line contains a single integer n (2 ≤ n ≤ 105) — the length of the game field.

The second line contains the description of the game field consisting of n symbols. If there is symbol '.' in position i — the cell i is empty. If there is symbol '*' in position i — in the cell i contains an asterisk. If there is symbol 'P' in position i — Packman is in the cell i.
It is guaranteed that on the game field there is at least one Packman and at least one asterisk.
output: Print minimum possible time after which Packmen can eat all asterisks.
note: In the first example Packman in position 4 will move to the left and will eat asterisk in position 1. He will spend 3 time units on it. During the same 3 time units Packman in position 6 will eat both of neighboring with it asterisks. For example, it can move to the left and eat asterisk in position 5 (in 1 time unit) and then move from the position 5 to the right and eat asterisk in the position 7 (in 2 time units). So in 3 time units Packmen will eat all asterisks on the game field.

In the second example Packman in the position 4 will move to the left and after 2 time units will eat asterisks in positions 3 and 2. Packmen in positions 5 and 8 will move to the right and in 2 time units will eat asterisks in positions 7 and 10, respectively. So 2 time units is enough for Packmen to eat all asterisks on the game field.

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n（2 ≤ n ≤ 10^5）——游戏场地的长度。
第二行包含由 n 个符号组成的游戏场地描述。如果位置 i 上的符号是 '.'，则单元格 i 为空。如果位置 i 上的符号是 '*'，则单元格 i 中有一个星号。如果位置 i 上的符号是 'P'，则 Packman 位于单元格 i。
保证游戏场地上至少有一个 Packman 和至少一个星号。

output.ai: 输出 Packman 吃掉所有星号后所需的最短时间。

problems.hint: For each string, the chosen substrings separate it into a few parts.

legend: After returned from forest, Alyona started reading a book. She noticed strings s and t, lengths of which are n and m respectively. As usual, reading bored Alyona and she decided to pay her attention to strings s and t, which she considered very similar.

Alyona has her favourite positive integer k and because she is too small, k does not exceed 10. The girl wants now to choose k disjoint non-empty substrings of string s such that these strings appear as disjoint substrings of string t and in the same order as they do in string s. She is also interested in that their length is maximum possible among all variants.
Formally, Alyona wants to find a sequence of k non-empty strings p1, p2, p3, ..., pk satisfying following conditions:
s can be represented as concatenation a1p1a2p2... akpkak + 1, where a1, a2, ..., ak + 1 is a sequence of arbitrary strings (some of them may be possibly empty);
t can be represented as concatenation b1p1b2p2... bkpkbk + 1, where b1, b2, ..., bk + 1 is a sequence of arbitrary strings (some of them may be possibly empty);
sum of the lengths of strings in sequence is maximum possible.
Please help Alyona solve this complicated problem and find at least the sum of the lengths of the strings in a desired sequence.
A substring of a string is a subsequence of consecutive characters of the string.
input: In the first line of the input three integers n, m, k (1 ≤ n, m ≤ 1000, 1 ≤ k ≤ 10) are given — the length of the string s, the length of the string t and Alyona's favourite number respectively.
The second line of the input contains string s, consisting of lowercase English letters.
The third line of the input contains string t, consisting of lowercase English letters.
output: In the only line print the only non-negative integer — the sum of the lengths of the strings in a desired sequence.
It is guaranteed, that at least one desired sequence exists.
note: The following image describes the answer for the second sample case:
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/82412f397df1757f13bada411b72f19deb004618.png)

legend.ai: 从森林回来后，Alyona 开始读一本书。她注意到了两个字符串 s 和 t，它们的长度分别为 n 和 m。和往常一样，读书让 Alyona 感到无聊，于是她决定把注意力放在她认为非常相似的字符串 s 和 t 上。
Alyona 有一个最喜欢的正整数 k。由于 k 的值很小，因此 k 不超过 10。现在，这个女孩想从字符串 s 中选出 k 个互不相交的非空子串，使得这些子串也以相同的顺序出现在字符串 t 中，且它们在 t 中也互不相交。她还希望这些子串的总长度在所有可能的方案中最大。
形式化地说，Alyona 想找到一个由 k 个非空字符串 p1, p2, p3, ..., pk 组成的序列，满足以下条件：
s 可以表示为 a1p1a2p2... akpkak + 1 的拼接，其中 a1, a2, ..., ak + 1 是由任意字符串组成的序列（其中一些字符串可以为空）；
t 可以表示为 b1p1b2p2... bkpkbk + 1 的拼接，其中 b1, b2, ..., bk + 1 是由任意字符串组成的序列（其中一些字符串可以为空）；
该序列中字符串的长度之和最大。
请帮助 Alyona 解决这个复杂的问题，并至少求出所需序列中各字符串长度之和。
字符串的子串是该字符串中由连续字符组成的子序列。

output.ai: 在唯一一行中输出唯一的非负整数，即所需序列中各字符串长度之和。
保证至少存在一个符合要求的序列。

legend: You are an all-powerful being and you have created a rectangular world. In fact, your world is so bland that it could be represented by a r×c$$$r \times c$$$ grid. Each cell on the grid represents a country. Each country has a dominant religion. There are only two religions in your world. One of the religions is called Beingawesomeism, who do good for the sake of being good. The other religion is called Pushingittoofarism, who do murders for the sake of being bad.

Oh, and you are actually not really all-powerful. You just have one power, which you can use infinitely many times! Your power involves missionary groups. When a missionary group of a certain country, say a$$$a$$$, passes by another country b$$$b$$$, they change the dominant religion of country b$$$b$$$ to the dominant religion of country a$$$a$$$.
In particular, a single use of your power is this:
You choose a horizontal 1×x$$$1 \times x$$$ subgrid or a vertical x×1$$$x \times 1$$$ subgrid. That value of x$$$x$$$ is up to you;
You choose a direction d$$$d$$$. If you chose a horizontal subgrid, your choices will either be NORTH or SOUTH. If you choose a vertical subgrid, your choices will either be EAST or WEST;
You choose the number s$$$s$$$ of steps;

You command each country in the subgrid to send a missionary group that will travel s$$$s$$$ steps towards direction d$$$d$$$. In each step, they will visit (and in effect convert the dominant religion of) all s$$$s$$$ countries they pass through, as detailed above.
The parameters x$$$x$$$, d$$$d$$$, s$$$s$$$ must be chosen in such a way that any of the missionary groups won't leave the grid.

The following image illustrates one possible single usage of your power. Here, A represents a country with dominant religion Beingawesomeism and P represents a country with dominant religion Pushingittoofarism. Here, we've chosen a 1×4$$$1 \times 4$$$ subgrid, the direction NORTH, and s=2$$$s = 2$$$ steps.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/3baf1f32ca655636504d471bbe121a91c9f3727a.png)

You are a being which believes in free will, for the most part. However, you just really want to stop receiving murders that are attributed to your name. Hence, you decide to use your powers and try to make Beingawesomeism the dominant religion in every country.
What is the minimum number of usages of your power needed to convert everyone to Beingawesomeism?
With god, nothing is impossible. But maybe you're not god? If it is impossible to make Beingawesomeism the dominant religion in all countries, you must also admit your mortality and say so.
input: The first line of input contains a single integer t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤2⋅104$$$1 \le t \le 2\cdot 10^4$$$) denoting the number of test cases.

The first line of each test case contains two space-separated integers r$$$r$$$ and c$$$c$$$ denoting the dimensions of the grid (1≤r,c≤60$$$1 \le r, c \le 60$$$). The next r$$$r$$$ lines each contains c$$$c$$$ characters describing the dominant religions in the countries. In particular, the j$$$j$$$-th character in the i$$$i$$$-th line describes the dominant religion in the country at the cell with row i$$$i$$$ and column j$$$j$$$, where:
"A" means that the dominant religion is Beingawesomeism;
"P" means that the dominant religion is Pushingittoofarism.
It is guaranteed that the grid will only contain "A" or "P" characters. It is guaranteed that the sum of the r⋅c$$$r \cdot c$$$ in a single file is at most 3⋅106$$$3 \cdot 10^6$$$.
output: For each test case, output a single line containing the minimum number of usages of your power needed to convert everyone to Beingawesomeism, or the string "MORTAL" (without quotes) if it is impossible to do so.
