legend: This problem is the most boring one you've ever seen.

Given a sequence of integers a1, a2, ..., an and a non-negative integer h, our goal is to partition the sequence into two subsequences (not necessarily consist of continuous elements). Each element of the original sequence should be contained in exactly one of the result subsequences. Note, that one of the result subsequences can be empty.

Let's define function f(ai, aj) on pairs of distinct elements (that is i ≠ j) in the original sequence. If ai and aj are in the same subsequence in the current partition then f(ai, aj) = ai + aj otherwise f(ai, aj) = ai + aj + h.

Consider all possible values of the function f for some partition. We'll call the goodness of this partiotion the difference between the maximum value of function f and the minimum value of function f.
Your task is to find a partition of the given sequence a that have the minimal possible goodness among all possible partitions.
input: The first line of input contains integers n and h (2 ≤ n ≤ 105, 0 ≤ h ≤ 108). In the second line there is a list of n space-separated integers representing a1, a2, ..., an (0 ≤ ai ≤ 108).
output: The first line of output should contain the required minimum goodness.
The second line describes the optimal partition. You should print n whitespace-separated integers in the second line. The i-th integer is 1 if ai is in the first subsequence otherwise it should be 2.
If there are several possible correct answers you are allowed to print any of them.
note: In the first sample the values of f are as follows: f(1, 2) = 1 + 2 + 2 = 5, f(1, 3) = 1 + 3 + 2 = 6 and f(2, 3) = 2 + 3 = 5. So the difference between maximum and minimum values of f is 1.
In the second sample the value of h is large, so it's better for one of the sub-sequences to be empty.

legend.ai: 这道题是你见过的最无聊的题。
给定一个整数序列 a1, a2, ..., an 和一个非负整数 h，我们的目标是将该序列划分为两个子序列（其中的元素不必连续）。原序列中的每个元素都应恰好包含在其中一个结果子序列中。注意，其中一个结果子序列可以为空。
我们定义原序列中两个不同元素（即 i ≠ j）组成的二元组上的函数 f(ai, aj)。如果 ai 和 aj 在当前划分中属于同一个子序列，则 f(ai, aj) = ai + aj；否则 f(ai, aj) = ai + aj + h。
考虑某个划分下函数 f 的所有可能取值。我们将该划分的优良度定义为函数 f 的最大值与最小值之差。
你的任务是将给定序列 a 划分为两个子序列，使其优良度在所有可能的划分中最小。

output.ai: 输出的第一行应包含所需的最小优良度。
第二行描述最优划分。你应在第二行输出 n 个以空格分隔的整数。如果 ai 属于第一个子序列，则第 i 个整数应为 1，否则应为 2。
如果存在多个可能的正确答案，你可以输出其中任意一个。

note.ai: 在第二个样例中，h 的值很大，因此让其中一个子序列为空会更好。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含整数 n 和 h（2 ≤ n ≤ 105， 0 ≤ h ≤ 108）。第二行包含 n 个以空格分隔的整数，表示 a1、a2、 ..., an（0 ≤ ai ≤ 108）。

legend: An undirected graph is called k-regular, if the degrees of all its vertices are equal k. An edge of a connected graph is called a bridge, if after removing it the graph is being split into two connected components.
Build a connected undirected k-regular graph containing at least one bridge, or else state that such graph doesn't exist.
input: The single line of the input contains integer k (1 ≤ k ≤ 100) — the required degree of the vertices of the regular graph.
output: Print "NO" (without quotes), if such graph doesn't exist.
Otherwise, print "YES" in the first line and the description of any suitable graph in the next lines.
The description of the made graph must start with numbers n and m — the number of vertices and edges respectively.

Each of the next m lines must contain two integers, a and b (1 ≤ a, b ≤ n, a ≠ b), that mean that there is an edge connecting the vertices a and b. A graph shouldn't contain multiple edges and edges that lead from a vertex to itself. A graph must be connected, the degrees of all vertices of the graph must be equal k. At least one edge of the graph must be a bridge. You can print the edges of the graph in any order. You can print the ends of each edge in any order.

The constructed graph must contain at most 106 vertices and 106 edges (it is guaranteed that if at least one graph that meets the requirements exists, then there also exists the graph with at most 106 vertices and at most 106 edges).
note: In the sample from the statement there is a suitable graph consisting of two vertices, connected by a single edge.

note.ai: 在题面中的样例里，存在一个合适的图，由两个顶点组成，并通过一条边相连。

input.ai: 输入仅一行，包含整数 k（1 ≤ k ≤ 100），表示正则图中顶点所需的度数。

output.ai: 如果不存在这样的图，输出 "NO"（不含引号）。
否则，第一行输出 "YES"，并在接下来的若干行中输出任意一个符合要求的图的描述。
构造图的描述必须以两个数字 n 和 m 开头，分别表示顶点数和边数。
接下来的 m 行中，每行必须包含两个整数 a 和 b（1 ≤ a，b ≤ n，a ≠ b），表示顶点 a 和 b 之间存在一条边。图中不应包含重边，也不应包含连接顶点自身的边。图必须是连通图，且图中所有顶点的度数都必须等于 k。图中至少有一条边是桥。你可以按任意顺序输出图中的边，也可以按任意顺序输出每条边的两个端点。
构造出的图最多包含 106 个顶点和 106 条边（保证如果至少存在一个满足要求的图，那么也存在一个顶点数不超过 106 且边数不超过 106 的图）。

legend.ai: 如果一个无向图中所有顶点的度数都等于 k，则称其为 k-正则图。如果删除一条边后，一个连通图被分成两个连通分量，则称这条边为桥。
构造一个包含至少一条桥的连通无向 k-正则图，或者说明不存在这样的图。

legend: A monster is attacking the Cyberland!
Master Yang, a braver, is going to beat the monster. Yang and the monster each have 3 attributes: hitpoints (HP), offensive power (ATK) and defensive power (DEF).

During the battle, every second the monster's HP decrease by max(0, ATKY - DEFM), while Yang's HP decreases by max(0, ATKM - DEFY), where index Y denotes Master Yang and index M denotes monster. Both decreases happen simultaneously Once monster's HP ≤ 0 and the same time Master Yang's HP > 0, Master Yang wins.
Master Yang can buy attributes from the magic shop of Cyberland: h bitcoins per HP, a bitcoins per ATK, and d bitcoins per DEF.
Now Master Yang wants to know the minimum number of bitcoins he can spend in order to win.
input: The first line contains three integers HPY, ATKY, DEFY, separated by a space, denoting the initial HP, ATK and DEF of Master Yang.
The second line contains three integers HPM, ATKM, DEFM, separated by a space, denoting the HP, ATK and DEF of the monster.
The third line contains three integers h, a, d, separated by a space, denoting the price of 1 HP, 1 ATK and 1 DEF.
All numbers in input are integer and lie between 1 and 100 inclusively.
output: The only output line should contain an integer, denoting the minimum bitcoins Master Yang should spend in order to win.
note: For the first sample, prices for ATK and DEF are extremely high. Master Yang can buy 99 HP, then he can beat the monster with 1 HP left.
For the second sample, Master Yang is strong enough to beat the monster, so he doesn't need to buy anything.

legend.ai: 一只怪物正在攻击 Cyberland！
勇敢的 Yang 大师准备击败这只怪物。Yang 和怪物各有 3 项属性：生命值（HP）、攻击力（ATK）和防御力（DEF）。
在战斗过程中，每秒怪物的 HP 会减少 max(0, ATKY - DEFM)，而 Yang 的 HP 会减少 max(0, ATKM - DEFY)，其中下标 Y 表示 Yang 大师，下标 M 表示怪物。两者的 HP 会同时减少。当怪物的 HP ≤ 0 且同时 Yang 大师的 HP > 0 时，Yang 大师获胜。
Yang 大师可以从 Cyberland 的魔法商店购买属性：每点 HP 需要 h 比特币，每点 ATK 需要 a 比特币，每点 DEF 需要 d 比特币。
现在杨大师想知道，为了获胜他最少需要花费多少比特币。

note.ai: 对于第一个样例，ATK 和 DEF 的价格都非常高。杨大师可以购买 99 点 HP，之后他就能击败怪物，并剩下 1 点 HP。
对于第二个样例，杨大师的实力足以击败怪物，因此他不需要购买任何东西。

input.ai: 第一行包含三个整数 HPY、ATKY 和 DEFY，相邻整数之间用空格分隔，分别表示杨大师的初始生命值、攻击力和防御力。
第二行包含三个整数 HPM、ATKM 和 DEFM，相邻整数之间用空格分隔，分别表示怪物的生命值、攻击力和防御力。
第三行包含三个整数 h、a 和 d，相邻整数之间用空格分隔，分别表示 1 点生命值、1 点攻击力和 1 点防御力的价格。
输入中的所有数字均为整数，且均在 1 到 100（含）之间。

output.ai: 唯一的输出行应包含一个整数，表示杨大师为了获胜所需花费的最少比特币数量。

legend: Vladik often travels by trains. He remembered some of his trips especially well and I would like to tell you about one of these trips:

Vladik is at initial train station, and now n people (including Vladik) want to get on the train. They are already lined up in some order, and for each of them the city code ai is known (the code of the city in which they are going to).

Train chief selects some number of disjoint segments of the original sequence of people (covering entire sequence by segments is not necessary). People who are in the same segment will be in the same train carriage. The segments are selected in such way that if at least one person travels to the city x, then all people who are going to city x should be in the same railway carriage. This means that they can’t belong to different segments. Note, that all people who travel to the city x, either go to it and in the same railway carriage, or do not go anywhere at all.

Comfort of a train trip with people on segment from position l to position r is equal to XOR of all distinct codes of cities for people on the segment from position l to position r. XOR operation also known as exclusive OR.
Total comfort of a train trip is equal to sum of comfort for each segment.
Help Vladik to know maximal possible total comfort.
input: First line contains single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 5000) — number of people.
Second line contains n space-separated integers a1, a2, ..., an (0 ≤ ai ≤ 5000), where ai denotes code of the city to which i-th person is going.
output: The output should contain a single integer — maximal possible total comfort.
note: In the first test case best partition into segments is: [4, 4] [2, 5, 2] [3], answer is calculated as follows: 4 + (2 xor 5) + 3 = 4 + 7 + 3 = 14
In the second test case best partition into segments is: 5 1 [3] 1 5 [2, 4, 2] 5, answer calculated as follows: 3 + (2 xor 4) = 3 + 6 = 9.

legend.ai: Vladik 经常乘火车旅行。他对其中一些旅行印象特别深刻，我想给你讲讲其中一次：
Vladik 在起始火车站，现在有 n 个人（包括 Vladik）想要上车。他们已经按某种顺序排好队，并且每个人的目的地城市编号 ai 已知（即他们将要前往的城市编号）。
列车长从原队伍序列中选取若干互不相交的段（不一定用这些段覆盖整个序列）。同一段中的人将坐在同一节车厢里。这些段的选取需满足：如果至少有一个人前往城市 x，那么所有前往城市 x 的人都必须在同一节车厢里。也就是说，他们不能属于不同的段。注意，所有前往城市 x 的人，要么都在同一节车厢里前往该城市，要么就根本不出行。
从位置 l 到位置 r 的乘车区间内所有人的乘车舒适度，等于该区间内所有不同城市代码的异或和。异或运算也称为排他性或运算。
一次乘车的总舒适度等于每个区间的舒适度之和。
请帮助 Vladik 求出可能的最大总舒适度。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 5000），表示人数。
第二行包含 n 个以空格分隔的整数 a1， a2， ...， an（0 ≤ ai ≤ 5000），其中 ai 表示第 i 个人要前往的城市的代码。

output.ai: 输出应包含一个整数，即可能的最大总舒适度。

note.ai: 在第一个测试用例中，最优的分段方式是：[4, 4] [2, 5, 2] [3]，答案计算如下：4 + (2 按位异或 5) + 3 = 4 + 7 + 3 = 14
在第二个测试用例中，最优的分段方式是：5 1 [3] 1 5 [2, 4, 2] 5，答案计算如下：3 + (2 按位异或 4) = 3 + 6 = 9。

legend: Little Chris is a huge fan of linear algebra. This time he has been given a homework about the unusual square of a square matrix.

The dot product of two integer number vectors x and y of size n is the sum of the products of the corresponding components of the vectors. The unusual square of an n × n square matrix A is defined as the sum of n dot products. The i-th of them is the dot product of the i-th row vector and the i-th column vector in the matrix A.

Fortunately for Chris, he has to work only in GF(2)! This means that all operations (addition, multiplication) are calculated modulo 2. In fact, the matrix A is binary: each element of A is either 0 or 1. For example, consider the following matrix A:
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/2c3ad2b03d2ce423c3d5acf492c838080055234f.png)
However, there is much more to the homework. Chris has to process q queries; each query can be one of the following:
given a row index i, flip all the values in the i-th row in A;
given a column index i, flip all the values in the i-th column in A;
find the unusual square of A.
To flip a bit value w means to change it to 1 - w, i.e., 1 changes to 0 and 0 changes to 1.
Given the initial matrix A, output the answers for each query of the third type! Can you solve Chris's homework?
input: The first line of input contains an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 1000), the number of rows and the number of columns in the matrix A. The next n lines describe the matrix: the i-th line contains n space-separated bits and describes the i-th row of A. The j-th number of the i-th line aij (0 ≤ aij ≤ 1) is the element on the intersection of the i-th row and the j-th column of A.
The next line of input contains an integer q (1 ≤ q ≤ 106), the number of queries. Each of the next q lines describes a single query, which can be one of the following:
1 i — flip the values of the i-th row;
2 i — flip the values of the i-th column;
3 — output the unusual square of A.
Note: since the size of the input and output could be very large, don't use slow output techniques in your language. For example, do not use input and output streams (cin, cout) in C++.
output: Let the number of the 3rd type queries in the input be m. Output a single string s of length m, where the i-th symbol of s is the value of the unusual square of A for the i-th query of the 3rd type as it appears in the input.

legend.ai: Little Chris 是线性代数的超级粉丝。这一次，他的作业是研究方阵的非寻常平方。
两个大小为 n 的整数向量 x 和 y 的点积，是两个向量对应分量乘积之和。n × n 方阵 A 的非寻常平方定义为 n 个点积之和。其中第 i 个点积是矩阵 A 的第 i 行向量与第 i 列向量的点积。
幸运的是，Chris 只需要在 GF(2) 中进行运算！这意味着所有运算（加法、乘法）都对 2 取模。事实上，矩阵 A 是二进制矩阵：A 的每个元素都只能是 0 或 1。例如，考虑下面的矩阵 A：
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/2c3ad2b03d2ce423c3d5acf492c838080055234f.png)
然而，这份作业的内容远不止这些。Chris 需要处理 q 次查询；每次查询可能是以下操作之一：
给定行下标 i，将 A 的第 i 行中的所有值翻转；
给定列下标 i，将 A 的第 i 列中的所有值翻转；
求 A 的特殊平方。
翻转位值 w，意味着将其变为 1 - w，即将 1 变为 0，将 0 变为 1。
给定初始矩阵 A，输出每次第三类查询的答案！你能解决 Chris 的家庭作业吗？

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 1000），表示矩阵 A 的行数和列数。接下来的 n 行描述该矩阵：第 i 行包含 n 个以空格分隔的位，并描述 A 的第 i 行。第 i 行中的第 j 个数 aij（0 ≤ aij ≤ 1）是 A 中第 i 行与第 j 列交点处的元素。
输入的下一行包含一个整数 q（1 ≤ q ≤ 106），表示查询的数量。接下来的 q 行中的每一行描述一个查询，查询可以是以下几种之一：
1 i —— 翻转第 i 行的所有值；
2 i —— 翻转第 i 列的所有值；
3 —— 输出 A 的非寻常平方。
注意：由于输入和输出的规模可能非常大，请不要在你所使用的语言中采用缓慢的输出方式。例如，在 C++ 中不要使用输入输出流（cin、cout）。

output.ai: 设输入中第 3 类查询的数量为 m。输出一个长度为 m 的字符串 s，其中 s 的第 i 个字符是输入中第 i 个第 3 类查询对应的 A 的非寻常平方的值。

statement.title: E. Furlo and Rublo and Game

legend: Furlo and Rublo play a game. The table has n piles of coins lying on it, the i-th pile has ai coins. Furlo and Rublo move in turns, Furlo moves first. In one move you are allowed to:
choose some pile, let's denote the current number of coins in it as x;
choose some integer y (0 ≤ y < x; x1 / 4 ≤ y ≤ x1 / 2) and decrease the number of coins in this pile to y. In other words, after the described move the pile will have y coins left.
The player who can't make a move, loses.
Your task is to find out, who wins in the given game if both Furlo and Rublo play optimally well.
input: The first line contains integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 77777) — the number of piles. The next line contains n integers a1, a2, ..., an (1 ≤ ai ≤ 777777777777) — the sizes of piles. The numbers are separated by single spaces.
Please, do not use the %lld specifier to read or write 64-bit integers in С++. It is preferred to use the cin, cout streams or the %I64d specifier.
output: If both players play optimally well and Furlo wins, print "Furlo", otherwise print "Rublo". Print the answers without the quotes.

legend.ai: Furlo 和 Rublo 在玩一个游戏。桌上有 n 堆硬币，第 i 堆中有 ai 枚硬币。Furlo 和 Rublo 轮流行动，Furlo 先手。每次行动可以：
选择某一堆，记其中当前的硬币数为 x；
选择一个整数 y（0 ≤ y < x；x1 / 4 ≤ y ≤ x1 / 2），并将该堆中的硬币数量减少到 y。换句话说，执行所描述的操作后，这堆中将剩下 y 枚硬币。
无法进行操作的玩家输掉比赛。
你的任务是判断：如果 Furlo 和 Rublo 都采取最优策略进行游戏，在给定的游戏中谁会获胜。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 77777），表示堆的数量。下一行包含 n 个整数 a1， a2， ...， an（1 ≤ ai ≤ 777777777777），表示各堆的大小。相邻数字之间用单个空格分隔。
请不要在 С++ 中使用 %lld 格式说明符读写 64 位整数。建议使用 cin、cout 流或 %I64d 格式说明符。

output.ai: 如果双方都采取最优策略进行游戏且 Furlo 获胜，则输出 "Furlo"，否则输出 "Rublo"。输出时不要包含引号。

legend: People in the Tomskaya region like magic formulas very much. You can see some of them below.
Imagine you are given a sequence of positive integer numbers p1, p2, ..., pn. Lets write down some magic formulas:
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/81ab130934a6699fcdd0da19288992c1c610bc69.png)
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e4038bbd3f52ecb87dbbdd560d05e7810522f6af.png)
Here, "mod" means the operation of taking the residue after dividing.

The expression ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b364f2e04c665b78b924ec10666327a4ef4635bc.png) means applying the bitwise xor (excluding "OR") operation to integers x and y. The given operation exists in all modern programming languages. For example, in languages C++ and Java it is represented by "^", in Pascal — by "xor".
People in the Tomskaya region like magic formulas very much, but they don't like to calculate them! Therefore you are given the sequence p, calculate the value of Q.
input: The first line of the input contains the only integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 106). The next line contains n integers: p1, p2, ..., pn (0 ≤ pi ≤ 2·109).
output: The only line of output should contain a single integer — the value of Q.

legend.ai: Tomskaya 地区的人们非常喜欢魔法公式。下面可以看到其中一些。
假设给定一个正整数序列 p1、p2、...、pn。让我们写出一些魔法公式：
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/81ab130934a6699fcdd0da19288992c1c610bc69.png)
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e4038bbd3f52ecb87dbbdd560d05e7810522f6af.png)
这里，“mod”表示除法取余运算。
表达式 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b364f2e04c665b78b924ec10666327a4ef4635bc.png) 表示对整数 x 和 y 进行按位异或(不包括“或”)运算。该运算存在于所有现代编程语言中。例如，在 C++ 和 Java 语言中，它表示为“^”，在 Pascal 中则表示为“xor”。
托木斯克地区的人们非常喜欢魔法公式，但他们不喜欢计算公式！因此给定序列 p，请计算 Q 的值。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含唯一的整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 106）。下一行包含 n 个整数：p1， p2， ...， pn（0 ≤ pi ≤ 2·109）。

output.ai: 输出的唯一一行应包含一个整数，即 Q 的值。

legend: Manao's friends often send him new songs. He never listens to them right away. Instead, he compiles them into a playlist. When he feels that his mind is open to new music, he opens the playlist and starts to listen to the songs.
Of course, there are some songs that Manao doesn't particuarly enjoy. To get more pleasure from the received songs, he invented the following procedure of listening to the playlist:
If after listening to some song Manao realizes that he liked it, then he remembers it and starts to listen to the next unlistened song.
If after listening to some song Manao realizes that he did not like it, he listens to all the songs he liked up to this point and then begins to listen to the next unlistened song.
For example, if Manao has four songs in the playlist, A, B, C, D (in the corresponding order) and he is going to like songs A and C in the end, then the order of listening is the following:
Manao listens to A, he likes it, he remembers it.
Manao listens to B, he does not like it, so he listens to A, again.
Manao listens to C, he likes the song and he remembers it, too.
Manao listens to D, but does not enjoy it and re-listens to songs A and C.
That is, in the end Manao listens to song A three times, to song C twice and songs B and D once. Note that if Manao once liked a song, he will never dislike it on a subsequent listening.

Manao has received n songs: the i-th of them is li seconds long and Manao may like it with a probability of pi percents. The songs could get on Manao's playlist in any order, so Manao wants to know the maximum expected value of the number of seconds after which the listening process will be over, for all possible permutations of the songs in the playlist.
input: The first line contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 50000). The i-th of the following n lines contains two integers, separated by a single space — li and pi (15 ≤ li ≤ 1000, 0 ≤ pi ≤ 100) — the length of the i-th song in seconds and the probability that Manao will like the song, in percents.
output: In a single line print a single real number — the maximum expected listening time over all permutations of songs. The answer will be considered valid if the absolute or relative error does not exceed 10 - 9.
note: Consider the first test case. If Manao listens to the songs in the order in which they were originally compiled, the mathematical expectation will be equal to 467.5 seconds. The maximum expected value is obtained by putting the first song at the end of the playlist.
Consider the second test case. The song which is 360 seconds long should be listened to first. The song 300 seconds long which Manao will dislike for sure should be put in the end.

legend.ai: Manao 的朋友们经常给他发送新歌曲。他从不立即收听这些歌曲，而是将它们整理到一个播放列表中。当他觉得自己已经准备好接受新音乐时，就会打开播放列表并开始收听歌曲。
当然，有些歌曲并不是 Manao 特别喜欢的。为了从收到的歌曲中获得更多乐趣，他发明了以下播放列表收听流程：
如果 Manao 听完某首歌曲后意识到自己喜欢它，那么他会记住这首歌，并开始收听下一首尚未听过的歌曲。
如果 Manao 听完某首歌曲后意识到自己不喜欢它，那么他会把截至目前为止自己喜欢的所有歌曲都听一遍，然后开始收听下一首尚未听过的歌曲。
例如，假设 Manao 的播放列表中有四首歌曲，依次为 A、B、C、D，并且最终他会喜欢歌曲 A 和 C，那么收听顺序如下：
Manao 收听歌曲 A，他喜欢这首歌，于是记住了它。
Manao 收听歌曲 B，他不喜欢这首歌，因此再次收听歌曲 A。
Manao 听了歌曲 C，他喜欢这首歌，也记住了它。
Manao 听了歌曲 D，但不喜欢这首歌，于是又听了一遍歌曲 A 和 C。
也就是说，最终 Manao 听了歌曲 A 三遍、歌曲 C 两遍，以及歌曲 B 和 D 各一遍。注意，如果 Manao 曾经喜欢过一首歌，那么在之后再次听到这首歌时，他永远不会不喜欢它。
Manao 收到了 n 首歌曲：其中第 i 首歌曲的时长为 li 秒，Manao 可能以 pi% 的概率喜欢它。这些歌曲可以按任意顺序加入 Manao 的播放列表，因此对于播放列表中歌曲的所有排列，Manao 想知道听歌过程结束时所经过秒数的最大期望值。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 50000）。接下来的 n 行中，第 i 行包含两个整数 li 和 pi，它们之间用一个空格分隔（15 ≤ li ≤ 1000，0 ≤ pi ≤ 100）：分别表示第 i 首歌曲的时长（单位为秒）以及 Manao 喜欢这首歌曲的概率（单位为百分比）。

output.ai: 在一行中输出一个实数，即所有歌曲排列中听歌时间的最大期望值。如果答案的绝对误差或相对误差不超过 10 - 9，则视为正确。

note.ai: 考虑第一个测试用例。如果 Manao 按照歌曲最初编排的顺序听歌，数学期望将等于 467.5 秒。将第一首歌放到播放列表末尾可以得到最大的期望值。
考虑第二个测试用例。应该先听时长为 360 秒的歌曲。Manao 一定会不喜欢的那首时长为 300 秒的歌曲应该放在最后。

legend: Alice got an array of length n$$$n$$$ as a birthday present once again! This is the third year in a row!
And what is more disappointing, it is overwhelmengly boring, filled entirely with zeros. Bob decided to apply some changes to the array to cheer up Alice.

Bob has chosen m$$$m$$$ changes of the following form. For some integer numbers x$$$x$$$ and d$$$d$$$, he chooses an arbitrary position i$$$i$$$ (1≤i≤n$$$1 \le i \le n$$$) and for every j∈[1,n]$$$j \in [1, n]$$$ adds x+d⋅dist(i,j)$$$x + d \cdot dist(i, j)$$$ to the value of the j$$$j$$$-th cell. dist(i,j)$$$dist(i, j)$$$ is the distance between positions i$$$i$$$ and j$$$j$$$ (i.e. dist(i,j)=|i−j|$$$dist(i, j) = |i - j|$$$, where |x|$$$|x|$$$ is an absolute value of x$$$x$$$).

For example, if Alice currently has an array [2,1,2,2]$$$[2, 1, 2, 2]$$$ and Bob chooses position 3$$$3$$$ for x=−1$$$x = -1$$$ and d=2$$$d = 2$$$ then the array will become [2−1+2⋅2, 1−1+2⋅1, 2−1+2⋅0, 2−1+2⋅1]$$$[2 - 1 + 2 \cdot 2,~1 - 1 + 2 \cdot 1,~2 - 1 + 2 \cdot 0,~2 - 1 + 2 \cdot 1]$$$ = [5,2,1,3]$$$[5, 2, 1, 3]$$$. Note that Bob can't choose position i$$$i$$$ outside of the array (that is, smaller than 1$$$1$$$ or greater than n$$$n$$$).
Alice will be the happiest when the elements of the array are as big as possible. Bob claimed that the arithmetic mean value of the elements will work fine as a metric.
What is the maximum arithmetic mean value Bob can achieve?

statement.title: C3. Smart Beaver and Resolving Collisions

legend: The Smart Beaver from ABBYY has a lot of hobbies. One of them is constructing efficient hash tables. One of the most serious problems in hash tables is resolving collisions. The Beaver is interested in this problem very much and he decided to explore it in detail.

We assume that the hash table consists of h cells numbered from 0 to h - 1. Objects are added to and removed from it. Every object has its own unique identifier. In addition, every object has a corresponding hash value — an integer between 0 and h - 1, inclusive. When an object is added to the table, if the cell corresponding to the hash value of the object is free, then this object goes there. If the cell is already occupied by another object, there is a collision. When an object is deleted from the table, the cell which it occupied becomes empty.

The Smart Beaver has recently learned about the method of linear probing to resolve collisions. It is as follows. Let's say that the hash value for the added object equals t and cell t of the table is already occupied. Then we try to add this object to cell (t + m) mod h. If it is also occupied, then we try cell (t + 2·m) mod h, then cell (t + 3·m) mod h, and so on. Note that in some cases it's possible that the new object can not be added to the table. It is guaranteed that the input for this problem doesn't contain such situations.
The operation a mod b means that we take the remainder of the division of number a by number b.

This technique immediately seemed very inoptimal to the Beaver, and he decided to assess its inefficiency. So, you are given a sequence of operations, each of which is either an addition of an object to the table or a deletion of an object from the table. When adding a new object, a sequence of calls to the table is performed. Calls to occupied cells are called dummy. In other words, if the result of the algorithm described above is the object being added to cell (t + i·m) mod h (i ≥ 0), then exactly i dummy calls have been performed.

Your task is to calculate the total number of dummy calls to the table for the given sequence of additions and deletions. When an object is deleted from the table, assume that no dummy calls are performed. The table is empty before performing the operations, that is, initially it doesn't contain any objects.
input: The first line of input contains three integers h, m and n (1 ≤ m < h), separated by spaces, where h is the size of the hash table, m is the number that is used to resolve collisions, n is the number of operations.

The following n lines contains the descriptions of the operations. Their execution order corresponds to the order in which they appear in the input file. Each operation is described by a single line. The operations are described as follows:

"+ id hash"This is the format of the operation that adds an object to the table. The first character is "+" (ASCII 43), followed by a single space, then the object identifier id (0 ≤ id ≤ 109), then another space, and the hash value of the given object hash (0 ≤ hash < h). The object identifier and the hash value of this object are integers.

"- id"This is the format of the operation that deletes an object from the table. The first character is "-" (ASCII 45), followed by a single space, then the object identifier id (0 ≤ id ≤ 109). The object identifier is an integer.

It is guaranteed that for all addition operations the value of id is unique. It is also guaranteed that the initial data is correct, that is, it's always possible to add an object to the hash table and there won't be any deletions of nonexisting objects.

The input limitations for getting 50 points are:
The input limitations for getting 100 points are:
output: Print a single number — the total number of dummy calls to the hash table.
Please, do not use the %lld specifier to read or write 64-bit integers in С++. It is preferred to use cin, cout streams and the %I64d specifier.

legend.ai: 来自 ABBYY 的 Smart Beaver 有很多爱好。其中之一是构造高效的哈希表。哈希表最严重的问题之一就是解决冲突。Beaver 对此问题非常感兴趣，并决定深入研究它。
我们假设哈希表由 h 个槽位组成，编号从 0 到 h-1。对象会被加入和移出该表。每个对象都有自己唯一的标识符；此外，每个对象都有一个对应的哈希值——一个在 0 到 h-1（含端点）之间的整数。当向表中加入一个对象时，如果该对象哈希值对应的槽位是空闲的，那么这个对象就放入该槽位；如果该槽位已被另一个对象占用，则发生冲突。当从表中删除一个对象时，它所占用的槽位会变为空。
Smart Beaver 最近学习了用线性探测解决冲突的方法。其过程如下：假设要加入的对象的哈希值为 t，且表中第 t 个槽位已被占用。那么我们尝试将该对象加入槽位 (t + m) mod h。如果该槽位也被占用，则再尝试槽位 (t + 2·m) mod h，然后是槽位 (t + 3·m) mod h，依此类推。注意，在某些情况下新对象可能无法加入哈希表。题目保证输入数据中不会出现这种情况。
运算 a mod b 表示取数 a 除以数 b 的余数。
这种方法在海狸看来立刻显得非常低效，于是它决定评估该方法的低效程度。现在，给定一个操作序列，其中每个操作要么是向表中添加一个对象，要么是从表中删除一个对象。添加新对象时，会对表执行一系列查询。对已被占用的单元格进行的查询称为虚假查询。换句话说，如果上述算法的结果是将要添加的对象放入单元格 (t + i·m) mod h（i ≥ 0），那么恰好执行了 i 次虚假查询。
你的任务是计算给定添加和删除操作序列中对表进行虚假查询的总次数。删除表中的对象时，认为不会执行任何虚假查询。在执行操作之前，表为空，也就是说，初始时表中不包含任何对象。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含三个整数 h、m 和 n（1 ≤ m < h），它们之间用空格分隔。其中，h 是哈希表的大小，m 是用于解决冲突的数值，n 是操作的数量。
接下来的 n 行包含操作的描述。操作的执行顺序与它们在输入文件中的出现顺序一致。每个操作由单独一行描述。操作描述如下：
"+ id hash"这是向表中添加对象的操作格式。第一个字符是“+”（ASCII 码 43），后跟一个空格，然后是对象标识符 id（0 ≤ id ≤ 109），再后跟一个空格，最后是给定对象的哈希值 hash（0 ≤ hash < h）。对象标识符和该对象的哈希值均为整数。
"- id"这是从表中删除对象的操作格式。第一个字符是“-”（ASCII 码 45），后跟一个空格，然后是对象标识符 id（0 ≤ id ≤ 109）。对象标识符为整数。
保证对于所有添加操作，id 的值都是唯一的。同时保证初始数据是正确的，也就是说，始终可以向哈希表中添加对象，并且不会删除不存在的对象。
获得 20 分的输入约束为：
获得 50 分的输入约束为：
获得 100 分的输入限制为：

output.ai: 输出一个数，即对哈希表进行虚拟调用的总次数。
请不要在 С++ 中使用 %lld 格式说明符来读写 64 位整数。建议使用 cin、cout 流以及 %I64d 格式说明符。

statement.title: E. Little Artem and Time Machine

legend: Little Artem has invented a time machine! He could go anywhere in time, but all his thoughts of course are with computer science. He wants to apply this time machine to a well-known data structure: multiset.
Artem wants to create a basic multiset of integers. He wants these structure to support operations of three types:
Add integer to the multiset. Note that the difference between set and multiset is that multiset may store several instances of one integer.

Remove integer from the multiset. Only one instance of this integer is removed. Artem doesn't want to handle any exceptions, so he assumes that every time remove operation is called, that integer is presented in the multiset.
Count the number of instances of the given integer that are stored in the multiset.

But what about time machine? Artem doesn't simply apply operations to the multiset one by one, he now travels to different moments of time and apply his operation there. Consider the following example.
First Artem adds integer 5 to the multiset at the 1-st moment of time.
Then Artem adds integer 3 to the multiset at the moment 5.
Then Artem asks how many 5 are there in the multiset at moment 6. The answer is 1.
Then Artem returns back in time and asks how many integers 3 are there in the set at moment 4. Since 3 was added only at moment 5, the number of integers 3 at moment 4 equals to 0.
Then Artem goes back in time again and removes 5 from the multiset at moment 3.
Finally Artyom asks at moment 7 how many integers 5 are there in the set. The result is 0, since we have removed 5 at the moment 3.

Note that Artem dislikes exceptions so much that he assures that after each change he makes all delete operations are applied only to element that is present in the multiset. The answer to the query of the third type is computed at the moment Artem makes the corresponding query and are not affected in any way by future changes he makes.
Help Artem implement time travellers multiset.
input: The first line of the input contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 100 000) — the number of Artem's queries.

Then follow n lines with queries descriptions. Each of them contains three integers ai, ti and xi (1 ≤ ai ≤ 3, 1 ≤ ti, xi ≤ 109) — type of the query, moment of time Artem travels to in order to execute this query and the value of the query itself, respectively. It's guaranteed that all moments of time are distinct and that after each operation is applied all operations of the first and second types are consistent.
output: For each ask operation output the number of instances of integer being queried at the given moment of time.

legend.ai: 小 Artem 发明了一台时间机器！他可以前往任何时间，但他所有的想法当然都与计算机科学有关。他想将这台时间机器应用于一种众所周知的数据结构：多重集合。
Artem 想要创建一个由整数构成的基本多重集合。他希望该数据结构支持以下三种类型的操作：
向多重集合中加入一个整数。注意，集合与多重集合的区别在于，多重集合可以存储同一个整数的多个实例。
从多重集合中移除一个整数。只会移除该整数的一个实例。Artem 不想处理任何异常，因此他假设每次调用移除操作时，该整数都存在于多重集合中。
统计多重集合中存储的给定整数的实例数量。
但是时间机器该怎么办呢？Artem 不会简单地逐个对多重集合应用操作，而是会前往不同的时间点，并在那里执行他的操作。请考虑下面的例子。
首先，Artem 在第 1 个时刻将整数 5 加入多重集合。
然后，Artem 在第 5 个时刻将整数 3 加入多重集合。
然后 Artem 询问在时刻 6 多重集中有多少个 5。答案是 1。
然后 Artem 回到过去，询问在时刻 4 集合中有多少个整数 3。由于 3 只在时刻 5 被加入，时刻 4 时整数 3 的数量等于 0。
然后 Artem 再次回到过去，在时刻 3 从多重集合中移除 5。
最后 Artyom 在时刻 7 询问集合中有多少个整数 5。结果是 0，因为我们在时刻 3 移除了 5。
注意，Artem 非常讨厌特殊情况，因此他保证在他每次做出修改之后，所有删除操作只会作用于多重集合中当前存在的元素。第三类查询的答案是在 Artem 发出对应查询的时刻计算的，不会受到他未来任何修改的影响。
帮助 Artem 实现一个时间旅行者的多重集合。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 100 000），表示 Artem 的查询数量。
接下来是 n 行查询描述。每行包含三个整数 ai、ti 和 xi（1 ≤ ai ≤ 3，1 ≤ ti, xi ≤ 10^9），分别表示查询类型、Artem 为执行该查询而前往的时间点以及查询本身的值。保证所有时间点互不相同，并且在应用每次操作后，所有第一类和第二类操作都是一致的。

output.ai: 对于每个询问操作，输出给定时间点被查询整数出现的次数。

legend: Generous sponsors of the olympiad in which Chloe and Vladik took part allowed all the participants to choose a prize for them on their own. Christmas is coming, so sponsors decided to decorate the Christmas tree with their prizes.

They took n prizes for the contestants and wrote on each of them a unique id (integer from 1 to n). A gift i is characterized by integer ai — pleasantness of the gift. The pleasantness of the gift can be positive, negative or zero. Sponsors placed the gift 1 on the top of the tree. All the other gifts hung on a rope tied to some other gift so that each gift hung on the first gift, possibly with a sequence of ropes and another gifts. Formally, the gifts formed a rooted tree with n vertices.

The prize-giving procedure goes in the following way: the participants come to the tree one after another, choose any of the remaining gifts and cut the rope this prize hang on. Note that all the ropes which were used to hang other prizes on the chosen one are not cut. So the contestant gets the chosen gift as well as the all the gifts that hang on it, possibly with a sequence of ropes and another gifts.

Our friends, Chloe and Vladik, shared the first place on the olympiad and they will choose prizes at the same time! To keep themselves from fighting, they decided to choose two different gifts so that the sets of the gifts that hang on them with a sequence of ropes and another gifts don't intersect. In other words, there shouldn't be any gift that hang both on the gift chosen by Chloe and on the gift chosen by Vladik. From all of the possible variants they will choose such pair of prizes that the sum of pleasantness of all the gifts that they will take after cutting the ropes is as large as possible.
Print the maximum sum of pleasantness that Vladik and Chloe can get. If it is impossible for them to choose the gifts without fighting, print Impossible.
input: The first line contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·105) — the number of gifts.
The next line contains n integers a1, a2, ..., an ( - 109 ≤ ai ≤ 109) — the pleasantness of the gifts.

The next (n - 1) lines contain two numbers each. The i-th of these lines contains integers ui and vi (1 ≤ ui, vi ≤ n, ui ≠ vi) — the description of the tree's edges. It means that gifts with numbers ui and vi are connected to each other with a rope. The gifts' ids in the description of the ropes can be given in arbirtary order: vi hangs on ui or ui hangs on vi.
It is guaranteed that all the gifts hang on the first gift, possibly with a sequence of ropes and another gifts.
output: If it is possible for Chloe and Vladik to choose prizes without fighting, print single integer — the maximum possible sum of pleasantness they can get together.
Otherwise print Impossible.

legend.ai: Chloe 和 Vladik 参加的奥林匹克竞赛的慷慨赞助商允许所有参赛者自行选择奖品。圣诞节即将到来，因此赞助商决定用他们的奖品装饰圣诞树。
他们为参赛者准备了 n 件奖品，并在每件奖品上写下一个唯一的编号（从 1 到 n 的整数）。第 i 件礼物由整数 ai 表示其愉悦度。礼物的愉悦度可以是正数、负数或零。赞助商将礼物 1 放在树顶。其他所有礼物都悬挂在系到某件其他礼物上的绳子上，因此每件礼物都悬挂在第一件礼物下方，中间可能经过一串绳子和其他礼物。形式化地说，这些礼物构成了一棵有 n 个顶点的树，且以 1 为根。
颁奖过程如下：参赛者依次来到这棵树前，选择任意一个尚未被选走的礼物，并剪断悬挂该奖品的绳子。注意，所有用于将其他奖品悬挂在所选奖品上的绳子都不会被剪断。因此，参赛者将获得所选礼物，以及通过一系列绳子和其他礼物悬挂在它上的所有礼物。
我们的朋友 Chloe 和 Vladik 在奥林匹克竞赛中并列第一名，因此他们将同时选择奖品！为了避免争抢，他们决定选择两个不同的礼物，使得通过一系列绳子和其他礼物悬挂在这两个礼物上的礼物集合不相交。换句话说，不应该存在同时悬挂在 Chloe 和 Vladik 所选礼物上的礼物。在所有可能的方案中，他们将选择这样一对奖品，使得剪断绳子后两人获得的所有礼物的愉悦度之和尽可能大。
输出 Vladik 和 Chloe 能获得的愉悦度之和的最大值。如果他们无法选择不会发生争抢的礼物，则输出 Impossible。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 2·105），表示礼物的数量。
下一行包含 n 个整数 a1, a2, ..., an（ - 109 ≤ ai ≤ 109），表示各个礼物的愉悦度。
接下来的（n - 1）行每行包含两个数。第 i 行包含整数 ui 和 vi（1 ≤ ui, vi ≤ n，ui ≠ vi），表示树中的一条边。也就是说，编号为 ui 和 vi 的礼物通过一根绳子相连。绳子描述中的礼物编号可以按任意顺序给出：vi 悬挂在 ui 上，或 ui 悬挂在 vi 上。
保证所有礼物都挂在第一个礼物上，中间可能隔着一串绳子和其他礼物。

output.ai: 如果 Chloe 和 Vladik 可以在不发生争执的情况下选择奖品，请输出一个整数，即他们两人能够获得的愉悦度总和的最大值。
否则输出 Impossible。

legend: It's that time of the year, Felicity is around the corner and you can see people celebrating all around the Himalayan region. The Himalayan region has n gyms. The i-th gym has gi Pokemon in it. There are m distinct Pokemon types in the Himalayan region numbered from 1 to m. There is a special evolution camp set up in the fest which claims to evolve any Pokemon. The type of a Pokemon could change after evolving, subject to the constraint that if two Pokemon have the same type before evolving, they will have the same type after evolving. Also, if two Pokemon have different types before evolving, they will have different types after evolving. It is also possible that a Pokemon has the same type before and after evolving.
Formally, an evolution plan is a permutation f of {1, 2, ..., m}, such that f(x) = y means that a Pokemon of type x evolves into a Pokemon of type y.

The gym leaders are intrigued by the special evolution camp and all of them plan to evolve their Pokemons. The protocol of the mountain states that in each gym, for every type of Pokemon, the number of Pokemon of that type before evolving any Pokemon should be equal the number of Pokemon of that type after evolving all the Pokemons according to the evolution plan. They now want to find out how many distinct evolution plans exist which satisfy the protocol.
Two evolution plans f1 and f2 are distinct, if they have at least one Pokemon type evolving into a different Pokemon type in the two plans, i. e. there exists an i such that f1(i) ≠ f2(i).

Your task is to find how many distinct evolution plans are possible such that if all Pokemon in all the gyms are evolved, the number of Pokemon of each type in each of the gyms remains the same. As the answer can be large, output it modulo 109 + 7.
input: The first line contains two integers n and m (1 ≤ n ≤ 105, 1 ≤ m ≤ 106) — the number of gyms and the number of Pokemon types.

The next n lines contain the description of Pokemons in the gyms. The i-th of these lines begins with the integer gi (1 ≤ gi ≤ 105) — the number of Pokemon in the i-th gym. After that gi integers follow, denoting types of the Pokemons in the i-th gym. Each of these integers is between 1 and m.
The total number of Pokemons (the sum of all gi) does not exceed 5·105.
output: Output the number of valid evolution plans modulo 109 + 7.

![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/5f569c7ffa0111a20a7bedc873c68fdf02d79d08.png)

legend.ai: 又到了这个时候，Felicity 即将到来，你可以看到喜庆的人们遍布整个喜马拉雅地区。喜马拉雅地区有 n 个健身房。第 i 个健身房中有 gi 只宝可梦。喜马拉雅地区有 m 种不同的宝可梦类型，编号从 1 到 m。节庆活动中设立了一个特殊的进化营，声称可以使任意宝可梦进化。宝可梦的类型可能会在进化后改变，但需要满足以下约束：如果两只宝可梦在进化前类型相同，那么它们在进化后的类型也相同；如果两只宝可梦在进化前类型不同，那么它们在进化后的类型也不同。宝可梦进化前后的类型也可能相同。
形式化地说，一个进化方案是集合 {1, 2, ..., m} 的一个排列 f，其中 f(x) = y 表示一只类型为 x 的宝可梦会进化为类型为 y 的宝可梦。
道馆馆主们对特殊进化训练营很感兴趣，他们都计划让自己的宝可梦进化。山上的规章规定：对于每个道馆和每种宝可梦，在进行任何宝可梦进化之前，该类型宝可梦的数量应当等于按照进化计划让所有宝可梦进化之后该类型宝可梦的数量。他们现在想知道满足这一规章的不同进化计划共有多少种。
如果两个进化计划 f1 和 f2 至少存在一种宝可梦类型在两个计划中进化成了不同的宝可梦类型，则称它们是不同的。也就是说，存在某个 i，使得 f1(i) ≠ f2(i)。
你的任务是求出所有道馆中的宝可梦都进化后，每个道馆中每种宝可梦的数量都保持不变的不同进化计划数量。由于答案可能很大，请输出答案对 109 + 7 取模的结果。

input.ai: 第一行包含两个整数 n 和 m（1 ≤ n ≤ 105，1 ≤ m ≤ 106），分别表示道馆的数量和宝可梦类型的数量。

宝可梦的总数量（所有 gi 之和）不超过 5·105。

legend: A boy named Gena really wants to get to the "Russian Code Cup" finals, or at least get a t-shirt. But the offered problems are too complex, so he made an arrangement with his n friends that they will solve the problems for him.

The participants are offered m problems on the contest. For each friend, Gena knows what problems he can solve. But Gena's friends won't agree to help Gena for nothing: the i-th friend asks Gena xi rubles for his help in solving all the problems he can. Also, the friend agreed to write a code for Gena only if Gena's computer is connected to at least ki monitors, each monitor costs b rubles.

Gena is careful with money, so he wants to spend as little money as possible to solve all the problems. Help Gena, tell him how to spend the smallest possible amount of money. Initially, there's no monitors connected to Gena's computer.
input: The first line contains three integers n, m and b (1 ≤ n ≤ 100; 1 ≤ m ≤ 20; 1 ≤ b ≤ 109) — the number of Gena's friends, the number of problems and the cost of a single monitor.

The following 2n lines describe the friends. Lines number 2i and (2i + 1) contain the information about the i-th friend. The 2i-th line contains three integers xi, ki and mi (1 ≤ xi ≤ 109; 1 ≤ ki ≤ 109; 1 ≤ mi ≤ m) — the desired amount of money, monitors and the number of problems the friend can solve. The (2i + 1)-th line contains mi distinct positive integers — the numbers of problems that the i-th friend can solve. The problems are numbered from 1 to m.
output: Print the minimum amount of money Gena needs to spend to solve all the problems. Or print -1, if this cannot be achieved.

legend.ai: 一个名叫 Gena 的男孩非常想进入“Russian Code Cup”决赛，至少也想得到一件 T 恤。但比赛提供的问题太复杂了，于是他和他的 n 个朋友达成协议，让他们替他解决这些问题。

Gena 很节省，所以他希望花费尽可能少的钱解决所有问题。请帮助 Gena，告诉他解决所有问题所需的最小花费。初始时，Gena 的电脑没有连接任何显示器。

legend: A multi-subject competition is coming! The competition has m$$$m$$$ different subjects participants can choose from. That's why Alex (the coach) should form a competition delegation among his students.
He has n$$$n$$$ candidates. For the i$$$i$$$-th person he knows subject si$$$s_i$$$ the candidate specializes in and ri$$$r_i$$$ — a skill level in his specialization (this level can be negative!).

The rules of the competition require each delegation to choose some subset of subjects they will participate in. The only restriction is that the number of students from the team participating in each of the chosen subjects should be the same.

Alex decided that each candidate would participate only in the subject he specializes in. Now Alex wonders whom he has to choose to maximize the total sum of skill levels of all delegates, or just skip the competition this year if every valid non-empty delegation has negative sum.
(Of course, Alex doesn't have any spare money so each delegate he chooses must participate in the competition).
input: The first line contains two integers n$$$n$$$ and m$$$m$$$ (1≤n≤105$$$1 \le n \le 10^5$$$, 1≤m≤105$$$1 \le m \le 10^5$$$) — the number of candidates and the number of subjects.

The next n$$$n$$$ lines contains two integers per line: si$$$s_i$$$ and ri$$$r_i$$$ (1≤si≤m$$$1 \le s_i \le m$$$, −104≤ri≤104$$$-10^4 \le r_i \le 10^4$$$) — the subject of specialization and the skill level of the i$$$i$$$-th candidate.
output: Print the single integer — the maximum total sum of skills of delegates who form a valid delegation (according to rules above) or 0$$$0$$$ if every valid non-empty delegation has negative sum.
note: In the first example it's optimal to choose candidates 1$$$1$$$, 2$$$2$$$, 3$$$3$$$, 4$$$4$$$, so two of them specialize in the 2$$$2$$$-nd subject and other two in the 3$$$3$$$-rd. The total sum is 6+6+5+5=22$$$6 + 6 + 5 + 5 = 22$$$.
In the second example it's optimal to choose candidates 1$$$1$$$, 2$$$2$$$ and 5$$$5$$$. One person in each subject and the total sum is 6+6+11=23$$$6 + 6 + 11 = 23$$$.
In the third example it's impossible to obtain a non-negative sum.

legend.ai: 一场多科目竞赛即将开始！这场竞赛有 m$$$m$$$ 个不同的科目可供参赛者选择。因此，教练 Alex 需要从他的学生中组建一支参赛队伍。
他有 n$$$n$$$ 名候选人。对于他认识的第 i$$$i$$$ 个人，他知道该候选人专长的科目为 si$$$s_i$$$，以及其在该专长领域的技能水平为 ri$$$r_i$$$(这个水平可能为负数！)。
竞赛规则要求每支队伍选择一些他们将参加的科目。唯一的限制是，对于每一个被选中的科目，队伍中参加该科目的学生人数必须相同。
Alex 决定让每位候选人只参加自己所擅长的科目。现在 Alex 想知道他应该选择哪些人，才能使所有代表的技能水平总和最大；或者，如果每支合法的非空队伍的总和都为负数，就放弃参加今年的竞赛。

接下来的 n$$$n$$$ 行中，每行包含两个整数：si$$$s_i$$$ 和 ri$$$r_i$$$(1≤si≤m$$$1 \le s_i \le m$$$，−104≤ri≤104$$$-10^4 \le r_i \le 10^4$$$)——第 i$$$i$$$ 位候选人的专业科目和技能水平。

legend: This is an interactive problem. In the output section below you will see the information about flushing the output.

On Sunday Leha the hacker took Nura from the house where she lives and went with her to one of the most luxurious restaurants in Vičkopolis. Upon arrival, they left the car in a huge parking lot near the restaurant and hurried inside the building.

In the restaurant a polite waiter immediately brought the menu to Leha and Noora, consisting of n dishes. It is interesting that all dishes in the menu are numbered with integers from 1 to n. After a little thought, the girl ordered exactly k different dishes from available in the menu. To pass the waiting time while the chefs prepare ordered dishes, the girl invited the hacker to play a game that will help them get to know each other better.

The game itself is very simple: Noora wants Leha to guess any two dishes among all ordered. At the same time, she is ready to answer only one type of questions. Leha can say two numbers x and y (1 ≤ x, y ≤ n). After that Noora chooses some dish a for the number x such that, at first, a is among the dishes Noora ordered (x can be equal to a), and, secondly, the value ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e5a4a1705bc256e413564795cc8b70857f0ae44c.png) is the minimum possible. By the same rules the girl chooses dish b for y. After that Noora says «TAK» to Leha, if ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a65cb6a9b614699e12e529560e2d39ffa39127db.png), and «NIE» otherwise. However, the restaurant is preparing quickly, so Leha has enough time to ask no more than 60 questions. After that he should name numbers of any two dishes Noora ordered.
Help Leha to solve this problem!
input: There are two numbers n and k (2 ≤ k ≤ n ≤ 105) in the single line of input denoting the number of dishes in the menu and the number of dishes Noora ordered.
output: If you want to provide an answer, output a string of the form 2 x y (1 ≤ x, y ≤ n, x ≠ y), if you think the dishes x and y was among dishes ordered by Noora. After that, flush the output and terminate your program.

While helping Leha, you can ask queries to Noora no more than 60 times. Each query should be printed in it's own line and have the form 1 x y (1 ≤ x, y ≤ n). You have to both print the end-of-line character and flush the output. After flushing you should read the answer for this query from input.
After each query jury's program will print one line «TAK» or «NIE» (without quotes) in input stream depending on the girl's answer.
To flush you can use (just after printing an integer and end-of-line):
fflush(stdout) in C++;
System.out.flush() in Java;
stdout.flush() in Python;
flush(output) in Pascal;
see the documentation for other languages.
Hacking

For hacking you should write numbers n and k (2 ≤ k ≤ n ≤ 105) in the first line and, for describing dishes Noora ordered, k different integers a1, a2, ..., ak (1 ≤ ai ≤ n), written in ascending order in the second line. Of course, solution you want to hack won't be able to read the numbers of ordered dishes.
note: There are three dishes in sample. Noora ordered dished numberes 2 and 3, which Leha should guess. If Noora receive requests for the first dish (x = 1), then she'll choose the second dish (a = 2) as the dish with the minimum value ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e5a4a1705bc256e413564795cc8b70857f0ae44c.png). For the second (x = 2) and the third (x = 3) dishes themselves will be optimal, because in that case ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/79add195d023131e992b60a354fec89501759e75.png).
Let Leha asks Noora about the next couple of dishes:
x = 1, y = 2, then he'll recieve «NIE» answer, because |1 - 2| > |2 - 2|

x = 3, y = 1, then he'll recieve «TAK» answer, because |3 - 3| ≤ |1 - 2|

x = 3, y = 2, then he'll recieve «TAK» answer, because |3 - 3| ≤ |2 - 2|

legend.ai: 这是一个交互题。在下面的输出部分，你会看到关于刷新输出的信息。
周日，黑客 Leha 把 Nura 从她住的房子里带出来，和她一起去了 Vičkopolis 最豪华的餐厅之一。到达后，他们把车停在餐厅附近的一个巨大停车场，然后匆匆走进大楼。

游戏本身非常简单：Noora 想让 Leha 在所有已点的菜中猜出任意两道。同时，她只准备回答一种类型的问题。Leha 可以说出两个数 x 和 y(1 ≤ x, y ≤ n)。之后 Noora 会为数字 x 选择一道菜 a，要求：首先，a 是 Noora 所点菜肴中的一道(x 可以等于 a)；其次，![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e5a4a1705bc256e413564795cc8b70857f0ae44c.png) 的值尽可能小。女孩按照同样的规则为 y 选择菜 b。之后，如果 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a65cb6a9b614699e12e529560e2d39ffa39127db.png)，Noora 就对 Leha 说“TAK”，否则说“NIE”。然而，餐厅上菜很快，所以 Leha 最多只能问 60 个问题。之后，他需要说出 Noora 所点的任意两道菜的编号。
帮助 Leha 解决这个问题！

problems.hint: You only need to decide where the "middle point" is.

legend: Polycarp plans to conduct a load testing of its new project Fakebook. He already agreed with his friends that at certain points in time they will send requests to Fakebook. The load testing will last n minutes and in the i-th minute friends will send ai requests.

Polycarp plans to test Fakebook under a special kind of load. In case the information about Fakebook gets into the mass media, Polycarp hopes for a monotone increase of the load, followed by a monotone decrease of the interest to the service. Polycarp wants to test this form of load.

Your task is to determine how many requests Polycarp must add so that before some moment the load on the server strictly increases and after that moment strictly decreases. Both the increasing part and the decreasing part can be empty (i. e. absent). The decrease should immediately follow the increase. In particular, the load with two equal neigbouring values is unacceptable.

For example, if the load is described with one of the arrays [1, 2, 8, 4, 3], [1, 3, 5] or [10], then such load satisfies Polycarp (in each of the cases there is an increasing part, immediately followed with a decreasing part). If the load is described with one of the arrays [1, 2, 2, 1], [2, 1, 2] or [10, 10], then such load does not satisfy Polycarp.
Help Polycarp to make the minimum number of additional requests, so that the resulting load satisfies Polycarp. He can make any number of additional requests at any minute from 1 to n.
input: The first line contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 100 000) — the duration of the load testing.
The second line contains n integers a1, a2, ..., an (1 ≤ ai ≤ 109), where ai is the number of requests from friends in the i-th minute of the load testing.
output: Print the minimum number of additional requests from Polycarp that would make the load strictly increasing in the beginning and then strictly decreasing afterwards.
note: In the first example Polycarp must make two additional requests in the third minute and four additional requests in the fourth minute. So the resulting load will look like: [1, 4, 5, 6, 5]. In total, Polycarp will make 6 additional requests.
In the second example it is enough to make one additional request in the third minute, so the answer is 1.
In the third example the load already satisfies all conditions described in the statement, so the answer is 0.

legend.ai: Polycarp 计划对他的新项目 Fakebook 进行负载测试。他已经和朋友们约定，在特定的时间点向 Fakebook 发送请求。负载测试将持续 n 分钟，在第 i 分钟，朋友们会发送 ai 个请求。
Polycarp 计划在一种特殊的负载下测试 Fakebook。如果有关 Fakebook 的信息登上大众媒体，Polycarp 希望负载先单调增加，随后用户对该服务的兴趣单调下降。Polycarp 想要测试这种形式的负载。
你的任务是确定 Polycarp 至少需要添加多少个请求，使得在某个时刻之前，服务器上的负载严格递增，而在该时刻之后严格递减。递增部分和递减部分都可以为空（即不存在）。递减部分应当紧接在递增部分之后。特别地，负载中不能出现两个相邻且相等的值。
例如，如果负载由数组 [1, 2, 8, 4, 3]、[1, 3, 5] 或 [10] 中的一个描述，那么这样的负载满足 Polycarp 的要求（在每种情况下，都存在一个递增部分，其后紧接着一个递减部分）。如果负载由数组 [1, 2, 2, 1]、[2, 1, 2] 或 [10, 10] 中的一个描述，那么这样的负载不满足 Polycarp 的要求。
请帮助 Polycarp 添加最少数量的请求，使得最终的负载满足 Polycarp 的要求。他可以在从 1 到 n 的任意一分钟内添加任意数量的请求。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 100 000），表示负载测试的持续时间。
第二行包含 n 个整数 a1, a2, ..., an（1 ≤ ai ≤ 109），其中 ai 表示负载测试第 i 分钟来自朋友的请求数量。

output.ai: 输出 Polycarp 需要添加的最少请求数量，使得负载开始时严格递增，之后严格递减。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，Polycarp 必须在第三分钟额外发送两个请求，并在第四分钟额外发送四个请求。因此，最终的负载将如下所示：[1, 4, 5, 6, 5]。总计 Polycarp 将额外发送 6 个请求。
在第二个样例中，只需在第三分钟额外发送一个请求，因此答案是 1。
在第三个样例中，负载已经满足题目中描述的所有条件，因此答案是 0。

problems.hint: You don't need many kinds of operations.

legend: In one of the games Arkady is fond of the game process happens on a rectangular field. In the game process Arkady can buy extensions for his field, each extension enlarges one of the field sizes in a particular number of times. Formally, there are n extensions, the i-th of them multiplies the width or the length (by Arkady's choice) by ai. Each extension can't be used more than once, the extensions can be used in any order.

Now Arkady's field has size h × w. He wants to enlarge it so that it is possible to place a rectangle of size a × b on it (along the width or along the length, with sides parallel to the field sides). Find the minimum number of extensions needed to reach Arkady's goal.
input: The first line contains five integers a, b, h, w and n (1 ≤ a, b, h, w, n ≤ 100 000) — the sizes of the rectangle needed to be placed, the initial sizes of the field and the number of available extensions.
The second line contains n integers a1, a2, ..., an (2 ≤ ai ≤ 100 000), where ai equals the integer a side multiplies by when the i-th extension is applied.
output: Print the minimum number of extensions needed to reach Arkady's goal. If it is not possible to place the rectangle on the field with all extensions, print -1. If the rectangle can be placed on the initial field, print 0.
note: In the first example it is enough to use any of the extensions available. For example, we can enlarge h in 5 times using the second extension. Then h becomes equal 10 and it is now possible to place the rectangle on the field.

input.ai: 第一行包含五个整数 a、b、h、w 和 n（1 ≤ a, b, h, w, n ≤ 100 000）——需要放置的矩形的尺寸、场地的初始尺寸以及可用扩展的数量。
第二行包含 n 个整数 a1, a2, ..., an（2 ≤ ai ≤ 100 000），其中 ai 等于使用第 i 次扩展时一条边所乘的整数。

output.ai: 输出达到 Arkady 的目标所需的最少扩展次数。如果使用所有扩展后仍无法将矩形放到场地上，输出 -1。如果矩形可以放在初始场地上，输出 0。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，使用任意一个可用扩展就足够了。例如，我们可以使用第二个扩展将 h 放大 5 倍。这样 h 变成 10，现在就可以将矩形放到场地上。

legend.ai: 在 Arkady 喜欢的一款游戏中，游戏过程发生在一个矩形场地上。在游戏过程中，Arkady 可以购买场地扩展，每个扩展可以将场地的某个边长扩大若干倍。形式化地说，共有 n 个扩展，其中第 i 个扩展可以将宽度或长度（由 Arkady 选择）乘以 ai。每个扩展至多使用一次，且扩展可以按任意顺序使用。
现在 Arkady 的场地大小为 h × w。他希望扩大场地，使其能够放置一个大小为 a × b 的矩形（可以沿宽度或长度放置，且矩形的边与场地的边平行）。求达到 Arkady 目标所需的最少扩展数量。

problems.hint: Consider the permutation as a graph, and eventually it should consist of $1$ cycle.

legend: Pavel cooks barbecue. There are n skewers, they lay on a brazier in a row, each on one of n positions. Pavel wants each skewer to be cooked some time in every of n positions in two directions: in the one it was directed originally and in the reversed direction.

Pavel has a plan: a permutation p and a sequence b1, b2, ..., bn, consisting of zeros and ones. Each second Pavel move skewer on position i to position pi, and if bi equals 1 then he reverses it. So he hope that every skewer will visit every position in both directions.

Unfortunately, not every pair of permutation p and sequence b suits Pavel. What is the minimum total number of elements in the given permutation p and the given sequence b he needs to change so that every skewer will visit each of 2n placements? Note that after changing the permutation should remain a permutation as well.

There is no problem for Pavel, if some skewer visits some of the placements several times before he ends to cook. In other words, a permutation p and a sequence b suit him if there is an integer k (k ≥ 2n), so that after k seconds each skewer visits each of the 2n placements.
It can be shown that some suitable pair of permutation p and sequence b exists for any n.
input: The first line contain the integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·105) — the number of skewers.
The second line contains a sequence of integers p1, p2, ..., pn (1 ≤ pi ≤ n) — the permutation, according to which Pavel wants to move the skewers.
The third line contains a sequence b1, b2, ..., bn consisting of zeros and ones, according to which Pavel wants to reverse the skewers.
output: Print single integer — the minimum total number of elements in the given permutation p and the given sequence b he needs to change so that every skewer will visit each of 2n placements.
note: In the first example Pavel can change the permutation to 4, 3, 1, 2.
In the second example Pavel can change any element of b to 1.

legend.ai: Pavel 做烧烤。有 n 根烤串，它们放在烤炉上排成一排，每根位于 n 个位置之一。Pavel 希望每一根烤串都能在 n 个位置中的每一个位置被烤一段时间，并且要包含两种朝向：一种是最初所指的方向，另一种是相反方向。
Pavel 有一个计划：一个排列 p 和一个由 0 和 1 组成的序列 b1, b2, ..., bn。每秒，Pavel 都会将位于位置 i 的烤签移动到位置 pi；如果 bi 等于 1，他还会将其翻转。因此，他希望每根烤签都能以两个方向经过每个位置。
遗憾的是，并非任意排列 p 和序列 b 都适合 Pavel。为了使每根烤签都能经过 2n 个位置中的每一个，他至少需要修改给定排列 p 和给定序列 b 中的多少个元素？注意，修改后的排列仍必须是一个排列。
如果某根烤签在 Pavel 停止烹饪之前多次经过某些位置，这对他来说并没有问题。换句话说，如果存在一个整数 k（k ≥ 2n），使得经过 k 秒后每根烤签都经过了 2n 个位置中的每一个，那么排列 p 和序列 b 就适合他。
可以证明，对于任意 n，都存在一对适合的排列 p 和序列 b。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 2·105）——烤签的数量。
第二行包含一个整数序列 p1, p2, ..., pn（1 ≤ pi ≤ n）——Pavel 希望据此移动烤签的排列。
第三行包含一个由 0 和 1 组成的序列 b1, b2, ..., bn，Pavel 将根据该序列翻转烤串。

output.ai: 输出一个整数，即他需要修改给定排列 p 和给定序列 b 中的元素总数的最小值，使得每根烤串都会经过 2n 个位置。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，Pavel 可以将排列修改为 4, 3, 1, 2。
在第二个样例中，Pavel 可以将 b 中的任意一个元素修改为 1。

problems.hint: Each person only need to consider one type of cards. So group the players.

legend: There are n$$$n$$$ players sitting at the card table. Each player has a favorite number. The favorite number of the j$$$j$$$-th player is fj$$$f_j$$$.

There are k⋅n$$$k \cdot n$$$ cards on the table. Each card contains a single integer: the i$$$i$$$-th card contains number ci$$$c_i$$$. Also, you are given a sequence h1,h2,…,hk$$$h_1, h_2, \dots, h_k$$$. Its meaning will be explained below.

The players have to distribute all the cards in such a way that each of them will hold exactly k$$$k$$$ cards. After all the cards are distributed, each player counts the number of cards he has that contains his favorite number. The joy level of a player equals ht$$$h_t$$$ if the player holds t$$$t$$$ cards containing his favorite number. If a player gets no cards with his favorite number (i.e., t=0$$$t=0$$$), his joy level is 0$$$0$$$.
Print the maximum possible total joy levels of the players after the cards are distributed. Note that the sequence h1,…,hk$$$h_1, \dots, h_k$$$ is the same for all the players.
input: The first line of input contains two integers n$$$n$$$ and k$$$k$$$ (1≤n≤500,1≤k≤10$$$1 \le n \le 500, 1 \le k \le 10$$$) — the number of players and the number of cards each player will get.
The second line contains k⋅n$$$k \cdot n$$$ integers c1,c2,…,ck⋅n$$$c_1, c_2, \dots, c_{k \cdot n}$$$ (1≤ci≤105$$$1 \le c_i \le 10^5$$$) — the numbers written on the cards.
The third line contains n$$$n$$$ integers f1,f2,…,fn$$$f_1, f_2, \dots, f_n$$$ (1≤fj≤105$$$1 \le f_j \le 10^5$$$) — the favorite numbers of the players.

The fourth line contains k$$$k$$$ integers h1,h2,…,hk$$$h_1, h_2, \dots, h_k$$$ (1≤ht≤105$$$1 \le h_t \le 10^5$$$), where ht$$$h_t$$$ is the joy level of a player if he gets exactly t$$$t$$$ cards with his favorite number written on them. It is guaranteed that the condition ht−1<ht$$$h_{t - 1}  \lt  h_t$$$ holds for each t∈[2..k]$$$t \in [2..k]$$$.
output: Print one integer — the maximum possible total joy levels of the players among all possible card distributions.
note: In the first example, one possible optimal card distribution is the following:
Player 1$$$1$$$ gets cards with numbers [1,3,8]$$$[1, 3, 8]$$$;
Player 2$$$2$$$ gets cards with numbers [2,2,8]$$$[2, 2, 8]$$$;
Player 3$$$3$$$ gets cards with numbers [2,2,8]$$$[2, 2, 8]$$$;
Player 4$$$4$$$ gets cards with numbers [5,5,5]$$$[5, 5, 5]$$$.
In the second example, no player can get a card with his favorite number. Thus, the answer is 0$$$0$$$.

legend.ai: 有 n$$$n$$$ 名玩家坐在牌桌旁。每名玩家都有一个喜欢的数字。第 j$$$j$$$ 名玩家喜欢的数字是 fj$$$f_j$$$。
桌上有 k⋅n$$$k \cdot n$$$ 张卡片。每张卡片上写着一个整数：第 i$$$i$$$ 张卡片上写着数字 ci$$$c_i$$$。此外，给定一个序列 h1,h2,…,hk$$$h_1, h_2, \dots, h_k$$$。其含义将在下文解释。
玩家需要以一种方式分配所有卡片，使得每位玩家恰好拿到 k$$$k$$$ 张卡片。所有卡片分配完毕后，每位玩家统计自己拿到的卡片中写有其最喜欢数字的卡片数量。如果一名玩家拿到了 t$$$t$$$ 张写有其最喜欢数字的卡片，那么该玩家的快乐值为 ht$$$h_t$$$。如果一名玩家没有拿到写有其最喜欢数字的卡片(即 t=0$$$t=0$$$)，那么其快乐值为 0$$$0$$$。
输出分配卡片后所有玩家快乐值之和的最大可能值。注意，序列 h1,…,hk$$$h_1, \dots, h_k$$$ 对所有玩家都相同。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含两个整数 n$$$n$$$ 和 k$$$k$$$(1≤n≤500，1≤k≤10$$$1 \le n \le 500, 1 \le k \le 10$$$)，分别表示玩家数量以及每位玩家将拿到的卡片数量。
第二行包含 k⋅n$$$k \cdot n$$$ 个整数 c1,c2,…,ck⋅n$$$c_1, c_2, \dots, c_{k \cdot n}$$$(1≤ci≤105$$$1 \le c_i \le 10^5$$$)，表示卡片上写的数字。
第三行包含 n$$$n$$$ 个整数 f1,f2,…,fn$$$f_1, f_2, \dots, f_n$$$(1≤fj≤105$$$1 \le f_j \le 10^5$$$)，表示各位玩家最喜欢的数字。

第四行包含 k$$$k$$$ 个整数 h1,h2,…,hk$$$h_1, h_2, \dots, h_k$$$(1≤ht≤105$$$1 \le h_t \le 10^5$$$)，其中 ht$$$h_t$$$ 表示一名玩家恰好获得 t$$$t$$$ 张写有其喜爱数字的卡片时的快乐值。保证对于每个 t∈[2..k]$$$t \in [2..k]$$$，均满足条件 ht−1<ht$$$h_{t - 1}  \lt  h_t$$$。

output.ai: 输出一个整数——在所有可能的卡片分配方案中，玩家快乐值总和的最大可能值。

statement.title: C. World of Darkraft: Battle for Azathoth

legend: Roma is playing a new expansion for his favorite game World of Darkraft. He made a new character and is going for his first grind.

Roma has a choice to buy exactly one of n$$$n$$$ different weapons and exactly one of m$$$m$$$ different armor sets. Weapon i$$$i$$$ has attack modifier ai$$$a_i$$$ and is worth cai$$$ca_i$$$ coins, and armor set j$$$j$$$ has defense modifier bj$$$b_j$$$ and is worth cbj$$$cb_j$$$ coins.

After choosing his equipment Roma can proceed to defeat some monsters. There are p$$$p$$$ monsters he can try to defeat. Monster k$$$k$$$ has defense xk$$$x_k$$$, attack yk$$$y_k$$$ and possesses zk$$$z_k$$$ coins. Roma can defeat a monster if his weapon's attack modifier is larger than the monster's defense, and his armor set's defense modifier is larger than the monster's attack. That is, a monster k$$$k$$$ can be defeated with a weapon i$$$i$$$ and an armor set j$$$j$$$ if ai>xk$$$a_i  \gt  x_k$$$ and bj>yk$$$b_j  \gt  y_k$$$. After defeating the monster, Roma takes all the coins from them. During the grind, Roma can defeat as many monsters as he likes. Monsters do not respawn, thus each monster can be defeated at most one.

Thanks to Roma's excessive donations, we can assume that he has an infinite amount of in-game currency and can afford any of the weapons and armor sets. Still, he wants to maximize the profit of the grind. The profit is defined as the total coins obtained from all defeated monsters minus the cost of his equipment. Note that Roma must purchase a weapon and an armor set even if he can not cover their cost with obtained coins.
Help Roma find the maximum profit of the grind.
input: The first line contains three integers n$$$n$$$, m$$$m$$$, and p$$$p$$$ (1≤n,m,p≤2⋅105$$$1 \leq n, m, p \leq 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of available weapons, armor sets and monsters respectively.

The following n$$$n$$$ lines describe available weapons. The i$$$i$$$-th of these lines contains two integers ai$$$a_i$$$ and cai$$$ca_i$$$ (1≤ai≤106$$$1 \leq a_i \leq 10^6$$$, 1≤cai≤109$$$1 \leq ca_i \leq 10^9$$$) — the attack modifier and the cost of the weapon i$$$i$$$.

The following m$$$m$$$ lines describe available armor sets. The j$$$j$$$-th of these lines contains two integers bj$$$b_j$$$ and cbj$$$cb_j$$$ (1≤bj≤106$$$1 \leq b_j \leq 10^6$$$, 1≤cbj≤109$$$1 \leq cb_j \leq 10^9$$$) — the defense modifier and the cost of the armor set j$$$j$$$.

The following p$$$p$$$ lines describe monsters. The k$$$k$$$-th of these lines contains three integers xk,yk,zk$$$x_k, y_k, z_k$$$ (1≤xk,yk≤106$$$1 \leq x_k, y_k \leq 10^6$$$, 1≤zk≤103$$$1 \leq z_k \leq 10^3$$$) — defense, attack and the number of coins of the monster k$$$k$$$.
output: Print a single integer — the maximum profit of the grind.

legend.ai: Roma 正在游玩他最喜欢的游戏《World of Darkraft》的一个新扩展包。他创建了一个新角色，准备进行第一次刷怪。
Roma 可以选择购买恰好一把 n$$$n$$$ 种不同武器中的武器，以及恰好一套 m$$$m$$$ 种不同护甲中的护甲。第 i$$$i$$$ 把武器具有攻击修正值 ai$$$a_i$$$，价值为 cai$$$ca_i$$$ 枚硬币；第 j$$$j$$$ 套护甲具有防御修正值 bj$$$b_j$$$，价值为 cbj$$$cb_j$$$ 枚硬币。

选择装备后，Roma 可以继续击败一些怪物。他可以尝试击败的怪物共有 p$$$p$$$ 只。第 k$$$k$$$ 只怪物具有防御力 xk$$$x_k$$$、攻击力 yk$$$y_k$$$，并持有 zk$$$z_k$$$ 枚硬币。当他的武器攻击修正值大于怪物的防御力，且护甲防御修正值大于怪物的攻击力时，Roma 就可以击败该怪物。也就是说，使用第 i$$$i$$$ 把武器和第 j$$$j$$$ 套护甲时，如果 ai>xk$$$a_i  \gt  x_k$$$ 且 bj>yk$$$b_j  \gt  y_k$$$，就可以击败第 k$$$k$$$ 只怪物。击败怪物后，Roma 会拿走它持有的全部硬币。在刷怪过程中，Roma 可以随意击败任意数量的怪物。怪物不会重生，因此每只怪物最多只能被击败一次。
由于 Roma 进行了大量捐赠，我们可以认为他拥有无限量的游戏货币，可以负担得起任何武器和护甲。然而，他仍然希望最大化刷怪的收益。收益定义为击败所有怪物获得的硬币总数减去装备的花费。注意，即使 Roma 无法用获得的硬币支付装备费用，他也必须购买一把武器和一套护甲。
请帮助 Roma 求出刷怪所能获得的最大收益。

input.ai: 第一行包含三个整数 n$$$n$$$、m$$$m$$$ 和 p$$$p$$$(1≤n,m,p≤2⋅105$$$1 \leq n, m, p \leq 2 \cdot 10^5$$$)，分别表示可用武器、护甲和怪物的数量。
接下来的 n$$$n$$$ 行描述可用的武器。其中第 i$$$i$$$ 行包含两个整数 ai$$$a_i$$$ 和 cai$$$ca_i$$$(1≤ai≤106$$$1 \leq a_i \leq 10^6$$$，1≤cai≤109$$$1 \leq ca_i \leq 10^9$$$)——武器 i$$$i$$$ 的攻击修正值和花费。
接下来的 m$$$m$$$ 行描述可用的护甲套装。其中第 j$$$j$$$ 行包含两个整数 bj$$$b_j$$$ 和 cbj$$$cb_j$$$(1≤bj≤106$$$1 \leq b_j \leq 10^6$$$，1≤cbj≤109$$$1 \leq cb_j \leq 10^9$$$)——护甲套装 j$$$j$$$ 的防御修正值和花费。
接下来的 p$$$p$$$ 行描述怪物。其中第 k$$$k$$$ 行包含三个整数 xk,yk,zk$$$x_k, y_k, z_k$$$(1≤xk,yk≤106$$$1 \leq x_k, y_k \leq 10^6$$$，1≤zk≤103$$$1 \leq z_k \leq 10^3$$$)——怪物 k$$$k$$$ 的防御力、攻击力和金币数量。

output.ai: 输出一个整数——刷怪所能获得的最大收益。
