legend: Arkady has a playlist that initially consists of n$$$n$$$ songs, numerated from 1$$$1$$$ to n$$$n$$$ in the order they appear in the playlist. Arkady starts listening to the songs in the playlist one by one, starting from song 1$$$1$$$. The playlist is cycled, i. e. after listening to the last song, Arkady will continue listening from the beginning.

Each song has a genre ai$$$a_i$$$, which is a positive integer. Let Arkady finish listening to a song with genre y$$$y$$$, and the genre of the next-to-last listened song be x$$$x$$$. If gcd(x,y)=1$$$\operatorname{gcd}(x, y) = 1$$$, he deletes the last listened song (with genre y$$$y$$$) from the playlist. After that he continues listening normally, skipping the deleted songs, and forgetting about songs he listened to before. In other words, after he deletes a song, he can't delete the next song immediately.
Here gcd(x,y)$$$\operatorname{gcd}(x, y)$$$ denotes the greatest common divisor (GCD) of integers x$$$x$$$ and y$$$y$$$.

For example, if the initial songs' genres were [5,9,2,10,15]$$$[5, 9, 2, 10, 15]$$$, then the playlist is converted as follows: [5, 9, 2, 10, 15] →$$$\to$$$ [5, 9, 2, 10, 15] →$$$\to$$$ [5, 2, 10, 15] (because gcd(5,9)=1$$$\operatorname{gcd}(5, 9) = 1$$$) →$$$\to$$$ [5, 2, 10, 15] →$$$\to$$$ [5, 2, 10, 15] →$$$\to$$$ [5, 2, 10, 15] →$$$\to$$$ [5, 2, 10, 15] →$$$\to$$$ [5, 2, 10, 15] →$$$\to$$$ [5, 10, 15] (because gcd(5,2)=1$$$\operatorname{gcd}(5, 2) = 1$$$) →$$$\to$$$ [5, 10, 15] →$$$\to$$$ [5, 10, 15] →$$$\to$$$ ... The bold numbers represent the two last played songs. Note that after a song is deleted, Arkady forgets that he listened to that and the previous songs.
Given the initial playlist, please determine which songs are eventually deleted and the order these songs are deleted.
input: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤10000$$$1 \le t \le 10\,000$$$). Description of the test cases follows.
The first line of each test case contains a single integer n$$$n$$$ (1≤n≤105$$$1 \le n \le 10^5$$$) — the number of songs.
The second line contains n$$$n$$$ integers a1,a2,…,an$$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ (1≤ai≤109$$$1 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$) — the genres of the songs.
It is guaranteed that the sum of n$$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed 105$$$10^5$$$.
output: For each test case, print a single line. First, print a single integer k$$$k$$$ — the number of deleted songs. After that print k$$$k$$$ distinct integers: deleted songs in the order of their deletion.
note: Explanation of the first test case is given in the statement.

In the third test case, the playlist is converted as follows: [1, 2] →$$$\to$$$ [1, 2] →$$$\to$$$ [1] (because gcd(1,2)=1$$$\operatorname{gcd}(1, 2) = 1$$$) →$$$\to$$$ [1] →$$$\to$$$ [1] (Arkady listened to the same song twice in a row) →$$$\to$$$ [] (because gcd(1,1)=1$$$\operatorname{gcd}(1, 1) = 1$$$).
The fourth test case is same as the third after deletion of the second song.
In the fifth test case, the same song is listened to over and over again, but since gcd(2,2)≠1$$$\operatorname{gcd}(2, 2) \ne 1$$$, it is not deleted.

legend.ai: Arkady 有一个播放列表，初始包含 n$$$n$$$ 首歌曲，按照它们在播放列表中出现的顺序，从 1$$$1$$$ 到 n$$$n$$$ 编号。Arkady 从歌曲 1$$$1$$$ 开始，逐首听播放列表中的歌曲。播放列表是循环的，也就是说，听完最后一首歌曲后，Arkady 会从开头继续听。

每首歌曲都有一个类型 ai$$$a_i$$$，它是一个正整数。假设 Arkady 听完了一首类型为 y$$$y$$$ 的歌曲，并且倒数第二首听过的歌曲的类型为 x$$$x$$$。如果 gcd(x,y)=1$$$\operatorname{gcd}(x, y) = 1$$$，他就会从播放列表中删除最后听的歌曲(类型为 y$$$y$$$)。之后，他会正常继续听歌，跳过已删除的歌曲，并忘记之前听过的歌曲。换句话说，删除一首歌曲后，他不能立即删除下一首歌曲。
此处 gcd(x,y)$$$\operatorname{gcd}(x, y)$$$ 表示整数 x$$$x$$$ 和 y$$$y$$$ 的最大公约数(GCD)。
给定初始播放列表，请确定最终会被删除的歌曲以及这些歌曲被删除的顺序。

input.ai: 每个测试包含多个测试用例。第一行包含测试用例的数量 t$$$t$$$(1≤t≤10000$$$1 \le t \le 10\,000$$$)。接下来是各测试用例的描述。
每个测试用例的第一行包含一个整数 n$$$n$$$(1≤n≤105$$$1 \le n \le 10^5$$$)，表示歌曲的数量。
第二行包含 n$$$n$$$ 个整数 a1,a2,…,an$$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$(1≤ai≤109$$$1 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$)，表示歌曲的类型。
保证所有测试用例中 n$$$n$$$ 的总和不超过 105$$$10^5$$$。

output.ai: 对于每个测试用例，输出一行。首先输出一个整数 k$$$k$$$，表示被删除的歌曲数量。随后输出 k$$$k$$$ 个互不相同的整数：按照删除顺序排列的被删除歌曲。

note.ai: 题面中给出了第一个测试用例的解释。

在第三个测试用例中，播放列表的转换过程如下：[1, 2] →$$$\to$$$ [1, 2] →$$$\to$$$ [1](因为 gcd(1,2)=1$$$\operatorname{gcd}(1, 2) = 1$$$)→$$$\to$$$ [1] →$$$\to$$$ [1](Arkady 连续两次听了同一首歌)→$$$\to$$$ [](因为 gcd(1,1)=1$$$\operatorname{gcd}(1, 1) = 1$$$)。
删除第二首歌曲后，第四个测试用例与第三个相同。
在第五个测试用例中，同一首歌曲被反复播放，但由于最大公约数(2,2)≠1$$$\operatorname{gcd}(2, 2) \ne 1$$$，因此它不会被删除。

problems.hint: Calculate the number of games when there is $n$ players.

legend: Daniel is organizing a football tournament. He has come up with the following tournament format:

In the first several (possibly zero) stages, while the number of teams is even, they split in pairs and play one game for each pair. At each stage the loser of each pair is eliminated (there are no draws). Such stages are held while the number of teams is even.

Eventually there will be an odd number of teams remaining. If there is one team remaining, it will be declared the winner, and the tournament ends. Otherwise each of the remaining teams will play with each other remaining team once in round robin tournament (if there are x teams, there will be ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/633d3cd6417e5c6e9ea549a0e8c5ec3fedb38b92.png) games), and the tournament ends.

For example, if there were 20 teams initially, they would begin by playing 10 games. So, 10 teams would be eliminated, and the remaining 10 would play 5 games. Then the remaining 5 teams would play 10 games in a round robin tournament. In total there would be 10+5+10=25 games.

Daniel has already booked the stadium for n games. Help him to determine how many teams he should invite so that the tournament needs exactly n games. You should print all possible numbers of teams that will yield exactly n games in ascending order, or -1 if there are no such numbers.
input: The first line contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 1018), the number of games that should be played.
Please, do not use the %lld specifier to read or write 64-bit integers in С++. It is preferred to use the cin, cout streams or the %I64d specifier.
output: Print all possible numbers of invited teams in ascending order, one per line. If exactly n games cannot be played, output one number: -1.

legend.ai: Daniel 正在组织一场足球锦标赛。他设计出了以下赛制：
在最初的若干个阶段中（可能为零个），只要队伍数量为偶数，就将队伍两两分组，每组进行一场比赛。在每个阶段中，每组的失败者都会被淘汰（比赛不会平局）。当队伍数量为偶数时，就会持续进行这样的阶段。
最终，剩余队伍的数量将变为奇数。如果只剩下一支队伍，则它将被宣布为获胜者，锦标赛结束。否则，所有剩余队伍将与其他每支剩余队伍各比赛一次，进行循环赛(如果有 x 支队伍，则会进行 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/633d3cd6417e5c6e9ea549a0e8c5ec3fedb38b92.png) 场比赛)，之后锦标赛结束。
例如，如果最初有 20 支队伍，它们将首先进行 10 场比赛。因此，10 支队伍会被淘汰，剩下的 10 支队伍再进行 5 场比赛。然后，剩下的 5 支队伍将进行 10 场循环赛。总共会进行 10+5+10=25 场比赛。
Daniel 已经为 n 场比赛预订了体育场。请帮助他确定应该邀请多少支队伍，使得锦标赛恰好需要进行 n 场比赛。请按升序输出所有能够恰好进行 n 场比赛的队伍数量；如果不存在这样的数量，则输出 -1。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 10^18），表示需要进行的比赛场数。
请不要在 С++ 中使用 %lld 格式说明符来读写 64 位整数。建议使用 cin、cout 流，或使用 %I64d 格式说明符。

output.ai: 按升序输出所有可能邀请的队伍数量，每行一个。如果无法恰好进行 n 场比赛，则输出一个数：-1。

problems.hint: Use greedy approach. If you order too many pizzas, adjust your solution.

legend: It's another Start[c]up finals, and that means there is pizza to order for the onsite contestants. There are only 2 types of pizza (obviously not, but let's just pretend for the sake of the problem), and all pizzas contain exactly S slices.

It is known that the i-th contestant will eat si slices of pizza, and gain ai happiness for each slice of type 1 pizza they eat, and bi happiness for each slice of type 2 pizza they eat. We can order any number of type 1 and type 2 pizzas, but we want to buy the minimum possible number of pizzas for all of the contestants to be able to eat their required number of slices. Given that restriction, what is the maximum possible total happiness that can be achieved?
input: The first line of input will contain integers N and S (1 ≤ N ≤ 105, 1 ≤ S ≤ 105), the number of contestants and the number of slices per pizza, respectively. N lines follow.

The i-th such line contains integers si, ai, and bi (1 ≤ si ≤ 105, 1 ≤ ai ≤ 105, 1 ≤ bi ≤ 105), the number of slices the i-th contestant will eat, the happiness they will gain from each type 1 slice they eat, and the happiness they will gain from each type 2 slice they eat, respectively.
output: Print the maximum total happiness that can be achieved.
note: In the first example, you only need to buy one pizza. If you buy a type 1 pizza, the total happiness will be 3·5 + 4·6 + 5·9 = 84, and if you buy a type 2 pizza, the total happiness will be 3·7 + 4·7 + 5·5 = 74.

legend.ai: 又到了 Start[c]up 决赛，这意味着需要为现场参赛者订购披萨。披萨只有 2 种类型（显然不止两种，但为了这道题，我们姑且这么假设），并且所有披萨都恰好包含 S 片。
已知第 i 位参赛者将食用 si 片披萨，并且每食用一片 1 型披萨可获得 ai 的幸福值，每食用一片 2 型披萨可获得 bi 的幸福值。我们可以订购任意数量的 1 型和 2 型披萨，但希望为所有参赛者购买尽可能少的披萨，使他们都能吃到所需数量的披萨片。在满足这一限制的前提下，能够获得的总幸福值最大是多少？

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含整数 N 和 S（1 ≤ N ≤ 105，1 ≤ S ≤ 105），分别表示参赛者数量和每个披萨包含的披萨片数量。接下来有 N 行。
其中第 i 行包含整数 si、ai 和 bi（1 ≤ si ≤ 105，1 ≤ ai ≤ 105，1 ≤ bi ≤ 105），分别表示第 i 位参赛者将食用的披萨片数量、他们每食用一片 1 型披萨片所获得的幸福值，以及他们每食用一片 2 型披萨片所获得的幸福值。

output.ai: 输出能够获得的最大总幸福值。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，你只需要购买一个披萨。如果购买 1 型披萨，总幸福值为 3·5 + 4·6 + 5·9 = 84；如果购买 2 型披萨，总幸福值为 3·7 + 4·7 + 5·5 = 74。

problems.hint: Each day provide a condition that the colors of the chosen pairs are the same.

legend: Arseniy is already grown-up and independent. His mother decided to leave him alone for m days and left on a vacation. She have prepared a lot of food, left some money and washed all Arseniy's clothes.

Ten minutes before her leave she realized that it would be also useful to prepare instruction of which particular clothes to wear on each of the days she will be absent. Arseniy's family is a bit weird so all the clothes is enumerated. For example, each of Arseniy's n socks is assigned a unique integer from 1 to n. Thus, the only thing his mother had to do was to write down two integers li and ri for each of the days — the indices of socks to wear on the day i (obviously, li stands for the left foot and ri for the right). Each sock is painted in one of k colors.

When mother already left Arseniy noticed that according to instruction he would wear the socks of different colors on some days. Of course, that is a terrible mistake cause by a rush. Arseniy is a smart boy, and, by some magical coincidence, he posses k jars with the paint — one for each of k colors.

Arseniy wants to repaint some of the socks in such a way, that for each of m days he can follow the mother's instructions and wear the socks of the same color. As he is going to be very busy these days he will have no time to change the colors of any socks so he has to finalize the colors now.

The new computer game Bota-3 was just realised and Arseniy can't wait to play it. What is the minimum number of socks that need their color to be changed in order to make it possible to follow mother's instructions and wear the socks of the same color during each of m days.
input: The first line of input contains three integers n, m and k (2 ≤ n ≤ 200 000, 0 ≤ m ≤ 200 000, 1 ≤ k ≤ 200 000) — the number of socks, the number of days and the number of available colors respectively.
The second line contain n integers c1, c2, ..., cn (1 ≤ ci ≤ k) — current colors of Arseniy's socks.
Each of the following m lines contains two integers li and ri (1 ≤ li, ri ≤ n, li ≠ ri) — indices of socks which Arseniy should wear during the i-th day.
output: Print one integer — the minimum number of socks that should have their colors changed in order to be able to obey the instructions and not make people laugh from watching the socks of different colors.
note: In the first sample, Arseniy can repaint the first and the third socks to the second color.
In the second sample, there is no need to change any colors.

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含三个整数 n、m 和 k（2 ≤ n ≤ 200 000，0 ≤ m ≤ 200 000，1 ≤ k ≤ 200 000）——分别表示袜子的数量、天数和可用颜色的数量。
第二行包含 n 个整数 c1, c2, ..., cn (1 ≤ ci ≤ k) — Arseniy 的袜子的当前颜色。
接下来的 m 行中每行包含两个整数 li 和 ri (1 ≤ li, ri ≤ n, li ≠ ri) — Arseniy 在第 i 天应穿的袜子编号。

output.ai: 输出一个整数 — 为了能够遵守指令，并且不会让人们因看到不同颜色的袜子而发笑，需要改变颜色的袜子的最少数量。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，Arseniy 可以将第一只和第三只袜子重新染色为第二种颜色。
在第二个样例中，不需要改变任何颜色。

legend.ai: Arseniy 已经长大并且独立了。他的母亲决定离开 m 天去度假，把他一个人留在家里。她准备了大量食物，留下了一些钱，并且洗好了 Arseniy 的所有衣服。
在她出发前十分钟，她意识到还有必要准备一份说明，规定在她不在的每一天具体该穿哪件衣服。Arseniy 的家人有点奇怪，所以所有衣服都有编号。例如，Arseniy 的 n 只袜子中的每一只都被分配了从 1 到 n 的唯一整数。因此，他的母亲只需为每一天写下两个整数 li 和 ri——第 i 天要穿的袜子的编号（显然，li 代表左脚，ri 代表右脚）。每只袜子都涂有 k 种颜色之一。
当母亲已经离开后，Arseniy 注意到按照这份说明，他在某些天会穿不同颜色的袜子。当然，这是一个因匆忙而造成的严重错误。Arseniy 是个聪明的男孩，而且由于某种神奇的巧合，他有 k 个颜料罐——对应 k 种颜色各一罐。
Arseniy 想要重新涂一些袜子的颜色，使得在 m 天中的每一天，他都能遵照母亲的说明穿上同一种颜色的袜子。由于这些天他会非常忙，没有时间再去改变任何袜子的颜色，所以他必须现在就确定好所有颜色。
新电脑游戏 Bota-3 刚刚发布，Arseniy 迫不及待想玩。为了能遵从母亲的说明，并在 m 天中的每一天都穿同一种颜色的袜子，最少需要改变多少只袜子的颜色？

problems.hint: Each condition represents $1/2$ segments in the leaves.

statement.title: D. Guess Your Way Out! II

legend: Amr bought a new video game "Guess Your Way Out! II". The goal of the game is to find an exit from the maze that looks like a perfect binary tree of height h. The player is initially standing at the root of the tree and the exit from the tree is located at some leaf node.
Let's index all the nodes of the tree such that
The root is number 1
Each internal node i (i ≤ 2h - 1 - 1) will have a left child with index = 2i and a right child with index = 2i + 1

The level of a node is defined as 1 for a root, or 1 + level of parent of the node otherwise. The vertices of the level h are called leaves. The exit to the maze is located at some leaf node n, the player doesn't know where the exit is so he has to guess his way out!

In the new version of the game the player is allowed to ask questions on the format "Does the ancestor(exit, i) node number belong to the range [L, R]?". Here ancestor(v, i) is the ancestor of a node v that located in the level i. The game will answer with "Yes" or "No" only. The game is designed such that it doesn't always answer correctly, and sometimes it cheats to confuse the player!.

Amr asked a lot of questions and got confused by all these answers, so he asked you to help him. Given the questions and its answers, can you identify whether the game is telling contradictory information or not? If the information is not contradictory and the exit node can be determined uniquely, output its number. If the information is not contradictory, but the exit node isn't defined uniquely, output that the number of questions is not sufficient. Otherwise output that the information is contradictory.
input: The first line contains two integers h, q (1 ≤ h ≤ 50, 0 ≤ q ≤ 105), the height of the tree and the number of questions respectively.

The next q lines will contain four integers each i, L, R, ans (1 ≤ i ≤ h, 2i - 1 ≤ L ≤ R ≤ 2i - 1, ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/efee5db22bd8e5a4848907ab50b074b75fa6f3c7.png)), representing a question as described in the statement with its answer (ans = 1 if the answer is "Yes" and ans = 0 if the answer is "No").
output: If the information provided by the game is contradictory output "Game cheated!" without the quotes.
Else if you can uniquely identify the exit to the maze output its index.
Otherwise output "Data not sufficient!" without the quotes.
note: Node u is an ancestor of node v if and only if
u is the same node as v,
u is the parent of node v,
or u is an ancestor of the parent of node v.
In the first sample test there are 4 leaf nodes 4, 5, 6, 7. The first question says that the node isn't in the range [4, 6] so the exit is node number 7.

In the second sample test there are 8 leaf nodes. After the first question the exit is in the range [10, 14]. After the second and the third questions only node number 14 is correct. Check the picture below to fully understand.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ed7035c51a810ae46fc6ef9e8e8319d343bfcfa9.png)

note.ai: 当且仅当节点 u 是节点 v 的祖先，
u 与 v 是同一个节点，
u 是节点 v 的父节点，
或者 u 是节点 v 的父节点的祖先。
在第一个样例测试中，有 4 个叶子节点 4、5、6、7。第一个问题说明该节点不在范围 [4, 6] 内，因此出口是编号为 7 的节点。
在第二个样例测试中，有 8 个叶子节点。第一个问题之后，出口位于范围 [10, 14] 内。在第二个和第三个问题之后，只有编号为 14 的节点是正确的。查看下面的图片以便完全理解。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ed7035c51a810ae46fc6ef9e8e8319d343bfcfa9.png)

legend.ai: Amr 买了一款名为“猜出你的路！II”的新电子游戏。游戏的目标是从一个看起来像高度为 h 的完美二叉树的迷宫中找到出口。玩家最初站在树的根节点，树的出口位于某个叶节点处。
现在，为树中的所有节点编号，使得
根节点的编号为 1。
每个内部节点 i（i ≤ 2h - 1 - 1）都有一个编号为 2i 的左孩子和一个编号为 2i + 1 的右孩子。
节点的层数定义如下：根节点的层数为 1；对于其他节点，其层数为其父节点层数加 1。位于第 h 层的顶点称为叶节点。迷宫的出口位于某个叶节点 n，但玩家不知道出口在哪里，因此他必须猜出逃生路线！
在游戏的新版本中，玩家可以询问格式为“节点编号 ancestor(exit, i) 是否属于区间 [L, R]？”的问题。其中，ancestor(v, i) 是节点 v 在第 i 层的祖先节点。游戏只会回答“Yes”或“No”。游戏被设计成不会始终正确回答，有时还会为了迷惑玩家而撒谎！
Amr 提出了许多问题，并被这些回答弄糊涂了，因此他请你帮助他。给定这些问题及其回答，你能判断游戏是否提供了相互矛盾的信息吗？如果信息不矛盾且出口节点可以唯一确定，则输出其编号。如果信息不矛盾，但出口节点无法唯一确定，则输出问题数量不足。否则输出信息相互矛盾。

input.ai: 第一行包含两个整数 h、q（1 ≤ h ≤ 50，0 ≤ q ≤ 105），分别表示树的高度和问题的数量。

接下来的 q 行每行包含四个整数 i、L、R、ans(1 ≤ i ≤ h，2i - 1 ≤ L ≤ R ≤ 2i - 1，![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/efee5db22bd8e5a4848907ab50b074b75fa6f3c7.png))，表示题面中所描述的一个问题及其回答(如果回答是“Yes”，则 ans = 1；如果回答是“No”，则 ans = 0)。

output.ai: 如果游戏提供的信息相互矛盾，则输出不带引号的“Game cheated!”。
否则，如果你可以唯一确定迷宫出口，则输出其编号。
否则，输出不带引号的“Data not sufficient!”。

titleZh.ai: D. Guess Your Way Out! II

problems.hint: Actually, you can find out each $n\bmod i$.

legend: Imp is watching a documentary about cave painting.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/8ec8a9fff94ac26b2c760e63823e96e9e224b87b.png)

Some numbers, carved in chaotic order, immediately attracted his attention. Imp rapidly proposed a guess that they are the remainders of division of a number n by all integers i from 1 to k. Unfortunately, there are too many integers to analyze for Imp.

Imp wants you to check whether all these remainders are distinct. Formally, he wants to check, if all ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/af9bf37ade74cbe9830bd367f7c2aeaf738ffd73.png), 1 ≤ i ≤ k, are distinct, i. e. there is no such pair (i, j) that:

![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d2e5b79d0b20795f51610e384d5973d0a2a091dd.png), where ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/cd0226f6733233da1ba1f4844ccc38fcceb2fd37.png) is the remainder of division x by y.
input: The only line contains two integers n, k (1 ≤ n, k ≤ 1018).
output: Print "Yes", if all the remainders are distinct, and "No" otherwise.
You can print each letter in arbitrary case (lower or upper).
note: In the first sample remainders modulo 1 and 4 coincide.

legend.ai: Imp 正在观看一部关于洞穴壁画的纪录片。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/8ec8a9fff94ac26b2c760e63823e96e9e224b87b.png)
一些以混乱顺序刻下的数字立刻吸引了他的注意。Imp 很快猜测，这些数字是某个数 n 分别除以从 1 到 k 的所有整数 i 所得到的余数。然而，要分析的整数太多了，Imp 无法完成。
Imp 想让你检查所有这些余数是否互不相同。形式化地说，他想检查对于所有 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/af9bf37ade74cbe9830bd367f7c2aeaf738ffd73.png)，1 ≤ i ≤ k，它们是否互不相同，即不存在满足以下条件的数对 (i, j)：
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d2e5b79d0b20795f51610e384d5973d0a2a091dd.png)，其中 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/cd0226f6733233da1ba1f4844ccc38fcceb2fd37.png) 是 x 除以 y 的余数。

input.ai: 唯一一行包含两个整数 n、k（1 ≤ n，k ≤ 1018）。

output.ai: 如果所有余数互不相同，则输出 "Yes"，否则输出 "No"。
每个字母的大小写可以任意（大写或小写）。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，模 1 和模 4 的余数相同。

problems.hint: $10^7$ should be used. Find out the maximum number of students who can get at least $k$ slices for each $k$.

legend: Santa Claus has n tangerines, and the i-th of them consists of exactly ai slices. Santa Claus came to a school which has k pupils. Santa decided to treat them with tangerines.

However, there can be too few tangerines to present at least one tangerine to each pupil. So Santa decided to divide tangerines into parts so that no one will be offended. In order to do this, he can divide a tangerine or any existing part into two smaller equal parts. If the number of slices in the part he wants to split is odd, then one of the resulting parts will have one slice more than the other. It's forbidden to divide a part consisting of only one slice.

Santa Claus wants to present to everyone either a whole tangerine or exactly one part of it (that also means that everyone must get a positive number of slices). One or several tangerines or their parts may stay with Santa.
Let bi be the number of slices the i-th pupil has in the end. Let Santa's joy be the minimum among all bi's.
Your task is to find the maximum possible joy Santa can have after he treats everyone with tangerines (or their parts).
input: The first line contains two positive integers n and k (1 ≤ n ≤ 106, 1 ≤ k ≤ 2·109) denoting the number of tangerines and the number of pupils, respectively.
The second line consists of n positive integers a1, a2, ..., an (1 ≤ ai ≤ 107), where ai stands for the number of slices the i-th tangerine consists of.
output: If there's no way to present a tangerine or a part of tangerine to everyone, print -1. Otherwise, print the maximum possible joy that Santa can have.
note: In the first example Santa should divide the second tangerine into two parts with 5 and 4 slices. After that he can present the part with 5 slices to the first pupil and the whole first tangerine (with 5 slices, too) to the second pupil.
In the second example Santa should divide both tangerines, so that he'll be able to present two parts with 6 slices and two parts with 7 slices.
In the third example Santa Claus can't present 2 slices to 3 pupils in such a way that everyone will have anything.

input.ai: 第一行包含两个正整数 n 和 k（1 ≤ n ≤ 106，1 ≤ k ≤ 2·109），分别表示橘子的数量和学生的数量。
第二行包含 n 个正整数 a1， a2， ...， an（1 ≤ ai ≤ 107），其中 ai 表示第 i 个橘子由多少瓣组成。

output.ai: 如果无法给每个人一个橘子或橘子的一部分，则输出 -1。否则，输出圣诞老人可能获得的最大快乐值。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，圣诞老人应将第二个橘子分成两部分，分别包含 5 瓣和 4 瓣。之后，他可以将包含 5 瓣的部分送给第一个学生，并将完整的第一个橘子（同样包含 5 瓣）送给第二个学生。
在第二个样例中，圣诞老人应将两个橘子都分开，这样他就能得到两份包含 6 瓣的部分和两份包含 7 瓣的部分。
在第三个样例中，圣诞老人无法以一种让每个人都得到至少一些橘子瓣的方式，将 2 瓣橘子分给 3 个学生。

legend.ai: 圣诞老人有 n 个橘子，其中第 i 个橘子恰好由 ai 瓣组成。圣诞老人来到了一所学校，这所学校有 k 名学生。圣诞老人决定把橘子分给他们。
然而，橘子的数量可能太少，无法保证每名学生至少得到一个完整的橘子。因此，圣诞老人决定将橘子分成若干部分，以免有人感到不满。为此，他可以将一个橘子或任意已有的部分分成两个大小尽可能相等的更小部分。如果他想分割的部分包含奇数瓣，那么分割后其中一部分将比另一部分多一瓣。禁止分割只包含一瓣的部分。
圣诞老人希望给每个人分发一个完整的橘子，或某个橘子恰好一个部分（这也意味着每个人都必须得到正数瓣）。可以有一个或多个橘子或它们的部分留在圣诞老人手中。
设 bi 表示第 i 名学生最终得到的瓣数。令圣诞老人的快乐值为所有 bi 中的最小值。
你的任务是求出圣诞老人将橘子（或它们的部分）分给所有人后，可能获得的最大快乐值。

problems.hint: Reduce the conditions to one.

legend: Polycarp has invited n$$$n$$$ friends to celebrate the New Year. During the celebration, he decided to take a group photo of all his friends. Each friend can stand or lie on the side.

Each friend is characterized by two values hi$$$h_i$$$ (their height) and wi$$$w_i$$$ (their width). On the photo the i$$$i$$$-th friend will occupy a rectangle hi×wi$$$h_i \times w_i$$$ (if they are standing) or wi×hi$$$w_i \times h_i$$$ (if they are lying on the side).

The j$$$j$$$-th friend can be placed in front of the i$$$i$$$-th friend on the photo if his rectangle is lower and narrower than the rectangle of the i$$$i$$$-th friend. Formally, at least one of the following conditions must be fulfilled:
hj<hi$$$h_j  \lt  h_i$$$ and wj<wi$$$w_j  \lt  w_i$$$ (both friends are standing or both are lying);
wj<hi$$$w_j  \lt  h_i$$$ and hj<wi$$$h_j  \lt  w_i$$$ (one of the friends is standing and the other is lying).
the first friend can be placed in front of the second: w1<h2$$$w_1  \lt  h_2$$$ and h1<w2$$$h_1  \lt  w_2$$$ (one of the them is standing and the other one is lying);
the third friend can be placed in front of the second: h3<h2$$$h_3  \lt  h_2$$$ and w3<w2$$$w_3  \lt  w_2$$$ (both friends are standing or both are lying).
In other cases, the person in the foreground will overlap the person in the background.
Help Polycarp for each i$$$i$$$ find any j$$$j$$$, such that the j$$$j$$$-th friend can be located in front of the i$$$i$$$-th friend (i.e. at least one of the conditions above is fulfilled).

Please note that you do not need to find the arrangement of all people for a group photo. You just need to find for each friend i$$$i$$$ any other friend j$$$j$$$ who can be located in front of him. Think about it as you need to solve n$$$n$$$ separate independent subproblems.
input: The first line contains one integer t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤104$$$1 \leq t \leq 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. Then t$$$t$$$ test cases follow.
The first line of each test case contains one integer n$$$n$$$ (1≤n≤2⋅105$$$1 \leq n \leq 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of friends.

This is followed by n$$$n$$$ lines, each of which contains a description of the corresponding friend. Each friend is described by two integers hi$$$h_i$$$ and wi$$$w_i$$$ (1≤hi,wi≤109$$$1 \leq h_i, w_i \leq 10^9$$$) — height and width of the i$$$i$$$-th friend, respectively.
It is guaranteed that the sum of n$$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed 2⋅105$$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output: For each test case output n$$$n$$$ integers on a separate line, where the i$$$i$$$-th number is the index of a friend that can be placed in front of the i$$$i$$$-th. If there is no such friend, then output -1.
If there are several answers, output any.
note: The first test case is described in the statement.
In the third test case, the following answers are also correct:

legend.ai: Polycarp 邀请了 n$$$n$$$ 位朋友来庆祝新年。在庆祝活动期间，他决定给所有朋友拍一张合影。每位朋友可以站立，也可以侧躺。
每位朋友由两个值 hi$$$h_i$$$(他们的身高)和 wi$$$w_i$$$(他们的宽度)刻画。在照片中，第 i$$$i$$$ 位朋友将占据一个 hi×wi$$$h_i \times w_i$$$ 的矩形(如果他站立)或一个 wi×hi$$$w_i \times h_i$$$ 的矩形(如果他侧躺)。
如果第 j$$$j$$$ 位朋友的矩形比第 i$$$i$$$ 位朋友的矩形更矮且更窄，那么可以将他放在照片中第 i$$$i$$$ 位朋友的前面。形式化地说，以下条件中至少有一个必须成立：
hj<hi$$$h_j  \lt  h_i$$$ 且 wj<wi$$$w_j  \lt  w_i$$$(两位朋友都站立或都侧躺)；
wj<hi$$$w_j  \lt  h_i$$$ 且 hj<wi$$$h_j  \lt  w_i$$$(一位朋友站立，另一位朋友侧躺)。
第一个朋友可以放在第二个朋友前面：w1<h2$$$w_1  \lt  h_2$$$ 且 h1<w2$$$h_1  \lt  w_2$$$(其中一个人站着，另一个人躺着)；
第三个朋友可以放在第二个朋友前面：h3<h2$$$h_3  \lt  h_2$$$ 且 w3<w2$$$w_3  \lt  w_2$$$(两个人都站着或都躺着)。
在其他情况下，前景中的人会与背景中的人重叠。
请帮助 Polycarp 对于每个 i$$$i$$$ 找到任意一个 j$$$j$$$，使得第 j$$$j$$$ 个朋友可以位于第 i$$$i$$$ 个朋友的前面(即上述条件中至少有一个成立)。
请注意，你不需要找出一张集体照片中所有人的排列方式。你只需要对于每个朋友 i$$$i$$$ 找到任意一个可以位于他前面的其他朋友 j$$$j$$$。可以把它看作需要解决 n$$$n$$$ 个相互独立的子问题。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 t$$$t$$$(1≤t≤104$$$1 \leq t \leq 10^4$$$)，表示测试用例的数量。接下来是 t$$$t$$$ 个测试用例。
每个测试用例的第一行包含一个整数 n$$$n$$$(1≤n≤2⋅105$$$1 \leq n \leq 2 \cdot 10^5$$$)，表示朋友的数量。
接下来有 n$$$n$$$ 行，每行包含对应朋友的描述。每个朋友由两个整数 hi$$$h_i$$$ 和 wi$$$w_i$$$(1≤hi,wi≤109$$$1 \leq h_i, w_i \leq 10^9$$$)描述，分别表示第 i$$$i$$$ 个朋友的身高和宽度。
保证所有测试用例中 n$$$n$$$ 的总和不超过 2⋅105$$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$。

output.ai: 对于每个测试用例，在单独一行中输出 n$$$n$$$ 个整数，其中第 i$$$i$$$ 个数是一个可以放在第 i$$$i$$$ 个朋友前面的朋友的编号。如果不存在这样的朋友，则输出 -1。
如果有多个答案，输出任意一个即可。

note.ai: 题目中描述了第一个测试用例。
在第三个测试用例中，以下答案也都是正确的：

problems.hint: Inequalities are easy to be dealt with, so process the equalities first.

legend: Mr. Apple, a gourmet, works as editor-in-chief of a gastronomic periodical. He travels around the world, tasting new delights of famous chefs from the most fashionable restaurants. Mr. Apple has his own signature method of review  — in each restaurant Mr. Apple orders two sets of dishes on two different days. All the dishes are different, because Mr. Apple doesn't like to eat the same food. For each pair of dishes from different days he remembers exactly which was better, or that they were of the same quality. After this the gourmet evaluates each dish with a positive integer.

Once, during a revision of a restaurant of Celtic medieval cuisine named «Poisson», that serves chestnut soup with fir, warm soda bread, spicy lemon pie and other folk food, Mr. Apple was very pleasantly surprised the gourmet with its variety of menu, and hence ordered too much. Now he's confused about evaluating dishes.

The gourmet tasted a set of n$$$n$$$ dishes on the first day and a set of m$$$m$$$ dishes on the second day. He made a table a$$$a$$$ of size n×m$$$n \times m$$$, in which he described his impressions. If, according to the expert, dish i$$$i$$$ from the first set was better than dish j$$$j$$$ from the second set, then aij$$$a_{ij}$$$ is equal to ">", in the opposite case aij$$$a_{ij}$$$ is equal to "<". Dishes also may be equally good, in this case aij$$$a_{ij}$$$ is "=".

Now Mr. Apple wants you to help him to evaluate every dish. Since Mr. Apple is very strict, he will evaluate the dishes so that the maximal number used is as small as possible. But Mr. Apple also is very fair, so he never evaluates the dishes so that it goes against his feelings. In other words, if aij$$$a_{ij}$$$ is "<", then the number assigned to dish i$$$i$$$ from the first set should be less than the number of dish j$$$j$$$ from the second set, if aij$$$a_{ij}$$$ is ">", then it should be greater, and finally if aij$$$a_{ij}$$$ is "=", then the numbers should be the same.
Help Mr. Apple to evaluate each dish from both sets so that it is consistent with his feelings, or determine that this is impossible.
input: The first line contains integers n$$$n$$$ and m$$$m$$$ (1≤n,m≤1000$$$1 \leq n, m \leq 1000$$$) — the number of dishes in both days.
Each of the next n$$$n$$$ lines contains a string of m$$$m$$$ symbols. The j$$$j$$$-th symbol on i$$$i$$$-th line is aij$$$a_{ij}$$$. All strings consist only of "<", ">" and "=".
output: The first line of output should contain "Yes", if it's possible to do a correct evaluation for all the dishes, or "No" otherwise.

If case an answer exist, on the second line print n$$$n$$$ integers — evaluations of dishes from the first set, and on the third line print m$$$m$$$ integers — evaluations of dishes from the second set.
note: In the first sample, all dishes of the first day are better than dishes of the second day. So, the highest score will be 2$$$2$$$, for all dishes of the first day.
In the third sample, the table is contradictory — there is no possible evaluation of the dishes that satisfies it.

legend.ai: Apple 先生是一位美食家，担任美食杂志的主编。他环游世界，品尝各家最时尚餐厅中著名厨师制作的新奇美食。Apple 先生有自己独特的评审方法：在每家餐厅，他会在不同的两天分别点两套菜。所有菜品都不相同，因为 Apple 先生不喜欢吃同样的食物。对于来自不同日期的每一对菜品，他都会准确记住哪一道更好，或者它们的质量相同。之后，这位美食家会为每道菜赋予一个正整数评价。
有一次，在评审一家名为 «Poisson» 的凯尔特中世纪风味餐厅时，这家餐厅供应松针栗子汤、温热的苏打面包、香辣柠檬派以及其他民间美食。餐厅丰富多样的菜单给 Apple 先生带来了极大的惊喜，于是他点了太多菜。现在，他对如何评价这些菜品感到困惑。

这位美食家第一天品尝了 n$$$n$$$ 道菜，第二天品尝了 m$$$m$$$ 道菜。他制作了一个大小为 n×m$$$n \times m$$$ 的表格 a$$$a$$$，其中记录了自己的感受。如果根据这位专家的判断，第一套菜中的第 i$$$i$$$ 道菜比第二套菜中的第 j$$$j$$$ 道菜更好，那么 aij$$$a_{ij}$$$ 等于“>”；反之，aij$$$a_{ij}$$$ 等于“<”。菜品也可能同样好，在这种情况下，aij$$$a_{ij}$$$ 等于“=”。

现在，Apple 先生希望你帮助他为每道菜进行评估。由于 Apple 先生非常严格，他会以使所使用的最大数字尽可能小的方式评估这些菜。但 Apple 先生也非常公平，因此他从不会以违背自己感受的方式评估这些菜。换句话说，如果 aij$$$a_{ij}$$$ 为 "<"，那么第一组中分配给第 i 道菜$$$i$$$的数字应小于第二组中第 j 道菜$$$j$$$的数字；如果 aij$$$a_{ij}$$$ 为 ">"，那么它应大于该数字；最后，如果 aij$$$a_{ij}$$$ 为 "="，那么两个数字应相同。
请帮助 Apple 先生为两套菜中的每一道菜赋值，使其符合他的感受，或者确定这是不可能的。

input.ai: 第一行包含两个整数 n$$$n$$$ 和 m$$$m$$$(1≤n,m≤1000$$$1 \leq n, m \leq 1000$$$)，表示两天的菜品数量。
接下来的 n$$$n$$$ 行中，每行包含一个由 m$$$m$$$ 个符号组成的字符串。第 i$$$i$$$ 行的第 j$$$j$$$ 个符号为 aij$$$a_{ij}$$$。所有字符串仅由 "<"、">" 和 "=" 组成。

output.ai: 如果可以正确评价所有菜品，输出的第一行应包含 "Yes"，否则输出 "No"。
如果存在答案，则在第二行输出 n$$$n$$$ 个整数，表示第一组菜品的评价；在第三行输出 m$$$m$$$ 个整数，表示第二组菜品的评价。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，第一天的所有菜品都优于第二天的菜品。因此，第一天所有菜品的最高评价均为 2$$$2$$$。
在第三个样例中，表格存在矛盾，不存在满足该表格的菜品评价方案。

problems.hint: If a graph is not connected, its complement is connected.

legend: Given three numbers n,a,b$$$n, a, b$$$. You need to find an adjacency matrix of such an undirected graph that the number of components in it is equal to a$$$a$$$, and the number of components in its complement is b$$$b$$$. The matrix must be symmetric, and all digits on the main diagonal must be zeroes.
In an undirected graph loops (edges from a vertex to itself) are not allowed. It can be at most one edge between a pair of vertices.

The adjacency matrix of an undirected graph is a square matrix of size n$$$n$$$ consisting only of "0" and "1", where n$$$n$$$ is the number of vertices of the graph and the i$$$i$$$-th row and the i$$$i$$$-th column correspond to the i$$$i$$$-th vertex of the graph. The cell (i,j)$$$(i,j)$$$ of the adjacency matrix contains 1$$$1$$$ if and only if the i$$$i$$$-th and j$$$j$$$-th vertices in the graph are connected by an edge.

A connected component is a set of vertices X$$$X$$$ such that for every two vertices from this set there exists at least one path in the graph connecting this pair of vertices, but adding any other vertex to X$$$X$$$ violates this rule.
The complement or inverse of a graph G$$$G$$$ is a graph H$$$H$$$ on the same vertices such that two distinct vertices of H$$$H$$$ are adjacent if and only if they are not adjacent in G$$$G$$$.
input: In a single line, three numbers are given n,a,b(1≤n≤1000,1≤a,b≤n)$$$n, a, b \,(1 \le n \le 1000, 1 \le a, b \le n)$$$: is the number of vertexes of the graph, the required number of connectivity components in it, and the required amount of the connectivity component in it's complement.
output: If there is no graph that satisfies these constraints on a single line, print "NO" (without quotes).

Otherwise, on the first line, print "YES"(without quotes). In each of the next n$$$n$$$ lines, output n$$$n$$$ digits such that j$$$j$$$-th digit of i$$$i$$$-th line must be 1$$$1$$$ if and only if there is an edge between vertices i$$$i$$$ and j$$$j$$$ in G$$$G$$$ (and 0$$$0$$$ otherwise). Note that the matrix must be symmetric, and all digits on the main diagonal must be zeroes.
If there are several matrices that satisfy the conditions — output any of them.

legend.ai: 给定三个数 n、a、b$$$n, a, b$$$。你需要找出这样一个无向图的邻接矩阵，使其连通分量的数量等于 a$$$a$$$，其补图中的连通分量数量等于 b$$$b$$$。该矩阵必须是对称矩阵，且主对角线上的所有数字都必须为 0。

legend: Each evening Roma plays online poker on his favourite website. The rules of poker on this website are a bit strange: there are always two players in a hand, there are no bets, and the winner takes 1 virtual bourle from the loser.

Last evening Roma started to play poker. He decided to spend no more than k virtual bourles — he will stop immediately if the number of his loses exceeds the number of his wins by k. Also Roma will leave the game if he wins enough money for the evening, i.e. if the number of wins exceeds the number of loses by k.

Next morning Roma found a piece of paper with a sequence on it representing his results. Roma doesn't remember the results exactly, and some characters in the sequence are written in a way such that it's impossible to recognize this character, so Roma can't recall whether he won k bourles or he lost.

The sequence written by Roma is a string s consisting of characters W (Roma won the corresponding hand), L (Roma lost), D (draw) and ? (unknown result). Roma wants to restore any valid sequence by changing all ? characters to W, L or D. The sequence is called valid if all these conditions are met:
In the end the absolute difference between the number of wins and loses is equal to k;
There is no hand such that the absolute difference before this hand was equal to k.
Help Roma to restore any such sequence.
input: The first line contains two numbers n (the length of Roma's sequence) and k (1 ≤ n, k ≤ 1000).
The second line contains the sequence s consisting of characters W, L, D and ?. There are exactly n characters in this sequence.
output: If there is no valid sequence that can be obtained from s by replacing all ? characters by W, L or D, print NO.
Otherwise print this sequence. If there are multiple answers, print any of them.

legend.ai: 每天晚上，Roma 都会在他最喜欢的网站上玩在线扑克。这个网站上的扑克规则有些奇怪：一局中始终有两名玩家，不下注，获胜者会从失败者那里赢得 1 个虚拟 bourle。
昨晚 Roma 开始玩扑克。他决定最多花费 k 个虚拟 bourle；如果他的失败次数超过获胜次数达到 k 次，他就会立即停止游戏。此外，如果他在当晚赢得了足够多的钱，也就是获胜次数超过失败次数达到 k 次，Roma 也会离开游戏。
第二天早上，Roma 发现了一张纸，上面写着一个表示他比赛结果的序列。Roma 不记得具体的比赛结果了，而且序列中的一些字符书写得难以辨认，因此 Roma 无法回忆起自己究竟赢了 k 局还是输了 k 局。
Roma 写下的序列是一个由字符 W（Roma 赢下对应的一局）、L（Roma 输掉对应的一局）、D（平局）和 ?（未知结果）组成的字符串 s。Roma 想要通过将所有 ? 字符改为 W、L 或 D，来还原出任意一个合法的序列。如果满足以下所有条件，则称该序列是合法的：
最终，获胜局数与失败局数之差的绝对值等于 k；
不存在这样的一局：在这一局之前，获胜局数与失败局数之差的绝对值等于 k。
请帮助 Roma 还原出任意一个这样的序列。

input.ai: 第一行包含两个整数 n（Roma 的序列长度）和 k（1 ≤ n，k ≤ 1000）。
第二行包含由字符 W、L、D 和 ? 组成的序列 s。该序列中恰好有 n 个字符。

output.ai: 如果不存在通过将 s 中所有的 ? 替换为 W、L 或 D 所得到的合法序列，则输出 NO。
否则输出该序列。如果有多个答案，输出其中任意一个即可。

problems.hint: If we fix the number of rented bikes, it is easy to choose which bikes to rent.

legend: A group of n schoolboys decided to ride bikes. As nobody of them has a bike, the boys need to rent them.
The renting site offered them m bikes. The renting price is different for different bikes, renting the j-th bike costs pj rubles.

In total, the boys' shared budget is a rubles. Besides, each of them has his own personal money, the i-th boy has bi personal rubles. The shared budget can be spent on any schoolchildren arbitrarily, but each boy's personal money can be spent on renting only this boy's bike.
Each boy can rent at most one bike, one cannot give his bike to somebody else.
What maximum number of schoolboys will be able to ride bikes? What minimum sum of personal money will they have to spend in total to let as many schoolchildren ride bikes as possible?
input: The first line of the input contains three integers n, m and a (1 ≤ n, m ≤ 105; 0 ≤ a ≤ 109). The second line contains the sequence of integers b1, b2, ..., bn (1 ≤ bi ≤ 104), where bi is the amount of the i-th boy's personal money. The third line contains the sequence of integers p1, p2, ..., pm (1 ≤ pj ≤ 109), where pj is the price for renting the j-th bike.
output: Print two integers r and s, where r is the maximum number of schoolboys that can rent a bike and s is the minimum total personal money needed to rent r bikes. If the schoolchildren cannot rent any bikes, then r = s = 0.
note: In the first sample both schoolchildren can rent a bike. For instance, they can split the shared budget in half (5 rubles each). In this case one of them will have to pay 1 ruble from the personal money and the other one will have to pay 2 rubles from the personal money. In total, they spend 3 rubles of their personal money. This way of distribution of money minimizes the amount of spent personal money.

legend.ai: 一群由 n 名男学生组成的小组决定去骑自行车。由于他们没有人拥有自行车，因此这些男孩需要租借自行车。
租借网站为他们提供了 m 辆自行车。不同自行车的租借价格不同，租借第 j 辆自行车需要花费 p_j 卢布。
男孩们共有的预算为 a 卢布。此外，每个人还有自己的个人资金，第 i 个男孩有 bi 卢布的个人资金。共有预算可以任意花费在任何学生身上，但每个男孩的个人资金只能用于租借这个男孩自己的自行车。
每个男孩最多可以租借一辆自行车，并且不能将自己的自行车让给其他人。
最多有多少名学生能够骑上自行车？为了让尽可能多的学生骑上自行车，他们总共需要花费的个人资金最少是多少？

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含三个整数 n、m 和 a（1 ≤ n，m ≤ 105；0 ≤ a ≤ 109）。第二行包含整数序列 b1， b2， ...， bn（1 ≤ bi ≤ 104），其中 bi 表示第 i 个男孩的个人资金数额。第三行包含整数序列 p1， p2， ...， pm（1 ≤ pj ≤ 109），其中 pj 表示租借第 j 辆自行车的价格。

output.ai: 输出两个整数 r 和 s，其中 r 表示能够租借自行车的学生数量的最大值，s 表示租借 r 辆自行车所需的最少个人资金总额。如果学生们无法租借任何自行车，则 r = s = 0。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，两名学生都可以租借自行车。例如，他们可以将共有预算平分，每人 5 卢布。在这种情况下，其中一人需要从个人资金中支付 1 卢布，另一人需要从个人资金中支付 2 卢布。总计，他们需要花费 3 卢布的个人资金。这种资金分配方式使个人资金的花费总额最少。

statement.title: C. Tokitsukaze and Two Colorful Tapes

legend: Tokitsukaze has two colorful tapes. There are n$$$n$$$ distinct colors, numbered 1$$$1$$$ through n$$$n$$$, and each color appears exactly once on each of the two tapes. Denote the color of the i$$$i$$$-th position of the first tape as cai$$$ca_i$$$, and the color of the i$$$i$$$-th position of the second tape as cbi$$$cb_i$$$.

Now Tokitsukaze wants to select each color an integer value from 1$$$1$$$ to n$$$n$$$, distinct for all the colors. After that she will put down the color values in each colored position on the tapes. Denote the number of the i$$$i$$$-th position of the first tape as numai$$$numa_i$$$, and the number of the i$$$i$$$-th position of the second tape as numbi$$$numb_i$$$.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c43e6f42a4cd7b8a218983155bef73e1fb7807c9.png)

For example, for the above picture, assuming that the color red has value x$$$x$$$ (1≤x≤n$$$1 \leq x \leq n$$$), it appears at the 1$$$1$$$-st position of the first tape and the 3$$$3$$$-rd position of the second tape, so numa1=numb3=x$$$numa_1=numb_3=x$$$.
Note that each color i$$$i$$$ from 1$$$1$$$ to n$$$n$$$ should have a distinct value, and the same color which appears in both tapes has the same value.
After labeling each color, the beauty of the two tapes is calculated as n∑i=1|numai−numbi|.$$\sum_{i=1}^{n}|numa_i-numb_i|.$$
Please help Tokitsukaze to find the highest possible beauty.
input: The first contains a single positive integer t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤104$$$1 \leq t \leq 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases.
For each test case, the first line contains a single integer n$$$n$$$ (1≤n≤105$$$1\leq n \leq 10^5$$$) — the number of colors.

The second line contains n$$$n$$$ integers ca1,ca2,…,can$$$ca_1, ca_2, \ldots, ca_n$$$ (1≤cai≤n$$$1 \leq ca_i \leq n$$$) — the color of each position of the first tape. It is guaranteed that ca$$$ca$$$ is a permutation.

The third line contains n$$$n$$$ integers cb1,cb2,…,cbn$$$cb_1, cb_2, \ldots, cb_n$$$ (1≤cbi≤n$$$1 \leq cb_i \leq n$$$) — the color of each position of the second tape. It is guaranteed that cb$$$cb$$$ is a permutation.
It is guaranteed that the sum of n$$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed 2⋅105$$$2 \cdot 10^{5}$$$.
output: For each test case, print a single integer — the highest possible beauty.
note: An optimal solution for the first test case is shown in the following figure:
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/33efd0f1d29332f2920727cec796463f3416ab5a.png)
The beauty is |4−3|+|3−5|+|2−4|+|5−2|+|1−6|+|6−1|=18$$$\left|4-3 \right|+\left|3-5 \right|+\left|2-4 \right|+\left|5-2 \right|+\left|1-6 \right|+\left|6-1 \right|=18$$$.
An optimal solution for the second test case is shown in the following figure:
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/be704f7644a30ed1c595245dc0cc4754a2fa91cd.png)
The beauty is |2−2|+|1−6|+|3−3|+|6−1|+|4−4|+|5−5|=10$$$\left|2-2 \right|+\left|1-6 \right|+\left|3-3 \right|+\left|6-1 \right|+\left|4-4 \right|+\left|5-5 \right|=10$$$.

现在，Tokitsukaze 想要为每种颜色选择一个从 1$$$1$$$ 到 n$$$n$$$ 的整数值，且所有颜色的值互不相同。之后，她会将颜色对应的值写在胶带上相应的彩色位置中。将第一条胶带第 i$$$i$$$ 个位置上的数字记为 numai$$$numa_i$$$，将第二条胶带第 i$$$i$$$ 个位置上的数字记为 numbi$$$numb_i$$$。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c43e6f42a4cd7b8a218983155bef73e1fb7807c9.png)
例如，对于上图，假设红色的值为 x$$$x$$$(1≤x≤n$$$1 \leq x \leq n$$$)，它出现在第一条胶带的第 1$$$1$$$ 个位置和第二条胶带的第 3$$$3$$$ 个位置，因此 numa1=numb3=x$$$numa_1=numb_3=x$$$。

problems.hint: For each day, if you skip $k$ lessons, there is a maximum amount of time you can save.

legend: Ivan is a student at Berland State University (BSU). There are n days in Berland week, and each of these days Ivan might have some classes at the university.

There are m working hours during each Berland day, and each lesson at the university lasts exactly one hour. If at some day Ivan's first lesson is during i-th hour, and last lesson is during j-th hour, then he spends j - i + 1 hours in the university during this day. If there are no lessons during some day, then Ivan stays at home and therefore spends 0 hours in the university.

Ivan doesn't like to spend a lot of time in the university, so he has decided to skip some lessons. He cannot skip more than k lessons during the week. After deciding which lessons he should skip and which he should attend, every day Ivan will enter the university right before the start of the first lesson he does not skip, and leave it after the end of the last lesson he decides to attend. If Ivan skips all lessons during some day, he doesn't go to the university that day at all.
Given n, m, k and Ivan's timetable, can you determine the minimum number of hours he has to spend in the university during one week, if he cannot skip more than k lessons?
input: The first line contains three integers n, m and k (1 ≤ n, m ≤ 500, 0 ≤ k ≤ 500) — the number of days in the Berland week, the number of working hours during each day, and the number of lessons Ivan can skip, respectively.

Then n lines follow, i-th line containing a binary string of m characters. If j-th character in i-th line is 1, then Ivan has a lesson on i-th day during j-th hour (if it is 0, there is no such lesson).
output: Print the minimum number of hours Ivan has to spend in the university during the week if he skips not more than k lessons.
note: In the first example Ivan can skip any of two lessons during the first day, so he spends 1 hour during the first day and 4 hours during the second day.
In the second example Ivan can't skip any lessons, so he spends 4 hours every day.

legend.ai: Ivan 是 Berland 国立大学（BSU）的一名学生。Berland 的一周有 n 天，在这些天中，Ivan 可能会在大学上课。
每个 Berland 日有 m 个工作小时，且大学的每节课恰好持续一小时。如果某天 Ivan 的第一节课在第 i 个小时，最后一节课在第 j 个小时，那么这一天他在大学中度过的时间为 j - i + 1 小时。如果某天没有课，那么 Ivan 会待在家里，因此在大学中度过 0 小时。
Ivan 不喜欢在大学里待太长时间，因此他决定逃掉一些课。他一周内逃掉的课不能超过 k 节。在决定逃掉哪些课、参加哪些课之后，每天 Ivan 会在他没有逃掉的第一节课开始前进入大学，并在他决定参加的最后一节课结束后离开大学。如果 Ivan 某天逃掉了所有课程，那么这一天他完全不会去大学。
给定 n、m、k 和 Ivan 的课表，请确定在一周内，如果他不能逃掉超过 k 节课，他至少需要在大学里待多少小时？

input.ai: 第一行包含三个整数 n、m 和 k（1 ≤ n，m ≤ 500，0 ≤ k ≤ 500），分别表示 Berland 一周的天数、每天的工作时长以及 Ivan 可以逃掉的课程数。
接下来有 n 行，第 i 行包含一个长度为 m 的 01 串。如果第 i 行的第 j 个字符为 1，那么 Ivan 在第 i 天的第 j 个小时有一节课；如果为 0，则该时间没有课程。

output.ai: 如果 Ivan 逃掉的课程数不超过 k，输出他一周内至少需要在大学里待的小时数。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，Ivan 可以在第一天的两节课中任选一节逃掉，因此他第一天需要待 1 个小时，第二天需要待 4 个小时。
在第二个样例中，Ivan 不能逃掉任何课程，因此他每天都需要待 4 个小时。

A word x is lexicographically greater than a word y of the same length, if the words are same up to some position, and then the word x has a larger character, than the word y.

We can prove that the probability equals to some fraction ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/8c774283e44990bd22fded6fe64d27b8a23c99ff.png), where P and Q are coprime integers, and ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/9a89b9238145afe8a88be1ad2fb4dc4a5901b1d1.png). The second line contains n integers a1, a2, ..., an (0 ≤ ai ≤ m) — the symbols of S1. If ai = 0, then the symbol at position i was erased.

legend: Summer is coming! It's time for Iahub and Iahubina to work out, as they both want to look hot at the beach. The gym where they go is a matrix a with n lines and m columns. Let number a[i][j] represents the calories burned by performing workout at the cell of gym in the i-th line and the j-th column.

Iahub starts with workout located at line 1 and column 1. He needs to finish with workout a[n][m]. After finishing workout a[i][j], he can go to workout a[i + 1][j] or a[i][j + 1]. Similarly, Iahubina starts with workout a[n][1] and she needs to finish with workout a[1][m]. After finishing workout from cell a[i][j], she goes to either a[i][j + 1] or a[i - 1][j].

There is one additional condition for their training. They have to meet in exactly one cell of gym. At that cell, none of them will work out. They will talk about fast exponentiation (pretty odd small talk) and then both of them will move to the next workout.

If a workout was done by either Iahub or Iahubina, it counts as total gain. Please plan a workout for Iahub and Iahubina such as total gain to be as big as possible. Note, that Iahub and Iahubina can perform workouts with different speed, so the number of cells that they use to reach meet cell may differs.
input: The first line of the input contains two integers n and m (3 ≤ n, m ≤ 1000). Each of the next n lines contains m integers: j-th number from i-th line denotes element a[i][j] (0 ≤ a[i][j] ≤ 105).
output: The output contains a single number — the maximum total gain possible.
note: Iahub will choose exercises a[1][1] → a[1][2] → a[2][2] → a[3][2] → a[3][3]. Iahubina will choose exercises a[3][1] → a[2][1] → a[2][2] → a[2][3] → a[1][3].

legend.ai: 夏天就要来了！Iahub 和 Iahubina 都想在海滩上展现出火辣的身材，因此是时候锻炼了。他们去的健身房是一个有 n 行 m 列的矩阵 a。数字 a[i][j] 表示在健身房第 i 行第 j 列的单元格中进行锻炼所消耗的卡路里数。
Iahub 从位于第 1 行第 1 列的锻炼开始。他需要以锻炼 a[n][m] 结束。完成锻炼 a[i][j] 后，他可以前往锻炼 a[i + 1][j] 或 a[i][j + 1]。类似地，Iahubina 从锻炼 a[n][1] 开始，并需要以锻炼 a[1][m] 结束。完成单元格 a[i][j] 中的锻炼后，她可以前往 a[i][j + 1] 或 a[i - 1][j]。
他们的训练还有一个额外条件：他们必须恰好在健身房的一个单元格中相遇。在那个单元格中，他们都不会进行锻炼。他们会讨论快速幂（相当奇怪的闲聊），然后两人都会前往下一项锻炼。
如果某项锻炼由 Iahub 或 Iahubina 中的任意一人完成，则该锻炼计入总收益。请为 Iahub 和 Iahubina 规划一套锻炼方案，使总收益尽可能大。注意，Iahub 和 Iahubina 可以以不同的速度进行锻炼，因此他们到达相遇单元格所经过的单元格数量可能不同。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含两个整数 n 和 m（3 ≤ n, m ≤ 1000）。接下来的 n 行中，每行包含 m 个整数：第 i 行的第 j 个数字表示 a[i][j]（0 ≤ a[i][j] ≤ 105）。

legend: Today is a holiday in the residence hall — Oleh arrived, in honor of which the girls gave him a string. Oleh liked the gift a lot, so he immediately thought up and offered you, his best friend, the following problem.

You are given a string s$$$s$$$ of length n$$$n$$$, which consists of the first 17$$$17$$$ lowercase Latin letters {a$$$a$$$, b$$$b$$$, c$$$c$$$, …$$$\ldots$$$, p$$$p$$$, q$$$q$$$} and question marks. And q$$$q$$$ queries. Each query is defined by a set of pairwise distinct lowercase first 17$$$17$$$ letters of the Latin alphabet, which can be used to replace the question marks in the string s$$$s$$$.

The answer to the query is the sum of the number of distinct substrings that are palindromes over all strings that can be obtained from the original string s$$$s$$$ by replacing question marks with available characters. The answer must be calculated modulo 998244353$$$998\,244\,353$$$.

Pay attention! Two substrings are different when their start and end positions in the string are different. So, the number of different substrings that are palindromes for the string aba will be 4$$$4$$$: a, b, a, aba.

Consider examples of replacing question marks with letters. For example, from the string aba??ee when querying {a$$$a$$$, b$$$b$$$} you can get the strings ababaee or abaaaee but you cannot get the strings pizza,  abaee, abacaba, aba?fee, aba47ee, or abatree.
Recall that a palindrome is a string that reads the same from left to right as from right to left.
input: The first line contains a single integer n$$$n$$$ (1≤n≤1000$$$1 \le n \le 1\,000$$$) — the length of the string s$$$s$$$.

The second line contains the string s$$$s$$$, which consists of n$$$n$$$ lowercase Latin letters and question marks. It is guaranteed that all letters in the string belong to the set {a$$$a$$$, b$$$b$$$, c$$$c$$$, …$$$\ldots$$$, p$$$p$$$, q$$$q$$$}.
The third line contains a single integer q$$$q$$$ (1≤q≤2⋅105$$$1 \le q \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of queries.

This is followed by q$$$q$$$ lines, each containing a single line t$$$t$$$ — a set of characters that can replace question marks (1≤|t|≤17$$$1 \le |t| \le 17$$$). It is guaranteed that all letters in the string belong to the set {a$$$a$$$, b$$$b$$$, c$$$c$$$, …$$$\ldots$$$, p$$$p$$$, q$$$q$$$} and occur at most once.
output: For each query print one number — the total numbers of palindromic substrings in all strings that can be obtained from the string s$$$s$$$, modulo 998244353$$$998\,244\,353$$$.
note: Consider the first example and the first query in it. We can get only one string as a result of replacing the question marks  — abaaaba. It has the following palindrome substrings:
baaab  — substring [2$$$2$$$; 6$$$6$$$].
abaaaba  — substring [1$$$1$$$; 7$$$7$$$].
In the third request, we get 4 lines: abaaaba, abababa, abbaaba, abbbaba.

给定一个长度为 n$$$n$$$ 的字符串 s$$$s$$$，它由前 17$$$17$$$ 个小写拉丁字母 {a$$$a$$$、b$$$b$$$、c$$$c$$$、…$$$\ldots$$$、p$$$p$$$、q$$$q$$$} 和问号组成。另有 q$$$q$$$ 次查询。每次查询由一个集合定义，该集合中的字符是拉丁字母表前 17$$$17$$$ 个小写字母，且两两不同；这些字符可以用来替换字符串 s$$$s$$$ 中的问号。

考虑将问号替换为字母的例子。例如，对于字符串 aba??ee，当查询字符集合 {a$$$a$$$, b$$$b$$$} 时，可以得到字符串 ababaee 或 abaaaee，但无法得到字符串 pizza、abaee、abacaba、aba?fee、aba47ee 或 abatree。

legend: Innovation technologies are on a victorious march around the planet. They integrate into all spheres of human activity!
A restaurant called "Dijkstra's Place" has started thinking about optimizing the booking system.

There are n booking requests received by now. Each request is characterized by two numbers: ci and pi — the size of the group of visitors who will come via this request and the total sum of money they will spend in the restaurant, correspondingly.
We know that for each request, all ci people want to sit at the same table and are going to spend the whole evening in the restaurant, from the opening moment at 18:00 to the closing moment.

Unfortunately, there only are k tables in the restaurant. For each table, we know ri — the maximum number of people who can sit at it. A table can have only people from the same group sitting at it. If you cannot find a large enough table for the whole group, then all visitors leave and naturally, pay nothing.
Your task is: given the tables and the requests, decide which requests to accept and which requests to decline so that the money paid by the happy and full visitors was maximum.
input: The first line of the input contains integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 1000) — the number of requests from visitors. Then n lines follow. Each line contains two integers: ci, pi (1 ≤ ci, pi ≤ 1000) — the size of the group of visitors who will come by the i-th request and the total sum of money they will pay when they visit the restaurant, correspondingly.

The next line contains integer k (1 ≤ k ≤ 1000) — the number of tables in the restaurant. The last line contains k space-separated integers: r1, r2, ..., rk (1 ≤ ri ≤ 1000) — the maximum number of people that can sit at each table.
output: In the first line print two integers: m, s — the number of accepted requests and the total money you get from these requests, correspondingly.

Then print m lines — each line must contain two space-separated integers: the number of the accepted request and the number of the table to seat people who come via this request. The requests and the tables are consecutively numbered starting from 1 in the order in which they are given in the input.
If there are multiple optimal answers, print any of them.

legend.ai: 创新技术正在全球范围内取得胜利！它们融入了人类活动的各个领域！
一家名为“Dijkstra's Place”的餐厅开始考虑如何优化预订系统。
目前已经收到 n 个预订请求。每个请求由两个数字表示：ci 和 pi，分别表示通过该请求到来的访客团体人数，以及他们将在餐厅消费的总金额。
我们知道，对于每个请求，所有 ci 个人都希望坐在同一张桌子旁，并且会在餐厅度过整个晚上，从 18:00 开门时一直到关门时。
遗憾的是，餐厅里只有 k 张桌子。对于每张桌子，我们知道 ri，即这张桌子最多可以容纳的人数。一张桌子旁只能坐来自同一团体的人。如果无法为整个团体找到足够大的桌子，那么所有访客都会离开，自然也不会支付任何费用。
你的任务是：给定这些桌子和预订请求，决定接受哪些请求、拒绝哪些请求，使满意且吃饱的访客所支付的总金额最大。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 1000），表示访客请求的数量。接下来有 n 行。每行包含两个整数：ci、pi（1 ≤ ci、pi ≤ 1000），分别表示第 i 个请求中到访的访客组人数，以及他们到餐厅用餐时将支付的总金额。
下一行包含一个整数 k（1 ≤ k ≤ 1000），表示餐厅中的桌子数量。最后一行包含 k 个以空格分隔的整数：r1、r2、...、rk（1 ≤ ri ≤ 1000），表示每张桌子最多可以容纳的人数。

output.ai: 第一行输出两个整数：m、s，分别表示接受的请求数量，以及通过这些请求获得的总金额。
接下来输出 m 行，每行必须包含两个以空格分隔的整数：接受的请求编号，以及安排该请求中的访客就座的桌子编号。请求和桌子按照输入中的顺序从 1 开始连续编号。
如果存在多个最优答案，输出其中任意一个即可。

legend: Vasya wrote down two strings s of length n and t of length m consisting of small English letters 'a' and 'b'. What is more, he knows that string t has a form "abab...", namely there are letters 'a' on odd positions and letters 'b' on even positions.
Suddenly in the morning, Vasya found that somebody spoiled his string. Some letters of the string s were replaced by character '?'.
Let's call a sequence of positions i, i + 1, ..., i + m - 1 as occurrence of string t in s, if 1 ≤ i ≤ n - m + 1 and t1 = si, t2 = si + 1, ..., tm = si + m - 1.

The boy defines the beauty of the string s as maximum number of disjoint occurrences of string t in s. Vasya can replace some letters '?' with 'a' or 'b' (letters on different positions can be replaced with different letter). Vasya wants to make some replacements in such a way that beauty of string s is maximum possible. From all such options, he wants to choose one with the minimum number of replacements. Find the number of replacements he should make.
input: The first line contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 105) — the length of s.
The second line contains the string s of length n. It contains small English letters 'a', 'b' and characters '?' only.
The third line contains a single integer m (1 ≤ m ≤ 105) — the length of t. The string t contains letters 'a' on odd positions and 'b' on even positions.
output: Print the only integer — the minimum number of replacements Vasya has to perform to make the beauty of string s the maximum possible.
note: In the first sample string t has a form 'a'. The only optimal option is to replace all characters '?' by 'a'.
In the second sample using two replacements we can make string equal to "aba?aba??". It is impossible to get more than two occurrences.

legend.ai: Vasya 写下了两个由小写英文字母 'a' 和 'b' 组成的字符串：长度为 n 的 s 和长度为 m 的 t。此外，他知道字符串 t 的形式是 "abab..."，即奇数位上是字母 'a'，偶数位上是字母 'b'。
突然在早上，Vasya 发现有人破坏了他的字符串。字符串 s 中的一些字母被替换成了字符 '?'。
如果 1 ≤ i ≤ n - m + 1，且 t1 = si, t2 = si+1, ..., tm = si+m-1，则称位置序列 i, i+1, ..., i+m-1 为 t 在 s 中的一次出现。
男孩将字符串 s 的美观度定义为 t 在 s 中互不相交出现的最大次数。Vasya 可以将某些 '?' 替换成 'a' 或 'b'（不同位置上的字母可以被替换成不同的字母）。Vasya 希望通过一些替换使得 s 的美观度尽可能大。在所有这样的方案中，他想选择替换次数最少的一个。求出他应该进行的替换次数。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5）——表示 s 的长度。
第二行包含长度为 n 的字符串 s。它仅包含小写英文字母 'a'、'b' 和字符 '?'。
第三行包含一个整数 m（1 ≤ m ≤ 105），表示字符串 t 的长度。字符串 t 在奇数位置包含字母 'a'，在偶数位置包含字母 'b'。

output.ai: 输出唯一的整数，即 Vasya 为使字符串 s 的美丽值达到可能的最大值而必须执行的最少替换次数。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，字符串 t 的形式为 'a'。唯一的最优方案是将所有字符 '?' 替换为 'a'。
在第二个样例中，通过进行两次替换，我们可以将字符串变为 "aba?aba??"。不可能得到超过两次出现。

legend: While Vasya finished eating his piece of pizza, the lesson has already started. For being late for the lesson, the teacher suggested Vasya to solve one interesting problem. Vasya has an array a and integer x. He should find the number of different ordered pairs of indexes (i, j) such that ai ≤ aj and there are exactly k integers y such that ai ≤ y ≤ aj and y is divisible by x.
In this problem it is meant that pair (i, j) is equal to (j, i) only if i is equal to j. For example pair (1, 2) is not the same as (2, 1).
input: The first line contains 3 integers n, x, k (1 ≤ n ≤ 105, 1 ≤ x ≤ 109, 0 ≤ k ≤ 109), where n is the size of the array a and x and k are numbers from the statement.
The second line contains n integers ai (1 ≤ ai ≤ 109) — the elements of the array a.
output: Print one integer — the answer to the problem.
note: In first sample there are only three suitable pairs of indexes — (1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 4).
In second sample there are four suitable pairs of indexes(1, 1), (2, 2), (3, 3), (4, 4).

legend.ai: Vasya 吃完自己的那块披萨时，课程已经开始了。由于上课迟到，老师建议 Vasya 解决一道有趣的问题。Vasya 有一个数组 a 和一个整数 x。他需要找出满足以下条件的不同有序下标对 (i, j) 的数量：ai ≤ aj，并且存在恰好 k 个整数 y，使得 ai ≤ y ≤ aj 且 y 能被 x 整除。

input.ai: 第一行包含 3 个整数 n、x、k（1 ≤ n ≤ 105，1 ≤ x ≤ 109，0 ≤ k ≤ 109），其中 n 表示数组 a 的大小，x 和 k 是题面中给出的数。

legend: Ghosts live in harmony and peace, they travel the space without any purpose other than scare whoever stands in their way.

There are n$$$n$$$ ghosts in the universe, they move in the OXY$$$OXY$$$ plane, each one of them has its own velocity that does not change in time: →V=Vx→i+Vy→j$$$\overrightarrow{V} = V_{x}\overrightarrow{i} + V_{y}\overrightarrow{j}$$$ where Vx$$$V_{x}$$$ is its speed on the x$$$x$$$-axis and Vy$$$V_{y}$$$ is on the y$$$y$$$-axis.

A ghost i$$$i$$$ has experience value EXi$$$EX_i$$$, which represent how many ghosts tried to scare him in his past. Two ghosts scare each other if they were in the same cartesian point at a moment of time.

As the ghosts move with constant speed, after some moment of time there will be no further scaring (what a relief!) and the experience of ghost kind GX=∑ni=1EXi$$$GX = \sum_{i=1}^{n} EX_i$$$ will never increase.

Tameem is a red giant, he took a picture of the cartesian plane at a certain moment of time T$$$T$$$, and magically all the ghosts were aligned on a line of the form y=a⋅x+b$$$y = a \cdot x + b$$$. You have to compute what will be the experience index of the ghost kind GX$$$GX$$$ in the indefinite future, this is your task for today.
Note that when Tameem took the picture, GX$$$GX$$$ may already be greater than 0$$$0$$$, because many ghosts may have scared one another at any moment between [−∞,T]$$$[-\infty, T]$$$.
input: The first line contains three integers n$$$n$$$, a$$$a$$$ and b$$$b$$$ (1≤n≤200000$$$1 \leq n \leq 200000$$$, 1≤|a|≤109$$$1 \leq |a| \leq 10^9$$$, 0≤|b|≤109$$$0 \le |b| \le 10^9$$$) — the number of ghosts in the universe and the parameters of the straight line.

Each of the next n$$$n$$$ lines contains three integers xi$$$x_i$$$, Vxi$$$V_{xi}$$$, Vyi$$$V_{yi}$$$ (−109≤xi≤109$$$-10^9 \leq x_i \leq 10^9$$$, −109≤Vxi,Vyi≤109$$$-10^9 \leq V_{x i}, V_{y i} \leq 10^9$$$), where xi$$$x_i$$$ is the current x$$$x$$$-coordinate of the i$$$i$$$-th ghost (and yi=a⋅xi+b$$$y_i = a \cdot x_i + b$$$).
It is guaranteed that no two ghosts share the same initial position, in other words, it is guaranteed that for all (i,j)$$$(i,j)$$$ xi≠xj$$$x_i \neq x_j$$$ for i≠j$$$i \ne j$$$.
output: Output one line: experience index of the ghost kind GX$$$GX$$$ in the indefinite future.
note: There are four collisions (1,2,T−0.5)$$$(1,2,T-0.5)$$$, (1,3,T−1)$$$(1,3,T-1)$$$, (2,4,T+1)$$$(2,4,T+1)$$$, (3,4,T+0.5)$$$(3,4,T+0.5)$$$, where (u,v,t)$$$(u,v,t)$$$ means a collision happened between ghosts u$$$u$$$ and v$$$v$$$ at moment t$$$t$$$. At each collision, each ghost gained one experience point, this means that GX=4⋅2=8$$$GX = 4 \cdot 2 = 8$$$.
In the second test, all points will collide when t=T+1$$$t = T + 1$$$.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/632930388686f4065fba42f9dba9a1c12c028844.png)
The red arrow represents the 1-st ghost velocity, orange represents the 2-nd ghost velocity, and blue represents the 3-rd ghost velocity.

legend.ai: 鬼魂们和谐而和平地生活着，它们在空间中移动，唯一的目的就是吓唬任何挡在它们前面的人。

宇宙中有 n$$$n$$$ 个鬼魂，它们在 OXY$$$OXY$$$ 平面上移动，每个鬼魂都有一个不会随时间改变的速度：→V=Vx→i+Vy→j$$$\overrightarrow{V} = V_{x}\overrightarrow{i} + V_{y}\overrightarrow{j}$$$，其中 Vx$$$V_{x}$$$ 是它在 x$$$x$$$ 轴方向上的速度，Vy$$$V_{y}$$$ 是它在 y$$$y$$$ 轴方向上的速度。
鬼魂 i$$$i$$$ 拥有经验值 EXi$$$EX_i$$$，表示过去曾有多少个鬼魂试图吓唬它。如果两个鬼魂在某一时刻处于同一个笛卡尔坐标点，那么它们就会互相吓唬。
由于鬼魂以恒定速度移动，经过一段时间后，将不会再发生吓唬事件(真是令人宽慰！)，鬼魂群体的经验值 GX=∑ni=1EXi$$$GX = \sum_{i=1}^{n} EX_i$$$ 将永远不会增加。
Tameem 是一颗红巨星，他在某个时刻 T$$$T$$$ 拍下了直角坐标系的照片，并且神奇地发现所有鬼魂都排列在形如 y=a⋅x+b$$$y = a \cdot x + b$$$ 的直线上。你需要计算在无限遥远的未来，GX$$$GX$$$ 种类鬼魂的经验指数，这就是今天的任务。
注意，在 Tameem 拍照时，GX$$$GX$$$ 可能已经大于 0$$$0$$$，因为在 [−∞,T]$$$[-\infty, T]$$$ 之间的任意时刻，都可能有许多鬼魂互相吓唬过。

input.ai: 接下来的 n$$$n$$$ 行中的每一行包含三个整数 xi$$$x_i$$$、Vxi$$$V_{xi}$$$、Vyi$$$V_{yi}$$$(−109≤xi≤109$$$-10^9 \leq x_i \leq 10^9$$$，−109≤Vxi,Vyi≤109$$$-10^9 \leq V_{x i}, V_{y i} \leq 10^9$$$)，其中 xi$$$x_i$$$ 是第 i$$$i$$$ 个鬼魂当前的 x$$$x$$$ 坐标(且 yi=a⋅xi+b$$$y_i = a \cdot x_i + b$$$)。
保证没有两个鬼魂拥有相同的初始位置，换句话说，对于所有 (i,j)$$$(i,j)$$$，当 i≠j$$$i \ne j$$$ 时都有 xi≠xj$$$x_i \neq x_j$$$。

output.ai: 输出一行：在无限遥远的未来，GX$$$GX$$$ 种类鬼魂的经验指数。

note.ai: 在第二个测试用例中，所有点将在 t=T+1$$$t = T + 1$$$ 时发生碰撞。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/632930388686f4065fba42f9dba9a1c12c028844.png)
红色箭头表示第 1 个幽灵的速度，橙色表示第 2 个幽灵的速度，蓝色表示第 3 个幽灵的速度。

legend: Marcin is a coach in his university. There are n$$$n$$$ students who want to attend a training camp. Marcin is a smart coach, so he wants to send only the students that can work calmly with each other.

Let's focus on the students. They are indexed with integers from 1$$$1$$$ to n$$$n$$$. Each of them can be described with two integers ai$$$a_i$$$ and bi$$$b_i$$$; bi$$$b_i$$$ is equal to the skill level of the i$$$i$$$-th student (the higher, the better). Also, there are 60$$$60$$$ known algorithms, which are numbered with integers from 0$$$0$$$ to 59$$$59$$$. If the i$$$i$$$-th student knows the j$$$j$$$-th algorithm, then the j$$$j$$$-th bit (2j$$$2^j$$$) is set in the binary representation of ai$$$a_i$$$. Otherwise, this bit is not set.

Student x$$$x$$$ thinks that he is better than student y$$$y$$$ if and only if x$$$x$$$ knows some algorithm which y$$$y$$$ doesn't know. Note that two students can think that they are better than each other. A group of students can work together calmly if no student in this group thinks that he is better than everyone else in this group.
Marcin wants to send a group of at least two students which will work together calmly and will have the maximum possible sum of the skill levels. What is this sum?
input: The first line contains one integer n$$$n$$$ (1≤n≤7000$$$1 \leq n \leq 7000$$$) — the number of students interested in the camp.
The second line contains n$$$n$$$ integers. The i$$$i$$$-th of them is ai$$$a_i$$$ (0≤ai<260$$$0 \leq a_i  \lt  2^{60}$$$).
The third line contains n$$$n$$$ integers. The i$$$i$$$-th of them is bi$$$b_i$$$ (1≤bi≤109$$$1 \leq b_i \leq 10^9$$$).
output: Output one integer which denotes the maximum sum of bi$$$b_i$$$ over the students in a group of students which can work together calmly. If no group of at least two students can work together calmly, print 0.
note: In the first sample test, it's optimal to send the first, the second and the third student to the camp. It's also possible to send only the first and the third student, but they'd have a lower sum of bi$$$b_i$$$.
In the second test, in each group of at least two students someone will always think that he is better than everyone else in the subset.

legend.ai: Marcin 是他所在大学的一名教练。有 n$$$n$$$ 名学生想参加训练营。Marcin 是一名聪明的教练，因此他只想派出能够彼此平和相处的学生。

让我们关注这些学生。他们的编号是从 1$$$1$$$ 到 n$$$n$$$ 的整数。每名学生可以用两个整数 ai$$$a_i$$$ 和 bi$$$b_i$$$ 描述；其中，bi$$$b_i$$$ 等于第 i$$$i$$$ 名学生的技能等级(越高越好)。此外，还有 60$$$60$$$ 种已知算法，它们的编号是从 0$$$0$$$ 到 59$$$59$$$ 的整数。如果第 i$$$i$$$ 名学生掌握第 j$$$j$$$ 种算法，那么 ai$$$a_i$$$ 的二进制表示中第 j$$$j$$$ 位(2j$$$2^j$$$)为 1；否则，该位为 0。
当且仅当学生 x$$$x$$$ 掌握了某种学生 y$$$y$$$ 不掌握的算法时，学生 x$$$x$$$ 才会认为自己比学生 y$$$y$$$ 更优秀。注意，两个学生可能会互相认为自己比对方更优秀。如果一个学生组中没有任何学生认为自己比该组中的所有其他学生都更优秀，那么这个学生组就可以平静地一起工作。
Marcin 想要派出一个至少包含两名学生的学生组，使他们能够平静地一起工作，并且技能等级总和达到可能的最大值。这个总和是多少？

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n$$$n$$$(1≤n≤7000$$$1 \leq n \leq 7000$$$)，表示对夏令营感兴趣的学生人数。
第二行包含 n$$$n$$$ 个整数。其中第 i$$$i$$$ 个整数为 ai$$$a_i$$$(0≤ai<260$$$0 \leq a_i  \lt  2^{60}$$$)。
第三行包含 n$$$n$$$ 个整数。其中第 i$$$i$$$ 个整数为 bi$$$b_i$$$(1≤bi≤109$$$1 \leq b_i \leq 10^9$$$)。

output.ai: 输出一个整数，表示一组能够平静地一起工作的学生中 bi$$$b_i$$$ 之和的最大值。如果不存在至少两名学生能够平静地一起工作，输出 0。

note.ai: 在第一个样例测试中，将第一名、第二名和第三名学生送去夏令营是最优的。也可以只将第一名和第三名学生送去，但这样 bi$$$b_i$$$ 之和会更小。
在第二个测试中，对于每个至少包含两名学生的组，其中总会有人认为自己比该子集中的所有其他人都优秀。

legend: Dasha decided to have a rest after solving the problem. She had been ready to start her favourite activity — origami, but remembered the puzzle that she could not solve.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/993f9826045f00eab45061e07146e461060398df.png)
The tree is a non-oriented connected graph without cycles. In particular, there always are n - 1 edges in a tree with n vertices.

The puzzle is to position the vertices at the points of the Cartesian plane with integral coordinates, so that the segments between the vertices connected by edges are parallel to the coordinate axes. Also, the intersection of segments is allowed only at their ends. Distinct vertices should be placed at different points.
Help Dasha to find any suitable way to position the tree vertices on the plane.

It is guaranteed that if it is possible to position the tree vertices on the plane without violating the condition which is given above, then you can do it by using points with integral coordinates which don't exceed 1018 in absolute value.
input: The first line contains single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 30) — the number of vertices in the tree.
Each of next n - 1 lines contains two integers ui, vi (1 ≤ ui, vi ≤ n) that mean that the i-th edge of the tree connects vertices ui and vi.
It is guaranteed that the described graph is a tree.
output: If the puzzle doesn't have a solution then in the only line print "NO".

Otherwise, the first line should contain "YES". The next n lines should contain the pair of integers xi, yi (|xi|, |yi| ≤ 1018) — the coordinates of the point which corresponds to the i-th vertex of the tree.
If there are several solutions, print any of them.
note: In the first sample one of the possible positions of tree is: ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e6990dc13943fd5dfda8c2bff6b56c498af05f58.png)

legend.ai: Dasha 解完这道题后决定休息一下。她本已准备开始自己最喜欢的活动——折纸，但又想起了那道她没能解出的谜题。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/993f9826045f00eab45061e07146e461060398df.png)
树是一个无向连通且无环的图。特别地，一个有 n 个顶点的树中总有 n - 1 条边。
题目要求将各个顶点放置在笛卡尔平面的整点上，使得相邻顶点之间的线段平行于坐标轴。此外，线段只允许在端点处相交。不同的顶点应放置在不同的点上。
请帮助 Dasha 找到一种合适的方法，将树的顶点放置在平面上。
保证如果能够在不违反上述条件的情况下将树的顶点放置在平面上，那么可以使用绝对值不超过 10^18 的整点来完成放置。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 30），表示树中顶点的数量。
接下来的 n - 1 行中，每行包含两个整数 ui、vi（1 ≤ ui、vi ≤ n），表示树的第 i 条边连接顶点 ui 和 vi。
保证所描述的图是一棵树。

否则，第一行应包含“YES”。接下来的 n 行应包含一对整数 xi、yi（|xi|， |yi| ≤ 1018），表示树中第 i 个顶点对应的点的坐标。
如果有多个解，输出任意一个即可。

legend: During the loading of the game "Dungeons and Candies" you are required to get descriptions of k levels from the server. Each description is a map of an n × m checkered rectangular field. Some cells of the field contain candies (each cell has at most one candy). An empty cell is denoted as "." on the map, but if a cell has a candy, it is denoted as a letter of the English alphabet. A level may contain identical candies, in this case the letters in the corresponding cells of the map will be the same.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/cdd8d81e392298ff9e83e9300c270413d026c364.png)

When you transmit information via a network, you want to minimize traffic — the total size of the transferred data. The levels can be transmitted in any order. There are two ways to transmit the current level A:
You can transmit the whole level A. Then you need to transmit n·m bytes via the network.

You can transmit the difference between level A and some previously transmitted level B (if it exists); this operation requires to transmit dA, B·w bytes, where dA, B is the number of cells of the field that are different for A and B, and w is a constant. Note, that you should compare only the corresponding cells of levels A and B to calculate dA, B. You cannot transform the maps of levels, i.e. rotate or shift them relatively to each other.
Your task is to find a way to transfer all the k levels and minimize the traffic.
input: The first line contains four integers n, m, k, w (1 ≤ n, m ≤ 10; 1 ≤ k, w ≤ 1000). Then follows the description of k levels. Each level is described by n lines, each line contains m characters. Each character is either a letter of the English alphabet or a dot ("."). Please note that the case of the letters matters.
output: In the first line print the required minimum number of transferred bytes.

Then print k pairs of integers x1, y1, x2, y2, ..., xk, yk, describing the way to transfer levels. Pair xi, yi means that level xi needs to be transferred by way yi. If yi equals 0, that means that the level must be transferred using the first way, otherwise yi must be equal to the number of a previously transferred level. It means that you will transfer the difference between levels yi and xi to transfer level xi. Print the pairs in the order of transferring levels. The levels are numbered 1 through k in the order they follow in the input.
If there are multiple optimal solutions, you can print any of them.

input.ai: 第一行包含四个整数 n、m、k、w（1 ≤ n，m ≤ 10；1 ≤ k，w ≤ 1000）。接下来是 k 个关卡的描述。每个关卡由 n 行组成，每行包含 m 个字符。每个字符要么是英文字母，要么是点号（“.”）。请注意，字母的大小写是有区别的。

output.ai: 第一行输出所需传输的最少字节数。

接下来输出 k 对整数 x1、y1、x2、y2、...、xk、yk，描述传输关卡的方式。数对 xi、yi 表示关卡 xi 需要通过方式 yi 进行传输。如果 yi 等于 0，则表示该关卡必须使用第一种方式传输；否则 yi 必须等于一个之前已经传输的关卡的编号。这意味着你将通过传输关卡 yi 和关卡 xi 之间的差异来传输关卡 xi。请按照传输关卡的顺序输出这些数对。关卡按照它们在输入中出现的顺序编号为 1 至 k。
如果存在多个最优解，你可以输出其中任意一个。

legend.ai: 在加载游戏“Dungeons and Candies”时，你需要从服务器获取 k 个关卡的描述。每个描述都是一个 n × m 的方格矩形区域地图。区域中的某些格子包含糖果（每个格子至多包含一颗糖果）。空格子在地图上用“.”表示；如果一个格子中有糖果，则用英文字母表中的一个字母表示。一个关卡中可能包含相同的糖果，此时地图上对应格子中的字母也会相同。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/cdd8d81e392298ff9e83e9300c270413d026c364.png)
通过网络传输信息时，你希望尽量减少流量，即传输数据的总大小。关卡可以按照任意顺序传输。传输当前关卡 A 有两种方式：
你可以传输整个关卡 A。此时需要通过网络传输 n·m 字节。
你可以传输关卡 A 与之前某个已传输关卡 B（如果存在）之间的差异；此操作需要传输 dA, B·w 字节，其中 dA, B 是关卡 A 和 B 中不同格子的数量，w 是一个常数。注意，计算 dA, B 时只能比较关卡 A 和 B 中对应的格子。你不能变换关卡地图，即不能将它们相互旋转或平移。
你的任务是找到一种传输所有 k 个关卡的方案，使流量最小。

legend: Little Vlad is fond of popular computer game Bota-2. Recently, the developers announced the new add-on named Bota-3. Of course, Vlad immediately bought only to find out his computer is too old for the new game and needs to be updated.

There are n video cards in the shop, the power of the i-th video card is equal to integer value ai. As Vlad wants to be sure the new game will work he wants to buy not one, but several video cards and unite their powers using the cutting-edge technology. To use this technology one of the cards is chosen as the leading one and other video cards are attached to it as secondary. For this new technology to work it's required that the power of each of the secondary video cards is divisible by the power of the leading video card. In order to achieve that the power of any secondary video card can be reduced to any integer value less or equal than the current power. However, the power of the leading video card should remain unchanged, i.e. it can't be reduced.

Vlad has an infinite amount of money so he can buy any set of video cards. Help him determine which video cards he should buy such that after picking the leading video card and may be reducing some powers of others to make them work together he will get the maximum total value of video power.
input: The first line of the input contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 200 000) — the number of video cards in the shop.
The second line contains n integers a1, a2, ..., an (1 ≤ ai ≤ 200 000) — powers of video cards.
output: The only line of the output should contain one integer value — the maximum possible total power of video cards working together.
note: In the first sample, it would be optimal to buy video cards with powers 3, 15 and 9. The video card with power 3 should be chosen as the leading one and all other video cards will be compatible with it. Thus, the total power would be 3 + 15 + 9 = 27. If he buys all the video cards and pick the one with the power 2 as the leading, the powers of all other video cards should be reduced by 1, thus the total power would be 2 + 2 + 14 + 8 = 26, that is less than 27. Please note, that it's not allowed to reduce the power of the leading video card, i.e. one can't get the total power 3 + 1 + 15 + 9 = 28.

In the second sample, the optimal answer is to buy all video cards and pick the one with the power 2 as the leading. The video card with the power 7 needs it power to be reduced down to 6. The total power would be 8 + 2 + 2 + 6 = 18.

legend.ai: 小弗拉德喜欢热门的电脑游戏 Bota-2。最近，开发者宣布了名为 Bota-3 的新扩展包。当然，弗拉德立即买了下来，却发现自己的电脑太旧，无法运行这款新游戏，需要进行升级。

商店里有 n 张显卡，第 i 张显卡的性能等于整数 ai。由于 Vlad 想确保新游戏能够运行，他想购买的不是一张显卡，而是多张显卡，并使用尖端技术将它们的性能结合起来。使用这项技术时，需要选出一张显卡作为主卡，并将其他显卡作为副卡连接到它上面。为了使这项新技术正常工作，要求每张副卡的性能都能被主卡的性能整除。为此，可以将任意副卡的性能降低为不超过其当前性能的任意整数值。但是，主卡的性能必须保持不变，也就是说不能降低主卡的性能。
Vlad 有无限多的钱，因此他可以买下任意一组显卡。请帮助他确定应该购买哪些显卡，使得在选出主卡并可以降低其他显卡的性能以使它们能够协同工作后，显卡性能总和最大。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，购买性能为 3、15 和 9 的显卡是最优选择。应选择性能为 3 的显卡作为主卡，其他所有显卡都与它兼容。因此，性能总和为 3 + 15 + 9 = 27。如果购买所有显卡，并选择性能为 2 的显卡作为主卡，那么其他显卡的性能都必须降低 1，因此性能总和为 2 + 2 + 14 + 8 = 26，小于 27。请注意，不允许降低主卡的性能，因此不能得到 3 + 1 + 15 + 9 = 28 的性能总和。
在第二个样例中，最优方案是购买所有显卡，并选择功率为 2 的显卡作为领头显卡。功率为 7 的显卡需要将其功率降低到 6。总功率为 8 + 2 + 2 + 6 = 18。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 200 000），表示商店中的显卡数量。
第二行包含 n 个整数 a1, a2, ..., an（1 ≤ ai ≤ 200 000），表示各张显卡的性能。

output.ai: 输出的唯一一行应包含一个整数，表示能够协同工作的显卡性能总和的最大值。

problems.hint: When $maxID-minID+1$ is fixed, what segment can you change? Where can you get?

legend: Vasya has got a robot which is situated on an infinite Cartesian plane, initially in the cell (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$. Robot can perform the following four kinds of operations:
Vasya also has got a sequence of n$$$n$$$ operations. Vasya wants to modify this sequence so after performing it the robot will end up in (x,y)$$$(x, y)$$$.

Vasya wants to change the sequence so the length of changed subsegment is minimum possible. This length can be calculated as follows: maxID−minID+1$$$maxID - minID + 1$$$, where maxID$$$maxID$$$ is the maximum index of a changed operation, and minID$$$minID$$$ is the minimum index of a changed operation. For example, if Vasya changes RRRRRRR to RLRRLRL, then the operations with indices 2$$$2$$$, 5$$$5$$$ and 7$$$7$$$ are changed, so the length of changed subsegment is 7−2+1=6$$$7 - 2 + 1 = 6$$$. Another example: if Vasya changes DDDD to DDRD, then the length of changed subsegment is 1$$$1$$$.

If there are no changes, then the length of changed subsegment is 0$$$0$$$. Changing an operation means replacing it with some operation (possibly the same); Vasya can't insert new operations into the sequence or remove them.
Help Vasya! Tell him the minimum length of subsegment that he needs to change so that the robot will go from (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$ to (x,y)$$$(x, y)$$$, or tell him that it's impossible.
input: The first line contains one integer number n (1≤n≤2⋅105)$$$n~(1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5)$$$ — the number of operations.
The second line contains the sequence of operations — a string of n$$$n$$$ characters. Each character is either U, D, L or R.
The third line contains two integers x,y (−109≤x,y≤109)$$$x, y~(-10^9 \le x, y \le 10^9)$$$ — the coordinates of the cell where the robot should end its path.
output: Print one integer — the minimum possible length of subsegment that can be changed so the resulting sequence of operations moves the robot from (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$ to (x,y)$$$(x, y)$$$. If this change is impossible, print −1$$$-1$$$.
note: In the first example the sequence can be changed to LULUU. So the length of the changed subsegment is 3−1+1=3$$$3 - 1 + 1 = 3$$$.
In the second example the given sequence already leads the robot to (x,y)$$$(x, y)$$$, so the length of the changed subsegment is 0$$$0$$$.
In the third example the robot can't end his path in the cell (x,y)$$$(x, y)$$$.

legend.ai: Vasya 有一个机器人，机器人位于无限大的笛卡尔平面上，初始位于单元格 (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$。机器人可以执行以下四种操作：
Vasya 还有一个包含 n$$$n$$$ 个操作的序列。Vasya 想要修改这个序列，使得执行完这些操作后机器人最终停在 (x,y)$$$(x, y)$$$。

Vasya 想要修改序列，使得被修改子段的长度尽可能小。这个长度可以按如下方式计算：maxID−minID+1$$$maxID - minID + 1$$$，其中 maxID$$$maxID$$$ 是被修改操作的最大下标，minID$$$minID$$$ 是被修改操作的最小下标。例如，如果 Vasya 把 RRRRRRR 改成 RLRRLRL，那么下标为 2$$$2$$$、5$$$5$$$ 和 7$$$7$$$ 的操作被修改，因此被修改子段的长度为 7−2+1=6$$$7 - 2 + 1 = 6$$$。另一个例子：如果 Vasya 把 DDDD 改成 DDRD，那么被修改子段的长度为 1$$$1$$$。
如果没有修改，那么被修改子段的长度为 0$$$0$$$。修改一个操作是指把它替换为某个操作(可能与原来相同)；Vasya 不能向序列中插入新操作，也不能删除操作。
帮帮 Vasya！告诉他需要修改的子段的最小长度，使得机器人能从 (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$ 到达 (x,y)$$$(x, y)$$$，或者告诉他这是不可能的。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n (1≤n≤2⋅105)$$$n~(1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5)$$$ — 操作的数量。
第二行包含操作序列，即一个长度为 n$$$n$$$ 的字符串。每个字符均为 U、D、L 或 R。
第三行包含两个整数 x,y(−109≤x,y≤109)$$$x, y~(-10^9 \le x, y \le 10^9)$$$，表示机器人应结束路径的单元格坐标。

output.ai: 输出一个整数，即为使操作序列发生改变后，机器人从 (0,0)$$$(0, 0)$$$ 移动到 (x,y)$$$(x, y)$$$，所需改变的子段的最小可能长度。如果无法完成改变，输出 −1$$$-1$$$。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，可以将序列改变为 LULUU。因此，改变的子段长度为 3−1+1=3$$$3 - 1 + 1 = 3$$$。
在第二个样例中，给定的序列已经可以使机器人到达 (x,y)$$$(x, y)$$$，因此改变的子段长度为 0$$$0$$$。
在第三个样例中，机器人无法在单元格 (x,y)$$$(x, y)$$$ 结束路径。
