legend: Andrew and Jerry are playing a game with Harry as the scorekeeper. The game consists of three rounds. In each round, Andrew and Jerry draw randomly without replacement from a jar containing n balls, each labeled with a distinct positive integer. Without looking, they hand their balls to Harry, who awards the point to the player with the larger number and returns the balls to the jar. The winner of the game is the one who wins at least two of the three rounds.

Andrew wins rounds 1 and 2 while Jerry wins round 3, so Andrew wins the game. However, Jerry is unhappy with this system, claiming that he will often lose the match despite having the higher overall total. What is the probability that the sum of the three balls Jerry drew is strictly higher than the sum of the three balls Andrew drew?
input: The first line of input contains a single integer n (2 ≤ n ≤ 2000) — the number of balls in the jar.
The second line contains n integers ai (1 ≤ ai ≤ 5000) — the number written on the ith ball. It is guaranteed that no two balls have the same number.
output: Print a single real value — the probability that Jerry has a higher total, given that Andrew wins the first two rounds and Jerry wins the third. Your answer will be considered correct if its absolute or relative error does not exceed 10 - 6.

Namely: let's assume that your answer is a, and the answer of the jury is b. The checker program will consider your answer correct, if ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c97ba2000ebfad962bff7ffd8d043594f5ae1086.png).
note: In the first case, there are only two balls. In the first two rounds, Andrew must have drawn the 2 and Jerry must have drawn the 1, and vice versa in the final round. Thus, Andrew's sum is 5 and Jerry's sum is 4, so Jerry never has a higher total.

In the second case, each game could've had three outcomes — 10 - 2, 10 - 1, or 2 - 1. Jerry has a higher total if and only if Andrew won 2 - 1 in both of the first two rounds, and Jerry drew the 10 in the last round. This has probability ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/3c0ec296285f607c66d594132fb91e5e5f2bb007.png).

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含一个整数 n（2 ≤ n ≤ 2000），表示罐子中球的数量。
第二行包含 n 个整数 ai（1 ≤ ai ≤ 5000）——第 i 个球上写的数字。保证没有两个球上的数字相同。

output.ai: 输出一个实数——在 Andrew 赢得前两轮且 Jerry 赢得第三轮的条件下，Jerry 的总和更大的概率。如果你的答案的绝对误差或相对误差不超过 10 - 6，则会被判定为正确。
具体来说：假设你的答案为 a，标准答案为 b。当 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c97ba2000ebfad962bff7ffd8d043594f5ae1086.png) 时，校验程序会判定你的答案正确。

note.ai: 在第一种情况中，只有两个球。在前两轮中，Andrew 必须抽到 2，而 Jerry 必须抽到 1；最后一轮则相反。因此，Andrew 的总和为 5，Jerry 的总和为 4，所以 Jerry 的总和不可能更大。
在第二种情况中，每局可能有三种结果：10 - 2、10 - 1 或 2 - 1。当且仅当 Andrew 在前两轮中都以 2 - 1 获胜，并且 Jerry 在最后一轮抽到 10 时，Jerry 的总和才会更大。该事件的概率为 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/3c0ec296285f607c66d594132fb91e5e5f2bb007.png)。

legend.ai: Andrew 和 Jerry 正在进行一场由 Harry 负责记分的游戏。游戏由三轮组成。每一轮中，Andrew 和 Jerry 从一个装有 n 个球的罐子中随机且不放回地抽取一个球，罐子中的每个球都标有一个互不相同的正整数。他们不看球上的数字，直接将球交给 Harry，由数字较大的玩家获得该轮的分数，随后将两个球放回罐子中。三轮中至少赢得两轮的玩家赢得整场游戏。
Andrew 赢得了第 1 轮和第 2 轮，而 Jerry 赢得了第 3 轮，因此 Andrew 赢得了比赛。然而，Jerry 对这种规则感到不满，认为尽管自己的总和更高，他仍然经常会输掉比赛。求 Jerry 抽到的三个球之和严格大于 Andrew 抽到的三个球之和的概率。

It was a Sunday morning when the three friends Selena, Shiro and Katie decided to have a trip to the nearby power station (do not try this at home). After arriving at the power station, the cats got impressed with a large power transmission system consisting of many chimneys, electric poles, and wires. At the entrance of the station, there is a map describing the complicated wiring system. Selena is the best at math among three friends. He decided to draw the map on the Cartesian plane. If there are more than two poles lying on the same line, they are connected by a single common wire.

legend: You are given a permutation p of numbers 1, 2, ..., n. Let's define f(p) as the following sum:
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e12229ecd64f361940afe4756d3f3d51ca05a329.png)
Find the lexicographically m-th permutation of length n in the set of permutations having the maximum possible value of f(p).
input: The single line of input contains two integers n and m (1 ≤ m ≤ cntn), where cntn is the number of permutations of length n with maximum possible value of f(p).

The problem consists of two subproblems. The subproblems have different constraints on the input. You will get some score for the correct submission of the subproblem. The description of the subproblems follows.
In subproblem B1 (3 points), the constraint 1 ≤ n ≤ 8 will hold.
In subproblem B2 (4 points), the constraint 1 ≤ n ≤ 50 will hold.
output: Output n number forming the required permutation.
note: In the first example, both permutations of numbers {1, 2} yield maximum possible f(p) which is equal to 4. Among them, (2, 1) comes second in lexicographical order.

legend.ai: 给定一个由数字 1、 2、...、n 组成的排列 p。我们将 f(p) 定义为以下和：
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e12229ecd64f361940afe4756d3f3d51ca05a329.png)
在所有使 f(p) 取得可能最大值的排列中，找出长度为 n 且字典序排名第 m 的排列。

input.ai: 输入仅一行，包含两个整数 n 和 m（1 ≤ m ≤ cntn），其中 cntn 表示使 f(p) 取得可能最大值的长度为 n 的排列数量。
本题包含两个子问题。子问题对输入有不同的约束条件。正确提交子问题的解法可以获得相应的分数。下面给出各个子问题的描述。
在子问题 B1（3 分）中，保证满足 1 ≤ n ≤ 8。
在子问题 B2（4 分）中，保证满足 1 ≤ n ≤ 50。

output.ai: 输出 n 个数组成所要求的排列。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，数字 {1, 2} 的两种排列都能得到等于 4 的可能最大值 f(p)。其中，(2, 1) 的字典序排在第二位。

legend: Kilani is playing a game with his friends. This game can be represented as a grid of size n×m$$$n \times m$$$, where each cell is either empty or blocked, and every player has one or more castles in some cells (there are no two castles in one cell).

The game is played in rounds. In each round players expand turn by turn: firstly, the first player expands, then the second player expands and so on. The expansion happens as follows: for each castle the player owns now, he tries to expand into the empty cells nearby. The player i$$$i$$$ can expand from a cell with his castle to the empty cell if it's possible to reach it in at most si$$$s_i$$$ (where si$$$s_i$$$ is player's expansion speed) moves to the left, up, right or down without going through blocked cells or cells occupied by some other player's castle. The player examines the set of cells he can expand to and builds a castle in each of them at once. The turned is passed to the next player after that.

The game ends when no player can make a move. You are given the game field and speed of the expansion for each player. Kilani wants to know for each player how many cells he will control (have a castle their) after the game ends.
input: The first line contains three integers n$$$n$$$, m$$$m$$$ and p$$$p$$$ (1≤n,m≤1000$$$1 \le n, m \le 1000$$$, 1≤p≤9$$$1 \le p \le 9$$$) — the size of the grid and the number of players.
The second line contains p$$$p$$$ integers si$$$s_i$$$ (1≤s≤109$$$1 \le s \le 10^9$$$) — the speed of the expansion for every player.

The following n$$$n$$$ lines describe the game grid. Each of them consists of m$$$m$$$ symbols, where '.' denotes an empty cell, '#' denotes a blocked cell and digit x$$$x$$$ (1≤x≤p$$$1 \le x \le p$$$) denotes the castle owned by player x$$$x$$$.
It is guaranteed, that each player has at least one castle on the grid.
output: Print p$$$p$$$ integers — the number of cells controlled by each player after the game ends.
note: The picture below show the game before it started, the game after the first round and game after the second round in the first example:
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/f914f492fa6d96af669ce8d109f973862a0d120e.png)

In the second example, the first player is "blocked" so he will not capture new cells for the entire game. All other player will expand up during the first two rounds and in the third round only the second player will move to the left.

legend.ai: Kilani 正在和他的朋友们玩一个游戏。这个游戏可以表示为一个大小为 n×m$$$n \times m$$$ 的网格，其中每个格子要么为空，要么被阻挡，并且每名玩家在一些格子中都有一个或多个城堡(同一个格子中不会有两个城堡)。

游戏分轮进行。在每一轮中，玩家依次扩张：首先第一名玩家扩张，然后第二名玩家扩张，以此类推。扩张过程如下：对于当前玩家拥有的每座城堡，他都尝试向附近的空格子扩张。如果玩家 i$$$i$$$ 可以在不经过被阻挡的格子或其他玩家城堡所在格子的情况下，通过向左、上、右或下移动至多 si$$$s_i$$$ 步到达某个空格子，则他可以从自己的城堡所在格子扩张到该空格子(其中 si$$$s_i$$$ 是玩家的扩张速度)。玩家找出他可以扩张到的所有格子，并立即在每个格子中建造一座城堡。之后轮到下一名玩家。
当没有玩家可以进行移动时，游戏结束。给定游戏场地以及每名玩家的扩张速度，Kilani 想知道游戏结束后每名玩家将控制多少个格子（在其中拥有城堡）。

input.ai: 第一行包含三个整数 n$$$n$$$、m$$$m$$$ 和 p$$$p$$$(1≤n,m≤1000$$$1 \le n, m \le 1000$$$，1≤p≤9$$$1 \le p \le 9$$$)，分别表示网格的大小和玩家数量。

接下来的 n$$$n$$$ 行描述游戏网格。每行包含 m$$$m$$$ 个符号，其中“.”表示空单元格，“#”表示被阻塞的单元格，数字 x$$$x$$$(1≤x≤p$$$1 \le x \le p$$$)表示属于玩家 x$$$x$$$ 的城堡。
保证每位玩家在网格上至少拥有一座城堡。

output.ai: 输出 p$$$p$$$ 个整数，表示游戏结束后每位玩家所控制的单元格数量。

statement.title: C. An impassioned circulation of affection

legend: Nadeko's birthday is approaching! As she decorated the room for the party, a long garland of Dianthus-shaped paper pieces was placed on a prominent part of the wall. Brother Koyomi will like it!

Still unsatisfied with the garland, Nadeko decided to polish it again. The garland has n pieces numbered from 1 to n from left to right, and the i-th piece has a colour si, denoted by a lowercase English letter. Nadeko will repaint at most m of the pieces to give each of them an arbitrary new colour (still denoted by a lowercase English letter). After this work, she finds out all subsegments of the garland containing pieces of only colour c — Brother Koyomi's favourite one, and takes the length of the longest among them to be the Koyomity of the garland.

For instance, let's say the garland is represented by "kooomo", and Brother Koyomi's favourite colour is "o". Among all subsegments containing pieces of "o" only, "ooo" is the longest, with a length of 3. Thus the Koyomity of this garland equals 3.

But problem arises as Nadeko is unsure about Brother Koyomi's favourite colour, and has swaying ideas on the amount of work to do. She has q plans on this, each of which can be expressed as a pair of an integer mi and a lowercase letter ci, meanings of which are explained above. You are to find out the maximum Koyomity achievable after repainting the garland according to each plan.
input: The first line of input contains a positive integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 1 500) — the length of the garland.
The second line contains n lowercase English letters s1s2... sn as a string — the initial colours of paper pieces on the garland.
The third line contains a positive integer q (1 ≤ q ≤ 200 000) — the number of plans Nadeko has.

The next q lines describe one plan each: the i-th among them contains an integer mi (1 ≤ mi ≤ n) — the maximum amount of pieces to repaint, followed by a space, then by a lowercase English letter ci — Koyomi's possible favourite colour.
output: Output q lines: for each work plan, output one line containing an integer — the largest Koyomity achievable after repainting the garland according to it.
note: In the first sample, there are three plans:
In the first plan, at most 1 piece can be repainted. Repainting the "y" piece to become "o" results in "kooomi", whose Koyomity of 3 is the best achievable;
In the second plan, at most 4 pieces can be repainted, and "oooooo" results in a Koyomity of 6;
In the third plan, at most 4 pieces can be repainted, and "mmmmmi" and "kmmmmm" both result in a Koyomity of 5.

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含一个正整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 1 500）——花环的长度。
第二行包含一个由 n 个小写英文字母 s1s2... sn 组成的字符串——花环上纸片的初始颜色。
第三行包含一个正整数 q（1 ≤ q ≤ 200 000）——Nadeko 拥有的方案数量。
接下来的 q 行每行描述一个方案：其中第 i 行包含一个整数 mi（1 ≤ mi ≤ n）——最多可以重新涂色的纸片数量，随后是一个空格，然后是一个小写英文字母 ci——Koyomi 可能喜欢的颜色。

output.ai: 输出 q 行：对于每个方案，输出一行，其中包含一个整数——按照该方案重新涂色花环后所能达到的最大 Koyomity。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，共有三个方案：
在第一个方案中，至多可以重新涂 1 个棋子。将“y”棋子重新涂成“o”后得到“kooomi”，其 Koyomity 为 3，这是能够达到的最佳结果；
在第二个方案中，至多可以重新涂 4 个棋子，得到“oooooo”，其 Koyomity 为 6；
在第三个方案中，至多可以重新涂 4 个棋子，得到“mmmmmi”和“kmmmmm”时，二者的 Koyomity 均为 5。

legend.ai: Nadeko 的生日就要到了！她为聚会装饰房间时，一条由石竹花形状的纸片组成的长花环被挂在了墙上的显眼位置。Koyomi 哥哥一定会喜欢的！

不过，Nadeko 对这条花环仍不满意，于是决定再次打磨它。花环上有 n 个纸片，从左到右编号为 1 到 n，第 i 个纸片的颜色为 si，用一个小写英文字母表示。Nadeko 最多可以重新涂 m 个纸片，并将每个纸片涂成任意的新颜色（仍用小写英文字母表示）。完成后，她找出了花环中所有仅包含颜色 c 的纸片的子段，其中 c 是 Koyomi 哥哥最喜欢的颜色，并将其中最长子段的长度称为这条花环的 Koyomity。
例如，假设花环表示为“kooomo”，而 Koyomi 哥哥最喜欢的颜色是“o”。在所有仅包含“o”色纸片的子段中，“ooo”最长，长度为 3。因此，这条花环的 Koyomity 等于 3。
但是，Nadeko 不确定 Koyomi 哥哥最喜欢的颜色，而且对于要进行多少工作也有不同的想法。她有 q 个计划，每个计划都可以表示为一对整数 mi 和小写字母 ci，其含义如上所述。你需要求出按照每个计划重新涂色后能够达到的最大 Koyomity。

legend: Filya just learned new geometry object — rectangle. He is given a field consisting of n × n unit cells. Rows are numbered from bottom to top with integer from 1 to n. Columns are numbered from left to right with integers from 1 to n. Cell, located at the intersection of the row r and column c is denoted as (r, c). Filya has painted two rectangles, such that their sides are parallel to coordinate axes and each cell lies fully inside or fully outside each of them. Moreover, no cell lies in both rectangles.

Later, hedgehog Filya became interested in the location of his rectangles but was unable to find the sheet of paper they were painted on. They were taken by Sonya and now she wants to play a little game with Filya. He tells her a query rectangle and she replies with the number of initial rectangles that lie fully inside the given query rectangle. The query rectangle should match the same conditions as initial rectangles. Rectangle lies fully inside the query if each o its cells lies inside the query.
Filya knows Sonya really well, so is sure that if he asks more than 200 questions she will stop to reply.

For each query an integer between 0 and 2 is returned — the number of initial rectangles that lie fully inside the query rectangle.

You are allowed to ask no more than 200 queries. After each query you should perform "flush" operation and read the answer.

In case you suppose you've already determined the location of two rectangles (or run out of queries) you should print "! x11 y11 x12 y12 x21 y21 x22 y22" (without quotes), where first four integers describe the bottom left and up right cells of the first rectangle, and following four describe the corresponding cells of the second rectangle. You can print the rectangles in an arbitrary order. After you have printed the answer, print the end of the line and perform "flush". Your program should terminate immediately after it print the answer.

problems.hint: We want to make the maximum number of $1$ on the diagonal. The operations is actually "moving" the grid up or down, left or right. "Moving" is relative.

legend: You are given a binary matrix $$$A$$$ of size $$$n \times n$$$. Rows are numbered from top to bottom from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$, columns are numbered from left to right from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$. The element located at the intersection of row $$$i$$$ and column $$$j$$$ is called $$$A_{ij}$$$. Consider a set of $$$4$$$ operations:
Cyclically shift all rows up. The row with index $$$i$$$ will be written in place of the row $$$i-1$$$ ($$$2 \le i \le n$$$), the row with index $$$1$$$ will be written in place of the row $$$n$$$.

Cyclically shift all rows down. The row with index $$$i$$$ will be written in place of the row $$$i+1$$$ ($$$1 \le i \le n - 1$$$), the row with index $$$n$$$ will be written in place of the row $$$1$$$.

Cyclically shift all columns to the left. The column with index $$$j$$$ will be written in place of the column $$$j-1$$$ ($$$2 \le j \le n$$$), the column with index $$$1$$$ will be written in place of the column $$$n$$$.

Cyclically shift all columns to the right. The column with index $$$j$$$ will be written in place of the column $$$j+1$$$ ($$$1 \le j \le n - 1$$$), the column with index $$$n$$$ will be written in place of the column $$$1$$$.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/f3922cf1689c2176413d7f60a8fb3753e52b7e6a.png)
You can perform an arbitrary (possibly zero) number of operations on the matrix; the operations can be performed in any order.
After that, you can perform an arbitrary (possibly zero) number of new xor-operations:
Select any element $$$A_{ij}$$$ and assign it with new value $$$A_{ij} \oplus 1$$$. In other words, the value of $$$(A_{ij} + 1) \bmod 2$$$ will have to be written into element $$$A_{ij}$$$.
Each application of this xor-operation costs one burl. Note that the $$$4$$$ shift operations — are free. These $$$4$$$ operations can only be performed before xor-operations are performed.

Output the minimum number of burles you would have to pay to make the $$$A$$$ matrix unitary. A unitary matrix is a matrix with ones on the main diagonal and the rest of its elements are zeros (that is, $$$A_{ij} = 1$$$ if $$$i = j$$$ and $$$A_{ij} = 0$$$ otherwise).
input: The first line of the input contains an integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) —the number of test cases in the test.
The descriptions of the test cases follow. Before each test case, an empty line is written in the input.
The first line of each test case contains a single number $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 2000$$$)
This is followed by $$$n$$$ lines, each containing exactly $$$n$$$ characters and consisting only of zeros and ones. These lines describe the values in the elements of the matrix.
It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n^2$$$ values over all test cases does not exceed $$$4 \cdot 10^6$$$.
output: For each test case, output the minimum number of burles you would have to pay to make the $$$A$$$ matrix unitary. In other words, print the minimum number of xor-operations it will take after applying cyclic shifts to the matrix for the $$$A$$$ matrix to become unitary.
note: In the first test case, you can do the following: first, shift all the rows down cyclically, then the main diagonal of the matrix will contain only "1". Then it will be necessary to apply xor-operation to the only "1" that is not on the main diagonal.
In the second test case, you can make a unitary matrix by applying the operation $$$2$$$ — cyclic shift of rows upward twice to the matrix.

legend.ai: 给定一个大小为 $$$n \times n$$$ 的二进制矩阵 $$$A$$$。行从上到下编号为 $$$1$$$ 到 $$$n$$$，列从左到右编号为 $$$1$$$ 到 $$$n$$$。位于第 $$$i$$$ 行和第 $$$j$$$ 列交点处的元素称为 $$$A_{ij}$$$。考虑一组包含 $$$4$$$ 个操作的操作：
将所有行循环上移。编号为 $$$i$$$ 的行将被写入编号为 $$$i-1$$$ 的行的位置($$$2 \le i \le n$$$)，编号为 $$$1$$$ 的行将被写入编号为 $$$n$$$ 的行的位置。
将所有行循环下移。编号为 $$$i$$$ 的行将被写入编号为 $$$i+1$$$ 的行的位置($$$1 \le i \le n - 1$$$)，编号为 $$$n$$$ 的行将被写入编号为 $$$1$$$ 的行的位置。
将所有列循环左移。编号为 $$$j$$$ 的列将被写入编号为 $$$j-1$$$ 的列的位置($$$2 \le j \le n$$$)，编号为 $$$1$$$ 的列将被写入编号为 $$$n$$$ 的列的位置。
将所有列循环右移。编号为 $$$j$$$ 的列将被写入编号为 $$$j+1$$$ 的列的位置($$$1 \le j \le n - 1$$$)，编号为 $$$n$$$ 的列将被写入编号为 $$$1$$$ 的列的位置。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/f3922cf1689c2176413d7f60a8fb3753e52b7e6a.png)
你可以对该矩阵执行任意（可能为零）次操作；这些操作可以按任意顺序执行。

每次执行该异或操作需要花费一个 burle。注意，$$$4$$$ 移位操作是免费的。这些 $$$4$$$ 操作只能在执行异或操作之前进行。

problems.hint: Where can you find a different way between the nodes? Count that in a tree.

legend: A connected undirected graph is called a vertex cactus, if each vertex of this graph belongs to at most one simple cycle.

A simple cycle in a undirected graph is a sequence of distinct vertices v1, v2, ..., vt (t > 2), such that for any i (1 ≤ i < t) exists an edge between vertices vi and vi + 1, and also exists an edge between vertices v1 and vt.

A simple path in a undirected graph is a sequence of not necessarily distinct vertices v1, v2, ..., vt (t > 0), such that for any i (1 ≤ i < t) exists an edge between vertices vi and vi + 1 and furthermore each edge occurs no more than once. We'll say that a simple path v1, v2, ..., vt starts at vertex v1 and ends at vertex vt.

You've got a graph consisting of n vertices and m edges, that is a vertex cactus. Also, you've got a list of k pairs of interesting vertices xi, yi, for which you want to know the following information — the number of distinct simple paths that start at vertex xi and end at vertex yi. We will consider two simple paths distinct if the sets of edges of the paths are distinct.
For each pair of interesting vertices count the number of distinct simple paths between them. As this number can be rather large, you should calculate it modulo 1000000007 (109 + 7).
input: The first line contains two space-separated integers n, m (2 ≤ n ≤ 105; 1 ≤ m ≤ 105) — the number of vertices and edges in the graph, correspondingly. Next m lines contain the description of the edges: the i-th line contains two space-separated integers ai, bi (1 ≤ ai, bi ≤ n) — the indexes of the vertices connected by the i-th edge.

The next line contains a single integer k (1 ≤ k ≤ 105) — the number of pairs of interesting vertices. Next k lines contain the list of pairs of interesting vertices: the i-th line contains two space-separated numbers xi, yi (1 ≤ xi, yi ≤ n; xi ≠ yi) — the indexes of interesting vertices in the i-th pair.
It is guaranteed that the given graph is a vertex cactus. It is guaranteed that the graph contains no loops or multiple edges. Consider the graph vertices are numbered from 1 to n.
output: Print k lines: in the i-th line print a single integer — the number of distinct simple ways, starting at xi and ending at yi, modulo 1000000007 (109 + 7).

legend.ai: 一个连通无向图被称为点仙人掌图，当且仅当该图中的每个顶点至多属于一个简单环。
无向图中的一个简单环是由互不相同的顶点 v1、v2、...、vt（t > 2）组成的序列，满足对于任意 i（1 ≤ i < t），顶点 vi 与 vi + 1 之间存在一条边，并且顶点 v1 与 vt 之间也存在一条边。
无向图中的一条简单路径是由不一定互不相同的顶点 v1、v2、...、vt（t > 0）组成的序列，满足对于任意 i（1 ≤ i < t），顶点 vi 与 vi + 1 之间存在一条边，并且每条边出现次数不超过一次。我们称一条简单路径 v1、v2、...、vt 从顶点 v1 开始，到顶点 vt 结束。
给定一个由 n 个顶点和 m 条边组成的图，且该图是一个点仙人掌图。此外，还给定了 k 对感兴趣的顶点 xi、yi，对于每一对顶点，你需要求出以下信息：从顶点 xi 开始并在顶点 yi 结束的不同简单路径的数量。如果两条路径所包含的边的集合不同，我们就认为它们是不同的简单路径。
对于每一对特殊顶点，计算它们之间不同简单路径的数量。由于这个数量可能很大，你需要将其对 1000000007（109 + 7）取模后计算。

input.ai: 第一行包含两个以空格分隔的整数 n、m（2 ≤ n ≤ 105；1 ≤ m ≤ 105），分别表示图中顶点和边的数量。接下来 m 行描述各条边：第 i 行包含两个以空格分隔的整数 ai、bi（1 ≤ ai、bi ≤ n），表示第 i 条边所连接的顶点编号。
下一行包含一个整数 k（1 ≤ k ≤ 105），表示特殊顶点对的数量。接下来 k 行包含特殊顶点对的列表：第 i 行包含两个以空格分隔的数 xi、yi（1 ≤ xi、yi ≤ n；xi ≠ yi），表示第 i 对中的特殊顶点编号。
保证给定的图是点仙人掌图。保证图中不包含环或重边。设图中的顶点编号为 1 至 n。

output.ai: 输出 k 行：第 i 行输出一个整数，表示从 xi 出发并到达 yi 的不同简单路径数量，对 1000000007（109 + 7）取模的结果。

legend: A substring of some string is called the most frequent, if the number of its occurrences is not less than number of occurrences of any other substring.

You are given a set of strings. A string (not necessarily from this set) is called good if all elements of the set are the most frequent substrings of this string. Restore the non-empty good string with minimum length. If several such strings exist, restore lexicographically minimum string. If there are no good strings, print "NO" (without quotes).
A substring of a string is a contiguous subsequence of letters in the string. For example, "ab", "c", "abc" are substrings of string "abc", while "ac" is not a substring of that string.
The number of occurrences of a substring in a string is the number of starting positions in the string where the substring occurs. These occurrences could overlap.
String a is lexicographically smaller than string b, if a is a prefix of b, or a has a smaller letter at the first position where a and b differ.
input: The first line contains integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 105) — the number of strings in the set.
Each of the next n lines contains a non-empty string consisting of lowercase English letters. It is guaranteed that the strings are distinct.
The total length of the strings doesn't exceed 105.
output: Print the non-empty good string with minimum length. If several good strings exist, print lexicographically minimum among them. Print "NO" (without quotes) if there are no good strings.
note: One can show that in the first sample only two good strings with minimum length exist: "cfmailru" and "mailrucf". The first string is lexicographically minimum.

legend.ai: 如果某个字符串的子串出现次数不少于任何其他子串的出现次数，则称该子串为出现次数最多的子串。
给定一个字符串集合。如果一个字符串（不一定属于该集合）的所有子串中，集合中的所有元素都是出现次数最多的子串，则称该字符串是好的。请还原一个长度最小的非空好字符串。如果存在多个这样的字符串，则还原字典序最小的字符串。如果不存在好字符串，输出 "NO"（不含引号）。
字符串的子串是字符串中连续的字母子序列。例如，"ab"、"c"、"abc" 是字符串 "abc" 的子串，而 "ac" 不是该字符串的子串。
一个子串在字符串中的出现次数，是指该子串在字符串中出现的起始位置数量。这些出现可以相互重叠。
如果字符串 a 是字符串 b 的前缀，或者 a 和 b 在第一个不同的位置上 a 的字母更小，则称字符串 a 的字典序小于字符串 b。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 105），表示集合中字符串的数量。
接下来的 n 行中，每行包含一个由小写英文字母组成的非空字符串。保证这些字符串互不相同。
字符串的总长度不超过 10^5。

output.ai: 输出长度最小的非空 good 字符串。如果存在多个 good 字符串，输出其中字典序最小的字符串。如果不存在 good 字符串，输出“NO”（不含引号）。

note.ai: 可以证明，在第一个样例中，只有两个长度最小的 good 字符串：“cfmailru”和“mailrucf”。前一个字符串的字典序更小。

statement.title: C. Sereja and the Arrangement of Numbers

legend: Let's call an array consisting of n integer numbers a1, a2, ..., an, beautiful if it has the following property:
consider all pairs of numbers x, y (x ≠ y), such that number x occurs in the array a and number y occurs in the array a;
for each pair x, y must exist some position j (1 ≤ j < n), such that at least one of the two conditions are met, either aj = x, aj + 1 = y, or aj = y, aj + 1 = x.

Sereja wants to build a beautiful array a, consisting of n integers. But not everything is so easy, Sereja's friend Dima has m coupons, each contains two integers qi, wi. Coupon i costs wi and allows you to use as many numbers qi as you want when constructing the array a. Values qi are distinct. Sereja has no coupons, so Dima and Sereja have made the following deal. Dima builds some beautiful array a of n elements. After that he takes wi rubles from Sereja for each qi, which occurs in the array a. Sereja believed his friend and agreed to the contract, and now he is wondering, what is the maximum amount of money he can pay.
Help Sereja, find the maximum amount of money he can pay to Dima.

It is guaranteed that all qi are distinct.

Please, do not use the %lld specifier to read or write 64-bit integers in С++. It is preferred to use the cin, cout streams or the %I64d specifier.
note: In the first sample Sereja can pay 5 rubles, for example, if Dima constructs the following array: [1, 2, 1, 2, 2]. There are another optimal arrays for this test.
In the third sample Sereja can pay 100 rubles, if Dima constructs the following array: [2].

对于每一对 x、y，都必须存在某个位置 j（1 ≤ j < n），使得以下两个条件中至少有一个成立：aj = x 且 aj + 1 = y，或者 aj = y 且 aj + 1 = x。

legend: Jeff got 2n real numbers a1, a2, ..., a2n as a birthday present. The boy hates non-integer numbers, so he decided to slightly "adjust" the numbers he's got. Namely, Jeff consecutively executes n operations, each of them goes as follows:
choose indexes i and j (i ≠ j) that haven't been chosen yet;
round element ai to the nearest integer that isn't more than ai (assign to ai: ⌊ ai ⌋);
round element aj to the nearest integer that isn't less than aj (assign to aj: ⌈ aj ⌉).

Nevertheless, Jeff doesn't want to hurt the feelings of the person who gave him the sequence. That's why the boy wants to perform the operations so as to make the absolute value of the difference between the sum of elements before performing the operations and the sum of elements after performing the operations as small as possible. legend.ai: Jeff 收到 2n 个实数 a1, a2, ..., a2n 作为生日礼物。这个男孩讨厌非整数，因此他决定对收到的数字进行一些细微的“调整”。具体来说，Jeff 连续执行 n 次操作，每次操作如下：
选择一对尚未被选过的下标 i 和 j（i ≠ j）；

不过，Jeff 不想伤害把这个序列送给他的人的感情。因此，这个男孩想要执行这些操作，使执行操作前的元素之和与执行操作后的元素之和之差的绝对值尽可能小。请帮助 Jeff 找出这个差的最小绝对值。

statement.title: D. Paths in a Complete Binary Tree

legend: T is a complete binary tree consisting of n vertices. It means that exactly one vertex is a root, and each vertex is either a leaf (and doesn't have children) or an inner node (and has exactly two children). All leaves of a complete binary tree have the same depth (distance from the root). So n is a number such that n + 1 is a power of 2.
In the picture you can see a complete binary tree with n = 15.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7cf45e9d9e44d8d0a3972224b62a35dd86b5f1b3.png)

Vertices are numbered from 1 to n in a special recursive way: we recursively assign numbers to all vertices from the left subtree (if current vertex is not a leaf), then assign a number to the current vertex, and then recursively assign numbers to all vertices from the right subtree (if it exists). In the picture vertices are numbered exactly using this algorithm. It is clear that for each size of a complete binary tree exists exactly one way to give numbers to all vertices. This way of numbering is called symmetric.
You have to write a program that for given n answers q queries to the tree.

Each query consists of an integer number ui (1 ≤ ui ≤ n) and a string si, where ui is the number of vertex, and si represents the path starting from this vertex. String si doesn't contain any characters other than 'L', 'R' and 'U', which mean traverse to the left child, to the right child and to the parent, respectively. Characters from si have to be processed from left to right, considering that ui is the vertex where the path starts. If it's impossible to process a character (for example, to go to the left child of a leaf), then you have to skip it. The answer is the number of vertex where the path represented by si ends.
For example, if ui = 4 and si = «UURL», then the answer is 10.
input: The first line contains two integer numbers n and q (1 ≤ n ≤ 1018, q ≥ 1). n is such that n + 1 is a power of 2.

The next 2q lines represent queries; each query consists of two consecutive lines. The first of these two lines contains ui (1 ≤ ui ≤ n), the second contains non-empty string si. si doesn't contain any characters other than 'L', 'R' and 'U'.
It is guaranteed that the sum of lengths of si (for each i such that 1 ≤ i ≤ q) doesn't exceed 105.
output: Print q numbers, i-th number must be the answer to the i-th query.

input.ai: 第一行包含两个整数 n 和 q（1 ≤ n ≤ 10^18，q ≥ 1）。保证 n + 1 是 2 的幂。
接下来的 2q 行表示若干查询；每个查询由连续的两行组成。其中第一行包含 ui（1 ≤ ui ≤ n），第二行包含非空字符串 si。si 中只包含字符 'L'、'R' 和 'U'。
保证所有 si 的长度之和（对每个满足 1 ≤ i ≤ q 的 i）不超过 10^5。

output.ai: 输出 q 个数，第 i 个数必须是第 i 个查询的答案。

legend.ai: T 是一棵由 n 个顶点组成的完全二叉树。这意味着其中恰好有一个顶点是根，并且每个顶点要么是叶子（没有子节点），要么是内部节点（恰好有两个子节点）。完全二叉树的所有叶子深度都相同（即到根的距离相同）。因此，n 是一个满足 n + 1 为 2 的幂的数。
图中展示了一棵 n = 15 的完全二叉树。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7cf45e9d9e44d8d0a3972224b62a35dd86b5f1b3.png)
顶点以一种特殊的递归方式从 1 编号到 n：我们先递归地为左子树中的所有顶点编号（如果当前顶点不是叶子），然后为当前顶点编号，最后递归地为右子树中的所有顶点编号（如果右子树存在）。图中的顶点正是使用该算法编号的。显然，对于每一种大小的完全二叉树，为所有顶点编号的方法都恰好只有一种。这种编号方式称为对称编号。
你需要编写一个程序，对于给定的 n，回答树上的 q 个查询。
每个查询由一个整数 ui（1 ≤ ui ≤ n）和一个字符串 si 组成，其中 ui 是顶点的编号，si 表示从该顶点开始的路径。字符串 si 只包含字符 'L'、'R' 和 'U'，分别表示移动到左儿子、右儿子和父节点。需要从左到右处理 si 中的字符，并将 ui 视为路径的起点。如果无法处理某个字符（例如，从叶子移动到左儿子），则跳过该字符。答案是由 si 表示的路径结束时所在顶点的编号。
例如，如果 ui = 4 且 si = «UURL»，那么答案是 10。

legend: Nauuo is a girl who loves drawing circles.
One day she has drawn a circle and wanted to draw a tree on it.
The tree is a connected undirected graph consisting of n$$$n$$$ nodes and n−1$$$n-1$$$ edges. The nodes are numbered from 1$$$1$$$ to n$$$n$$$.
Nauuo wants to draw a tree on the circle, the nodes of the tree should be in n$$$n$$$ distinct points on the circle, and the edges should be straight without crossing each other.
"Without crossing each other" means that every two edges have no common point or the only common point is an endpoint of both edges.

Nauuo wants to draw the tree using a permutation of n$$$n$$$ elements. A permutation of n$$$n$$$ elements is a sequence of integers p1,p2,…,pn$$$p_1,p_2,\ldots,p_n$$$ in which every integer from 1$$$1$$$ to n$$$n$$$ appears exactly once.
After a permutation is chosen Nauuo draws the i$$$i$$$-th node in the pi$$$p_i$$$-th point on the circle, then draws the edges connecting the nodes.

The tree is given, Nauuo wants to know how many permutations are there so that the tree drawn satisfies the rule (the edges are straight without crossing each other). She only wants to know the answer modulo 998244353$$$998244353$$$, can you help her?
It is obvious that whether a permutation is valid or not does not depend on which n$$$n$$$ points on the circle are chosen.
input: The first line contains a single integer n$$$n$$$ (2≤n≤2⋅105$$$2\le n\le 2\cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of nodes in the tree.
Each of the next n−1$$$n-1$$$ lines contains two integers u$$$u$$$ and v$$$v$$$ (1≤u,v≤n$$$1\le u,v\le n$$$), denoting there is an edge between u$$$u$$$ and v$$$v$$$.
It is guaranteed that the given edges form a tree.
output: The output contains a single integer — the number of permutations suitable to draw the given tree on a circle satisfying the rule, modulo 998244353$$$998244353$$$.
note: Example 1
All valid permutations and their spanning trees are as follows.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/4bbeb64c560c5faab632ae54f8543dbda91b3145.png)
Here is an example of invalid permutation: the edges (1,3)$$$(1,3)$$$ and (2,4)$$$(2,4)$$$ are crossed.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/28c77a9b93eca97a2911d8fe525f9bed5cf5a027.png)
Example 2
Every permutation leads to a valid tree, so the answer is 4!=24$$$4! = 24$$$.

legend.ai: Nauuo 是一个喜欢画圆的女孩。
一天，她画了一个圆，并想在圆上画一棵树。
这棵树是一个由 n$$$n$$$ 个节点和 n−1$$$n-1$$$ 条边组成的连通无向图。节点编号从 1$$$1$$$ 到 n$$$n$$$。
Nauuo 想在圆上绘制一棵树，树的节点应位于圆上的 n$$$n$$$ 个互不相同的点上，并且边应为直线且彼此不相交。
“彼此不相交”是指任意两条边没有公共点，或者它们唯一的公共点是这两条边的端点。
Nauuo 想使用一个由 n$$$n$$$ 个元素组成的排列来绘制这棵树。由 n$$$n$$$ 个元素组成的排列是一个整数序列 p1,p2,…,pn$$$p_1,p_2,\ldots,p_n$$$，其中从 1$$$1$$$ 到 n$$$n$$$ 的每个整数都恰好出现一次。
选定一个排列后，Nauuo 将第 i$$$i$$$ 个节点绘制在圆上的第 pi$$$p_i$$$ 个点上，然后绘制连接这些节点的边。
给定这棵树，Nauuo 想知道有多少个排列能够使绘制出的树满足规则(边为直线且彼此不相交)。她只想知道答案对 998244353$$$998244353$$$ 取模后的结果，你能帮助她吗？
显然，一个排列是否有效与选择圆上的哪 n$$$n$$$ 个点无关。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n$$$n$$$(2≤n≤2⋅105$$$2\le n\le 2\cdot 10^5$$$)，表示树中的节点数。
接下来的 n−1$$$n-1$$$ 行中，每行包含两个整数 u$$$u$$$ 和 v$$$v$$$(1≤u,v≤n$$$1\le u,v\le n$$$)，表示 u$$$u$$$ 和 v$$$v$$$ 之间存在一条边。
保证给出的边构成一棵树。

output.ai: 输出一个整数，表示满足规则、适合在圆上绘制给定树的排列数量，对 998244353$$$998244353$$$ 取模。

legend: Little town Nsk consists of n junctions connected by m bidirectional roads. Each road connects two distinct junctions and no two roads connect the same pair of junctions. It is possible to get from any junction to any other junction by these roads. The distance between two junctions is equal to the minimum possible number of roads on a path between them.

In order to improve the transportation system, the city council asks mayor to build one new road. The problem is that the mayor has just bought a wonderful new car and he really enjoys a ride from his home, located near junction s to work located near junction t. Thus, he wants to build a new road in such a way that the distance between these two junctions won't decrease.

You are assigned a task to compute the number of pairs of junctions that are not connected by the road, such that if the new road between these two junctions is built the distance between s and t won't decrease.
input: The firt line of the input contains integers n, m, s and t (2 ≤ n ≤ 1000, 1 ≤ m ≤ 1000, 1 ≤ s, t ≤ n, s ≠ t) — the number of junctions and the number of roads in Nsk, as well as the indices of junctions where mayors home and work are located respectively. The i-th of the following m lines contains two integers ui and vi (1 ≤ ui, vi ≤ n, ui ≠ vi), meaning that this road connects junctions ui and vi directly. It is guaranteed that there is a path between any two junctions and no two roads connect the same pair of junctions.
output: Print one integer — the number of pairs of junctions not connected by a direct road, such that building a road between these two junctions won't decrease the distance between junctions s and t.

legend.ai: 小镇 Nsk 由 n 个路口组成，这些路口之间通过 m 条双向道路相连。每条道路连接两个不同的路口，且不存在两条道路连接同一对路口。通过这些道路，可以从任意路口到达任意其他路口。两个路口之间的距离等于连接它们的路径上道路数量的最小值。
为了改善交通系统，市议会要求市长修建一条新道路。问题在于，市长刚买了一辆很棒的新车，非常享受从位于路口 s 附近的家前往位于路口 t 附近的工作地点的驾车过程。因此，他希望以一种不会缩短这两个路口之间距离的方式修建新道路。
你的任务是计算不直接由道路相连的路口对数，使得在这两个路口之间修建新道路后，s 与 t 之间的距离不会缩短。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含整数 n、m、s 和 t（2 ≤ n ≤ 1000，1 ≤ m ≤ 1000，1 ≤ s, t ≤ n，s ≠ t），分别表示 Nsk 中路口和道路的数量，以及市长家和工作地点所在路口的编号。接下来的 m 行中，第 i 行包含两个整数 ui 和 vi（1 ≤ ui, vi ≤ n，ui ≠ vi），表示这条道路直接连接路口 ui 和 vi。保证任意两个路口之间都存在路径，且不存在两条道路连接同一对路口。

output.ai: 输出一个整数，即不由直接道路相连的路口对数，使得在这两个路口之间修建道路后，路口 s 与 t 之间的距离不会缩短。

legend: Sereja has an n × m rectangular table a, each cell of the table contains a zero or a number one. Sereja wants his table to meet the following requirement: each connected component of the same values forms a rectangle with sides parallel to the sides of the table. Rectangles should be filled with cells, that is, if a component form a rectangle of size h × w, then the component must contain exactly hw cells.
A connected component of the same values is a set of cells of the table that meet the following conditions:
every two cells of the set have the same value;
the cells of the set form a connected region on the table (two cells are connected if they are adjacent in some row or some column of the table);
it is impossible to add any cell to the set unless we violate the two previous conditions.
Can Sereja change the values of at most k cells of the table so that the table met the described requirement? What minimum number of table cells should he change in this case?
input: The first line contains integers n, m and k (1 ≤ n, m ≤ 100; 1 ≤ k ≤ 10). Next n lines describe the table a: the i-th of them contains m integers ai1, ai2, ..., aim (0 ≤ ai, j ≤ 1) — the values in the cells of the i-th row.
output: Print -1, if it is impossible to meet the requirement. Otherwise, print the minimum number of cells which should be changed.

legend.ai: Sereja 有一个 n × m 的矩形表格 a，表格中的每个单元格都包含 0 或 1。Sereja 希望他的表格满足以下要求：每个相同值的连通分量都构成一个边与表格边平行的矩形。矩形应当由单元格完整填充，也就是说，如果某个分量构成一个大小为 h × w 的矩形，那么该分量必须恰好包含 hw 个单元格。
相同值的连通分量是满足以下条件的表格单元格集合：
集合中的任意两个单元格都具有相同的值；
集合中的单元格在表格上构成一个连通区域（如果两个单元格在表格的同一行或同一列中相邻，则称它们相连）；
除非违反前两个条件，否则不可能向集合中添加任何单元格。
Sereja 能否改变表格中至多 k 个单元格的值，使表格满足上述要求？在这种情况下，他至少需要改变多少个表格单元格？

input.ai: 第一行包含整数 n、m 和 k（1 ≤ n，m ≤ 100；1 ≤ k ≤ 10）。接下来的 n 行描述表格 a：其中第 i 行包含 m 个整数 ai1，ai2，...，aim（0 ≤ ai, j ≤ 1），表示第 i 行各单元格中的值。

output.ai: 如果无法满足要求，输出 -1。否则，输出需要更改单元格的最小数量。

legend: This problem is different from the easy version. In this version Ujan makes at most 2n$$$2n$$$ swaps. In addition, k≤1000,n≤50$$$k \le 1000, n \le 50$$$ and it is necessary to print swaps themselves. You can hack this problem if you solve it. But you can hack the previous problem only if you solve both problems.
After struggling and failing many times, Ujan decided to try to clean up his house again. He decided to get his strings in order first.

Ujan has two distinct strings s$$$s$$$ and t$$$t$$$ of length n$$$n$$$ consisting of only of lowercase English characters. He wants to make them equal. Since Ujan is lazy, he will perform the following operation at most 2n$$$2n$$$ times: he takes two positions i$$$i$$$ and j$$$j$$$ (1≤i,j≤n$$$1 \le i,j \le n$$$, the values i$$$i$$$ and j$$$j$$$ can be equal or different), and swaps the characters si$$$s_i$$$ and tj$$$t_j$$$.

Ujan's goal is to make the strings s$$$s$$$ and t$$$t$$$ equal. He does not need to minimize the number of performed operations: any sequence of operations of length 2n$$$2n$$$ or shorter is suitable.
input: The first line contains a single integer k$$$k$$$ (1≤k≤1000$$$1 \leq k \leq 1000$$$), the number of test cases.
For each of the test cases, the first line contains a single integer n$$$n$$$ (2≤n≤50$$$2 \leq n \leq 50$$$), the length of the strings s$$$s$$$ and t$$$t$$$.

Each of the next two lines contains the strings s$$$s$$$ and t$$$t$$$, each having length exactly n$$$n$$$. The strings consist only of lowercase English letters. It is guaranteed that strings are different.
output: For each test case, output "Yes" if Ujan can make the two strings equal with at most 2n$$$2n$$$ operations and "No" otherwise. You can print each letter in any case (upper or lower).

In the case of "Yes" print m$$$m$$$ (1≤m≤2n$$$1 \le m \le 2n$$$) on the next line, where m$$$m$$$ is the number of swap operations to make the strings equal. Then print m$$$m$$$ lines, each line should contain two integers i,j$$$i, j$$$ (1≤i,j≤n$$$1 \le i, j \le n$$$) meaning that Ujan swaps si$$$s_i$$$ and tj$$$t_j$$$ during the corresponding operation. You do not need to minimize the number of operations. Any sequence of length not more than 2n$$$2n$$$ is suitable.

Ujan 的目标是使字符串 s$$$s$$$ 和 t$$$t$$$ 相等。他不需要最小化所执行操作的次数：长度为 2n$$$2n$$$ 或更短的任意操作序列都可以。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 k$$$k$$$ (1≤k≤1000$$$1 \leq k \leq 1000$$$)，表示测试用例的数量。
对于每个测试用例，第一行包含一个整数 n$$$n$$$ (2≤n≤50$$$2 \leq n \leq 50$$$)，表示字符串 s$$$s$$$ 和 t$$$t$$$ 的长度。

output.ai: 对于每个测试用例，如果 Ujan 能在不超过 2n$$$2n$$$ 次操作内使两个字符串相等，则输出 "Yes"，否则输出 "No"。每个字母都可以使用任意大小写(大写或小写)输出。

如果答案为 "Yes"，则在下一行输出 m$$$m$$$ (1≤m≤2n$$$1 \le m \le 2n$$$)，其中 m$$$m$$$ 是使两个字符串相等所需的交换操作次数。然后输出 m$$$m$$$ 行，每行应包含两个整数 i,j$$$i, j$$$ (1≤i,j≤n$$$1 \le i, j \le n$$$)，表示在对应操作中 Ujan 交换 si$$$s_i$$$ 和 tj$$$t_j$$$。不需要最小化操作次数。长度不超过 2n$$$2n$$$ 的任意序列都可以。

legend: Berland has managed to repel the flatlanders' attack and is now starting the counter attack.

Flatland has n cities, numbered from 1 to n, and some pairs of them are connected by bidirectional roads. The Flatlandian maps show roads between cities if and only if there is in fact no road between this pair of cities (we do not know whether is it a clever spy-proof strategy or just saving ink). In other words, if two cities are connected by a road on a flatland map, then there is in fact no road between them. The opposite situation is also true: if two cities are not connected by a road on a flatland map, then in fact, there is a road between them.

The berlanders got hold of a flatland map. Now Vasya the Corporal is commissioned by General Touristov to find all such groups of flatland cities, that in each group of cities you can get from any city to any other one, moving along the actual roads. Also the cities from different groups are unreachable from each other, moving along the actual roads. Indeed, destroying such groups one by one is much easier than surrounding all Flatland at once!
Help the corporal complete this task and finally become a sergeant! Don't forget that a flatland map shows a road between cities if and only if there is in fact no road between them.
input: The first line contains two space-separated integers n and m (1 ≤ n ≤ 5·105, 0 ≤ m ≤ 106) — the number of cities and the number of roads marked on the flatland map, correspondingly.

Next m lines contain descriptions of the cities on the map. The i-th line contains two integers ai and bi (1 ≤ ai, bi ≤ n, ai ≠ bi) — the numbers of cities that are connected by the i-th road on the flatland map.
It is guaranteed that each pair of cities occurs in the input no more than once.
output: On the first line print number k — the number of groups of cities in Flatland, such that in each group you can get from any city to any other one by flatland roads. At the same time, the cities from different groups should be unreachable by flatland roads.
On each of the following k lines first print ti (1 ≤ ti ≤ n) — the number of vertexes in the i-th group. Then print space-separated numbers of cities in the i-th group.
The order of printing groups and the order of printing numbers in the groups does not matter. The total sum ti for all k groups must equal n.
note: In the first sample there are roads only between pairs of cities 1-4 and 2-3.
In the second sample there is no road between cities 1 and 2, but still you can get from one city to the other one through city number 3.

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，只有连接城市 1 和 4、城市 2 和 3 的道路。
在第二个样例中，城市 1 和城市 2 之间没有道路，但你仍然可以经过编号为 3 的城市从一个城市到达另一个城市。

legend.ai: Berland 成功击退了平原人的进攻，现在开始进行反击。

Flatland 有 n 座城市，编号从 1 到 n，其中一些城市对之间由双向道路连接。Flatland 的地图当且仅当某对城市之间实际上不存在道路时，才会显示这两座城市之间有道路（我们不知道这是巧妙的防间谍策略，还是单纯为了节省墨水）。换句话说，如果 Flatland 地图上显示两座城市之间有道路，那么实际上这两座城市之间没有道路。反过来也一样：如果 Flatland 地图上没有显示两座城市之间有道路，那么实际上这两座城市之间存在道路。
Berland 人得到了一张 Flatland 地图。现在，上尉 Vasya 受 General Touristov 委托，需要找出所有这样的 Flatland 城市分组：在每组城市中，沿着实际存在的道路，可以从任意一座城市到达组内任意其他城市；同时，不同分组中的城市之间沿着实际存在的道路互不可达。事实上，逐个摧毁这些分组要比一次性包围整个 Flatland 容易得多！
请帮助这位上尉完成任务，最终晋升为中士！别忘了，Flatland 地图当且仅当两座城市之间实际上没有道路时，才会显示它们之间有道路。

input.ai: 第一行包含两个以空格分隔的整数 n 和 m（1 ≤ n ≤ 5·10^5，0 ≤ m ≤ 10^6），分别表示城市数量以及 Flatland 地图上标记的道路数量。
接下来的 m 行包含地图中城市的描述。第 i 行包含两个整数 ai 和 bi（1 ≤ ai，bi ≤ n，ai ≠ bi）——平原地图中由第 i 条道路连接的城市编号。
保证输入中每对城市最多出现一次。

output.ai: 第一行输出整数 k——平原中城市组的数量，使得在每个组内，都可以通过平原道路从任意城市到达任意其他城市。同时，不同组中的城市之间不能通过平原道路互相到达。
接下来的 k 行中，首先输出 ti（1 ≤ ti ≤ n）——第 i 个组中的顶点数。然后输出第 i 个组中的城市编号，编号之间用空格分隔。
输出各组的顺序以及各组中编号的顺序均不作要求。所有 k 个组的 ti 之和必须等于 n。

legend: You are given array a with n integers and m queries. The i-th query is given with three integers li, ri, xi.
For the i-th query find any position pi (li ≤ pi ≤ ri) so that api ≠ xi.
input: The first line contains two integers n, m (1 ≤ n, m ≤ 2·105) — the number of elements in a and the number of queries.
The second line contains n integers ai (1 ≤ ai ≤ 106) — the elements of the array a.
Each of the next m lines contains three integers li, ri, xi (1 ≤ li ≤ ri ≤ n, 1 ≤ xi ≤ 106) — the parameters of the i-th query.
output: Print m lines. On the i-th line print integer pi — the position of any number not equal to xi in segment [li, ri] or the value  - 1 if there is no such number.

legend.ai: 给定一个包含 n 个整数的数组 a 和 m 次查询。第 i 次查询由三个整数 li、ri、xi 给出。
对于第 i 次查询，找出任意一个位置 pi（li ≤ pi ≤ ri），使得 api ≠ xi。

input.ai: 第一行包含两个整数 n、m（1 ≤ n，m ≤ 2·105），分别表示数组 a 中元素的数量和查询的数量。
第二行包含 n 个整数 ai（1 ≤ ai ≤ 106），表示数组 a 中的元素。
接下来的 m 行中的每一行包含三个整数 l_i、r_i、x_i（1 ≤ l_i ≤ r_i ≤ n，1 ≤ x_i ≤ 10^6），表示第 i 个查询的参数。

output.ai: 输出 m 行。第 i 行输出整数 p_i，表示区间 [l_i, r_i] 中任意一个不等于 x_i 的数的位置；如果不存在这样的数，则输出 - 1。

problems.hint: 1. What doesn't change when the operation is applied? Is it a sufficient condition? 2. What are the important variable of the final string?

legend: Sherlock Holmes found a mysterious correspondence of two VIPs and made up his mind to read it. But there is a problem! The correspondence turned out to be encrypted. The detective tried really hard to decipher the correspondence, but he couldn't understand anything.

At last, after some thought, he thought of something. Let's say there is a word s, consisting of |s| lowercase Latin letters. Then for one operation you can choose a certain position p (1 ≤ p < |s|) and perform one of the following actions:
either replace letter sp with the one that alphabetically follows it and replace letter sp + 1 with the one that alphabetically precedes it;
or replace letter sp with the one that alphabetically precedes it and replace letter sp + 1 with the one that alphabetically follows it.

Let us note that letter "z" doesn't have a defined following letter and letter "a" doesn't have a defined preceding letter. That's why the corresponding changes are not acceptable. If the operation requires performing at least one unacceptable change, then such operation cannot be performed.
Two words coincide in their meaning iff one of them can be transformed into the other one as a result of zero or more operations.

Sherlock Holmes needs to learn to quickly determine the following for each word: how many words can exist that coincide in their meaning with the given word, but differs from the given word in at least one character? Count this number for him modulo 1000000007 (109 + 7).
input: The input data contains several tests. The first line contains the only integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 104) — the number of tests.
Next t lines contain the words, one per line. Each word consists of lowercase Latin letters and has length from 1 to 100, inclusive. Lengths of words can differ.
output: For each word you should print the number of different other words that coincide with it in their meaning — not from the words listed in the input data, but from all possible words. As the sought number can be very large, print its value modulo 1000000007 (109 + 7).
note: Some explanations about the operation:
Note that for each letter, we can clearly define the letter that follows it. Letter "b" alphabetically follows letter "a", letter "c" follows letter "b", ..., "z" follows letter "y".
Preceding letters are defined in the similar manner: letter "y" precedes letter "z", ..., "a" precedes letter "b".
Note that the operation never changes a word's length.
In the first sample you can obtain the only other word "ba". In the second sample you cannot obtain any other word, so the correct answer is 0.

Consider the third sample. One operation can transform word "klmbfxzb" into word "klmcexzb": we should choose p = 4, and replace the fourth letter with the following one ("b"  →  "c"), and the fifth one — with the preceding one ("f"  →  "e"). Also, we can obtain many other words from this one. An operation can transform word "ya" only into one other word "xb".

Word "ya" coincides in its meaning with words "xb", "wc", "vd", ..., "ay" (overall there are 24 other words). The word "klmbfxzb has many more variants — there are 3320092814 other words that coincide with in the meaning. So the answer for the first word equals 24 and for the second one equals 320092793 — the number 3320092814 modulo 109 + 7

output.ai: 对于每个单词，你需要输出与它含义相同的其他不同单词的数量。这些单词不只包括输入数据中列出的单词，还包括所有可能的单词。由于所求数量可能非常大，请输出其对 1000000007 (109 + 7) 取模后的结果。

note.ai: 关于该操作的一些说明：
注意，对于每个字母，我们都可以明确地定义跟在它后面的字母。按字母表顺序，字母 "b" 在字母 "a" 后面，字母 "c" 在字母 "b" 后面，……，字母 "z" 在字母 "y" 后面。
前面的字母也以类似的方式定义：字母 "y" 在字母 "z" 前面，……，字母 "a" 在字母 "b" 前面。
注意，该操作不会改变单词的长度。
在第一个样例中，你可以得到唯一的另一个单词 "ba"。在第二个样例中，你无法得到任何其他单词，因此正确答案是 0。
考虑第三个样例。一次操作可以将单词“klmbfxzb”变为“klmcexzb”：我们应选择 p = 4，并将第四个字母替换为后一个字母（“b”  →  “c”），将第五个字母替换为前一个字母（“f”  →  “e”）。此外，我们还可以从这个单词得到许多其他单词。一次操作只能将单词“ya”变为另一个单词“xb”。
单词“ya”的含义与单词“xb”、“wc”、“vd”、……、“ay”相同（总共有另外 24 个单词）。单词“klmbfxzb”的变体则多得多，其含义相同的其他单词有 3320092814 个。因此，第一个单词的答案为 24，第二个单词的答案为 320092793，即 3320092814 对 109 + 7 取模的结果。

legend.ai: Sherlock Holmes 发现了两位 VIP 之间的一封神秘信件，于是决定阅读它。但问题来了！这封信件竟然经过了加密。侦探费尽心思尝试破译信件，但他什么也看不懂。
最后，经过一番思考，他想到了一个办法。设有一个由 |s| 个小写拉丁字母组成的单词 s。一次操作中，你可以选择一个位置 p（1 ≤ p < |s|），并执行以下操作之一：
要么将字母 s_p 替换为字典序中紧随其后的字母，并将字母 s_{p + 1} 替换为字典序中紧随其前的字母；
或将字母 sp 替换为按字母表顺序排在它之前的字母，并将字母 sp + 1 替换为按字母表顺序排在它之后的字母。
注意，字母“z”没有定义的后继字母，字母“a”也没有定义的前驱字母。因此，相应的变换是不允许的。如果某次操作至少需要执行一次不允许的变换，那么该操作无法执行。
当且仅当其中一个单词可以通过零次或多次操作转换为另一个单词时，这两个单词的含义相同。
Sherlock Holmes 需要学会快速确定对于每个单词，存在多少个与给定单词含义相同、但与给定单词至少有一个字符不同的单词。请对这个数量对 1000000007（10^9 + 7）取模后告诉他。

input.ai: 输入数据包含多组测试。第一行包含唯一的整数 t（1 ≤ t ≤ 10^4），表示测试组数。
接下来的 t 行包含这些单词，每行一个。每个单词由小写拉丁字母组成，长度在 1 到 100 之间（含端点）。不同单词的长度可以不同。

legend: Theofanis started playing the new online game called "Among them". However, he always plays with Cypriot players, and they all have the same name: "Andreas" (the most common name in Cyprus).
In each game, Theofanis plays with n$$$n$$$ other players. Since they all have the same name, they are numbered from 1$$$1$$$ to n$$$n$$$.

The players write m$$$m$$$ comments in the chat. A comment has the structure of "i$$$i$$$ j$$$j$$$ c$$$c$$$" where i$$$i$$$ and j$$$j$$$ are two distinct integers and c$$$c$$$ is a string (1≤i,j≤n$$$1 \le i, j \le n$$$; i≠j$$$i \neq j$$$; c$$$c$$$ is either imposter or crewmate). The comment means that player i$$$i$$$ said that player j$$$j$$$ has the role c$$$c$$$.
An imposter always lies, and a crewmate always tells the truth.
Help Theofanis find the maximum possible number of imposters among all the other Cypriot players, or determine that the comments contradict each other (see the notes for further explanation).
Note that each player has exactly one role: either imposter or crewmate.
input: The first line contains a single integer t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤104$$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. Description of each test case follows.

The first line of each test case contains two integers n$$$n$$$ and m$$$m$$$ (1≤n≤2⋅105$$$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$; 0≤m≤5⋅105$$$0 \le m \le 5 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of players except Theofanis and the number of comments.

Each of the next m$$$m$$$ lines contains a comment made by the players of the structure "i$$$i$$$ j$$$j$$$ c$$$c$$$" where i$$$i$$$ and j$$$j$$$ are two distinct integers and c$$$c$$$ is a string (1≤i,j≤n$$$1 \le i, j \le n$$$; i≠j$$$i \neq j$$$; c$$$c$$$ is either imposter or crewmate).
There can be multiple comments for the same pair of (i,j)$$$(i, j)$$$.
It is guaranteed that the sum of all n$$$n$$$ does not exceed 2⋅105$$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$ and the sum of all m$$$m$$$ does not exceed 5⋅105$$$5 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output: For each test case, print one integer — the maximum possible number of imposters. If the comments contradict each other, print −1$$$-1$$$.
note: In the first test case, imposters can be Andreas 2$$$2$$$ and 3$$$3$$$.
In the second test case, imposters can be Andreas 1$$$1$$$, 2$$$2$$$, 3$$$3$$$ and 5$$$5$$$.

In the third test case, comments contradict each other. This is because player 1$$$1$$$ says that player 2$$$2$$$ is an imposter, and player 2$$$2$$$ says that player 1$$$1$$$ is a crewmate. If player 1$$$1$$$ is a crewmate, then he must be telling the truth, so player 2$$$2$$$ must be an imposter. But if player 2$$$2$$$ is an imposter then he must be lying, so player 1$$$1$$$ can't be a crewmate. Contradiction.

legend.ai: Theofanis 开始玩一款名为“Among them”的新在线游戏。然而，他总是与塞浦路斯玩家一起游戏，并且他们都有相同的名字：“Andreas”（这是塞浦路斯最常见的名字）。
在每场游戏中，Theofanis 会与 n$$$n$$$ 名其他玩家一起进行游戏。由于他们都有相同的名字，因此他们的编号从 1$$$1$$$ 到 n$$$n$$$。

玩家们在聊天中发送了 m$$$m$$$ 条评论。一条评论的格式为“i$$$i$$$ j$$$j$$$ c$$$c$$$”，其中 i$$$i$$$ 和 j$$$j$$$ 是两个不同的整数，c$$$c$$$ 是一个字符串(1≤i,j≤n$$$1 \le i, j \le n$$$；i≠j$$$i \neq j$$$；c$$$c$$$ 要么是 imposter，要么是 crewmate)。这条评论表示玩家 i$$$i$$$ 说玩家 j$$$j$$$ 的身份是 c$$$c$$$。

注意，每名玩家恰好拥有一个身份：冒充者或船员。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 t$$$t$$$(1≤t≤104$$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$)，表示测试用例的数量。接下来是每个测试用例的描述。
每个测试用例的第一行包含两个整数 n$$$n$$$ 和 m$$$m$$$(1≤n≤2⋅105$$$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$；0≤m≤5⋅105$$$0 \le m \le 5 \cdot 10^5$$$)，分别表示除 Theofanis 外的玩家数量和评论数量。

同一对 (i,j)$$$(i, j)$$$ 可能有多条评论。

output.ai: 对于每个测试用例，输出一个整数，即内鬼数量的最大可能值。如果评论相互矛盾，则输出 −1$$$-1$$$。

在第三个测试用例中，评论相互矛盾。这是因为玩家 1$$$1$$$ 说玩家 2$$$2$$$ 是内鬼，而玩家 2$$$2$$$ 说玩家 1$$$1$$$ 是船员。如果玩家 1$$$1$$$ 是船员，那么他说的必须是真话，因此玩家 2$$$2$$$ 必须是内鬼。但如果玩家 2$$$2$$$ 是内鬼，那么他说的必定是假话，所以玩家 1$$$1$$$ 不可能是船员。矛盾。

legend: One day Petya got a birthday present from his mom: a book called "The Legends and Myths of Graph Theory". From this book Petya learned about a hydra graph.

A non-oriented graph is a hydra, if it has a structure, shown on the figure below. Namely, there are two nodes u and v connected by an edge, they are the hydra's chest and stomach, correspondingly. The chest is connected with h nodes, which are the hydra's heads. The stomach is connected with t nodes, which are the hydra's tails. Note that the hydra is a tree, consisting of h + t + 2 nodes.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/16648c075592d18dd689fda9aae45370aa62b8c0.png)
Also, Petya's got a non-directed graph G, consisting of n nodes and m edges. Petya got this graph as a last year birthday present from his mom. Graph G contains no self-loops or multiple edges.
Now Petya wants to find a hydra in graph G. Or else, to make sure that the graph doesn't have a hydra.
input: The first line contains four integers n, m, h, t (1 ≤ n, m ≤ 105, 1 ≤ h, t ≤ 100) — the number of nodes and edges in graph G, and the number of a hydra's heads and tails.
Next m lines contain the description of the edges of graph G. The i-th of these lines contains two integers ai and bi (1 ≤ ai, bi ≤ n, a ≠ b) — the numbers of the nodes, connected by the i-th edge.
It is guaranteed that graph G contains no self-loops and multiple edges. Consider the nodes of graph G numbered with integers from 1 to n.
output: If graph G has no hydra, print "NO" (without the quotes).

Otherwise, in the first line print "YES" (without the quotes). In the second line print two integers — the numbers of nodes u and v. In the third line print h numbers — the numbers of the nodes that are the heads. In the fourth line print t numbers — the numbers of the nodes that are the tails. All printed numbers should be distinct.
If there are multiple possible answers, you are allowed to print any of them.
note: The first sample is depicted on the picture below:
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/1c8c8b9458fa2f6fcea9f9ba033143a1b63dd241.png)

input.ai: 第一行包含四个整数 n、m、h、t（1 ≤ n，m ≤ 105，1 ≤ h，t ≤ 100）——图 G 中节点和边的数量，以及一只九头蛇的头和尾的数量。
接下来的 m 行包含图 G 的边的描述。其中第 i 行包含两个整数 ai 和 bi（1 ≤ ai，bi ≤ n，a ≠ b）——由第 i 条边连接的节点编号。
保证图 G 不包含自环和重边。将图 G 中的节点编号为 1 至 n 的整数。

output.ai: 如果图 G 中不存在九头蛇，输出 "NO"（不含引号）。
否则，第一行输出 "YES"（不含引号）。第二行输出两个整数——节点 u 和 v 的编号。第三行输出 h 个整数——作为头的节点编号。第四行输出 t 个整数——作为尾的节点编号。所有输出的数字都应互不相同。
如果有多个可行答案，允许输出其中任意一个。

legend.ai: 一天，Petya 从妈妈那里收到了一份生日礼物：一本名为《图论中的传说与神话》的书。Petya 从这本书中了解到了九头蛇图。
如果一个无向图具有下图所示的结构，那么它就是一条九头蛇。具体来说，有两个节点 u 和 v 通过一条边相连，它们分别是九头蛇的胸部和胃部。胸部与 h 个节点相连，这些节点就是九头蛇的头。胃部与 t 个节点相连，这些节点就是九头蛇的尾巴。注意，九头蛇是一棵树，由 h + t + 2 个节点组成。
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/16648c075592d18dd689fda9aae45370aa62b8c0.png)
此外，Petya 还有一个由 n 个节点和 m 条边组成的无向图 G。这张图是妈妈去年送给他的生日礼物。图 G 不包含自环或重边。
现在，Petya 想在图 G 中找到一条九头蛇。或者确认图中不存在九头蛇。

![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/1c8c8b9458fa2f6fcea9f9ba033143a1b63dd241.png)

legend: Andrey needs one more problem to conduct a programming contest. He has n friends who are always willing to help. He can ask some of them to come up with a contest problem. Andrey knows one value for each of his fiends — the probability that this friend will come up with a problem if Andrey asks him.

Help Andrey choose people to ask. As he needs only one problem, Andrey is going to be really upset if no one comes up with a problem or if he gets more than one problem from his friends. You need to choose such a set of people that maximizes the chances of Andrey not getting upset.
input: The first line contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 100) — the number of Andrey's friends. The second line contains n real numbers pi (0.0 ≤ pi ≤ 1.0) — the probability that the i-th friend can come up with a problem. The probabilities are given with at most 6 digits after decimal point.
output: Print a single real number — the probability that Andrey won't get upset at the optimal choice of friends. The answer will be considered valid if it differs from the correct one by at most 10 - 9.
note: In the first sample the best strategy for Andrey is to ask only one of his friends, the most reliable one.
In the second sample the best strategy for Andrey is to ask all of his friends to come up with a problem. Then the probability that he will get exactly one problem is 0.1·0.8 + 0.9·0.2 = 0.26.

output.ai: 输出一个实数，即 Andrey 在选择朋友的最优方案下不会感到沮丧的概率。如果答案与正确答案的绝对误差不超过 10 - 9，则该答案会被判定为正确。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，Andrey 的最佳策略是只询问他的一位朋友，也就是最可靠的那位朋友。
在第二个样例中，Andrey 的最佳策略是让所有朋友都想出一个问题。这样，他恰好得到一个问题的概率为 0.1·0.8 + 0.9·0.2 = 0.26。

legend.ai: Andrey 还需要一道题目来举办编程竞赛。他有 n 个总是愿意提供帮助的朋友。他可以请其中一些人提出一道竞赛题目。对于每位朋友，Andrey 都知道一个值：如果 Andrey 向这位朋友请求帮助，该朋友提出一道题目的概率。
请帮助 Andrey 选择要请求的人员。由于他只需要一道题目，如果没有人提出题目，或者从朋友那里得到了多于一道题目，Andrey 都会非常失望。你需要选择一个人员集合，使 Andrey 不失望的概率最大。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 100），表示 Andrey 的朋友数量。第二行包含 n 个实数 pi（0.0 ≤ pi ≤ 1.0），表示第 i 位朋友能够提出一道题目的概率。每个概率的小数点后最多有 6 位数字。

statement.title: D. N Problems During K Days

legend: Polycarp has to solve exactly n$$$n$$$ problems to improve his programming skill before an important programming competition. But this competition will be held very soon, most precisely, it will start in k$$$k$$$ days. It means that Polycarp has exactly k$$$k$$$ days for training!

Polycarp doesn't want to procrastinate, so he wants to solve at least one problem during each of k$$$k$$$ days. He also doesn't want to overwork, so if he solves x$$$x$$$ problems during some day, he should solve no more than 2x$$$2x$$$ problems during the next day. And, at last, he wants to improve his skill, so if he solves x$$$x$$$ problems during some day, he should solve at least x+1$$$x+1$$$ problem during the next day.

More formally: let [a1,a2,…,ak]$$$[a_1, a_2, \dots, a_k]$$$ be the array of numbers of problems solved by Polycarp. The i$$$i$$$-th element of this array is the number of problems Polycarp solves during the i$$$i$$$-th day of his training. Then the following conditions must be satisfied:
sum of all ai$$$a_i$$$ for i$$$i$$$ from 1$$$1$$$ to k$$$k$$$ should be n$$$n$$$;
ai$$$a_i$$$ should be greater than zero for each i$$$i$$$ from 1$$$1$$$ to k$$$k$$$;
the condition ai<ai+1≤2ai$$$a_i  \lt  a_{i + 1} \le 2 a_i$$$ should be satisfied for each i$$$i$$$ from 1$$$1$$$ to k−1$$$k-1$$$.
Your problem is to find any array a$$$a$$$ of length k$$$k$$$ satisfying the conditions above or say that it is impossible to do it.
input: The first line of the input contains two integers n$$$n$$$ and k$$$k$$$ (1≤n≤109,1≤k≤105$$$1 \le n \le 10^9, 1 \le k \le 10^5$$$) — the number of problems Polycarp wants to solve and the number of days Polycarp wants to train.
output: If it is impossible to find any array a$$$a$$$ of length k$$$k$$$ satisfying Polycarp's rules of training, print "NO" in the first line.

Otherwise print "YES" in the first line, then print k$$$k$$$ integers a1,a2,…,ak$$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_k$$$ in the second line, where ai$$$a_i$$$ should be the number of problems Polycarp should solve during the i$$$i$$$-th day. If there are multiple answers, you can print any.

legend.ai: Polycarp 必须恰好解决 n$$$n$$$ 个问题，以便在一场重要的编程竞赛前提高自己的编程能力。但这场竞赛很快就要举行了，更准确地说，竞赛将在 k$$$k$$$ 天后开始。这意味着 Polycarp 恰好有 k$$$k$$$ 天用于训练！

legend: It was recycling day in Kekoland. To celebrate it Adil and Bera went to Central Perk where they can take bottles from the ground and put them into a recycling bin.
We can think Central Perk as coordinate plane. There are n bottles on the ground, the i-th bottle is located at position (xi, yi). Both Adil and Bera can carry only one bottle at once each.
For both Adil and Bera the process looks as follows:
Choose to stop or to continue to collect bottles.
If the choice was to continue then choose some bottle and walk towards it.
Pick this bottle and walk to the recycling bin.
Go to step 1.

Adil and Bera may move independently. They are allowed to pick bottles simultaneously, all bottles may be picked by any of the two, it's allowed that one of them stays still while the other one continues to pick bottles.

They want to organize the process such that the total distance they walk (the sum of distance walked by Adil and distance walked by Bera) is minimum possible. Of course, at the end all bottles should lie in the recycling bin.

Then follow n lines, each of them contains two integers xi and yi (0 ≤ xi, yi ≤ 109) — position of the i-th bottle.
It's guaranteed that positions of Adil, Bera, recycling bin and all bottles are distinct.
output: Print one real number — the minimum possible total distance Adil and Bera need to walk in order to put all bottles into recycling bin. Your answer will be considered correct if its absolute or relative error does not exceed 10 - 6.

legend: Let's call the following process a transformation of a sequence of length n$$$n$$$.

If the sequence is empty, the process ends. Otherwise, append the greatest common divisor (GCD) of all the elements of the sequence to the result and remove one arbitrary element from the sequence. Thus, when the process ends, we have a sequence of n$$$n$$$ integers: the greatest common divisors of all the elements in the sequence before each deletion.
You are given an integer sequence 1,2,…,n$$$1, 2, \dots, n$$$. Find the lexicographically maximum result of its transformation.

A sequence a1,a2,…,an$$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ is lexicographically larger than a sequence b1,b2,…,bn$$$b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_n$$$, if there is an index i$$$i$$$ such that aj=bj$$$a_j = b_j$$$ for all j<i$$$j  \lt  i$$$, and ai>bi$$$a_i  \gt  b_i$$$.
input: The first and only line of input contains one integer n$$$n$$$ (1≤n≤106$$$1\le n\le 10^6$$$).
output: Output n$$$n$$$ integers  — the lexicographically maximum result of the transformation.
note: In the first sample the answer may be achieved this way:
We get the sequence [1,1,3]$$$[1, 1, 3]$$$ as the result.

legend.ai: 我们将以下过程称为长度为 n$$$n$$$ 的序列的变换。
如果序列为空，则过程结束。否则，将序列中所有元素的最大公约数(GCD)追加到结果中，并从序列中删除任意一个元素。因此，当过程结束时，我们得到一个包含 n$$$n$$$ 个整数的序列：每次删除前序列中所有元素的最大公约数。
给定整数序列 1,2,…,n$$$1, 2, \dots, n$$$。求其变换结果中字典序最大的序列。
如果存在一个下标 i$$$i$$$，使得对于所有 j<i$$$j  \lt  i$$$，均有 aj=bj$$$a_j = b_j$$$，且 ai>bi$$$a_i  \gt  b_i$$$，则称序列 a1,a2,…,an$$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ 的字典序大于序列 b1,b2,…,bn$$$b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_n$$$。

legend: You have an n × m rectangle table, its cells are not initially painted. Your task is to paint all cells of the table. The resulting picture should be a tiling of the table with squares. More formally:

One coloring (let's call it X) is considered lexicographically less than the other one (let's call it Y), if:
consider all the table cells from left to right and from top to bottom (first, the first cell in the first row, then the second cell in the first row and so on);

the letter that marks the color of the cell in X, goes alphabetically before the letter that marks the color of the cell in Y.

legend: Today on Informatics class Nastya learned about GCD and LCM (see links below). Nastya is very intelligent, so she solved all the tasks momentarily and now suggests you to solve one of them as well.

We define a pair of integers (a, b) good, if GCD(a, b) = x and LCM(a, b) = y, where GCD(a, b) denotes the greatest common divisor of a and b, and LCM(a, b) denotes the least common multiple of a and b.
You are given two integers x and y. You are to find the number of good pairs of integers (a, b) such that l ≤ a, b ≤ r. Note that pairs (a, b) and (b, a) are considered different if a ≠ b.

note: In the first example there are two suitable good pairs of integers (a, b): (1, 2) and (2, 1).
In the second example there are four suitable good pairs of integers (a, b): (1, 12), (12, 1), (3, 4) and (4, 3).
In the third example there are good pairs of integers, for example, (3, 30), but none of them fits the condition l ≤ a, b ≤ r.

input.ai: 唯一一行包含四个整数 l、r、x、y（1 ≤ l ≤ r ≤ 10^9，1 ≤ x ≤ y ≤ 10^9）。

在第三个样例中存在满足条件的整数对，例如 (3、30)，但它们都不满足条件 l ≤ a、b ≤ r。

legend: Asya loves animals very much. Recently, she purchased n$$$n$$$ kittens, enumerated them from 1$$$1$$$ and n$$$n$$$ and then put them into the cage. The cage consists of one row of n$$$n$$$ cells, enumerated with integers from 1$$$1$$$ to n$$$n$$$ from left to right. Adjacent cells had a partially transparent partition wall between them, hence there were n−1$$$n - 1$$$ partitions originally. Initially, each cell contained exactly one kitten with some number.

Observing the kittens, Asya noticed, that they are very friendly and often a pair of kittens in neighboring cells wants to play together. So Asya started to remove partitions between neighboring cells. In particular, on the day i$$$i$$$, Asya:
Noticed, that the kittens xi$$$x_i$$$ and yi$$$y_i$$$, located in neighboring cells want to play together.
Removed the partition between these two cells, efficiently creating a single cell, having all kittens from two original cells.
Since Asya has never putted partitions back, after n−1$$$n - 1$$$ days the cage contained a single cell, having all kittens.

For every day, Asya remembers numbers of kittens xi$$$x_i$$$ and yi$$$y_i$$$, who wanted to play together, however she doesn't remember how she placed kittens in the cage in the beginning. Please help her and find any possible initial arrangement of the kittens into n$$$n$$$ cells.

It's guaranteed, that there is at least one answer possible. In case there are multiple possible answers, print any of them.
note: The answer for the example contains one of several possible initial arrangements of the kittens.
The picture below shows how the cells were united for this initial arrangement. Note, that the kittens who wanted to play together on each day were indeed in adjacent cells.
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/2bc8ecf1d73b5bf637e7d4f74a0abc5de310332d.png)

legend.ai: Asya 非常喜欢动物。最近，她购买了 n$$$n$$$ 只小猫，给它们编号为 1$$$1$$$ 到 n$$$n$$$，然后将它们放进笼子里。笼子由一排 n$$$n$$$ 个单元格组成，从左到右编号为 1$$$1$$$ 到 n$$$n$$$。相邻单元格之间有一面半透明的隔板，因此最初共有 n−1$$$n - 1$$$ 面隔板。开始时，每个单元格中恰好有一只带有某个编号的小猫。
观察这些小猫时，Asya 注意到它们非常友好，并且相邻格子中的一对小猫经常想一起玩耍。因此，Asya 开始拆除相邻格子之间的隔板。具体来说，在第 i$$$i$$$ 天，Asya：
注意到位于相邻格子中的小猫 x$$$x_i$$$ 和 y$$$y_i$$$ 想一起玩耍。
拆除了这两个格子之间的隔板，从而有效地将它们合并成一个格子，其中包含原来两个格子里的所有小猫。
由于 Asya 从未重新放回隔板，因此 n−1$$$n - 1$$$ 天后，笼子中只剩下一个格子，里面有所有小猫。
对于每一天，Asya 都记得想一起玩耍的小猫 x$$$x_i$$$ 和 y$$$y_i$$$ 的编号，但她不记得一开始是如何将小猫放入笼子中的。请帮助她找出一种将小猫放入 n$$$n$$$ 个格子中的可能初始排列。

input.ai: 以下 n−1$$$n - 1$$$ 行中的每一行包含整数 xi$$$x_i$$$ 和 yi$$$y_i$$$(1≤xi,yi≤n$$$1 \le x_i, y_i \le n$$$，xi≠yi$$$x_i \ne y_i$$$)，表示由于当天移除边界而聚在一起的两只小猫的编号。
保证在这一天之前，小猫 xi$$$x_i$$$ 和 yi$$$y_i$$$ 位于不同的格子中。

输出的所有整数必须互不相同。
保证至少存在一种可行答案。如果有多种可行答案，输出其中任意一种即可。

One fragment of the prophecy is a sequence of n digits. The first digit isn't zero. Limak thinks that it's a list of some special years. It's hard to see any commas or spaces, so maybe ancient people didn't use them. Now Limak wonders what years are listed there.
Limak assumes three things:

There are no leading zeros.

Limak is going to consider all possible ways to split a sequence into numbers (years), satisfying the conditions above. He will do it without any help. However, he asked you to tell him the number of ways to do so. Since this number may be very large, you are only asked to calculate it modulo 109 + 7.

legend.ai: Limak 是一只小北极熊。他在雪地里发现了一卷写有古老预言的卷轴。Limak 不懂任何古代语言，因此无法理解这则预言。但他认识数字！
预言的一个片段是一个由 n 个数字组成的序列。第一个数字不为零。Limak 认为这是一张特殊年份的列表。很难看出其中有任何逗号或空格，所以古人可能没有使用它们。现在，Limak 想知道其中列出了哪些年份。
Limak 作出以下三个假设：

Limak 将考虑把一个序列划分为若干个数字（年份）的所有可能方式，并且这些数字满足上述条件。他将独自完成这件事。不过，他请你告诉他这样划分的方案数。由于这个数字可能非常大，你只需计算它对 10^9+7 取模的结果。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 5000），表示数字的个数。
第二行包含一个数字字符串，其长度等于 n。保证第一个数字不是 '0'。

legend: Tomash keeps wandering off and getting lost while he is walking along the streets of Berland. It's no surprise! In his home town, for any pair of intersections there is exactly one way to walk from one intersection to the other one. The capital of Berland is very different!

Tomash has noticed that even simple cases of ambiguity confuse him. So, when he sees a group of four distinct intersections a, b, c and d, such that there are two paths from a to c — one through b and the other one through d, he calls the group a "damn rhombus". Note that pairs (a, b), (b, c), (a, d), (d, c) should be directly connected by the roads. Schematically, a damn rhombus is shown on the figure below:
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c52c38049d87baaa213c83b4aef02548380a0349.png)
Other roads between any of the intersections don't make the rhombus any more appealing to Tomash, so the four intersections remain a "damn rhombus" for him.
Given that the capital of Berland has n intersections and m roads and all roads are unidirectional and are known in advance, find the number of "damn rhombi" in the city.
When rhombi are compared, the order of intersections b and d doesn't matter.
input: The first line of the input contains a pair of integers n, m (1 ≤ n ≤ 3000, 0 ≤ m ≤ 30000) — the number of intersections and roads, respectively. Next m lines list the roads, one per line. Each of the roads is given by a pair of integers ai, bi (1 ≤ ai, bi ≤ n;ai ≠ bi) — the number of the intersection it goes out from and the number of the intersection it leads to. Between a pair of intersections there is at most one road in each of the two directions.
It is not guaranteed that you can get from any intersection to any other one.
output: Print the required number of "damn rhombi".

legend.ai: Tomash 在 Berland 的街道上行走时，总是不停地走失。真是一点也不奇怪！在他的家乡，任意两个路口之间都恰好有一条步行路线。但 Berland 的首都却大不相同！
Tomash 注意到，即使是简单的歧义情况也会让他感到困惑。因此，当他看到四个互不相同的路口 a、b、c 和 d，且从 a 到 c 存在两条路径，一条经过 b，另一条经过 d 时，他就把这组路口称为“该死的菱形”。注意，路口对 (a, b)、(b, c)、(a, d)、(d, c) 之间都应该有直接相连的道路。示意图如下所示：
![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c52c38049d87baaa213c83b4aef02548380a0349.png)
任意路口之间的其他道路并不会让这个菱形在 Tomash 眼中变得更讨喜，因此这四个路口对他来说仍然是一个“该死的菱形”。
已知 Berland 的首都有 n 个路口和 m 条道路，所有道路都是单向的，并且事先已知。请求出城市中“该死的菱形”的数量。
比较菱形时，路口 b 和 d 的顺序并不重要。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含两个整数 n、m（1 ≤ n ≤ 3000，0 ≤ m ≤ 30000），分别表示路口数和道路数。接下来 m 行每行描述一条道路。每条道路由两个整数 ai、bi 表示（1 ≤ ai，bi ≤ n；ai ≠ bi），分别表示道路起点路口和终点路口的编号。对于一对路口，在每个方向上至多有一条道路。
无法保证你能从任意一个路口到达其他任意路口。

output.ai: 输出所需数量的“该死的菱形”。

titleZh.ai: D. 存在的难以忍受的争议

problems.hint: How will the distance between $u$ and $v$ change?

legend: Sergey Semyonovich is a mayor of a county city N and he used to spend his days and nights in thoughts of further improvements of Nkers' lives. Unfortunately for him, anything and everything has been done already, and there are no more possible improvements he can think of during the day (he now prefers to sleep at night). However, his assistants have found a solution and they now draw an imaginary city on a paper sheet and suggest the mayor can propose its improvements.

Right now he has a map of some imaginary city with n$$$n$$$ subway stations. Some stations are directly connected with tunnels in such a way that the whole map is a tree (assistants were short on time and enthusiasm). It means that there exists exactly one simple path between each pair of station. We call a path simple if it uses each tunnel no more than once.

One of Sergey Semyonovich's favorite quality objectives is the sum of all pairwise distances between every pair of stations. The distance between two stations is the minimum possible number of tunnels on a path between them.

Sergey Semyonovich decided to add new tunnels to the subway map. In particular, he connected any two stations u$$$u$$$ and v$$$v$$$ that were not connected with a direct tunnel but share a common neighbor, i.e. there exists such a station w$$$w$$$ that the original map has a tunnel between u$$$u$$$ and w$$$w$$$ and a tunnel between w$$$w$$$ and v$$$v$$$. You are given a task to compute the sum of pairwise distances between all pairs of stations in the new map.
input: The first line of the input contains a single integer n$$$n$$$ (2≤n≤200000$$$2 \leq n \leq 200\,000$$$) — the number of subway stations in the imaginary city drawn by mayor's assistants. Each of the following n−1$$$n - 1$$$ lines contains two integers ui$$$u_i$$$ and vi$$$v_i$$$ (1≤ui,vi≤n$$$1 \leq u_i, v_i \leq n$$$, ui≠vi$$$u_i \ne v_i$$$), meaning the station with these indices are connected with a direct tunnel.
It is guaranteed that these n$$$n$$$ stations and n−1$$$n - 1$$$ tunnels form a tree.
output: Print one integer that is equal to the sum of distances between all pairs of stations after Sergey Semyonovich draws new tunnels between all pairs of stations that share a common neighbor in the original map.
note: In the first sample, in the new map all pairs of stations share a direct connection, so the sum of distances is 6$$$6$$$.
In the second sample, the new map has a direct tunnel between all pairs of stations except for the pair (1,4)$$$(1, 4)$$$. For these two stations the distance is 2$$$2$$$.

legend.ai: Sergey Semyonovich 是县城 N 的市长，他过去总是日夜思考如何进一步改善 N 市居民的生活。遗憾的是，对他而言，一切能做的事情都已经完成了，白天他再也想不出任何可以改进的地方（现在他更喜欢在晚上睡觉）。不过，他的助手们找到了一个解决办法：他们在一张纸上绘制一座虚构的城市，并建议市长提出改进方案。
现在，他有一张某座虚构城市的地图，上面有 n$$$n$$$ 个地铁站。部分车站之间通过隧道直接相连，使得整张地图构成一棵树(助手们时间和热情都有限)。这意味着任意两个车站之间恰好存在一条简单路径。若一条路径中每条隧道至多被使用一次，我们就称其为简单路径。
Sergey Semyonovich 最喜欢的质量指标之一，是所有车站对之间距离的总和。两个车站之间的距离，是连接它们的路径上隧道数量的最小可能值。

谢尔盖·谢苗诺维奇决定向地铁线路图中添加新的隧道。具体来说，他将任意两个站点 u$$$u$$$ 和 v$$$v$$$ 连接起来：它们之间原本没有直接隧道，但有一个公共邻居。也就是说，存在这样一个站点 w$$$w$$$，使得原地图中 u$$$u$$$ 与 w$$$w$$$ 之间有一条隧道，且 w$$$w$$$ 与 v$$$v$$$ 之间有一条隧道。现在给定一项任务，请计算新地图中所有站点对之间的距离总和。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含一个整数 n$$$n$$$(2≤n≤200000$$$2 \leq n \leq 200\,000$$$)，表示由市长助理绘制的虚构城市中的地铁站数量。接下来的 n−1$$$n - 1$$$ 行中，每行包含两个整数 ui$$$u_i$$$ 和 vi$$$v_i$$$(1≤ui,vi≤n$$$1 \leq u_i, v_i \leq n$$$，ui≠vi$$$u_i \ne v_i$$$)，表示编号为这两个数的站点之间通过直接隧道相连。
保证这 n$$$n$$$ 个站点和 n−1$$$n - 1$$$ 条隧道构成一棵树。

output.ai: 输出一个整数，表示谢尔盖·谢苗诺维奇在原地图中所有具有公共邻居的站点对之间修建新隧道后，所有站点对之间的距离总和。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，新地图中所有站点对之间都有直接连接，因此距离总和为 6$$$6$$$。
在第二个样例中，除了站点对 (1,4)$$$(1, 4)$$$ 之外，新地图中所有站点对之间都有直接隧道。对于这两个站点，它们之间的距离为 2$$$2$$$。

legend: Polycarp is a head of a circus troupe. There are n$$$n$$$ — an even number — artists in the troupe. It is known whether the i$$$i$$$-th artist can perform as a clown (if yes, then ci=1$$$c_i = 1$$$, otherwise ci=0$$$c_i = 0$$$), and whether they can perform as an acrobat (if yes, then ai=1$$$a_i = 1$$$, otherwise ai=0$$$a_i = 0$$$).
Split the artists into two performances in such a way that:
each artist plays in exactly one performance,
the number of artists in the two performances is equal (i.e. equal to n2$$$\frac{n}{2}$$$),
the number of artists that can perform as clowns in the first performance is the same as the number of artists that can perform as acrobats in the second performance.
input: The first line contains a single integer n$$$n$$$ (2≤n≤5000$$$2 \le n \le 5\,000$$$, n$$$n$$$ is even) — the number of artists in the troupe.
The second line contains n$$$n$$$ digits c1c2…cn$$$c_1 c_2 \ldots c_n$$$, the i$$$i$$$-th of which is equal to 1$$$1$$$ if the i$$$i$$$-th artist can perform as a clown, and 0$$$0$$$ otherwise.
The third line contains n$$$n$$$ digits a1a2…an$$$a_1 a_2 \ldots a_n$$$, the i$$$i$$$-th of which is equal to 1$$$1$$$, if the i$$$i$$$-th artist can perform as an acrobat, and 0$$$0$$$ otherwise.
output: Print n2$$$\frac{n}{2}$$$ distinct integers — the indices of the artists that should play in the first performance.
If there are multiple answers, print any.
If there is no solution, print a single integer −1$$$-1$$$.
note: In the first example, one of the possible divisions into two performances is as follows: in the first performance artists 1$$$1$$$ and 4$$$4$$$ should take part. Then the number of artists in the first performance who can perform as clowns is equal to 1$$$1$$$. And the number of artists in the second performance who can perform as acrobats is 1$$$1$$$ as well.
In the second example, the division is not possible.

In the third example, one of the possible divisions is as follows: in the first performance artists 3$$$3$$$ and 4$$$4$$$ should take part. Then in the first performance there are 2$$$2$$$ artists who can perform as clowns. And the number of artists in the second performance who can perform as acrobats is 2$$$2$$$ as well.

legend.ai: Polycarp 是一个马戏团的团长。马戏团中有 n$$$n$$$ 名艺术家，且人数为偶数。已知第 i$$$i$$$ 名艺术家是否可以扮演小丑(如果可以，则 ci=1$$$c_i = 1$$$，否则 ci=0$$$c_i = 0$$$)，以及他们是否可以表演杂技(如果可以，则 ai=1$$$a_i = 1$$$，否则 ai=0$$$a_i = 0$$$)。
将这些演员分成两场演出，使得：
每位演员恰好参加其中一场演出，
两场演出中的演员数量相等(即均为 n2$$$\frac{n}{2}$$$)，
第一场演出中能够扮演小丑的演员人数，与第二场演出中能够表演杂技的演员人数相同。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n$$$n$$$(2≤n≤5000$$$2 \le n \le 5\,000$$$，n$$$n$$$ 为偶数)——剧团中艺术家的数量。
第二行包含 n$$$n$$$ 个数字 c1c2…cn$$$c_1 c_2 \ldots c_n$$$，如果第 i$$$i$$$ 位艺术家可以扮演小丑，则其中第 i$$$i$$$ 个数字等于 1$$$1$$$，否则等于 0$$$0$$$。
第三行包含 n$$$n$$$ 个数字 a1a2…an$$$a_1 a_2 \ldots a_n$$$，如果第 i$$$i$$$ 位艺术家可以表演杂技，则其中第 i$$$i$$$ 个数字等于 1$$$1$$$，否则等于 0$$$0$$$。

output.ai: 输出 n2$$$\frac{n}{2}$$$ 个互不相同的整数——应在第一场演出中表演的艺术家的编号。
如果有多个答案，输出任意一个。
如果无解，输出一个整数 −1$$$-1$$$。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，一种将其分成两场表演的方案如下：第一场表演应由艺术家 1$$$1$$$ 和 4$$$4$$$ 参加。随后，第一场表演中能够扮演小丑的艺术家数量为 1$$$1$$$。第二场表演中能够表演杂技的艺术家数量同样为 1$$$1$$$。
在第二个样例中，无法完成这样的划分。
在第三个样例中，一种可行的划分方案如下：第一场表演应由艺术家 3$$$3$$$ 和 4$$$4$$$ 参加。随后，第一场表演中有 2$$$2$$$ 位艺术家能够扮演小丑。第二场表演中能够表演杂技的艺术家数量同样为 2$$$2$$$。

statement.title: D2. Submarine in the Rybinsk Sea (hard edition)

legend: This problem differs from the previous one only in the absence of the constraint on the equal length of all numbers a1,a2,…,an$$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$.

A team of SIS students is going to make a trip on a submarine. Their target is an ancient treasure in a sunken ship lying on the bottom of the Great Rybinsk sea. Unfortunately, the students don't know the coordinates of the ship, so they asked Meshanya (who is a hereditary mage) to help them. He agreed to help them, but only if they solve his problem.

Let's denote a function that alternates digits of two numbers f(a1a2…ap−1ap,b1b2…bq−1bq)$$$f(a_1 a_2 \dots a_{p - 1} a_p, b_1 b_2 \dots b_{q - 1} b_q)$$$, where a1…ap$$$a_1 \dots a_p$$$ and b1…bq$$$b_1 \dots b_q$$$ are digits of two integers written in the decimal notation without leading zeros.

In other words, the function f(x,y)$$$f(x, y)$$$ alternately shuffles the digits of the numbers x$$$x$$$ and y$$$y$$$ by writing them from the lowest digits to the older ones, starting with the number y$$$y$$$. The result of the function is also built from right to left (that is, from the lower digits to the older ones). If the digits of one of the arguments have ended, then the remaining digits of the other argument are written out. Familiarize with examples and formal definitions of the function below.
